12	## 1. What this software is
13	
14	A long-running **archival engine**: you give it YouTube playlist/channel URLs,
15	it downloads every video, fetches sidecar metadata (subtitles, thumbnails,
16	descriptions, info.json), converts to a target container, and keeps going
17	forever — watching RSS feeds for new uploads and rescanning on a schedule.
18	
19	It is designed to survive **crashes, hard kills, network drops, full disks, and
20	files deleted behind its back**. Every state transition is persisted in SQLite,
21	so a restart continues where the last run stopped rather than starting over.
22	That principle — *never throw away work that has already been done* — is the
23	single most important thing to understand before changing failure-handling code.
24	
25	| Layer | Technology |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Runtime | Bun ≥ 1.0 (uses `bun:sqlite`, `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.serve`) |
28	| Language | TypeScript, ESM, strict mode |
29	| Job store | SQLite (`archive.db`, WAL mode) |
30	| Media tools | `yt-dlp` (extraction), `ffmpeg` (transcode/remux) |
31	| Frontend | Single-file vanilla-JS dashboard (`web_ui.html`) |
32	| Config | Zod-validated `config.json` |
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. Quick start
37	
38	```bash
39	bun install            # zod (+ dev: typescript, @types/bun)
40	# Alternative reproducible dependency install when using npm:
41	npm ci                  # installs from package-lock.json; Bun is still the runtime
42	bun run start          # run the engine (reads ./config.json, creates it if absent)
43	bun run start --port 3010 # override the dashboard port for this run only
44	bun run config         # interactive config manager (TTY)
45	bun run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
46	bun test               # full suite: unit + end-to-end (mocked tools; no network needed)
47	bun run check          # typecheck + tests
48	bun run build:win      # cross-compile dist/youtube-archive.exe (Windows)
49	                         start-archive.bat runs it from dist\ first, then the
50	                         app folder, then falls back to `bun run`
51	```
52	
53	Runtime requirements: `yt-dlp` and `ffmpeg` on `PATH` (or `ytDlpPath` /
54	`ffmpegPath` in config). `checkDependencies()` probes them **before** the
55	database opens and exits with install hints if missing. YouTube's n-challenge
56	also needs a JS runtime (Deno recommended, then Node, then Bun); a missing
57	runtime is a warning, not a startup failure, and n-challenge errors are
58	retryable rather than permanent.
59	
60	**Sandbox note:** YouTube is unreachable from this environment. The test suite
61	therefore runs the real engine against mock binaries (`tests/mocks/`) — see
62	section 9. Do not "fix" failing integration tests by adding network calls.
63	**Windows note:** the mocks are shebang scripts, and Windows neither reads
64	shebangs nor spawns extensionless files, so the integration harness compiles
65	them into real executables with `bun build --compile` (cached per run, a few
66	seconds once) and pins every tool path in the engine's config to the mocks —
67	bare-name PATH discovery could otherwise pick up real yt-dlp/ffmpeg/aria2c
68	installed on the machine. Three more Windows facts the code already accounts for:
69	some Bun builds for Windows do not implement `statfs` at all (see gotcha 22 —
70	go through `diskUsage()`), and Windows does not reparent orphans, so the mocks'
71	`process.ppid` watchdogs are inert there (see 9.3). A third one matters for the
72	unit tests: a bare executable name is resolved by the OS through the *invoking*
73	process's PATH, so spawning `["aria2c"]` with an injected `env` that has no PATH
74	still finds an installed aria2c. `resolveTool` therefore treats an injected
75	`ToolSearchEnv.env` as the whole search space and skips the bare-name candidates
76	when it carries no PATH — that is what makes "nothing is installed" testable on
77	Windows (`tests/tools.test.ts`), instead of passing only on a machine that
78	happens not to have the binary.
79	
80	### Local data, secrets, and generated files
81	
82	Runtime files are operator data, not source. Never stage or commit `config.json`
83	(it can contain private source URLs and `webToken`), `cookies.txt` (account
84	credentials), `archive.db` and its `-wal`/`-shm` files, `downloaded_videos.txt`,
85	error/report logs, downloaded media, `.part`/`.aria2` partials, `dist/`, or
86	`node_modules/`. Tests should use temporary working directories and the checked-in
87	mock fixtures. When adding new runtime outputs, add appropriate `.gitignore`
88	rules without hiding source or test fixtures; inspect `git status --short` before
89	finishing a change.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 3. Architecture
94	
95	```
96	batch_playlist_downloader.ts   entry point → src/engine.ts main()
97	update_config.ts               config manager → imports src/config.ts (shared schema)
98	web_ui.html                    dashboard frontend, served by src/web.ts
99	config.json                    user config (created from defaults on first run)
100	archive.db                     SQLite job store (+ -wal/-shm while running)
101	error.log                      rotating error log
102	src/
103	  config.ts      Zod schema, DEFAULT_CONFIG, load/loadSafe/save (atomic), live-write lock, QUALITY_FORMATS
104	  db.ts          SQLite schema, migrations, atomic claim transactions, claim leases (token/heartbeat/CAS), helpers
105	  lease.ts       database-level engine lease (owner token, expiry, monotonic fencing) — one engine per archive.db
106	  state.ts       shared mutable runtime state (leaf module — imports nothing)
107	  tools.ts       yt-dlp/ffmpeg/aria2c/JS-runtime discovery, cookiesArgs, jsRuntimeArgs, validateCookies
108	  download-args.ts PURE yt-dlp command construction (downloader engine, tuning)
109	  download-output.ts bounded pipe decoding + validated FILEPATH records (no fs calls)
110	  audio-tracks.ts PURE multi-audio track parsing/selection + the yt-dlp -J probe
111	  settings.ts    dashboard-editable config allow-list + validate/persist/apply
112	  retry.ts       PURE retry policy: backoff, watchdog, error classification
113	  resilience.ts  pause/resume, circuit breaker, network + disk guards (diskUsage = the only statfs caller)
114	  reconcile.ts   self-healing sweeps (crashes, stale claims, missing files, failed jobs) + partial-file housekeeping
115	  relocate.ts    secondary-storage relocation pass (finished files that need no conversion still move)
116	  unconverted-scan.ts  "Scan Unconverted Videos": imports untracked local media + re-queues finished jobs whose file is not in the chosen target container
117	  sources.ts     Web UI URL validation/canonicalization + durable source-list additions
118	  scanner.ts     playlist/channel listing + deduplicated ingestion
119	  autoscale.ts   dynamic download-slot management
120	  workers/
121	    download.ts  yt-dlp download loop + all failure classification
122	    metadata.ts  sidecar fetching loop
123	    convert.ts   ffmpeg transcode/remux + secondary-storage move loop
124	  rss.ts         cheap per-channel RSS watcher (parseRssFeed is pure)
125	  polling.ts     daemon-mode full rescans
126	  dashboard.ts   TUI rendering
127	  report.ts      human-readable run report
128	  web.ts         Bun.serve dashboard + JSON API (route table) + token auth
129	  history.ts     heartbeated run_history rows
130	  lifecycle.ts   worker supervision + graceful shutdown
131	  engine.ts      orchestration (main): wires everything together
132	tests/           bun test suite (see section 9)
133	```
134	
135	### Import graph (acyclic — keep it that way)
136	
137	```
138	state.ts → config defaults/types ──────────────┐ (shared runtime-state leaf)
139	config.ts, util.ts, logger.ts, retry.ts,
140	archive.ts, tools.ts, download-output.ts         │ (leaf modules, zero deps)
141	audio-tracks.ts → config (types), tools          │ (pure parsing/selection + -J probe)
142	db.ts → config                                  │
143	lease.ts → db, logger                           │ (the engine lease; db must never import it)
144	resilience.ts → config, db, logger, state       │
145	reconcile.ts → archive, config, db, download-args, lease, logger, retry, state, tools│
146	relocate.ts → config, db, lease, logger, state, util, workers/convert    │ (relocation pass)
147	sources.ts → config, state                     │
148	scanner.ts → config, db, state, tools, util     │
149	autoscale.ts → db, state                        │
150	dashboard.ts → autoscale, config, db, state, util│
151	report.ts → autoscale, db, state, util          │
152	download-args.ts → audio-tracks, config, db (types), download-output, retry, tools, util    │ (pure)
153	web.ts → audio-tracks, autoscale, config, db, download-args, lease, logger, reconcile, report, resilience, retry, scanner, sources, state, tools, util
154	rss.ts → config, logger, scanner, state, tools   │
155	polling.ts → config, logger, scanner, state     │
156	history.ts → db, logger, state                  │
157	lifecycle.ts → dashboard, db, history, lease, logger, resilience, state
158	workers/* → config, dashboard, db, download-args, download-output, logger, resilience, retry, state, tools, util (+ autoscale/archive/reconcile; download.ts also audio-tracks)
159	engine.ts → everything (composition root)
160	```
161	
162	**Rule:** if you need a new shared behavior, put it in a leaf module and inject
163	it. Workers must never import `engine.ts`, and `state.ts` must stay
164	dependency-free — it is the module that breaks every import cycle.
165	
166	### Startup order (engine.ts `main()`)
167	
168	1. `loadConfig()` → apply per-run CLI overrides → `setConfig()` (must be first:
169	   dependency search uses paths from it). `--offline` / `YTA_OFFLINE` override
170	   `offlineMode` in memory; `--port <n>` selects the HTTP listener port for this
171	   run. Neither override is written to config.json, so a one-off option does not
172	   change the next normal start — and the dependency probe below sees offline mode.
173	2. `checkDependencies()` — fails fast with install hints. In offline mode a
174	   missing yt-dlp is a note, not a failure (nothing spawns it); **ffmpeg stays
175	   required** — conversion is the point of an offline pass
176	3. `initDatabase("archive.db")` — schema + migrations + claim transactions
177	4. `acquireEngineLease()` — **before any sweep: the database-level single-instance
178	   lock**. A live owner (another process, whatever its web port) makes this
179	   process exit 1 without touching a job row; an expired lease — or one whose
180	   owning process is provably gone — is taken over with `fencing + 1`.
181	   `startEngineLeaseHeartbeat()` renews it for the rest of the run; a lost lease
182	   pauses the engine (`ENGINE_LEASE_LOST`).
183	5. `startWebServer()` — the HTTP lock, acquired second so a refused start never
184	   holds the port. A second instance (autostart task + a manual start) dies here
185	   with an actionable error instead of re-queueing a live instance's work.
186	6. `reconcileCrashedJobs()` → `reconcileSupersededFiles()` →
187	   `reconcileMissingFiles()` (the superseded sweep MUST run before the
188	   missing-file sweep: an interrupted `.superseded` stash looks like a deleted
189	   file to it, and the video would be re-queued over a backup that is sitting
190	   right there; the missing-file sweep itself skips jobs with a conversion in
191	   progress — the converter legitimately has those files in mid-transition
192	   under `deleteSourceAfterConvert`; every one of these sweeps refuses to run
193	   without the engine lease)
194	7. `startRunHistory()` + heartbeat interval
195	8. `mkdir(outputRoot)` → `cleanOrphanedFiles()` → `autoscaler.init()`
196	9. cookie validation (if enabled)
197	10. scan every configured playlist/channel into the jobs table (skipped in offline mode)
198	11. `initDashboard()`
199	12. `networkMonitor()` (if enabled; skips probes while offline),
200	    `reapStaleClaims` (60s, lease-gated), `autoscaleTick` (15s),
201	    `requeueFailedJobs` (60s), `cookiesWatch` (60s, local file observation),
202	    `startRssPolling()` (always armed; no fetch while offline/disabled),
203	    `startRelocation()` (one pass +5s, then every 60s)
204	13. supervised worker pools (download × N, metadata × N, convert × N — the download
205	    and metadata loops stay idle in offline mode; workers are always started, so a
206	    live settings toggle takes effect without a restart)
207	14. `startAutonomousPolling()` if daemon mode (armed offline but does not scan until online)
208	
209	---
210	
211	## 4. Data model
212	
213	### The `jobs` table (one row per video, keyed by YouTube video id)
214	
215	| Field | Meaning |
216	| --- | --- |
217	| `id` | YouTube video id (primary key → natural dedupe) |
218	| `url` | canonical `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>` |
219	| `title`, `folder`, `index` | display name, output folder, `001`-style ordering |
220	| `output_directory` | absolute-ish path where files land |
221	| `target_format` | `mp4` \| `mkv` \| `webm` \| `mp3` \| `m4a`; editable per job (NULL follows the live global format) |
222	| `video_quality` | nullable per-job override (`highest`, `4k`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `480p`, `audio`); NULL follows global quality |
223	| `want_subtitles` / `want_thumbnail` / `want_description` | 0/1 sidecar flags |
224	| `duration` | seconds from the listing (drives the watchdog) |
225	| `download_status` | `pending` \| `downloading` \| `downloaded` \| `paused` \| `failed` \| `waiting_live` |
226	| `conversion_status` | `pending` \| `in_progress` \| `done` \| `failed` \| `not_needed` |
227	| `metadata_status` | `pending` \| `in_progress` \| `done` \| `failed` \| `not_needed` |
228	| `pause_reason` | `user` \| `interrupted` \| `waiting_live` \| NULL |
229	| `*_claimed_by` / `*_claimed_at` | worker id + timestamp of the atomic claim (display/diagnostics; ownership is the token) |
230	| `*_claim_token` | random UUID minted by the claim — the claim's real identity, since worker ids (`dl-1`) repeat across processes. Every progress/success/failure/release update is a CAS on it |
231	| `*_heartbeat_at` | last lease renewal for that stage's claim. Downloads renew it on every progress line and on a timer; conversion/metadata renew on an interval (`startClaimHeartbeat`, default 30 s, test override `YTA_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_MS`). The reaper's staleness window is measured from `COALESCE(heartbeat, claimed_at)`, never from `updated_at` |
232	| `retry_count` | no-progress download failures in the current retry window |
233	| `conversion_retry_count`, `metadata_retry_count` | per-stage attempt budgets |
234	| `resume_count` | `--continue` resumes spent for this job |
235	| `best_progress` | high-water mark of progress % (drives budget forgiveness) |
236	| `partial_file_path` | the `.part` file to resume from (NULL once complete); always absolute, so it resolves from any cwd |
237	| `file_path`, `file_size`, `integrity` | final location + SHA-256 |
238	| `audio_tracks` | JSON array of discovered audio tracks (null = not probed yet) |
239	| `audio_selection` | JSON array of per-job language codes (null = follow the global multi-audio mode) |
240	| `superseded_file` | backup path of the previous media file while a deliberate re-download runs (see §7.2) |
241	| `relocated_to` | the secondary-storage ROOT this job's media was moved under (NULL = still in the output tree). A root, not a boolean, so pointing `secondaryStoragePath` somewhere new re-offers every file; written by `finalizeConversion` (conversion move), `relocateFinishedJobs` (relocation/adoption) and cleared by `recordSuccess` (a fresh download lands in the output tree) |
242	| `progress`, `speed`, `eta` | live values for the dashboard |
243	| `last_error` | last failure message (classified by `retry.ts`) |
244	
245	Other tables: `playlist_state(folder, next_index)`,
246	`run_history(id, started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, downloaded, skipped, failed, total_queued)`,
247	and `engine_lease` — the database-level single-instance row (`id = 1`):
248	
249	| Field | Meaning |
250	| --- | --- |
251	| `owner` | random per-process token (`host:pid:random`), NULL when free/released |
252	| `fencing` | monotonic generation counter, incremented on every acquisition/takeover |
253	| `pid`, `host` | the owning process, so a restart can prove a crashed owner is gone and take over at once |
254	| `acquired_at` / `heartbeat_at` / `expires_at` | acquisition time, last renewal, and the expiry used by refusal/takeover |
255	
256	Acquisition is one immediate transaction (`src/lease.ts`): it refuses a live
257	foreign owner without writing anything, and otherwise takes the row over with
258	`fencing + 1` (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE owner IS NULL OR
259	expires_at <= now OR the owner process is gone RETURNING …`). `owner` is
260	released on graceful shutdown (the row is kept, so fencing survives); a hard
261	kill is handled by the PID check or, failing that, the expiry.
262	
263	### State machine
264	
265	```
266	ingest ──► pending ──claim──► downloading ──success──► downloaded
267	              ▲                    │
268	              │                    ├─ transient ──► pending (keep .part, backoff)
269	              │                    ├─ corrupt ────► pending (resume_count++, .part kept)
270	              │                    ├─ resume refused (416 range / aria2c control file)
271	              │                    │                ► pending, .part + .aria2 DISCARDED (restart)
272	              │                    ├─ permanent ──► failed immediately (never auto-requeued)
273	              │                    ├─ live ───────► waiting_live (requeued by next scan)
274	              │                    └─ shutdown ───► paused + interrupted (auto-resume)
275	              └── sweep (cooldown) ── retryable failed → pending + fresh retry window
276	
277	downloaded ──► metadata worker ──► metadata: pending → in_progress → done | failed
278	downloaded ──► convert worker ──► conversion: pending → in_progress → done | failed
279	                                      (skipped when conversion_status = 'not_needed',
280	                                       which recordSuccess re-opens when yt-dlp's
281	                                       actual output container differs from the
282	                                       requested one — see "Container contract")
283	```
284	
285	**Claims are the concurrency primitive.** Each stage claims work with a single
286	atomic `UPDATE … WHERE id = (SELECT … LIMIT 1) RETURNING *` inside a
287	`db.transaction`. Two workers can never grab the same job. Never add a
288	read-then-write claim sequence.
289	
290	**A claim is a lease, and the token is its identity.** The claim mints a random
291	`*_claim_token` (worker ids like `dl-1` repeat across processes and mean
292	nothing for ownership) and stamps `*_heartbeat_at`; the worker renews it while
293	the stage runs. Every later write — progress, success, failure, release — goes
294	through `updateClaimedJob` / `releaseClaimedJob` (`db.ts`), which append
295	`AND <stage>_claim_token IS ? AND <stage>_claimed_by IS ?` and return the
296	changed-row count:
297	
298	- **1** → the update landed;
299	- **0** → the claim was reaped, released, or taken over — the worker must not
300	  change job state (it logs and walks away). Do not write a bare
301	  `UPDATE jobs … WHERE id = ?` in a worker for anything that depends on owning
302	  the job.
303	
304	The reaper uses the same primitive, with the lease-expiry predicate as an extra
305	condition (`reapStaleClaim`), so it cannot reset a job whose claim was renewed
306	or already reclaimed by someone else. `ownsClaim` is the read-only form, used
307	before destructive filesystem steps (the converter's source delete, the
308	secondary-storage move, the `.superseded` restore).
309	
310	Conversion claims additionally require `metadata_status IN ('done','not_needed','failed')`
311	— the converter waits for metadata to be *terminal*, not necessarily successful.
312	
313	---
314	
315	## 5. The worker loops
316	
317	All three workers follow the same shape:
318	
319	```ts
320	while (!abortController.signal.aborted) {
321	  if (isPaused()) { await Bun.sleep(2000); continue; }
322	  const job = claimXJob(workerId);
323	  if (!job) { await Bun.sleep(pollMs); continue; }
324	  try { await doWork(job, config); }
325	  catch (err) { await handleFailure(job, config, err); }
326	  finally { /* cleanup: unregister proc, autoscaler speed */ }
327	}
328	```
329	
330	- **downloadWorker** — gates on `activeDlSlots.has(id)` (autoscaling) and
331	  `checkDiskSpace()` before claiming. Spawns yt-dlp with `--continue`,
332	  `--no-overwrites`, `--download-archive`, parses `PROGRESS:` lines from the
333	  progress template into the DB, and captures the final path from
334	  `--print after_move:FILEPATH:%(filepath)s` (validated before any filesystem call).
335	- **metadataWorker** — second yt-dlp pass with `--skip-download`, writes only
336	  requested sidecar types absent next to the media file (same basename), and
337	  records the file list in `metadata_files`. `metadata-files.ts` owns the
338	  case-insensitive sidecar classification; `metadata-scan.ts` backs the
339	  dashboard's manual `POST /api/metadata/scan` action, which checks all
340	  database-tracked downloaded jobs and queues only missing requested types.
341	- **converterWorker** — ffmpeg mp3 transcode or remux (`-c:v copy`) that also
342	  muxes subtitle sidecars and cover art from the metadata stage
343	  (`src/media-embed.ts` owns the argv, `src/subtitles.ts` the language tags),
344	  then optionally moves the media file **and its sidecars** to
345	  `secondaryStoragePath/<folder>/`, then hashes it. The remux maps `0:v?`,
346	  `0:a?`, and the source's own `0:s?`/`0:t?`; a sidecar subtitle set is
347	  authoritative, and a sidecar cover replaces the source's attached picture, so
348	  a retry can never duplicate tracks. Same-container work (mp4 → mp4 just to
349	  embed) writes a `.yta-tmp.<ext>` sibling and renames it over the source only
350	  after ffmpeg succeeds.
351	
352	Workers are supervised (`lifecycle.ts supervise()`): a crashed loop is logged
353	and restarted after 5s. Never let a worker loop exit on error.
354	
355	**The three claims are mutually exclusive on the stage that owns the media
356	file** (`db.ts`, gotcha 24). A download is never claimed while
357	`conversion_status` or `metadata_status` is `in_progress`, and metadata is
358	never claimed while `conversion_status` is `in_progress`. All three pools share
359	one job row and one file on disk, so without those exclusions a re-queued
360	download starts yt-dlp writing to the very path the converter is reading — the
361	"file deleted before conversion finished" race. `conversion_status = 'done'`
362	stays claimable by the metadata worker on purpose: `requeueFailedJobs()`
363	re-queues a failed sidecar pass on an already-converted job.
364	
365	---
366	
367	## 6. Reliability policies — where each lives
368	
369	| Policy | Location | Notes |
370	| --- | --- | --- |
371	| Exponential backoff + jitter | `retry.ts computeBackoffMs()` | base × 2^attempt, capped, +0–30% jitter; RNG injectable for tests |
372	| Download watchdog | `retry.ts computeDownloadTimeoutMs()` | 3× duration + 5 min, clamped to config min/max; unknown duration → min |
373	| Transient vs permanent errors | `retry.ts isTransientDownloadError / isPermanentDownloadError` | permanent = private/removed/unavailable/members-only/age-gated/paid/geo-blocked/404/410/copyright. The classifier also *labels* the reason (`classifyTerminalDownloadError` → `Private video`, `Video unavailable`, `Not available in your region`, …) for the dashboard, `last_error`, `/api/failed` and the run report |
374	| Terminal skips stay skipped | `retry.ts TERMINAL_ERROR_MARKER` + `workers/download.ts parkTerminal()` | A permanent failure is written as `[terminal] <label> — skipped, it will not be retried automatically. yt-dlp: <tail>`, so the reason survives a truncated tail and every requeue path (`requeueFailedJobs`, `POST /api/failed/requeue`, `/api/reliability`'s `resumableFailed`, the orphan-partial sweep) reads the same predicate. The raw tail is kept for diagnosis; the skip writes **no** `error.log` line and spends no retry budget (a playlist full of dead videos must not trip the circuit breaker). Only an unclassified permanent message still logs |
375	| Format fallback ladder | `retry.ts nextFormatFallback()` + `workers/download.ts` format branch | `Requested format is not available` → clear a stale pinned audio probe if there is one, else persist the next lower `video_quality` override (`4k → 1440p → 1080p → 720p → 480p → highest`) and retry immediately with a readable message. The ladder is **monotonic**, so it cannot loop and needs no retry budget; `highest` is `bv+ba/b` (any stream), so failing there is a genuine terminal `No format available` skip. `audio` never falls back to a video preset |
376	
377	| Bad downloader arguments | `retry.ts isDownloaderArgsError` → pause in `workers/download.ts` | aria2c exit 28 + option help block; parks the job, pauses the engine (`BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`) |
378	| Retry-budget forgiveness | `workers/download.ts handleDownloadFailure()` + `retry.ts progressAwareRetryState()` | `retry_count` only increments when `progress <= best_progress`; `best_progress` is committed at a failure boundary, not every progress update |
379	| Resume budget | `workers/download.ts` corrupt branch | `.part` kept until `resume_count >= maxResumeAttempts`, then discarded |
380	| Unrecoverable resume (HTTP 416) | `retry.ts isUnrecoverableResumeError` → `workers/download.ts` | `--continue` asks the CDN for a range the remote stream no longer has — the "stuck at 99.0%" loop. Resuming can never finish, so the `.part` AND its `.aria2` go through `removePartialFiles`, `progress`/`best_progress` are zeroed, and the job restarts from scratch |
381	| Claim-lost reporting | `db.ts startClaimHeartbeat()` | `onLost` fires AT MOST ONCE per claim: the worker releases its own claim in the statement that records the outcome and then sleeps for the backoff, so a per-tick report printed "download claim lost" every 30 s per retrying video and buried error.log |
382	| Partial-file bookkeeping | `workers/download.ts` + `reconcile.ts findPartialFile()` | recorded on failure, cleared on success |
383	| Partial-path freeze | `reconcile.ts recordJobPartial() / recordPartialPaths()` | records the on-disk `.part` before a job stops being `downloading`, so a paused/interrupted job really resumes instead of restarting |
384	| Pause bookkeeping | `workers/download.ts parkPaused()` | parks an in-flight job as `paused` **and** freezes its partial path |
385	| Circuit breaker | `resilience.ts notePipelineFailure()` | N consecutive failures per stage pauses the engine (`TOO_MANY_FAILURES`) |
386	| Pause / resume | `resilience.ts triggerPause / triggerResume` | SIGINTs child yt-dlp; resume re-queues paused jobs and clears their claim columns. Parking an in-flight download keeps its claim (owner+token) so the worker's own release still matches |
387	| Network monitor | `resilience.ts networkMonitor()` | probes 3 hosts, pauses after 2 consecutive failures |
388	| Cookies watcher | `reconcile.ts cookiesWatch()` + `tools.ts detectCookiesChange()` | 60s sweep: reports cookies.txt appearing / changing / vanishing mid-run and counts the credential-blocked jobs it may rescue (never auto-requeues them) |
389	| Disk guard | `resilience.ts diskUsage()` → `checkDiskSpace()` | `diskUsage` is the **only** `statfs` caller: statfs → PowerShell `Get-PSDrive` fallback → `-1/-1` degraded mode (never bricks the engine, never 500s `/api/status`) |
390	| Crash recovery | `reconcile.ts reconcileCrashedJobs()` | `downloading` → `paused + interrupted` (auto-claimable); also clears orphan claims from legacy user-paused downloads while keeping them held. **Refuses to run without the engine lease** — this sweep resets every in-flight claim, so it may only touch a database its own process owns. Clearing each row's claim token is what fences the previous engine's stale workers out |
391	| Stale-claim reaper | `reconcile.ts reapStaleClaims(config)` | Lease-gated (only the engine holding the engine lease reaps) and **heartbeat-based**: downloads silent >`max(20 min, maxDownloadMinutes)` (actively owned jobs are additionally protected in-process, and progress renews the heartbeat), conversions silent >3 h, metadata silent >15 min — `staleClaimCondition()` is the single predicate, shared with the dashboard's stale-claims panel so the two cannot drift. Each reclaim is `reapStaleClaim()`, a CAS on `(token, owner, status, expired-heartbeat)`: a worker that renewed its heartbeat, or a second reaper that got there first, makes the update match 0 rows and the job is left alone. Also sweeps the stranded `.aria2` control files of the jobs it actually reclaimed this tick (a dead worker's pair whose data file is gone would wedge the next attempt) through the same `removePartialFiles` contract: a locked control file is reported and retried on the next tick, never forced |
392	| Missing-file reconciliation | `reconcile.ts reconcileMissingFiles()` | scrubs the yt-dlp archive + re-queues |
393	| Failed-job sweep | `reconcile.ts requeueFailedJobs()` | after cooldown, non-permanent failures start a fresh per-video retry window; permanent download and metadata source errors stay parked; `ignoreCooldown` for the UI button |
394	| Partial-file cleanup | `reconcile.ts cleanOrphanedFiles()` | keeps every resume-able partial — `pending`/`downloading`/`paused`/`waiting_live` owners and retryable failures waiting for cooldown are **never** aged out; deletes exhausted partials when auto-requeue is disabled, partials nothing will resume once they are a week old (`PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS`), day-old orphans (`ORPHAN_PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS`) and unowned `.superseded` backups. Recorded paths and walked paths are compared through `pathKey()` (absolute + case-folded), because the DB stores absolute paths while the walk is relative to `outputRoot`. Returns `{removed, locked}`: a partial whose control file is locked keeps BOTH files, is counted as `locked`, logged, and retried by a later sweep — never counted as removed |
395	| Per-video ignore | `db.ts ignored_videos` + `scanner.ts ingestItems()` + `web_ui.html` Ignored Videos panel | Explicit job deletion stores a durable tombstone outside `jobs`/`job_sources`, so startup scans and RSS rescans do not recreate the video. `DELETE /api/ignored-videos/:id` clears the tombstone and archive entry; a later scan can queue it for an intentional re-download |
396	| Cross-source video dedupe | `scanner.ts ingestItems()` + `archive.ts readArchiveIds()` | `jobs.id` deduplicates queued rows across source URLs and records extra `job_sources` ownership. If source cleanup removes a completed row, the configured downloader archive is the fallback that keeps another playlist from re-queueing that ID |
397	| Metadata sidecar backfill | `metadata-files.ts` + `metadata-scan.ts` + `workers/metadata.ts` + `POST /api/metadata/scan` | Manual dashboard action, database-tracked downloaded jobs only. Respects per-job subtitle/thumbnail/description choices and global info.json setting; caches directory listings, skips missing media/unreadable folders/active stages, and queues only absent requested types. The worker rechecks and writes only missing sidecars without downloading media again. Successful source-side absences are persisted in `metadata_unavailable`; failed jobs keep their retry budget. Per-job sidecar toggles explicitly clear that kind to allow a deliberate recheck. Offline mode is rejected; no automatic recurring scans |
398	| Offline mode | `config.ts offlineMode` + `offlineOverrideFromRuntime()` → loop guards in `workers/download.ts`, `workers/metadata.ts`, `scanner.ts`, `rss.ts`, `polling.ts`, and `resilience.ts` | No download, scan, RSS fetch, sidecar fetch, cookie validation, or network probe while offline. The download/metadata loops and scheduled network watchers stay armed but idle, so a live dashboard toggle works in either direction without a restart; queued jobs keep their status and `.part` files. The cookie watcher only reads local files and continues. Conversion + relocation keep running. Conversion deliberately keeps its ordering rule (`claimConvertJob` still requires terminal metadata), so a job waiting on sidecars waits — the mode finishes local work, it does not reorder the pipeline. `--offline`/`YTA_OFFLINE` set it for one run only; the stored setting is untouched |
399	| Secondary-storage relocation | `relocate.ts relocateFinishedJobs()` (driven by `startRelocation()`) | Moves finished media (sidecars first, `moveToSecondaryStorage`) whose conversion is already `done`/`not_needed`, adopts a file a crashed run copied but never recorded, and re-offers every file when `secondaryStoragePath` changes (that is what `relocated_to` stores — the ROOT, not a boolean). Claim-free by design: one engine per `archive.db` (lease) + one pass in flight per process + idempotent steps + a CAS on the old path. It never moves a job that is downloading/converting/mid-sidecar, a file already under the root, or a job deleted mid-move |
400	| Superseded-file recovery | `reconcile.ts reconcileSupersededFiles()` | startup heal of the deliberate-re-download hand-off: rolls back a stash whose rename never ran (`file_path` not yet recorded), restores a backup whose retry never became claimable, drops a backup whose re-download already finished, and adopts a legacy rename-first backup instead of letting the missing-file sweep re-queue the video |

#### Tool: Read

**Input:**

```json
{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\shah\\Downloads\\Projects\\new-build\\AGENTS.md",
  "limit": 400,
  "offset": 400
}
```

**Response:**

400	| Superseded-file recovery | `reconcile.ts reconcileSupersededFiles()` | startup heal of the deliberate-re-download hand-off: rolls back a stash whose rename never ran (`file_path` not yet recorded), restores a backup whose retry never became claimable, drops a backup whose re-download already finished, and adopts a legacy rename-first backup instead of letting the missing-file sweep re-queue the video |
401	| Archive scrubbing | `archive.ts removeFromArchive()` | needed whenever a file disappears, else yt-dlp skips it forever |
402	| Signature self-heal | `workers/download.ts` | auto-runs `yt-dlp -U` and retries with a clean budget |
403	| Engine lease release | `lease.ts releaseEngineLease()` (from `lifecycle.ts handleShutdown()`) | owner → NULL with an immediate expiry, so a clean restart never waits for a TTL; the row (and its fencing counter) is kept |
404	| WAL checkpoint | `lifecycle.ts handleShutdown()` | keeps `archive.db` self-contained after exit |
405	
406	**Adding a new failure class:** extend the classifiers in `retry.ts` (pure,
407	unit-tested), then handle it in `workers/download.ts handleDownloadFailure()`
408	in the right precedence order: signature → downloader-args → format availability
409	(stale audio probe → quality fallback ladder → terminal) →
410	**unrecoverable resume (416)** → corrupt → archive-scrub → live/premiere →
411	permanent (terminal skip) → transient/other retryable budget.
412	
413	**The order is the design.** A broader classifier placed first swallows the
414	narrower one: a 416 must precede the corrupt-resume branch (which would spend its
415	budget resuming the very partial that cannot be resumed) and the permanent class
416	(which would park the job while keeping the broken resume state on disk).
417	The same rule binds the two **format-availability** halves: `isFormatAvailabilityError`
418	matches text (`Requested format is not available`) that `isPermanentDownloadError`
419	also matches, so the format branch must run first — otherwise a stale selector
420	would park a perfectly downloadable video forever. Inside it, the stale-audio
421	clear must run before the quality ladder (re-probing is cheaper and fixes the
422	common cause), and the ladder before the terminal skip.
423	
424	**Terminal means terminal, but only for the sweeps.** `parkTerminal` writes the
425	marker; a human can still re-queue the job deliberately
426	(`POST /api/jobs/:id/retry` clears `last_error`). Do not add a "helpful"
427	auto-requeue for these rows — the original complaint this class exists for is a
428	playlist that retried its dead videos forever and filled `error.log` doing it.
429	
430	The **downloader-args** class (`retry.ts isDownloaderArgsError`, aria2c exit 28
431	+ the option's help block) is a global misconfiguration, not a video problem:
432	the handler parks the job and `triggerPause("BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS …")` so one
433	bad knob cannot burn every retry budget in the playlist before the circuit
434	breaker trips.

438	## 7. Configuration
439	
440	- **Single source of truth:** `src/config.ts` (`ConfigSchema` + `DEFAULT_CONFIG`).
441	  The engine and `update_config.ts` both import it — never re-declare the schema.
442	- `loadConfig()` (engine) exits the process on invalid config;
443	  `loadConfigSafe()` (manager) falls back to defaults.
444	- Partial configs are merged over `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so new keys are always
445	  backwards compatible with existing `config.json` files.
446	- Cross-field rules are enforced with `.refine()`: backoff max ≥ base,
447	  maxDownloadMinutes ≥ downloadTimeoutMinutes, minDownloadWorkers ≤ maxDownloadWorkers.
448	- **Adding a key:** add it to `ConfigSchema` and `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, add a prompt
449	to the relevant `update_config.ts` menu (4 = download, 5 = feature toggles,
450	6 = reliability), and add a test in `tests/config.test.ts`.
451	`tests/config-manager.test.ts` asserts every schema key is reachable from the
452	manager, so an un-prompted key fails the suite rather than becoming
453	hand-edit-only.
454	- The config manager prompts for the download root, cookies, and feature
455	toggles. Its reliability menu should use `STALE_CLAIM_THRESHOLDS` for sweep
456	values. If changing its resume-state display, ensure it opens `archive.db`:
457	`config.archiveFile` is yt-dlp's plain-text history file, not the SQLite job
458	database.
459	
460	Offline key: `offlineMode` (boolean, default false) — no downloads at all; the
461	engine only converts files that need conversion and moves finished files to
462	secondary storage, leaving queued jobs untouched. It is the one setting whose
463	runtime override (`--offline` / `YTA_OFFLINE=1`, parsed by
464	`offlineOverrideFromRuntime()`) is applied to the in-memory config only, before
465	`checkDependencies()`; `config.json` is never rewritten by it. In offline mode a
466	missing yt-dlp is a note instead of a fatal install hint, `ffmpeg` remains
467	required, and the relocation pass (below) keeps the archive tidy.
468	
469	Relocation key: `secondaryStoragePath` pairs with the jobs table's
470	`relocated_to` column — the secondary-storage root each file was moved under.
471	NULL means "still in the output tree".
472	
473	Embedding keys: `embedSubtitles` (default true) and `embedThumbnail` (default
474	true) are applied by the converter, not by yt-dlp: `--embed-subs` /
475	`--embed-thumbnail` act on the file yt-dlp just wrote, and the converter's
476	remux used to discard the resulting tracks (the old map was `0:v:0` + `0:a`
477	only; an MKV cover is an attachment). `embedMetadata` still adds
478	`--embed-metadata --embed-chapters` to the download itself. At ingest,
479	`embedSubtitles`/`embedThumbnail` force `want_subtitles`/`want_thumbnail` on
480	and set `conversion_status = 'pending'`, which is what routes an mp4-target job
481	through the converter at all (`scanner.ts`). A multi-audio MKV is still kept as
482	MKV: `convertJob` re-derives the effective container from the job's cached
483	audio selection when the target is mp4 and two or more tracks are selected.
484	
485	Reliability keys: `maxResumeAttempts`, `retryBackoffBaseSeconds`,
486	`retryBackoffMaxSeconds`, `requeueFailedAfterMinutes`, `verifyExistingFiles`,
487	`downloadTimeoutMinutes`, `maxDownloadMinutes`.
488	
489	Performance/concurrency keys: `useAria2c`, `connectionsPerDownload`,
490	`minSplitSize`, `concurrentFragments`, `fragmentRetries`, `httpChunkSize`,
491	`bufferSize`, `autoscaleEnabled`, `maxConcurrentDownloads`,
492	`minDownloadWorkers`, `maxDownloadWorkers`, `autoscaleRampStep`, and
493	`maxBandwidthKBps`. See section 7.1 for downloader flags and the distinction
494	between initial/fixed slots and the autoscaler floor/ceiling.
495	
496	### 7.1 How downloads actually reach yt-dlp (`src/download-args.ts`)
497	
498	`buildDownloadPlan({ job, config, activeSlots, aria2cAvailable })` is the single
499	place that builds the yt-dlp argv. It is pure and unit-tested — add new flags
500	there, not in the worker. What it emits today:
501	
502	- `--downloader aria2c --downloader-args aria2c:-x N -s N -j N` when aria2c is
503	  installed and `useAria2c` is true. The complete `aria2c:...` value is passed as
504	  ONE argv element with no inner quotes; yt-dlp shlex-parses the text after the
505	  prefix. yt-dlp's own baseline is `-x16 -s16 -j16 --min-split-size 1M`, so
506	  `minSplitSize` is emitted whenever it differs from `1M` — and *also* when it is
507	  not a size at all, because a value aria2c rejects must reach aria2c and surface
508	  as the `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS` pause instead of being dropped silently.
509	- `--limit-rate N` as an integer byte/second value when a cap is configured.
510	  The configured KB/s cap is divided by the current active slot count and
511	  converted to bytes/second; there is no per-worker minimum (a minimum would
512	  violate small caps). yt-dlp maps this onto the external downloader's rate
513	  limit (`aria2c --max-overall-download-limit`). Because active downloads keep
514	  the rate they started with, the aggregate is best-effort during autoscaling;
515	  new download attempts use the latest slot count.
516	- Native tuning (`--concurrent-fragments`, `--fragment-retries`, and the opt-in
517	  `--http-chunk-size` / `--buffer-size`) applies to DASH/HLS fragments and the
518	  fallback path.
519	
520	Facts worth knowing before you touch it:
521	
522	- **aria2c only serves http/https/ftp.** For HLS, DASH-segment, and live streams
523	  yt-dlp silently falls back to its native downloader — the engine does not need
524	  to special-case those protocols.
525	- **aria2c hard-caps `-x/--max-connection-per-server` at 16** ("Possible Values:
526	  1-16" in its help). A higher value makes it exit 28 — *bad/unrecognized
527	  option* — before transferring a byte, so `buildAria2cArgs` clamps `-x` to
528	  `ARIA2C_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_SERVER` while `-s`/`-j` keep the configured value.
529	  Any other rejected option (e.g. a malformed `minSplitSize`) surfaces as the
530	  `isDownloaderArgsError` class and pauses the engine instead of failing the
531	  whole batch video by video.
532	- **External downloads still land in yt-dlp's `<name>.part` temp file**, so
533	  `partial_file_path` tracking and `--continue` resume behave identically. This
534	  is why enabling aria2c does not regress resume.
535	- `aria2c` is discovered in `tools.ts` (`resolvedTools.aria2cPath`, `null` when
536	  absent) and is **optional** — a missing binary warns at startup and never
537	  exits. `checkDependencies` takes the aria2c keys as optional config fields.
538	
539	### 7.2 Multi-audio tracks (YouTube multi-language audio)
540	
541	YouTube serves some videos with several audio tracks (original + auto-dubbed);
542	yt-dlp exposes each as an audio-only format whose id carries the track index
543	(`251-0`, `251-1`, …), repeats it per quality variant, and appends `-drc` to
544	Dynamic Range Compression duplicates. `src/audio-tracks.ts` owns this:
545	
546	- `extractAudioTracks(info)` collapses a `-J` dump to one entry per track (best
547	  stream by bitrate/codec, drc and progressive formats dropped).
548	- `selectAudioTracks(tracks, mode, languages, jobSelection)` implements the
549	  policy: per-job selection (JSON in `jobs.audio_selection`, set from the
550	  dashboard) wins over the global `multiAudioMode` (`off` | `all` |
551	  `languages` + `audioTrackLanguages`).
552	- `multiAudioFormatSelector(base, tracks)` splices the track ids into the
553	  QUALITY_FORMATS preset; `buildDownloadPlan` then adds `--audio-multistreams
554	  --merge-output-format mkv` for 2+ tracks. One track = a normal merge with
555	  that track pinned; `videoQuality: "audio"` never multi-streams.
556	- `probeAudioTracks(url, config)` is the single `-J` call, hard-capped at
557	  `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (it runs inside a download slot and behind a dashboard
558	  button, so it must surface a timeout instead of hanging). The download
559	  worker runs it once per job (only when a mode/selection will consume it),
560	  caches the result in `jobs.audio_tracks`, and a probe failure logs and
561	  falls back to single audio — it never fails a download.
562	- The default MP4 path marks a multi-track download as `not_needed`, so yt-dlp's
563	  MKV is retained. If a per-job/global target format explicitly requests
564	  conversion, `workers/convert.ts` maps every audio stream; MP4 re-encodes each
565	  stream as AAC. `countAudioStreams()` drives that choice/logging — it does not
566	  bypass a requested container conversion. The download worker's container
567	  check (below) applies the same exemption: a ≥2-track download is never
568	  flipped to conversion just for being MKV.
569	
570	#### Container contract (why conversion runs for mp4 targets)
571	
572	The scanner pre-marks jobs whose target is mp4 `conversion_status =
573	'not_needed'` — a fast path that trusts yt-dlp to produce mp4. yt-dlp makes no
574	such promise: the QUALITY_FORMATS presets prefer VP9/Opus at most resolutions,
575	those codecs merge into webm/mkv (`--embed-thumbnail` used to force a
576	`.webm` → `.mkv` remux too, but embedding now happens in the converter). An
577	archive built on the fast path alone therefore ends up MKV while the dashboard
578	says mp4 — the "selected mp4, got mkv" bug.
579	
580	Embedding extends the same contract: a job that asks for a subtitle track or a
581	cover (`embedSubtitles` / `embedThumbnail`) is `conversion_status = 'pending'`
582	from ingest even when the produced container already matches, because the
583	embedding pass lives in the converter. The converter skips ffmpeg entirely when
584	there is nothing to add (target container already correct, no sidecar subtitle
585	set, no missing cover), so the extra stage is a claim + finalize in that case.
586	
587	The contract is now: **the produced container is checked once the download is
588	final** (after every yt-dlp postprocessor ran, i.e. on the `after_move:` path
589	`recordSuccess` records). When the file's extension differs from
590	`effectiveTargetFormat(job, config)` and the download is single-track,
591	`recordSuccess` flips `conversion_status` from `not_needed` to `pending` in
592	the same atomic claim-CAS update; the converter then remuxes (video copied,
593	audio to AAC for mp4) and skips files already in the target container. Rows
594	already `pending`/`failed` are untouched. The sweep equivalent for an archive
595	built before this check is `requeueWrongContainerJobs` (src/unconverted-scan.ts,
596	the dashboard's "Scan Unconverted Videos"): it re-opens the conversion stage of
597	finished jobs whose file is not in the chosen target — in place, never
598	re-downloading — and exempts multi-track MKVs for the same reason.
599	
600	Dashboard: `/api/jobs` returns `audio_tracks` / `audio_selection` as parsed
601	arrays; `POST /api/jobs/<id>/audio-probe` refreshes the list;
602	`POST /api/jobs/<id>/audio-tracks` saves (`{tracks:[…]}`) or resets
603	(`{tracks:null}`) the per-job selection, applied on the next attempt. The
604	`POST /api/jobs/<id>/override` route edits target format / quality / audio
605	language overrides; `{retry:true}` saves and re-queues in one idle-job
606	transaction (so a downloaded file is archived/stashed before workers can claim
607	it). The job drawer offers one-click save & re-download.
608	
609	#### Re-downloading an archived video (retry = replace)
610	
611	Retrying a downloaded job — the flow that applies a saved audio selection —
612	must get past two yt-dlp gates, and the engine does both in `retryJobById`
613	(web.ts) **before** the job becomes claimable:
614	
615	1. `removeFromArchive()` scrubs the id from the archive file, otherwise yt-dlp
616	   answers *"has already been recorded in the archive"* and exits 0 without
617	   downloading anything (the old silent no-op bug).
618	2. `stashDownloadedFile()` (reconcile.ts) moves the existing media file to
619	   `<file>.superseded`, because `--no-overwrites` skips a download whose
620	   target file still exists. The job's `file_path` is cleared and the backup
621	   path recorded in `superseded_file` — **the row is written before the
622	   rename**, so a crash between the two steps leaves recoverable state instead
623	   of a file nothing points at. If the rename itself fails the row is put back
624	   and the retry aborts with a 500 instead of starting a download yt-dlp would
625	   skip.
626	
627	**Exception — a format-only override converts in place.** When the override
628	changed ONLY `targetFormat` (the quality preset and audio-track selection are
629	untouched — different streams would require a real download) and the job is
630	`downloaded` with its file still on disk, `retryJobById` takes the
631	convert-in-place shortcut instead of the flow above: the override is persisted,
632	`conversion_status` re-opens (`not_needed`/`done` → `pending`), and neither the
633	archive nor the media file is touched — the converter remuxes the file already
634	in hand (video copied, audio to AAC for mp4, full encode for mp3). The route
635	answers `convertedOnly: true` and the dashboard says so. When the file is
636	already in the requested container there is nothing to convert either, and the
637	retry falls through to the literal re-download the button promises.
638	
639	The backup is the safety net: the download worker deletes it on success
640	(`dropSupersededFile`) and — if the re-download fails permanently — restores
641	it and marks the job downloaded again (`restoreSupersededFile`), so a failed
642	re-fetch never destroys the previously archived file. Every crash window of
643	the hand-off is healed by `reconcileSupersededFiles()` at the next startup:
644	an interrupted rename is rolled back (the file never moved, so the row
645	re-claims it), a backup whose retry never became claimable is restored, a
646	backup whose replacement already succeeded is deleted, and a legacy
647	rename-first backup (`file_path` gone, `<file_path>.superseded` present, no
648	pointer recorded) is adopted back into place — otherwise
649	`reconcileMissingFiles` would re-queue the video and the old file would stay
650	unmanaged.
651	
652	#### Unavailable formats recover instead of parking the job
653	
654	`retry.ts isFormatAvailabilityError()` matches yt-dlp's *"Requested format is
655	not available"* — which `isPermanentDownloadError` ALSO matches. The download
656	worker checks it FIRST, in two steps:
657	
658	1. **Stale multi-audio probe.** When a job carried stored `audio_tracks`,
659	   YouTube has most likely renumbered its formats since the probe, so the
660	   worker clears `audio_tracks` (forcing a fresh probe; the per-job language
661	   selection survives) and retries within the normal no-progress budget — a
662	   re-probe can pin the same stale ids again, so this half does need a bound.
663	2. **Quality fallback ladder.** With no stale probe to blame, the preset itself
664	   matched nothing: the worker persists the next lower `video_quality` override
665	   and retries immediately (no backoff — the next attempt is a different
666	   command), announcing it in the dashboard for `FORMAT_SWITCH_NOTICE_MS` so the
667	   downgrade is visible, logging one line, and counting `stats.formatFallbacks`.
668	   The ladder (`FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER`) is strictly descending and ends at
669	   `highest` (`bv+ba/b`, i.e. "any stream the extractor found"), so it cannot
670	   loop and spends no retry budget — see the table in section 6.
671	
672	Both steps run before the permanent classification. Only a job whose ladder is
673	exhausted falls through to a terminal skip, labelled
674	`No format available (tried down to <preset>)`.
675	
676	#### Control files: never delete a `.part` without its `.aria2`
677	
678	aria2c writes a *control file* beside every in-progress download
679	(`<name>.part.aria2`) holding which pieces arrived. Two rules follow, and both
680	are load-bearing:
681	
682	1. **Resume depends on the pair.** An interrupted transfer leaves
683	   `<name>.part` + `<name>.part.aria2`; the next attempt resumes from them. This
684	   is why enabling aria2c does not weaken the resume/reliability behaviour.
685	2. **Discarding a partial must delete both.** aria2c defaults to
686	   `--allow-overwrite=false`, whose documented behaviour is *"if a file already
687	   exists but the corresponding control file doesn't exist, then aria2 will not
688	   re-download the file."* A stranded control file therefore makes aria2c unable
689	   to resume (the data is gone) *and* unwilling to restart — the job retries
690	   forever. Exit status 10 (*"piece length was different from one in .aria2
691	   control file"*) is the other way this bites.
692	
693	Always go through `removePartialFiles(path)` (`src/reconcile.ts`), never a bare
694	`unlink()`. It removes the data file and the control file together, and
695	`cleanOrphanedFiles()` also sweeps control files whose data file has vanished.
696	`findPartialFile()` deliberately matches only the data file — a control file on
697	its own is litter, not resumable state.
698	
699	---
700	
701	## 8. Web API (`src/web.ts`)
702	
703	Auth: every request (UI + API) is gated when `webToken` is set — via cookie
704	(`yta_token`, HttpOnly after sign-in), `Authorization: Bearer`, `X-Web-Token`,
705	or `?token=`. Comparison is timing-safe. Default bind is `127.0.0.1`.
706	
707	Routing is a `ROUTES` table of `{methods, pattern, handler}` with `:param`
708	segments — not an if-chain. The contract every route shares: a
709	`{ ok: true|false, … }` envelope, a **JSON** 404 for an unknown API path, and a
710	**JSON** 405 (+ `Allow`) for a known path with the wrong method. Trailing
711	slashes collapse (`/api/jobs/` is `/api/jobs`). Static action paths are listed
712	*before* `:param` routes so a wrong method answers 405 instead of binding the
713	segment as an id (gotcha 21).
714	
715	
716	Request deadlines: `Bun.serve()` is started with an explicit `idleTimeout`
717	(`WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 60s). Bun's default is 10s, and any response that
718	has not started by then is dropped, with `warn: Bun.serve() timed out a
719	request after 10 seconds. Pass `idleTimeout` to configure.` printed at most
720	once per process — and in some Bun 1.4 builds only when stderr is flushed at
721	exit, which is why operators report it at Ctrl+C for a request that died
722	minutes earlier. Passing the option also stops Bun from installing that
723	warning handler (`has_idle_timeout`), so the message cannot come back.
724	
725	Routes that legitimately outlive that default declare `deadlineSeconds` in
726	their `ROUTES` entry: `/api/scan`, `/api/scan/unconverted` and
727	`/api/metadata/scan` 15m, `/api/cookies/export` 5m,
728	`/api/jobs/:id/audio-probe` 120s. `handleApi` applies it with
729	`server.timeout(req, n)`; `handleRequest` takes the server as an optional
730	third argument, so unit tests can drive the routes without a socket. Shutdown
731	closes the listener first (`stopAcceptingRequests` -> `stop(false)`, in-flight
732	responses drain) instead of only at the very end.
733	
734	Job retry and per-job override must check all pipeline stages and claims inside
735	an immediate SQLite transaction (`withIdleJobs()`
736	for id-based operations). If any targeted row is downloading, converting, fetching
737	metadata, or still holds a download/conversion claim, return HTTP 409 with
738	`{ ok: false, error: "Job is currently in progress" }` and make no partial bulk changes.
739	The cancel-flavoured routes are the deliberate exception: `POST /api/jobs/pause`,
740	`POST /api/jobs/:id/stop`, `DELETE /api/jobs/:id`, `DELETE /api/jobs` and
741	`POST /api/queue/purge` park or remove rows that are active *and interrupt their
742	children* (park first, then signal, so the worker releases its own claim through
743	its token and the `.part` stays resumable). Refusing those rows would make each
744	button useless for exactly the job the operator is clicking it about.
745	
746	| Method | Route | Purpose |
747	| --- | --- | --- |
748	| GET | `/` | dashboard (login page when a token is required) |
749	| GET · HEAD | `/api/ping` | liveness probe used by the UI |
750	| GET | `/api/version` | engine/runtime info (`Bun.version`, platform/arch, uptime seconds) |
751	| GET | `/api/status` | stats, speed, ETA, disk, live worker lines, pause state, `runtime`; `diskSpace.free` reads `"unknown"` when no disk probe could answer |
752	| GET | `/api/jobs` | `{ ok, jobs }` — up to 500 jobs with status/retry/progress fields (`JOB_COLUMNS` in `web.ts` is the single source of truth for what the dashboard may read: per-stage retry counters, `best_progress`, `partial_file_path`, `relocated_to`, the `created_at` / `updated_at` stamps the drawer and the history tab show), plus parsed `audio_tracks` / `audio_selection` / `metadata_files` / `metadata_unavailable` and boolean `want_*` sidecar flags |
753	| GET | `/api/jobs/:id` | one job, read fresh from the DB — the detail drawer fetches this instead of trusting a poll-cycle-old list row |
754	| POST | `/api/scan` | `{url, folder?, singleVideo?}` → validate/canonicalize → save source to `config.json` → scan & ingest; returns `saved`, `source: {url, key, added}`, and counts. `singleVideo: true` keeps only `v=` from a `watch?v=…&list=…` link (`parseSourceUrl(url, {singleVideo})`). Save failure starts no scan; scan failure keeps the saved source. Folder override applies only to this scan |
755	| POST | `/api/scan/batch` | `{urls: string \| string[], folder?, singleVideo?}` → one line per link (blank and `#` lines skipped, max 2000) → `saveBatchSources()` in one config write → background `scanSourcesBatch()`; returns per-line `errors`, `sources` counts, and `scanning`. Invalid-only batches return 400 and save nothing |
756	| POST | `/api/queue/purge` | delete every idle pending / paused / waiting_live / failed job **and the rows that are downloading right now**, interrupting those children first so nothing keeps writing after the button; returns `{ok, deleted, stopped}` |
757	| POST | `/api/pause` · `/api/resume` | global pause / resume-all |
758	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/retry` | re-queue one idle job (all stages, budgets reset); 404 for an unknown id, 409 while any pipeline stage/claim is active. For a downloaded job this is a deliberate re-download: the id is scrubbed from the yt-dlp archive and the existing file stashed as `.superseded` first (§7.2). 500 when the previous file cannot be moved aside |
759	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/override` | partial `{targetFormat?, videoQuality?, audioTracks?}` edit; nullable values reset to global behavior. Optional `retry:true` applies the override and queues a deliberate re-download atomically (or retries current settings when sent alone); 400 invalid payload, 404 unknown id, 409 active pipeline stage |
760	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/reset-failures` | zero the per-stage retry counters; 404 for an unknown id |
761	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/sidecars` | per-job sidecar toggles: `{subtitles?, thumbnail?, description?}` (booleans). Flipping a flag on for a finished download re-opens the metadata stage so the worker fetches the files against the existing media; flipping off never deletes fetched files. 400 for an empty/non-boolean body |
762	| POST | `/api/metadata/scan` | manual whole-library sidecar check; only downloaded DB jobs, skips offline mode, queues missing requested metadata without re-downloading media |
763	| POST | `/api/jobs/pause` | bulk user-pause by `{ids: []}`: parks each row with `pause_reason = 'user'` and interrupts its transfer, keeping a mid-download claim so the `.part` still resumes; 400 when no ids are given |
764	| DELETE | `/api/jobs` | bulk delete by `{ids: []}`, cancelling active children the same way; `{ok, deleted, stopped}` |
765	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/audio-tracks` | per-job audio-track selection: `{tracks:["es",…]}` saves it, `{tracks:null}` returns the job to the global mode |
766	| POST | `/api/jobs/:id/audio-probe` | runs the yt-dlp `-J` probe for one job, stores + returns its audio tracks |
767	| DELETE | `/api/jobs/:id` | delete one job, cancelling its in-flight child first so no yt-dlp keeps writing into a file nothing tracks; 404 for an unknown id, `{ok, deleted, stopped}` otherwise |
768	| POST | `/api/retry/:id` · `/api/failcount/reset/:id` · `/api/jobs/delete` | **legacy aliases** of the canonical routes above — kept on purpose for older dashboards and scripts |
769	| GET | `/api/failed` | failed jobs |
770	| POST | `/api/failed/requeue` | force-requeue eligible failed jobs (cooldown ignored, permanent errors still skipped) |
771	| GET | `/api/reliability` | pause state, kept partials, retryable count, active policy, active downloader engine (`downloader.engine` / `.path` / `.connectionsPerDownload` / `.concurrentFragments` / `.maxBandwidthKBps` / `.autoscaleRampStep`), plus a `resume` block (`resumablePartials` / `interrupted` / `staleClaims`) and a `sweeps` array (`id` / `label` / `cadence` / `detail` / `pending`; `missingFiles.pending` is `null` because that sweep stats every file) |
772	| GET | `/api/settings` | the dashboard-editable keys: `{fields, values, nonDefault}` where each field carries its label/type/range/help so the UI renders generically |
773	| POST | `/api/settings` | apply a partial patch. Validates the **whole** config against `ConfigSchema` (so cross-field refinements hold), persists to `config.json`, and `setConfig()`s it live. Rejects (400) any key outside the allow-list, an out-of-range value, or a malformed body — and changes nothing when it rejects |
774	| GET | `/api/history?limit=20` | run history rows |
775	| GET | `/api/logs?type=error\|report&limit=100` | error.log or the run report |
776	
777	Frontend is plain JS in `web_ui.html` — no build step. After editing it,
778	re-extract the inline `<script>` and syntax-check it (see section 9.4).
779	
780	The page has no types and no imports, so **the key names it reads are the
781	contract** — see gotcha 41 and `tests/web-ui-contract.test.ts`, which executes
782	the real inline script over a stub DOM against `handleRequest` and asserts the
783	job table renders. Every list endpoint answers with an envelope
784	(`{ ok, jobs }`, `{ ok, sources }`, `{ ok, logs }`), never a bare array.

791	
792	```bash
793	bun test                       # everything (unit + end-to-end; uses mock tools)
794	bun test tests/retry.test.ts   # one file
795	bun run typecheck              # tsc --noEmit (tsconfig covers *.ts, src/**, tests/**)
796	bun run check                  # typecheck + full suite (what CI/the definition of done means)
797	```

844	### 9.3 End-to-end tests with mock tools
845	
846	`tests/mocks/yt-dlp`, `tests/mocks/ffmpeg`, and `tests/mocks/aria2c` are Bun
847	scripts that implement just enough of each CLI for the engine to run its full
848	pipeline. The mock yt-dlp honours `--downloader aria2c` by spawning the mock
849	aria2c and recording the argv it received to `<out>.aria2-args`, which is how
850	the aria2c integration test proves the connection tuning and the bandwidth cap
851	actually reach the downloader. The integration
852	test prepends `tests/mocks` to `PATH`, writes a `config.json` into a temp dir,
853	and spawns the real `batch_playlist_downloader.ts`, then drives it over HTTP
854	(`/api/status`, `/api/jobs`, `/api/reliability`) and asserts final job states.
855	
856	Scenarios: happy path (scan → download → metadata → convert), transient-failure
857	retries with backoff, corrupt-partial resume, permanent failures (never
858	requeued), restart reconciliation after deleting files, aria2c multi-connection
859	downloads (args + cap verified), the native fallback when aria2c is missing in
860	TWO ways — the documented `aria2cPath: "none"` switch, and (POSIX) a real
861	dependency probe over a PATH that holds nothing but the mock yt-dlp, proving
862	discovery itself answers "not installed" instead of failing the run — the
863	multi-audio probe falling back to a single-audio download both when `-J` fails
864	and when it hangs (the timeout is shortened with
865	`YTA_AUDIO_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, a test-only override read by
866	`src/audio-tracks.ts`), the secondary-storage hand-off (media + sidecars land
867	under `<secondaryStoragePath>/<folder>/` and `file_path` records the new
868	location; a move whose destination is blocked keeps the only copy in the
869	download folder, fails the conversion, and stores the move error in
870	`last_error`),
871	aria2c option validation (`-x` above the 16 cap is clamped; a malformed
872	`--min-split-size` pauses the engine with `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS` instead of
873	failing the batch), and
874	four aria2c resume/self-healing scenarios: resume from the control file,
875	discarding a partial *with* its control file when the resume budget runs out, a
876	hard kill mid-transfer followed by a resume on restart, and deleted files being
877	re-fetched — plus the HTTP 416 scenario, where the mock aria2c answers a RESUME
878	only (never a fresh transfer) with `HTTP Error 416: Requested range not
879	satisfiable`; the run must end downloaded, with the `.part` + `.aria2` pair gone
880	and `resumed=false` in the mock's argv record, proving the engine restarted from
881	scratch instead of looping on the stale resume state. Two more scenarios pin the durable-work guarantees end to end: a
882	paused job's ABSOLUTE `partial_file_path` survives the startup sweep while
883	`outputRoot` is the default RELATIVE `./downloads` (the counterexample that
884	used to delete a day-old "orphan" that was the job's only resume state), and a
885	crashed rename-first stash (`file_path` gone, `<file_path>.superseded` present)
886	is adopted back on startup — the media's marker bytes prove it was restored,
887	not re-downloaded. The error-handling classes have their own end-to-end
888	scenarios: **unavailable videos** (`FAKE_FAIL_MODE=private|unavailable`,
889	optionally with a unique `FAKE_FAIL_MESSAGE` marker) must be attempted exactly
890	once — the mock's `.attempts` counter is the proof — with `[terminal]` in
891	`last_error`, no marker in the `error.log` delta, `resumableFailed: 0` on
892	`/api/reliability`, an unchanged `.attempts` after a forced
893	`POST /api/failed/requeue`, and a report that reads `⛔ Private video`; and the
894	**format fallback ladder** (`FAKE_FORMAT_FAILS_SELECTOR='height<=1080'`, or the
895	sentinel `all` for a video with no usable formats) must step the persisted
896	`video_quality` override down, announce it in the dashboard (the 1.5 s notice
897	pause is what makes it observable), record it in `error.log`, download with the
898	fallback selector recorded in the mock's `.ytdlp-args`, and — with `all` — stop
899	after three attempts (720p → 480p → highest) as a terminal `No format
900	available` skip instead of retrying.
901	
902	The mock aria2c reproduces the real control-file lifecycle (interrupted →
903	`.part` + `.aria2`; resume → `resumed=yes`; success → control file removed) and
904	**fails hard if it is handed a control file whose data file is missing** — that
905	is the wedged state the engine must never create, so a regression in
906	`removePartialFiles` fails the suite rather than hanging a download. Like the
907	real binary it also validates option values: `-x` outside 1-16 or a
908	`--min-split-size` that is not a size dies with exit 28 and the option's help
909	block, which is how the clamp and the `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS` pause are tested.
910	Injection:
911	`FAKE_ARIA2C_FAIL_TIMES` / `FAKE_ARIA2C_FAIL_MODE` (failure originates inside the
912	external downloader, independently of the yt-dlp mock's own `FAKE_FAIL_TIMES`)
913	and `FAKE_ARIA2C_INFLIGHT_MS` (hold a transfer open so a kill can interrupt it).
914	The yt-dlp mock kills its aria2c child when its own parent dies, so a hard-killed
915	engine leaves a realistic interrupted state instead of an orphan finishing the
916	download.
917	
918	**That watchdog is POSIX-only.** Both mocks detect the death by polling
919	`process.ppid`, which changes only because POSIX reparents orphans to PID 1.
920	Windows keeps the original parent-PID value, so on win32 neither watcher ever
921	fires and an orphaned mock runs to completion — the crash-recovery scenario
922	("a hard kill mid-download resumes on restart") is only meaningful on POSIX. To
923	make it work on Windows, kill the whole process tree from the harness
924	(`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`) instead of relying on `process.ppid`.
925	
926	The mock yt-dlp also speaks multi-audio: `--dump-single-json` answers with a
927	three-track format list (en original + es/hi dubs, quality variants and `-drc`
928	duplicates included, exactly the soup `extractAudioTracks` must clean), and a
929	download carrying `--audio-multistreams` writes `<base>.mkv` instead of
930	`<base>.mp4` while recording its whole argv to `<base>.ytdlp-args` — that file
931	is how the integration test proves the format selector and the multistream/MKV
932	flags really reached yt-dlp. The mock ffmpeg answers the stream probe
933	(`ffmpeg -hide_banner -i <file>`, no output arg) with a two-audio-stream banner
934	for `.mkv` inputs and one otherwise, which is what `countAudioStreams()` sees.
935	
936	The mock also honours `--download-archive` the way real yt-dlp does: an id
937	already recorded is skipped with yt-dlp's exact *"has already been recorded in
938	the archive"* message and exit 0 (no file, no progress), and a successful
939	download appends `youtube <id>`. This fidelity is load-bearing — it is what
940	makes the deliberate-re-download contract (§7.2) observable in tests: without
941	scrubbing the archive, the retry integration test would hang on a silent skip.
942	
943	Mock controls (environment variables):
944	
945	| Variable | Effect |
946	| --- | --- |
947	| `FAKE_FAIL_TIMES=N` | fail the first N download attempts, leaving a `.part` file behind |
948	| `FAKE_FAIL_MODE` | `transient` \| `permanent` \| `corrupt` (which error message to emit) |
949	| `FAKE_DELAY_MS` | artificial per-attempt delay |
950	| `FAKE_OUTPUT_STRESS=1` | CR-only progress + oversized stdout/stderr, renamed Unicode final file with split UTF-8 and no trailing newline |
951	| `FAKE_OMIT_FINAL_PATH=1` | no after_move output, so the engine must find the expected media in the job folder |
952	| `FAKE_SCAN_LOG=path` | append every scanned URL, proving live daemon rescans and persisted startup sources |
953	| `FAKE_EMPTY_SCAN=1` | a valid source with no videos, proving source persistence does not depend on jobs added |
954	| `FAKE_HANG=1` | never exit (watchdog testing) |
955	| `FAKE_PROBE_FAIL=1` \| `=json` | make the `-J` audio-track probe fail (HTTP error / unparsable output) so the single-audio fallback runs end to end |
956	| `FAKE_PROBE_HANG=1` | make `-J` never answer, so the probe watchdog fires (pair with `YTA_AUDIO_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` to keep the test short) |
957	| `FAKE_ARIA2C_BIN` | absolute path of the sibling aria2c mock (set by the integration harness so that hop never depends on PATH) |
958	| `FAKE_ARIA2C_FAIL_TIMES=N` | fail the first N attempts *inside* aria2c, leaving the `.part` + `.part.aria2` pair |
959	| `FAKE_ARIA2C_FAIL_MODE` | `transient` \| `corrupt` \| `range416` (which aria2c-side error message to emit; `range416` bites ONLY when the run resumes from a control file — the "stuck at 99%" state) |
960	| `FAKE_ARIA2C_INFLIGHT_MS=N` | hold a transfer open N ms so a hard kill lands mid-flight, with partial + control file on disk |
961	
962	**When adding an engine behavior, add an integration scenario rather than
963	mocking internals** — the mocks are the contract boundary.
964	
965	### 9.4 Editing `web_ui.html`
966	
967	```bash
968	python3 - <<'PY'
969	import re
970	html = open('web_ui.html').read()
971	open('/tmp/inline.js','w').write('\n;\n'.join(re.findall(r'<script>(.*?)</script>', html, re.S)))
972	PY
973	node --check /tmp/inline.js   # syntax gate before committing UI changes
974	```
975	
976	### 9.5 Fixtures that spawn a process (POSIX vs Windows)
977	
978	`tests/scanner.test.ts` and `tests/yt-dlp-update.test.ts` drive a fake tool binary,
979	and four rules there exist because the same suite passed on Linux and failed on
980	Windows — an environment assumption is still a broken test:
981	
982	- **Build the fixture once, in `beforeAll`.** win32 cannot launch a shebang script
983	  at all, so the fixture is compiled with `bun build --compile`; the compile costs
984	  seconds and the freshly written `.exe` costs more on its first launch
985	  (antivirus). Doing it per test overran Bun's 5 s default per-test budget, and
986	  the failure that came back was `exit 143` — the harness' own SIGTERM to the
987	  dangling fixture, not anything the tool did. Those tests carry an explicit
988	  budget (`WIN ? 30_000 : 10_000`) while every bound the test is *about* stays as
989	  tight as it was: the 250 ms scan timeout, the 200 ms updater kill.
990	- **Configure the fixture with a file, never `process.env`.** `bun test` snapshots
991	  the environment, so a variable assigned by a test never reaches a child it
992	  spawns — on any platform. The fixture reads `mode.txt` from its own temp dir.
993	- **A process-tree probe is POSIX-only.** `pgrep`, `ps`, a `bash` job: wrap the
994	  test in `test.skipIf(WIN)` rather than inventing a Windows equivalent, and name
995	  in the comment what covers the same guarantee there (`taskkill /t` in
996	  `killProcessTree`, and the aria2c scenarios in 9.3 — see gotcha 23). An
997	  assertion that cannot tell "no orphans" from "no pgrep binary" is worse than a
998	  skip, and an exit code like 130 ("128 + SIGINT") is a shell convention, not a
999	  fact about the kill.
1000	- **Removing a fixture's temp dir must retry.** A child killed moments ago still
1001	  holds its cwd and executable, so `rm` fails with `EPERM` and surfaces as an
1002	  "unhandled error between tests". Retry on `EPERM`/`EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY` and let
1003	  the last failure pass quietly: a stray temp dir is noise. Close any database
1004	  handle the test opened first, or the same lock is what blocks the removal.
1005

1008	## 10. Gotchas (read before changing things)
1009	
1010	1. **ESM live bindings.** `db` is `export let db` reassigned by `initDatabase()`.
1011	   Importers see the new value because bindings are live — but you can never
1012	   assign to an imported binding. Route mutations through setter functions
1013	   (`state.ts` does this: `setPaused`, `setConfig`, `setTty`).
1014	2. **Claim transactions must be created inside `initDatabase()`.** Defining
1015	   `db.transaction(...)` at module top level evaluates `db` while it is still
1016	   `undefined` and crashes startup. This is load-bearing; don't "clean it up".
1017	3. **Everything is CWD-relative.** `archive.db`, `config.json`, `error.log`,
1018	   `downloaded_videos.txt`, and `web_ui.html` are resolved from `process.cwd()`.
1019	   Tests therefore run the engine in a temp dir; the compiled exe expects
1020	   `web_ui.html` next to it.
1021	4. **Windows path rules are enforced everywhere.** `hardenName()` strips
1022	   control chars, trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`,
1023	   `COM1`…); `fitBaseFilename()` keeps paths under MAX_PATH (260) by truncating
1024	   and appending `[videoId]`. Any new filename construction must go through
1025	   these helpers.
1026	5. **`partial_file_path` must always point at a real `.part` file or NULL.**
1027	   Storing a completed path there makes the corrupt-handler delete good files
1028	   (that was a real bug). Keep it in sync: set on failure, NULL on success.
1029	6. **Never re-queue permanent errors.** `isPermanentDownloadError()` gates the
1030	   sweep; bypassing it causes infinite retry loops against dead videos.
1031	   YouTube **n-challenge** failures (`n challenge solving failed`, missing JS
1032	   runtime) are *not* permanent even when the same stderr also says
1033	   `Requested format is not available` — that text is a symptom of the unsolved
1034	   player JS. `isNChallengeError()` wins (and is checked before the reason
1035	   table, but *after* the `[terminal]` marker: only the terminal path writes
1036	   that, and it never writes it for an n-challenge failure). Widening the
1037	   patterns is cheap; **narrowing** them is how the retry loop comes back — every
1038	   wording that fails to classify falls into the transient budget, parks as
1039	   `failed`, and is re-queued by the cooldown sweep forever.
1040	7. **`bun:sqlite` specifics.** `MAX(a,b)` is the scalar two-arg form; use
1041	   `COALESCE` before it. `datetime('now', '-N minutes')` modifiers must be
1042	   built from validated integers, never user text. Open read-only handles
1043	   (`new Database(path, { readonly: true })`) when inspecting a live DB.
1044	8. **Progress updates are throttled to 500ms** and go straight to SQLite —
1045	   keep DB writes inside the progress loop cheap.
1046	9. **Don't add blocking work to the worker claim path.** Long operations belong
1047	   inside the try-block after a claim, or the whole pool stalls.
1048	10. **TUI vs piped output.** `dashboard.ts` no-ops when `isTty()` is false;
1049	    log lines must remain parseable when stdout is a pipe (integration tests
1050	    rely on this).
1051	11. **Backwards compatibility.** Existing users have `archive.db` files from
1052	    older versions. New columns go through `ensureColumn()`; never assume a
1053	    fresh schema. The legacy-migration test in `tests/db.test.ts` is the guard.
1054	12. **`--downloader-args` value is one argv element.** The engine builds
1055	    `aria2c:-x 16 -s 16 -j 16` as a single string and yt-dlp shlex-splits the
1056	    text after `aria2c:` itself. **No inner quotes** — they survive argv on
1057	    Windows, the whole list becomes one shlex token, and aria2c rejects `-x`
1058	    with exit 28 before transferring a byte (the BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS pause).
1059	    Splitting it into separate argv entries breaks parsing too (the mock
1060	    yt-dlp in `tests/mocks/` strips the `aria2c:` prefix — keep that in sync
1061	    if you change the format).

1063	    (`.part` + `.part.aria2`); use `removePartialFiles()` or the next attempt
1064	    wedges forever. `tests/reconcile.test.ts` and the "exhausting the resume
1065	    budget" integration scenario both fail if this regresses — the latter was

1080	18. **One instance per `archive.db` — the LEASE is the lock.** `main()` takes

1091	    reports a `fatal` result when it is locked** (orphaned aria2c, antivirus).

1100	    `unlink` fails on it (EISDIR), so removal recurses and reports honestly.
1101	20. **The converter guards every destructive step with
1102	    `stillOwnsConversion`** (source delete, EACH move inside
1103	    `moveToSecondaryStorage`, the final done-update) and updates `file_path`
