140	async function exchangeToken(req: Request, config: Config, url: URL): Promise<Response> {
141	  const expected = effectiveWebToken(config);
142	  if (!expected) return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Token authentication is not configured" }, { status: 404 });
143	  let body: unknown;
144	  try {
145	    body = await req.json();
146	  } catch {
147	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Expected a JSON body" }, { status: 400 });
148	  }
149	  const token = body && typeof body === "object" && typeof (body as { token?: unknown }).token === "string"
150	    ? (body as { token: string }).token.trim()
151	    : "";
152	  if (!token || !timingSafeEq(token, expected)) {
153	    return Response.json(
154	      { ok: false, error: "Invalid token" },
155	      { status: 401, headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
156	    );
157	  }
158	  return Response.json(
159	    { ok: true },
160	    { headers: { "Set-Cookie": tokenCookie(token, url), "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
161	  );
162	}

219	/**
220	 * How long one HTTP request may take before Bun closes its socket (seconds).
221	 *
222	 * Bun's default is 10 s, and any handler that has not answered by then gets its
223	 * connection reset AND a warning on stderr:
224	 *
225	 *   warn: Bun.serve() timed out a request after 10 seconds. Pass `idleTimeout`
226	 *   to configure.
227	 *
228	 * That message is printed at most once per process and (in some Bun 1.4 builds)
229	 * only when stderr is flushed at exit, which is why operators report it while
230	 * pressing Ctrl+C rather than when the request actually died. Ten seconds is
231	 * far too short here: a playlist scan or a cookie export takes minutes, and the
232	 * dashboard then reported a network error for work that was still running
233	 * server-side.
234	 *
235	 * Passing `idleTimeout` explicitly also stops Bun from installing the warning
236	 * handler at all (its `should_add_timeout_handler_for_warning` is false once
237	 * the option is present), so the message cannot come back. Handlers that
238	 * legitimately outlive this value declare `deadlineSeconds` in the route table.
239	 */
240	export const WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60;
241	
242	/**
243	 * The slice of Bun's server object the router needs, structurally typed so
244	 * tests (which call handleRequest with no server) and stubs stay simple.
245	 */
246	export interface RequestDeadlineServer {
247	  /** Reset this request's idle timer; 0 means "no limit". */
248	  timeout(request: Request, seconds: number): void;
249	}
250	
251	export function startWebServer(port: number, config: Config, hostname: string = config.webBind || "127.0.0.1") {
252	  return Bun.serve({
253	    // LAN-safe default: listen on loopback unless webBind is explicitly set
254	    // (e.g. 0.0.0.0 to reach the UI from other devices on the LAN).
255	    port,
256	    hostname,
257	    idleTimeout: WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
258	    async fetch(req, server) {
259	      // Every request is wrapped: a handler crash returns JSON 500 instead of
260	      // hanging the socket, and the error lands in error.log.
261	      try {
262	        // Read the live config, not the one captured at startup: settings
263	        // changed from the dashboard (POST /api/settings) must be reflected by
264	        // every endpoint immediately, and setConfig() replaces the object.
265	        return await handleRequest(req, getConfig(), server);
266	      } catch (e: any) {
267	        logError("http", `${req.method} ${new URL(req.url).pathname}: ${e?.stack || e}`);
268	        return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Internal server error" }, { status: 500 });
269	      }
270	    },
271	  });
272	}
273	
274	export async function handleRequest(
275	  req: Request,
276	  config: Config,
277	  server?: RequestDeadlineServer | null,
278	): Promise<Response> {
279	  const url = new URL(req.url);
280	
281	  if (!isSameOriginMutation(req, url)) {
282	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Cross-origin mutations are not allowed" }, { status: 403 });
283	  }
284	
285	  if (url.pathname === "/") {
286	    const queryToken = url.searchParams.get("token");
287	    const expected = effectiveWebToken(config);
288	    const validQueryToken = !!queryToken && !!expected && timingSafeEq(queryToken.trim(), expected);
289	    if (expected && !isAuthorized(req, url, config)) {
290	      // Missing/wrong token → the sign-in page (401 so browsers don't treat it
291	      // as the real app). Sign-in itself exchanges credentials via POST and
292	      // never puts the token in the address bar.
293	      return new Response(LOGIN_PAGE, {
294	        status: 401,
295	        headers: {
296	          "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
297	          "Cache-Control": "no-store",
298	          "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
299	        },
300	      });
301	    }
302	    if (existsSync("./web_ui.html")) {
303	      const headers: Record<string, string> = {
304	        "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
305	        "Cache-Control": "no-store",
306	        "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
307	      };
308	      // Keep the documented query-token compatibility path, but only a query
309	      // token that actually matches the configured secret may replace a cookie.
310	      if (validQueryToken) headers["Set-Cookie"] = tokenCookie(queryToken!.trim(), url);
311	      return new Response(Bun.file("./web_ui.html"), { headers });
312	    }

316	  // Sign-in exchange is the only unauthenticated mutation endpoint. All other

337	// --- API routing --------------------------------------------------------------
338	// A route table instead of an if-chain: patterns support `:param` segments,
339	// every response shares the `{ok, ...}` envelope, unknown API paths get a JSON
340	// 404, and a known path with the wrong method gets a JSON 405 (+ Allow).
341	//
342	// Legacy action paths stay alive as aliases of the canonical per-job routes so
343	// existing bookmarks, scripts, and older dashboards keep working:
344	//   POST /api/retry/:id             → POST /api/jobs/:id/retry
345	//   POST /api/failcount/reset/:id   → POST /api/jobs/:id/reset-failures
346	//   POST /api/jobs/delete {ids}     → DELETE /api/jobs {ids}
347	
348	type RouteParams = Record<string, string>;
349	type RouteHandler = (ctx: {
350	  req: Request;
351	  config: Config;
352	  url: URL;
353	  params: RouteParams;
354	}) => Response | Promise<Response>;
355	
356	interface Route {
357	  methods: string[];
358	  pattern: string;
359	  handler: RouteHandler;
360	  /**
361	   * Seconds this handler may take before Bun closes its socket.
362	   *
363	   * Only for handlers that do real work inside the request (a playlist scan, a
364	   * cookie export, a live audio probe). Without it they are cut at
365	   * WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS while the work carries on server-side, so the
366	   * dashboard reports a failure for a scan that actually succeeded.
367	   */
368	  deadlineSeconds?: number;
369	}
370	
371	/** Minutes-scale work: a playlist/channel scan over a large source. */
372	const SCAN_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 15 * 60;
373	/** A browser cookie read plus the live YouTube check it performs. */
374	const COOKIE_EXPORT_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 5 * 60;
375	/** A `yt-dlp -J` audio-track probe; the probe itself gives up at 90s. */
376	const AUDIO_PROBE_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 120;
377	
378	/** Match a `/api/…/:param` pattern against path segments; null = no match. */
379	function matchRoute(pattern: string, segments: string[]): RouteParams | null {
380	  const parts = pattern.split("/").filter(Boolean);
381	  if (parts.length !== segments.length) return null;
382	  const params: RouteParams = {};
383	  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
384	    const p = parts[i];
385	    if (p.startsWith(":")) {
386	      if (!segments[i]) return null; // never bind an empty param
387	      try {
388	        params[p.slice(1)] = decodeURIComponent(segments[i]);
389	      } catch {
390	        // A malformed percent escape is an invalid path, not a handler crash.
391	        return null;
392	      }
393	    } else if (p !== segments[i]) {
394	      return null;
395	    }
396	  }
397	  return params;
398	}

434	// by their token as well as the worker id, so a row whose status was flipped

436	const ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE = `
437	  COALESCE(download_status, '') = 'downloading'
438	  OR download_claimed_by IS NOT NULL
439	  OR download_claim_token IS NOT NULL
440	  OR COALESCE(conversion_status, '') = 'in_progress'
441	  OR conversion_claimed_by IS NOT NULL
442	  OR conversion_claim_token IS NOT NULL
443	  OR COALESCE(metadata_status, '') = 'in_progress'
444	  OR metadata_claim_token IS NOT NULL
445	`;

449	type IdleJobResult<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false };
450	
451	/**
452	 * Stop every in-flight child (download / conversion / sidecar fetch) belonging
453	 * to these jobs.
454	 *
455	 * Deletion and purge used to be database-only operations: the row disappeared
456	 * while yt-dlp kept downloading in the terminal and wrote a file nobody
457	 * tracked — and the download worker then reported a lost claim. Interrupting
458	 * the children first is what makes the buttons mean what they say. The kill is
459	 * claim-safe: a worker that no longer owns its row writes nothing (see the
460	 * claim-token CAS in db.ts), and a deleted row is treated as a normal outcome.
461	 */
462	function stopActiveStages(ids: Iterable<string>) {
463	  return cancelActiveStages(ids);
464	}
465	
466	/**
467	 * First half of a deletion: announce the cancellation (so a worker that is
468	 * still waiting on the multi-audio probe refuses to spawn a downloader for a
469	 * job that is about to disappear) and interrupt whatever child is running.
470	 */
471	function beginCancellation(ids: string[]): CancelledStages {
472	  const unique = [...new Set(ids)];
473	  if (unique.length === 0) return { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
474	  for (const id of unique) markJobCancelled(id);
475	  return stopActiveStages(unique);
476	}
477	
478	/**
479	 * Second half, run right after the rows are gone: a child that registered in
480	 * the instant between the ownership re-check and the row deletion is caught
481	 * here. Workers that never spawn are caught by the cancellation mark (checked
482	 * immediately after `Bun.spawn`), so between the two no child survives a
483	 * deleted job.
484	 */
485	function finishCancellation(ids: string[]): CancelledStages {
486	  if (ids.length === 0) return { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
487	  return stopActiveStages(ids);
488	}
489	
490	/** How many distinct jobs actually had a live child interrupted, across stages. */
491	function stoppedCount(...stages: CancelledStages[]): number {
492	  const ids = new Set<string>();
493	  for (const stage of stages) {
494	    for (const id of stage.downloads) ids.add(id);
495	    for (const id of stage.conversions) ids.add(id);
496	    for (const id of stage.metadata) ids.add(id);
497	  }
498	  return ids.size;
499	}

501	/**
502	 * Park a job that is mid-download as a user pause, keeping its .part for a
503	 * later resume. The claim is deliberately left in place: the worker still owns
504	 * this row, so it observes `pause_reason = 'user'` when its (now interrupted)
505	 * download returns and releases the claim through its own token.
506	 */
507	function parkDownloadingJobs(ids: string[]): void {
508	  if (ids.length === 0) return;
509	  const placeholders = ids.map(() => "?").join(",");
510	  db.run(
511	    `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'paused', pause_reason = 'user', speed = 0, eta = 0,
512	       updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
513	     WHERE id IN (${placeholders}) AND download_status = 'downloading'`,
514	    ids,
515	  );
516	}
517	
518	/** Run a synchronous job mutation only while none of its rows has a live stage claim. */
519	function withIdleJobs<T>(ids: string[], operation: () => T): IdleJobResult<T> {
520	  const placeholders = ids.map(() => "?").join(",");
521	  const transaction = db.transaction(() => {
522	    const active = db
523	      .query(`SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE id IN (${placeholders}) AND (${ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE}) LIMIT 1`)
524	      .get(...ids);
525	    if (active) return { ok: false as const };
526	    return { ok: true as const, value: operation() };
527	  });
528	  return transaction.immediate();
529	}

535	interface JobOverride {
536	  targetFormat?: string | null;
537	  videoQuality?: string | null;
538	  /** Language codes from the track picker; null restores the global audio mode. */
539	  audioTracks?: string[] | null;

541	
542	const JOB_TARGET_FORMATS = new Set(["mp4", "mkv", "webm", "mp3", "m4a"]);
543	
544	function parseJobOverride(body: unknown): { ok: true; value: JobOverride } | { ok: false; error: string } {
545	  if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body)) {
546	    return { ok: false, error: "A JSON object with at least one override is required" };
547	  }
548	  const raw = body as Record<string, unknown>;
549	  const allowed = new Set(["targetFormat", "videoQuality", "audioTracks", "retry"]);
550	  const unexpected = Object.keys(raw).find((key) => !allowed.has(key));
551	  if (unexpected) return { ok: false, error: `Unknown override field: ${unexpected}` };
552	  const value: JobOverride = {};
553	  let provided = false;
554	
555	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "targetFormat")) {
556	    provided = true;
557	    if (raw.targetFormat !== null && (typeof raw.targetFormat !== "string" || !JOB_TARGET_FORMATS.has(raw.targetFormat))) {
558	      return { ok: false, error: "targetFormat must be mp4, mkv, webm, mp3, m4a, or null" };
559	    }
560	    value.targetFormat = raw.targetFormat as string | null;
561	  }
562	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "videoQuality")) {
563	    provided = true;
564	    if (raw.videoQuality !== null && (typeof raw.videoQuality !== "string" || !Object.hasOwn(QUALITY_FORMATS, raw.videoQuality))) {
565	      return { ok: false, error: `videoQuality must be one of ${Object.keys(QUALITY_FORMATS).join(", ")} or null` };
566	    }
567	    value.videoQuality = raw.videoQuality as string | null;
568	  }
569	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "audioTracks")) {
570	    provided = true;
571	    if (raw.audioTracks !== null && !Array.isArray(raw.audioTracks)) {
572	      return { ok: false, error: "audioTracks must be an array of language codes or null" };
573	    }
574	    if (Array.isArray(raw.audioTracks)) {
575	      if (raw.audioTracks.length > 40 || raw.audioTracks.some((track) =>
576	        typeof track !== "string" || !track.trim() || track.trim().length > 32
577	      )) {
578	        return { ok: false, error: "audioTracks must contain up to 40 non-empty language codes (32 characters max)" };
579	      }
580	      const languages = [...new Set(raw.audioTracks.map((track) => (track as string).trim()))];
581	      value.audioTracks = languages.length ? languages : null;
582	    } else {
583	      value.audioTracks = null;
584	    }
585	  }
586	
587	  if (raw.retry !== undefined && typeof raw.retry !== "boolean") {
588	    return { ok: false, error: "retry must be a boolean" };
589	  }
590	  if (!provided && raw.retry !== true) {
591	    return { ok: false, error: "Provide at least one of: targetFormat, videoQuality, audioTracks" };
592	  }
593	  return { ok: true, value };
594	}

596	/** Apply a validated override inside the surrounding SQLite transaction. */
597	function persistJobOverride(id: string, override: JobOverride): void {
598	  const sets: string[] = [];
599	  const values: (string | null)[] = [];
600	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "targetFormat")) {
601	    sets.push("target_format = ?");
602	    values.push(override.targetFormat ?? null);
603	  }
604	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "videoQuality")) {
605	    sets.push("video_quality = ?");
606	    values.push(override.videoQuality ?? null);
607	  }
608	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "audioTracks")) {
609	    sets.push("audio_selection = ?");
610	    values.push(override.audioTracks?.length ? JSON.stringify(override.audioTracks) : null);
611	  }
612	  if (sets.length === 0) return;
613	  db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET ${sets.join(", ")}, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [...values, id]);
614	}

814	      // the next attempt's directory scan may resume from it — say so instead
815	      // of pretending the restart is clean.
816	      logError("web", `${id}: retry could not wipe locked partial ${partial}: ${removal.error}`);
817	      return {
818	        changed: 1,
819	        partialWarning:
820	          `Partial file is locked (${removal.error}). Close the program holding it — ` +
821	          `the next attempt may resume from the leftover partial instead of starting at 0%.`,
822	        convertedOnly: false,
823	      };
824	    }
825	  }
826	  return { changed: 1, partialWarning: null, convertedOnly: false };
827	}

829	/** Save per-job settings without queuing a download. */
830	function saveJobOverrideById(id: string, config: Config, override: JobOverride): number | "in-progress" {
831	  const result = withIdleJobs([id], () => {
832	    const row = db.query("SELECT id, download_status, target_format, video_quality FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(id) as
833	      | { id: string; download_status: string; target_format: string | null; video_quality: string | null }
834	      | null;
835	    if (!row) return 0;
836	    persistJobOverride(id, override);
837	    const fresh = db.query("SELECT target_format, video_quality FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(id) as {
838	      target_format: string | null;
839	      video_quality: string | null;
840	    };
841	    const formatOrQualityChanged =
842	      (Object.hasOwn(override, "targetFormat") && override.targetFormat !== row.target_format) ||
843	      (Object.hasOwn(override, "videoQuality") && override.videoQuality !== row.video_quality);
844	    const needsConversion =
845	      formatOrQualityChanged || effectiveTargetFormat(fresh, config) !== "mp4" || effectiveVideoQuality(fresh, config) === "audio";
846	    // A queued job will use the new container on its next fetch. Leave an
847	    // already-downloaded job alone unless retry=true (which stashes/re-fetches
848	    // it atomically), but make sure queued work gets its post-download remux.
849	    if (row.download_status !== "downloaded" && needsConversion) {
850	      db.run(
851	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
852	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
853	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
854	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
855	        [id],
856	      );
857	    }
858	    return 1;
859	  });
860	  return result.ok ? result.value : "in-progress";
861	}

863	/** Clear every per-stage failure counter for one job. */
864	function resetFailCounters(id: string): number {
865	  if (!id) return 0;
866	  return db.run(
867	    `UPDATE jobs SET retry_count = 0, metadata_retry_count = 0, conversion_retry_count = 0, last_error = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
868	    [id],
869	  ).changes;
870	}

872	/**
873	 * Delete a set of jobs by id (bulk action from the dashboard).
874	 *
875	 * Deletion is a cancellation too: any in-flight download, encode, or sidecar
876	 * fetch is interrupted first. The database transaction also stores a durable
877	 * per-video ignore tombstone before removing each row, so the next playlist
878	 * scan cannot quietly put a deleted job back in the queue.
879	 */
880	async function deleteJobsBulk(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
881	  const body: any = await req.json().catch(() => null);
882	  const ids: string[] = Array.isArray(body?.ids)
883	    ? [...new Set<string>(body.ids.filter((x: unknown): x is string => typeof x === "string" && x.length > 0).slice(0, 500))]
884	    : [];
885	  if (ids.length === 0) {
886	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Expected a JSON body with a non-empty ids array" }, { status: 400 });
887	  }
888	
889	  // Cancellation is part of the deletion: mark, interrupt, atomically save a
890	  // durable ignore tombstone and delete the rows, then sweep once more.
891	  let cancellationStarted = false;
892	  let stoppedBefore: CancelledStages = { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
893	  try {
894	    cancellationStarted = true;
895	    stoppedBefore = beginCancellation(ids);
896	    const result = deleteJobsAndIgnore(ids);
897	    const late = finishCancellation(ids);
898	    return Response.json({
899	      ok: true,
900	      ...result,
901	      stopped: stoppedCount(stoppedBefore, late),
902	    });
903	  } catch (error: any) {
904	    if (cancellationStarted) {
905	      try {
906	        finishCancellation(ids);
907	      } catch {}
908	      for (const id of ids) clearJobCancelled(id);
909	    }
910	    const message = String(error?.message || error);
911	    logError("job-delete", `Bulk delete failed for ${ids.length} selected job(s): ${message}`);
912	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: `Could not delete selected jobs: ${message}` }, { status: 500 });
913	  }
914	}

1278	      const body = await req.json().catch(() => ({}));
1279	      const flags: { column: string; key: string; kind: MetadataKind }[] = [
1280	        { column: "want_subtitles", key: "subtitles", kind: "subtitles" },
1281	        { column: "want_thumbnail", key: "thumbnail", kind: "thumbnail" },
1282	        { column: "want_description", key: "description", kind: "description" },
1283	      ];
1284	      const sets: string[] = [];
1285	      const values: (number | string)[] = [];
1286	      const explicitRetries = new Set<MetadataKind>();
1287	      for (const f of flags) {
1288	        const v = (body as Record<string, unknown>)[f.key];
1289	        if (v === undefined) continue;
1290	        if (typeof v !== "boolean") {
1291	          return Response.json(
1292	            { ok: false, error: `${f.key} must be a boolean` },

1294	          );
1295	        }
1296	        sets.push(`${f.column} = ?`);
1297	        values.push(v ? 1 : 0);
1298	        if (v === true) explicitRetries.add(f.kind);
1299	      }
1300	      if (sets.length === 0) {
1301	        return Response.json(
1302	          { ok: false, error: "Provide at least one of: subtitles, thumbnail, description" },
1303	          { status: 400 },

1307	      db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET ${sets.join(", ")}, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, values);

1311	        if (remaining.length !== unavailable.length) {

1313	        }

2108	async function handleApi(
2109	  req: Request,
2110	  config: Config,
2111	  url: URL,
2112	  pathname: string,
2113	  server?: RequestDeadlineServer | null,
2114	): Promise<Response> {
2115	  const segments = pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
2116	  // A static path (/api/jobs/pause) that exists with a different method is a
2117	  // 405 — it must never fall through to a :param route and be read as an id.
2118	  // Several routes may share one pattern (/api/settings GET + POST), so the
2119	  // verdict is per pattern: 405 only when NO route with that exact pattern
2120	  // accepts this method.
2121	  const exactAllow = new Set<string>();
2122	  let exactPath = false;
2123	  let exactAccepted = false;
2124	  for (const route of ROUTES) {
2125	    if (route.pattern.includes(":")) continue;
2126	    if (!matchRoute(route.pattern, segments)) continue;
2127	    exactPath = true;
2128	    for (const m of route.methods) exactAllow.add(m);
2129	    if (route.methods.includes(req.method)) exactAccepted = true;
2130	  }
2131	  if (exactPath && !exactAccepted) {
2132	    return methodNotAllowed(req.method, pathname, [...exactAllow]);
2133	  }
2134	
2135	  const allow = new Set<string>();
2136	  for (const route of ROUTES) {
2137	    const params = matchRoute(route.pattern, segments);
2138	    if (!params) continue;
2139	    if (!route.methods.includes(req.method)) {
2140	      for (const m of route.methods) allow.add(m);
2141	      continue;
2142	    }
2143	    // Give this one request its own deadline before the handler blocks for
2144	    // minutes. No server means no live socket (unit tests call handleRequest
2145	    // directly), and a handler that fails here must still run: the deadline is
2146	    // a convenience, never a reason to answer 500.
2147	    if (route.deadlineSeconds && server) {
2148	      try {
2149	        server.timeout(req, route.deadlineSeconds);
2150	      } catch {
2151	        // The request is not attached to a live connection any more.
2152	      }
2153	    }
2154	    return await route.handler({ req, config, url, params });
2155	  }
2156	  if (allow.size > 0) {
2157	    return methodNotAllowed(req.method, pathname, [...allow]);
2158	  }
2159	  return Response.json({ ok: false, error: `Unknown API path: ${pathname}` }, { status: 404 });
2160	}

2165	    { status: 405, headers: { Allow: allow.sort().join(", ") } },

## Audit findings (ranked by severity)

I verified the AGENTS.md §6 precedence order in `handleDownloadFailure` — it matches the documented sequence exactly; no ordering bug there. The real issues found:

**1. `probeMediaStreams` has no timeout — a wedged ffmpeg probe pins a converter worker forever (`src/workers/convert.ts:88-114`)**
Unlike `runFfmpeg` (timeout), the download watchdog, and the metadata watchdog, the `ffmpeg -i` stream probe is spawned with no `AbortSignal`, no timer, and no kill fallback. If ffmpeg hangs on a corrupt/odd file, `await Promise.all(...proc.exited)` never settles. Worse, the converter's claim heartbeat (`converterWorker` line 211) keeps renewing the lease, so the stale-claim reaper will never reclaim it either — the worker is wedged until manual intervention. This directly violates gotcha 38 ("process timeouts and cleanup on every external-tool path").

**2. `requeueFailedJobs` is neither lease- nor pause-gated (`src/engine.ts:336`, `src/reconcile.ts:468-556`)**
Every other mutating sweep checks `holdsEngineLease()` (`reconcileCrashedJobs`, `reapStaleClaims`, `relocationTick`), per gotcha 18. The 60s `requeueFailedJobs` interval does not: after `ENGINE_LEASE_LOST` (which pauses the engine), it keeps flipping `failed` rows to `pending` and clearing claim columns in a database another engine process now owns. It also ignores `isPaused()`, so it re-queues work while the engine is paused for `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`/disk-full — re-arming rows the operator deliberately parked via cooldown.

**3. `runFfmpeg` timeout has no hard-kill escalation (`src/workers/convert.ts:61-77`)**
On timeout it only calls `ctl.abort()`. The download (`cleanupDownloadProcess`) and metadata (`stopMetadataProcess`) paths escalate SIGINT → grace → SIGKILL; ffmpeg that ignores the abort signal leaves `await Promise.all([stderr, exited])` unsettled, and with the heartbeat renewing, the claim is never reaped — same permanent wedge shape as finding 1.

**4. Permanent-looking wordings fall through every classifier (`src/retry.ts:46-81, 416-449`)**
Gotcha 6 warns every unclassified wording loops forever via the transient budget + cooldown sweep. Still unmatched: "Join this channel to get access…" (YouTube's actual members-only wording — the rules only know "members-only" and "only available to … members"), "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot", and "requires verification to watch". These park as ordinary `failed` and are resurrected every cooldown, filling error.log — the exact complaint the terminal class exists to prevent.

**5. `handleDownloadFailure` itself can throw and kill the worker loop (`src/workers/download.ts:199-207`)**
The `catch` block awaits the failure handler with no nested guard; any throw from it (e.g. a SQLite call failing mid-shutdown, since `readProgressState`/`releaseOwned` are unguarded DB writes) escapes the `while` loop, terminating the worker against the "never let a worker loop exit on error" rule and stranding its claim until the reaper. Same shape in `converterWorker`/`metadataWorker`.

**6. `ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE` omits `metadata_claimed_by` (`src/web.ts:436-445`)**
Download and conversion arms check both `claimed_by IS NOT NULL` and `claim_token IS NOT NULL`; metadata checks only the token. A legacy migrated row holding `metadata_claimed_by` with a NULL token is treated as idle by the retry/override routes — inconsistent with the other two stages.

**7. Archive scrub is not rolled back when the stash fails (`src/web.ts:733-739`)**
`removeFromArchive` runs before `stashDownloadedFile`; if the rename throws, the DB transaction rolls back but the archive entry stays scrubbed, so the fallback `readArchiveIds()` dedupe no longer suppresses that video if the row is ever deleted.

**8. Minor: `cookiesWatch` credential count uses `LIKE '%age%'` (`src/reconcile.ts:425`)** — a substring match that also counts any `last_error` containing "storage", "message", "coverage", inflating the operator-facing rescue count. **Also** `/api/history` (`src/web.ts:2076-2078`) passes unvalidated `parseInt` output as `LIMIT ?` — `NaN`/negative values become an unbounded full-table query.

196	      exited = await Promise.race([

200	        }),
201	      ]);
202	    } finally {
203	      if (graceTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(graceTimer);

205	    if (!exited && proc.exitCode === null) {

208	      } catch {
209	        // The child may have exited just before the force-kill.
210	      }
211	    }
212	  }
213	  await proc.exited.catch(() => {});
214	}

457	/**
458	 * Re-queue failed jobs once they have cooled down for
459	 * `requeueFailedAfterMinutes`. Permanent download failures (private, removed,
460	 * age-gated, geo-blocked, dead URLs) are never retried. A cooldown starts a
461	 * fresh retry window for each stage; the worker's per-video cap still bounds
462	 * each burst of immediate retries, while a later sweep can recover from a
463	 * longer outage without operator intervention.
464	 *
465	 * Pass `ignoreCooldown: true` (used by the "Requeue all failed" web button) to
466	 * retry every eligible job immediately.
467	 */
468	export function requeueFailedJobs(config: Config, opts: { ignoreCooldown?: boolean } = {}): RequeueResult {
469	  const result: RequeueResult = { downloads: 0, conversions: 0, metadata: 0 };
470	  const ignoreCooldown = !!opts.ignoreCooldown;
471	  if (!ignoreCooldown && config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes <= 0) return result;
472	  // SQLite modifier built only from a validated integer — never user text.
473	  // With ignoreCooldown there is no age filter at all (a `-0 minutes` modifier
474	  // would still exclude rows whose updated_at falls in the current second).
475	  const modifier = ignoreCooldown ? "" : `AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-${Math.floor(config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes)} minutes')`;
476	
477	  try {
478	    // --- Downloads -----------------------------------------------------------
479	    const failedDownloads = db
480	      .query(
481	        `SELECT id, last_error, output_directory, title, "index", partial_file_path FROM jobs
482	         WHERE download_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
483	      )
484	      .all() as any[];
485	    for (const row of failedDownloads) {
486	      if (isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
487	      // Scheduling a retry is not itself a failed attempt. Reset the current
488	      // no-progress budget here; the next worker outcome is what spends it.
489	      // Reset resume_count = 0 so the job gets a fresh resume budget for this window.
490	      let validPartial = row.partial_file_path && existsSync(row.partial_file_path) ? row.partial_file_path : null;
491	      if (!validPartial && row.output_directory && row.title) {
492	        const found = findPartialFileSync(row.output_directory, jobFittedBaseFilename(row));
493	        if (found) validPartial = found;
494	      }
495	      db.run(
496	        `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'pending', retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0,
497	           partial_file_path = ?, pause_reason = NULL,
498	           download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
499	           download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
500	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
501	        [validPartial, row.id],
502	      );
503	      result.downloads++;
504	    }
505	
506	    // --- Conversions -----------------------------------------------------------
507	    const failedConversions = db
508	      .query(
509	        `SELECT id FROM jobs
510	         WHERE conversion_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
511	      )
512	      .all() as any[];
513	    for (const row of failedConversions) {
514	      db.run(
515	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
516	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
517	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
518	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
519	        [row.id],
520	      );
521	      result.conversions++;
522	    }
523	
524	    // --- Metadata -------------------------------------------------------------
525	    const failedMetadata = db
526	      .query(
527	        `SELECT id, file_path, last_error FROM jobs
528	         WHERE metadata_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
529	      )
530	      .all() as any[];
531	    for (const row of failedMetadata) {
532	      // Without the media file or after a permanent source error the metadata
533	      // fetch cannot succeed. Leave those rows terminal; the per-job sidecar
534	      // control is the explicit retry path if the operator wants to try again.
535	      if (!row.file_path || !existsSync(row.file_path) || isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
536	      db.run(
537	        `UPDATE jobs SET metadata_status = 'pending', metadata_retry_count = 0,
538	           metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
539	           metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
540	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
541	        [row.id],
542	      );
543	      result.metadata++;

545	
546	    const total = result.downloads + result.conversions + result.metadata;

551	    }
552	  } catch (e: any) {
553	    logError("requeue", String(e?.message || e));
554	  }

Verified finding 2: `requeueFailedJobs` mutates job state with no `holdsEngineLease()` gate and no `isPaused()` check. Note the comment at engine.ts:333-335 says it deliberately keeps running in offline mode (conversion requeues needed). So the pause gating question: should it skip when paused? When paused with BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS, requeuing failed downloads would set them to pending, but the download workers are idle while paused, so rows just sit pending. That's not harmful per se — but it does reset retry windows. Hmm. Actually the more serious issue is lease gating: after ENGINE_LEASE_LOST, this process must not touch job rows. #### Thinking

Confirmed. `requeueFailedJobs` is the only mutating sweep without lease gating. For pause: the comment in engine.ts says conversions should keep being re-queued even in offline mode. But when the engine is paused (BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS, disk-full, TOO_MANY_FAILURES, ENGINE_LEASE_LOST), the sweep should arguably not requeue. Actually for ENGINE_LEASE_LOST the pause happens + lease gate covers it. For other pauses — hmm, requeueing failed rows to pending while paused is mostly harmless but it does reset retry windows and clears claims on failed rows (claims shouldn't exist on failed rows anyway). The clear gap per gotcha 18: lease gating. I'll add lease gating. For pause, I need to be careful about offline mode — offline mode doesn't pause the engine. Pauses are: user pause, LOW_DISK_SPACE, TOO_MANY_FAILURES, BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS, ENGINE_LEASE_LOST, NETWORK. If engine paused with TOO_MANY_FAILURES, requeueing failed rows after cooldown is... the cooldown sweep design says "a later sweep can recover from a longer outage without operator intervention" — but circuit breaker requires operator resume. Requeueing rows to pending while engine paused means when the operator resumes, the whole queue retries. That's probably fine/desired.

I'll add lease gate only (matching relocateTick would also add isPaused but the engine comment says conversion requeue matters in offline mode — offline doesn't pause). Actually relocate gates on isPaused too. But for requeue, pausing for BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS and resetting failed download rows to pending is undesirable: it burns... no, retry_count reset to 0 means the next window is fresh — that's the intent of cooldown. Hmm, but the rows go pending and when unpaused they're retried. That's the designed behavior of the cooldown sweep anyway.

I'll add just the lease gate — minimal, clearly correct, matches gotcha 18. Where to gate? Inside requeueFailedJobs (so the web button path... no wait, the web button /api/failed/requeue uses ignoreCooldown: true and is run by the engine process that holds the lease — if the lease were lost, the button shouldn't work either). Hmm, but gating inside would change web button behavior when lease lost — that's correct behavior actually (don't mutate a DB another engine owns). But tests may call requeueFailedJobs directly without a lease. Let me check tests using requeueFailedJobs.

4	 * Exponential backoff with jitter, in milliseconds.
5	 *
6	 * attempt 0 → base, 1 → 2×base, 2 → 4×base … capped at maxSeconds, plus up to
7	 * 30% random jitter so many workers that failed together don't retry in
8	 * lockstep. The RNG is injectable to keep tests deterministic.
9	 */
10	export function computeBackoffMs(
11	  attempt: number,
12	  baseSeconds: number,
13	  maxSeconds: number,
14	  rnd: () => number = Math.random,
15	): number {
16	  const a = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number.isFinite(attempt) ? attempt : 0));
17	  const base = Math.max(1, baseSeconds);
18	  const cap = Math.max(base, maxSeconds);
19	  const exponential = Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** a);
20	  const jittered = exponential * (1 + 0.3 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, rnd())));
21	  return Math.round(jittered * 1000);
22	}

29	 * real duration — 3× realtime plus 5 minutes of slack — clamped between the
30	 * configured minimum and ceiling. Unknown duration → the minimum.

33	  durationSeconds: number | null | undefined,

39	  const scaled = (durationSeconds * 3 + 300) * 1000;
40	  return Math.max(minMs, Math.min(maxMs, scaled));

The `LIKE '%age%'` matches any word containing "age" — "storage", "message", "coverage", "language", "manage", "page". This inflates the count. Simplest improvement: replace `LIKE '%age%'` with more specific patterns: '%confirm your age%', '%age-restricted%', '%age restricted%', '%inappropriate for some users%'. Also add '%not a bot%' for bot-check. That's a real fix.

Now the "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" classification. How does yt-dlp classify? yt-dlp treats it as an error that suggests cookies; it's not permanent (with cookies it works). It falls to transient → retried forever without cookies. Hmm — the retry loop: transient failures spend per-video cap then park as failed; cooldown sweep requeues. So a bot-check failure without cookies burns retries each window. That is by design for credential errors? Age-gated is permanent ("sign in to confirm your age" → permanent). Bot-check is analogous: without cookies it never succeeds. But with cookies it works — and it can appear intermittently (YouTube throttling datacenter IPs). yt-dlp's own recommendation is cookies or PO tokens. Marking it permanent would park videos that could succeed with cookies later — but the operator can retry manually after adding cookies, same as age-gated. Hmm, but age-gated with cookies also succeeds — yet it's classified permanent.

What does the project intend? The cookiesWatch counts "credential-related" failed jobs — login/sign in/age/cookie — suggesting those jobs may be parked failed with those errors and rescued by cookies. That implies credential errors including bot-check should be... currently bot-check ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot") contains "sign in" → matches the credential count. And it's transient → retried per window, eventually parks as failed (retry budget), cooldown sweep requeues forever though. Hmm — the "requeue forever" is the loop complaint: gotcha 6 says every unclassified wording "parks as failed, and is re-queued by the cooldown sweep forever."

For bot-check: is retrying with cookies sensible? When cookies appear, next attempt uses them. So the loop isn't entirely wasted — it's a wait-for-cookies state. But burning retries forever is noisy. yt-dlp docs suggest it needs cookies/PO token. I think the right classification per this codebase's philosophy: "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" is credential-shaped, not permanent (cookies may fix it at any time, and it's often transient/IP-based). The current behavior retries it — noisy but self-healing when cookies arrive.

Actually wait — is it currently transient? Yes, falls through all classifiers. Is that a gap? The failure budget eventually parks it as `failed` (terminal? no, non-permanent failed → requeued after cooldown forever). The infinite cooldown requeue loop is the documented complaint class. But for credential errors, cooldown requeue is arguably desired so new cookies get used.

Hmm, this is a judgment call. A cleaner improvement: add a dedicated classifier `isCredentialError` for bot-check/login-required and have the requeue sweep treat them specially (e.g., requeue but without burning error.log, or park with a readable reason like "Sign in required (bot check) — add cookies"). But that's inventing new behavior beyond "fill gaps".

Actually SQLite docs: if LIMIT evaluates to NULL, then there is no upper bound. So NaN→NULL could return the whole table. Negative limit → treated as no limit too. So `?limit=-1` dumps entire history. Minor but real validation gap at a system boundary.
- logs: `slice(-limit)` with NaN → slice(-NaN) = slice(0)? `slice(-NaN)` → NaN→0 → whole array. Negative → slice(-(-5))=slice(5)... eh.

Fix: clamp to a sane positive integer (e.g. 1..500 for history, 1..1000 for logs).

183	  }

185	  for (const entry of entries) {
186	    if (out.length >= MAX_FILES) return true;
187	    const full = join(root, entry.name);
188	    if (entry.name.startsWith(".")) continue; // hidden files/dirs
189	    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
190	      // `.ytdl` directories are yt-dlp fragment state, never a source file.
191	      if (entry.name.endsWith(".ytdl")) continue;
192	      if (await walk(full, depth + 1, out)) truncated = true;
193	    } else if (entry.isFile()) {
194	      out.push(full);
195	    }
196	  }
197	  return truncated;
198	}

200	/**
201	 * Scan `rootDir` (default: the configured output root) for video files that
202	 * are not tracked in the jobs table and insert one conversion-queued job per
203	 * file, with `targetFormat` pre-selected. Tracked jobs whose finished media is
204	 * NOT in `targetFormat` are re-queued for conversion as well (their conversion
205	 * stage re-opens; nothing is re-downloaded).
206	 *
207	 * The work is purely local (disk walk + INSERTs) — no network — so it is safe
208	 * to run while offline mode is on; the conversions themselves are ffmpeg remuxes
209	 * that also need no network.
210	 */
211	export async function scanUnconvertedVideos(
212	  config: Config,
213	  targetFormat: string,
214	  rootDir?: string,
215	): Promise<UnconvertedScanResult> {
216	  const root = resolve(rootDir ?? config.outputRoot);
217	  const tracked = trackedPaths();
218	  const files: string[] = [];
219	  const truncated = await walk(root, 0, files);
220	
221	  const result: UnconvertedScanResult = {
222	    root,
223	    targetFormat,
224	    filesSeen: files.length,
225	    videoFiles: 0,
226	    imported: 0,
227	    requeued: 0,
228	    keptMultiTrack: 0,
229	    alreadyTracked: 0,
230	    tooSmall: 0,
231	    truncated,
232	  };
233	
234	  // Pass 1: tracked jobs already finished in the wrong container get their
235	  // conversion stage re-opened (see requeueWrongContainerJobs — this is how an
236	  // archive of mkv/webm downloads requested as mp4 gets repaired in place).
237	  requeueWrongContainerJobs(config, targetFormat, root, result);
238	
239	  interface Candidate {
240	    id: string;
241	    url: string;
242	    title: string;
243	    outputDirectory: string;
244	    folder: string;
245	    filePath: string;
246	    fileSize: number;
247	  }
248	  const candidates: Candidate[] = [];
249	
250	  for (const file of files) {
251	    if (!VIDEO_EXTENSIONS.has(extname(file).toLowerCase())) continue;
252	    result.videoFiles++;
253	    if (tracked.has(pathKey(file))) {
254	      result.alreadyTracked++;
255	      continue;
256	    }
257	    let size = 0;
258	    try {
259	      size = (await stat(file)).size;
260	    } catch {
261	      continue; // vanished between the walk and the stat
262	    }
263	    if (size < MIN_FILE_SIZE) {
264	      result.tooSmall++;
265	      continue;
266	    }
267	    const outputDirectory = dirname(file);
268	    // Group label: the first folder below the scanned root ("Unconverted" when
269	    // the file sits directly in the root).
270	    const rel = relative(root, outputDirectory);
271	    const firstSegment = rel && rel !== "." ? rel.split(sep)[0] : "";
272	    candidates.push({
273	      id: localFileJobId(file),
274	      url: pathToFileURL(file).href,
275	      title: hardenName(basename(file, extname(file))) || "Untitled video",
276	      outputDirectory,
277	      folder: sanitizeFolderName(firstSegment || "Unconverted"),
278	      filePath: file,
279	      fileSize: size,
280	    });
281	  }
282	
283	  if (candidates.length === 0) return result;
284	
285	  const insert = db.transaction((batch: Candidate[]) => {
286	    const stmt = db.prepare(
287	      `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO jobs
288	         (id, url, title, output_directory, target_format, want_subtitles, want_thumbnail,
289	          want_description, folder, file_path, file_size, progress, speed, eta,
290	          download_status, conversion_status, metadata_status)
291	       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, 0, ?, ?, ?, 100, 0, 0, 'downloaded', 'pending', 'not_needed')`,
292	    );
293	    for (const c of batch) {
294	      // INSERT OR IGNORE: a concurrent scan or a re-run after a partial batch
295	      // must never duplicate a file.
296	      result.imported += stmt.run(
297	        c.id,
298	        c.url,
299	        c.title,
300	        c.outputDirectory,
301	        targetFormat,
302	        c.folder,
303	        c.filePath,
304	        c.fileSize,
305	      ).changes;
306	    }
307	  });
308	  insert(candidates);
309	
310	  return result;
311	}

#### Thinking

The failing tests: `requeueWrongContainerJobs` filters `if (key !== root && !key.startsWith(root + sep)) continue;` — the path is under the root. On Windows, `key` is lowercased by `pathKey` but `root` is NOT lowercased! `root = resolve(rootDir ?? config.outputRoot)` — a mixed-case temp path like `C:\Users\SHAH~1\AppData\Local\Temp\unconverted-scan-XXX`. `key` is lowercased, `root` isn't, so `key.startsWith(root + sep)` fails on Windows. Same for `existsSync(row.file_path)` — that's fine.

So bug: `requeueWrongContainerJobs` compares case-folded key against a non-folded root. Fix: fold the root too — `const rootKey = pathKey(root)`.

Test 2 failure (multi-audio): also because the same filter fails, so keptMultiTrack never reached.

Third failing test: idle timeout audio probe test. Let me look at it.

找到了——这两个错误容器的失败是 Windows 大小写敏感性 bug：`requeueWrongContainerJobs` 将一个大小写折叠的 `pathKey` 与一个未折叠的 `root` 进行比较，因此 `startsWith` 在 Windows 上永远不会匹配。我来检查一下第三个失败（idle-timeout 测试）。

Elapsed = 5ms — the request answered immediately. That means the probe didn't run — the stub yt-dlp likely failed instantly on Windows (shebang script — `#!C:\...\bun.exe` — Windows can't execute shebangs per AGENTS.md gotcha!). The AGENTS.md says: "the mocks are shebang scripts, and Windows neither reads shebangs nor spawns extensionless files". So this test spawns a shebang stub on Windows — it fails immediately, probe returns instantly.

What did the route return? status probably 200 with ok:false or tracks missing? Actually elapsed=5ms and then it failed at the elapsed assertion before checking body. The probe probably failed immediately (ENOENT spawning the stub) and returned an error response.

So this test is inherently broken on Windows the same way the integration mocks are — the harness in integration tests compiles mocks with `bun build --compile`. The fix: this test should be skipped on Windows or the stub compiled. AGENTS.md 9.5 says fixtures that spawn a process need `bun build --compile` on win32.

318	export function formatTerminalErrorMessage(info: TerminalErrorInfo, raw: string | null | undefined): string {

320	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
321	    .trim()
322	    .slice(0, 300);

326	/** Split a stored terminal message back into label + detail (for reports/UI). */
327	export function parseStoredTerminalError(
328	  message: string | null | undefined,
329	): { label: string; detail: string } | null {

336	// --- Format fallback ladder --------------------------------------------------
337	//
338	// "Requested format is not available" is a SELECTOR problem, not a dead video:
339	// the preset the plan asked for has no matching stream. Instead of letting the
340	// failure burn the retry budget and park the video (the old behaviour) the
341	// download worker steps the quality override DOWN one rung and immediately
342	// retries with the new selector.
343	//
344	// The ladder is monotonic — every step persists a strictly lower per-job
345	// `video_quality` override, and nothing ever moves back up — so a job can
346	// descend it at most once and the recovery needs no retry budget to be bounded.
347	// The last rung is `highest` (`bv+ba/b`): it accepts any stream the extractor
348	// found, so a failure there means the video really has no usable formats.
349	export const FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER: readonly string[] = ["4k", "1440p", "1080p", "720p", "480p", "highest"];
350	
351	/**
352	 * The next lower quality preset for `current`, or null when there is none.
353	 *
354	 * `audio` never falls back to a video preset (that would silently download a
355	 * video stream for an audio-only request) and an unknown key has no defined
356	 * position on the ladder — both end the recovery, which the worker records as a
357	 * terminal format failure.
358	 */
359	export function nextFormatFallback(current: string | null | undefined): string | null {
360	  const key = String(current ?? "")
361	    .trim()
362	    .toLowerCase();
363	  if (!key || key === "audio") return null;
364	  const index = FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER.indexOf(key);
365	  return index >= 0 && index + 1 < FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER.length ? FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER[index + 1] : null;
366	}

373	 * wording also avoids the classifier phrases on purpose — a switch note left on
374	 * a row must never be mistaken for a dead video by the cooldown sweep.
375	 */
376	export function formatSwitchMessage(from: string, to: string): string {
377	  return `Requested quality ${from} is not available for this video — switched to ${to} automatically.`;

#### Thinking

Now the bot-check. "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" — this is a credentials issue, retryable after cookies. It should NOT be permanent. Currently it's not in any classifier, so it falls into transient budget, fails, gets re-queued by cooldown forever — bad, but the alternative (permanent) is also wrong because valid cookies fix it.

The AGENTS.md doc says cookies.txt watcher counts credential-blocked jobs via the LIKE query (login/sign in/age/cookie). "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" contains "sign in", so it's counted as credential-related. #### Thinking

For the archive-scrub rollback: `removeFromArchive` runs at web.ts:746 inside `withIdleJobs`. `stashDownloadedFile` can throw (rename fails) — then the route returns 500 and the transaction rolls back, but the archive file (plain text, outside SQLite) stays scrubbed. Consequence: if the job row is later deleted (source cleanup), the archive fallback dedupe won't suppress re-queueing that video. Minor but real.

Fix: record whether the archive was modified and re-append the id if the stash throws. But removeFromArchive doesn't report whether it removed something. Simplest robust fix: wrap the stash in try/catch; on failure, restore the archive entry by appending `youtube <id>` back. Appending a duplicate line is harmless (Set-based reading). Actually readArchiveIds splits on whitespace; duplicate lines fine.

But also note `removeFromArchive` returns false on failure — if it returned false, nothing was scrubbed... no wait, it returns true if archiveFile is empty/nonexistent (nothing to scrub) or after successful rewrite; false only on error. It doesn't say whether the id was present.

Simple approach: before calling removeFromArchive, check if the id is in readArchiveIds; if stash throws and the id was present, re-append. Let me implement:

```ts
const archiveHadId = readArchiveIds(config.archiveFile).has(id);
try {
  removeFromArchive(config.archiveFile, id);
  stashDownloadedFile(id, row.file_path);
} catch (err) {
  // The stash failed: the job stays as it was (transaction rolls back), but the
  // archive file is plain text outside SQLite — re-append the id or the
  // archive-fallback dedupe would no longer suppress this video after a
  // source cleanup deletes the row.
  if (archiveHadId) appendToArchive(config.archiveFile, id);
  throw err;
}
```

Need appendToArchive in archive.ts. And import readArchiveIds in web.ts. Let me check imports in web.ts.

归档清理发生在普通的 SQLite 之外的文本文件上，所以当 stash 失败时，必须显式地将其回滚。我会在 archive.ts 中添加一个 append 辅助函数。

A duplicate line is harmless (readers use a\n * Set). Returns false when the file cannot be written.\n */\nexport function appendToArchive(archiveFile: string, videoId: string): boolean {\n  try {\n    if (!archiveFile) return false;\n    const existing = existsSync(archiveFile) ? readFileSync(archiveFile, \"utf-8\") : \"\";\n    const needsNewline = existing.length > 0 && !existing.endsWith(\"\\n\");\n    writeFileSync(archiveFile, `${existing}${needsNewline ? \"\\n\" : \"\"}youtube ${videoId}\\n`);\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}",

1	# YT Playlist Downloader
2	
3	Batch YouTube playlist downloader and converter, built with Bun + TypeScript.
4	Feed it a list of playlist or video links and it handles fetching, format
5	selection, subtitle/thumbnail/description extraction, and conversion — with
6	a terminal UI and a web dashboard to watch it all happen.
7	
8	## Features
9	
10	- **Batch downloads** from a list of YouTube playlist or video URLs defined in `config.json`
11	- **Cross-playlist deduplication by video ID** — different playlist/channel URLs
12	  that contain the same video share one queued job; if source cleanup removes
13	  its row after download, the configured yt-dlp archive still prevents another
14	  playlist from queuing that completed ID.
15	- **Concurrent worker pools** for downloading, metadata fetching, and format conversion, all driven by job state in a central SQLite database
16	- **aria2c multi-connection downloads** — files split across up to 64 streams (16 by default) with automatic fallback to yt-dlp's native downloader when aria2c is not installed or for HLS/live streams. aria2c's own per-server connection cap (16) is clamped automatically, and a downloader argument aria2c rejects (exit 28) pauses the engine with a `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS` reason instead of failing every video in the batch
17	- **Dashboard download-speed profiles & Turbo IDM** — one-click **Standard**, **Maximum speed**, and **Aggressive (IDM)** presets stage aria2c, fragment, chunk, buffer, User-Agent, and bandwidth settings in Downloader Settings, plus a 1-click **⚡ Turbo IDM** toggle right in the main dashboard controls (or press <kbd>t</kbd>). Aggressive (IDM) mode uses 32 connections per download (split threshold 512K), 64 native DASH/HLS fragments, 10M HTTP chunks, a 64K socket buffer, and uncapped bandwidth for maximum network utilization like Internet Download Manager. Every setting remains individually tunable.
18	- **Bandwidth-aware scaling** — an optional per-download rate limit is divided across active download slots; the autoscaler grows the pool while the queue has backlog and reported bandwidth headroom. Because yt-dlp limits each process independently, a slot change does not retune transfers already running, so the aggregate is best-effort during scale changes
19	- **Resilient by design** — interrupted downloads keep their `.part` file and resume exactly where they stopped; the retry budget only shrinks while a video makes no forward progress
20	- **A resume that can never finish is discarded, not retried** — when the saved partial no longer matches what the server will serve (`HTTP Error 416: Requested range not satisfiable`, or aria2c refusing a file whose control state is gone), resuming repeats the failure forever and the video sits at 99.0%. The engine deletes the `.part` **and** its `.aria2` control file, resets progress, and restarts that video from zero
21	- **Automatic retries** with exponential backoff + jitter on transient failures (network drops, throttling, timeouts)
22	- **Signature-extraction failures self-heal once** — only yt-dlp's signature/nsig decipher errors trigger `yt-dlp -U`; updater output is bounded, it has a hard timeout, concurrent requests share one update, and a failed update leaves the normal retry budget intact
23	- **Disk-full failures pause the engine** — ENOSPC and common Windows/POSIX “disk full” errors preserve the partial and pause all workers for operator action instead of burning retries against an unwritable drive
24	- **Unavailable videos are skipped, not retried** — private, deleted, members-only, age-gated, paid or geo-blocked videos are attempted **once**, classified with a plain-language reason (`Private video`, `Video unavailable`, `Not available in your region`, …), and parked as a terminal skip: no retry budget, no cooldown requeue, no `error.log` line per dead video, and no circuit-breaker trip for a whole playlist of them. The rest of the playlist keeps downloading, and the reason stays readable in the dashboard, the Failed tab, `/api/failed` and the run report
25	- **An unavailable format is switched, not retried** — when yt-dlp answers `Requested format is not available`, the engine steps the quality down one rung (`4k → 1440p → 1080p → 720p → 480p → highest`), persists it as that job's quality override, and says so: `🎚️ Format 1080p not available — switched to 720p`. The ladder only ever moves down, so it cannot loop, and a stale multi-audio probe is cleared and re-probed first. Only a job that fails at every rung — a video with no usable formats — is parked, with `No format available` recorded as its reason
26	
27	- **Self-healing sweeps** — crashed jobs resume, stale claims are reclaimed, deleted downloads are re-fetched, and failed jobs are retried after a cooldown. With aria2c these sweeps resume from the download's `.aria2` control file, and a discarded partial always takes its control file with it
28	- **Delete means don't re-download** — videos removed with Delete Selected or the per-job delete action are remembered in SQLite and skipped by all later source scans, including after restart. The dashboard's Ignored Videos panel lets you allow a video again.
29	- **Resume state is protected, not aged away** — the startup sweep only deletes a `.part` once nothing will resume it: a `pending`, `paused`, or `waiting_live` job keeps its partial as long as the job exists, and a crash in the deliberate-re-download hand-off (`.superseded`) is rolled back or finished at the next start instead of leaving the old file unmanaged
30	- **Single-instance safety: one engine per `archive.db`** — a database-level engine lease (owner token + expiring heartbeat + monotonic fencing number) is taken before the startup sweeps, so a second engine pointed at the same database refuses to start with an actionable message even if it uses a different `webPort` — it can never re-queue the running instance's in-flight work. The lease is renewed while the engine runs, released on a clean exit, taken over automatically after a crash, and shown on the reliability panel
31	- **Claims are leases, not names** — every job claim carries a unique token and a heartbeat: download progress renews a download's lease, conversion and metadata stages heartbeat on an interval, and every progress, success, failure and release update must present that token (compare-and-swap). A worker that lost its claim — reaped after its lease lapsed, or superseded by a restarted engine — changes no job state instead of overwriting the new owner's
32	- **Locked work is never destroyed to make progress** — if a restart-from-scratch hits a partial file locked by another program (orphaned aria2c/ffmpeg, antivirus), the video is retried later with that exact reason in `last_error` instead of being wedged. The same rule holds for every sweep: a locked resume pair is kept intact and reported, never counted as cleaned, and a stranded `.aria2` control file left by a dead worker is swept before the reclaimed job retries — a control file whose data is gone makes aria2c neither resume nor restart
33	- **Duration-aware watchdog** — long videos are not killed by a flat 15-minute timeout
34	- **Disk space precheck** before starting a batch
35	- **Graceful shutdown** — safely stops in-flight downloads on exit
36	- **Terminal UI (TUI)** with live progress across all workers
37	- Correct format selection across VP9/AV1 containers (fixes yt-dlp/ffmpeg mismatches)
38	- **Multi-audio tracks** — YouTube's multi-language audio (the player's *Audio track* menu: original + auto-dubbed tracks). Keep every track, or just the languages you want, muxed into one MKV whose audio is switchable in any player — plus a per-video track picker in the dashboard
39	- **Subtitles and cover art embedded in the video** — the converter muxes the downloaded subtitle files into the finished file as selectable tracks (MP4 `mov_text`, MKV `copy`, WebM `webvtt`) and attaches the saved thumbnail as cover art, in the same pass that remuxes to the target container. The tracks therefore survive a webm/mkv → mp4 conversion, which used to drop both (the old remux mapped only the first video stream and the audio). Sidecar files are still written next to the media. Two independent switches (`embedSubtitles`, `embedThumbnail`) control it; turning either on also makes new jobs fetch the file it needs. Subtitle tracks are tagged with ISO 639-2 language codes (`en` → `eng`) so players show the right language, and live-chat "subtitles" are excluded from the fetch.
40	- Compatible with authenticated downloads (`--cookies`) and YouTube's n-challenge (a JS runtime — Deno, Node, or Bun — is discovered at startup and passed to yt-dlp)
41	- **cookies.txt is watched while the engine runs** — export it from your browser after startup (or replace it when it expires) and the next download attempt uses it; the engine logs the switch and tells you how many credential-blocked jobs it may rescue
42	- **Save Browser Cookies** — the dashboard's 🍪 button (or `POST /api/cookies/export`) reads a browser you are signed in to and saves its YouTube/Google cookies as `cookies.txt`. The export is staged first and only replaces `cookies.txt` when it contains a signed-in session; the previous file is kept as `cookies.txt.bak`. Close the browser if it reports that its cookie store is locked. When `cookies.txt` is rejected, the log now says why (JSON instead of Netscape format, fields not TAB-separated, no YouTube session, or expired), and each browser fallback logs yt-dlp's actual reason instead of a generic "no usable cookies"
43	- **Offline mode** — one switch (`offlineMode`, the dashboard's 📴 toggle, `--offline`, or `YTA_OFFLINE=1`) stops every download, scan, RSS watch and sidecar fetch, and leaves the engine doing the work that needs no network: converting files that still need conversion and moving finished files to secondary storage. Queued downloads wait untouched and start when the mode ends
44	- **Files that need no conversion still reach secondary storage** — a relocation pass moves finished media (sidecars included) whose conversion is already done, adopts a file a crashed run copied but never recorded, and re-relocates everything when `secondaryStoragePath` points somewhere new. It never copies a file onto itself and never overwrites a job that was re-downloaded meanwhile
45	- **Web dashboard** with live job status, bulk actions, failed-job recovery, a reliability panel, per-job detail, and an in-browser settings editor for the downloader
46	
47	## Tech Stack
48	
49	- [Bun](https://bun.sh) + TypeScript — runtime and application logic
50	- [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) — video and metadata extraction
51	- [aria2c](https://aria2.github.io/) — optional multi-connection downloading
52	- [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) — format conversion
53	
54	## Requirements
55	
56	- Bun ≥ 1.0
57	- `yt-dlp` and `ffmpeg` available on `PATH` (or configured explicitly)
58	- [aria2c](https://aria2.github.io/) **optional** — enables multi-connection downloads; without it the engine uses yt-dlp's native downloader
59	- A JavaScript runtime for YouTube's n-challenge: [Deno](https://deno.com) (recommended; yt-dlp's default), Node.js ≥ 22, or Bun. The engine discovers one at startup and passes `--js-runtimes` to every yt-dlp call. Without a runtime, YouTube downloads fail with "n challenge solving failed" — that is retried, never parked as a permanent video error. See [yt-dlp EJS](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/EJS).
60	- Tested on Windows 11
61	
62	Dependencies are checked automatically on startup; the app exits with a clear
63	error if anything required is missing. A missing aria2c or JS runtime is
64	reported as a warning and never blocks startup.
65	
66	## Development
67	
68	```bash
69	bun install
70	bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
71	bun test            # unit + end-to-end suite (mocked yt-dlp/ffmpeg, no network needed)
72	bun run check       # both
73	```
74	
75	The checked-in `package-lock.json` also supports reproducible npm dependency
76	installation with `npm ci`; Bun is still required to run the app and test suite.
77	Runtime data (`config.json`, `cookies.txt`, `archive.db`, logs, and the default
78	`downloads/` tree) is ignored by Git. Review `.gitignore` before adding any new
79	runtime output path.
80	
81	The end-to-end tests (`tests/integration.test.ts`) run the real engine against
82	the mock binaries in `tests/mocks/`, covering the happy path, transient-failure
83	retries, corrupt-partial resume, permanent failures, and restart reconciliation.
84

93	## Configuration
94	
95	Your saved sources and settings live in **`config.json` in the app's working
96	folder**, next to `archive.db`. `src/config.ts` only defines the schema and
97	shipped defaults; the Web UI does not edit TypeScript source files.
98	
99	For example (omitted keys use their defaults):
100	
101	```json
102	{
103	  "playlists": ["https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=..."],
104	  "channels": ["https://www.youtube.com/@SomeChannel"],
105	  "channelPlaylists": ["https://www.youtube.com/@SomeChannel/playlists"],
106	  "offlineMode": false,
107	  "outputRoot": "D:/Downloads/YT",
108	  "targetFormat": "mp4",
109	  "downloadSubtitles": true,
110	  "embedSubtitles": true,
111	  "writeThumbnail": true,
112	  "embedThumbnail": true,
113	  "writeDescription": false
114	}
115	```
116	
117	Keep `config.json` private: it can contain source URLs and a `webToken`.
118	`cookies.txt` contains authentication credentials and must also stay local; do
119	not commit either file.
120	
121	### Offline mode (no downloads)
122	
123	`offlineMode: true` turns the engine into a local post-processor: **nothing is
124	downloaded**, and the only work left is the work that needs no network.
125	
126	| Stage | Offline mode |
127	| --- | --- |
128	| Scans, RSS watching, daemon rescans | **idle** — no YouTube requests while offline; scheduled watchers resume when the mode ends |
129	| Downloads (yt-dlp / aria2c) | **off** — queued jobs stay `pending`, unclaimed, with their `.part` files intact |
130	| Metadata sidecars (subs/thumbnail/description/info.json) | **off** — every sidecar is a network fetch; `pending` stays `pending` |
131	| Conversion (ffmpeg) | **on** — files that still need conversion are converted |
132	| Secondary-storage move | **on** — finished files are moved, sidecars included |
133	| Cookie validation, network probes | **off** — the monitor does not probe or pause local work while offline; local cookie-file watching continues |
134	
135	Queued downloads are *left exactly as they are*: they are not skipped, failed,
136	or paused, so turning offline mode off resumes the queue where it stood. The
137	RSS watcher and daemon rescans are also armed while offline, but idle; they
138	resume automatically when the mode ends, without restarting the engine. A scan
139	already in flight may finish its request, but results are discarded if offline
140	mode was enabled before ingestion. The file that gets converted or moved is
141	finished for real — a converted file is recorded, and a moved file's new path
142	is recorded, both with the same crash-safe updates a normal run uses.
143	
144	Turn it on from the dashboard (**⚙️ Settings → 📴 Offline mode**, applied live,
145	no restart), from `config.json`, from `bun run config`, or for a single run
146	without touching `config.json`:
147	
148	```bash
149	bun run start --offline        # this run only; config.json is not modified
150	bun run start --offline=false  # override a machine-wide YTA_OFFLINE=1
151	YTA_OFFLINE=1 bun run start    # same as --offline (scheduled tasks, shortcuts)
152	```
153	
154	Choose a different dashboard port for one run without changing `config.json`:
155	
156	```bash
157	bun run start --port 3010
158	# Equivalent form:
159	bun run start --port=3010
160	```
161	
162	The value must be an integer from 1 to 65535; the override lasts only for this
163	process and is not written to `config.json`.
164	
165	The dashboard shows a blue **📴 Offline mode** banner while it is on, with how
166	many finished files are still waiting to move to secondary storage, and the
167	Reliability panel lists that relocation pass like the other sweeps.
168	
169	### Adding sources from the Web UI
170	
171	**Save & Scan** saves the pasted URL to the appropriate list in `config.json`
172	**before** scanning/queuing videos in `archive.db`. Playlist links go in
173	`playlists`, channel links in `channels`, and a channel's `/playlists` tab in
174	`channelPlaylists`. Single-video links also use the existing `playlists` list.
175	Share/tracking parameters are removed; a watch link with `list=` keeps the
176	playlist, not just the currently selected video. Repeated scans do not append
177	duplicate sources or duplicate jobs, even if all videos were already queued.
178	
179	Videos are queued as yt-dlp lists them, so a large playlist starts downloading
180	while the rest of it is still being scanned. The request returns once the whole
181	listing has been read.
182	
183	**Downloading a whole channel** (`https://www.youtube.com/@Handle`, with or without
184	a trailing `/`): the channel's uploads, live streams and Shorts are all listed.
185	Every video goes into **one folder named after the channel** (for example
186	`downloads/LearnGandC/`), not a separate `… - Videos` / `… - Shorts` folder per tab,
187	and RSS uploads go to the same folder. Shorts follow `skipShorts`: a Shorts entry
188	has no duration in the listing, so its tab decides, and it is skipped by default.
189	A channel listing is only stopped after 30 minutes with no output, so very large
190	channels finish instead of hitting the 10-minute limit used for playlists. Playlist
191	entries inside a listing are not queued as videos.
192	
193	**All playlists of a channel**: a channel link also downloads every playlist on
194	its `/playlists` tab. Each playlist gets its own folder named after the playlist
195	(for example `downloads/Season 1/`), and the playlist's jobs belong to the channel,
196	so removing the channel removes them too. A video that is both in an uploads tab
197	and a playlist stays in the channel folder it was queued into first. Pasting a
198	channel's `/playlists` link on its own does the same thing without the uploads.
199	A channel with no playlists tab is fine; the uploads still download.
200	
201	**Single video only** (the checkbox under the URL box) changes that one case:
202	a `watch?v=…&list=…&index=…` link saves only the video `v=` and drops the
203	playlist. Links without a video id are unaffected.
204	
205	**📋 Batch Links** opens a box for many links at once, one per line, or an
206	uploaded `.txt` file. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. All
207	valid links are saved to `config.json` in one write, then scanned in the
208	background with four workers, so a long list does not hold the page open. The
209	result shows counts by kind (playlists, single videos, channels), duplicates,
210	and each invalid line with its line number. Invalid lines stay in the box so
211	you can fix them and import again.
212	
213	**🧾 Metadata Only** fetches sidecar files (subtitles, thumbnail, description, `info.json`) for a pasted video or playlist without downloading any video. Files are written into the folder the videos would use and named exactly as the download will name them (`NNN - Title`), so a later download reuses them instead of fetching them again. Tasks run one at a time in the background and appear in the modal with per-video progress and errors. Tick *Single video only* for `watch?v=…&list=…` links to fetch just that video.
214	
215	- The response confirms **Saved to config.json**; a failed write is shown as
216	  an error and does not start a scan. Writes replace the file atomically, and
217	  concurrent source/settings updates cannot overwrite each other.
218	- An empty/temporarily unavailable source stays saved for future scans. A valid
219	  empty listing is distinct from a yt-dlp failure: nonzero exits and scans that
220	  exceed the 10-minute watchdog are shown as scan failures, not reported as
221	  "No videos found." If scanning fails after saving, the UI says the source was
222	  saved separately from the scan failure.
223	- Saved sources are scanned again at startup. With `daemonMode: true` and
224	  `rescanIntervalHours > 0`, full rescans include **all three lists**, including
225	  playlists added while running. Enabled RSS polling also picks up new channel
226	  entries without a restart, even if the engine started with no channels.
227	- The optional folder override is for **this scan**; it is recorded on the
228	  queued jobs, not stored as a source-level override in the config.
229	- Links submitted with an older version were one-off scans. Paste those source
230	  links once more to save them; you do **not** need to delete existing jobs or
231	  downloads. To completely remove a saved source, use **Saved sources → Remove**
232	  in the dashboard. It removes the URL from `config.json` and deletes its
233	  source-owned job rows from `archive.db`; jobs still referenced by another
234	  configured source are retained. Already-downloaded media files and the
235	  yt-dlp download-history file are not deleted, so a later overlapping playlist
236	  still skips those completed video IDs after their job rows are gone when
237	  `archiveFile` is enabled. The `bun run config` manager performs the same
238	  cleanup when saving removed sources (stop the engine before
239	  using the terminal manager). Purging the queue alone does not remove sources
240	  from future scans.
