922	      // sweep's next attempt starts clean instead of straight back into a 416.

924	      notePipelineFailure("dl", config);

928	    }
929	    if (partial) {
930	      // A fresh attempt still has to survive a genuinely broken stream, so the
931	      // no-progress budget is charged (it forgives again as soon as the restart
932	      // gets further than the previous attempt did).
933	      const backoff = computeBackoffMs(retry.retryCount, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds);

936	      return;
937	    }
938	    // Nothing on disk to resume: a 416 with no partial can only come from stale
939	    // media-URL state, and the next attempt re-extracts the formats anyway.
940	    // Nothing was deleted, so no work is lost — the budget just bounds the loop.
941	    const backoff = computeBackoffMs(retry.retryCount, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds);
942	    updateWorkerLine(id, `🧹 Resume refused (HTTP 416), nothing to discard — retrying in ${Math.round(backoff / 1000)}s | ${job.title}`, config);

944	  }
945	
946	  // Corrupt/incomplete partial: keep resuming up to maxResumeAttempts, then
947	  // discard the pair and restart. Every failed attempt still goes through the
948	  // progress-aware budget so repeated corruptions cannot loop forever.
949	  if (lower.includes("unable to resume") || lower.includes("incomplete") || lower.includes("corrupt")) {
950	    const resumeCount = (job.resume_count || 0) + 1;
951	    const partial =
952	      job.partial_file_path && existsSync(job.partial_file_path)
953	        ? job.partial_file_path
954	        : await findPartialFile(job.output_directory, base);
955	    const current = readProgressState(job.id);
956	    const retry = progressAwareRetryState(
957	      current.retryCount,
958	      current.bestProgress,
959	      current.progress,
960	      perVideoCap(config),
961	    );
962	    const restartFromScratch = resumeCount >= Math.max(1, config.maxResumeAttempts) || !partial;

969	      if (removal.fatal) {
970	        // Keep both files if a process/antivirus holds either one. This is a
971	        // retryable failure, but its no-progress attempt still spends budget.
972	        const msg = `partial file locked, cannot restart cleanly (${removal.error}). Close the program holding it — usually an orphaned aria2c/ffmpeg or antivirus scanning the download folder.`;
973	        const status = retry.exhausted ? "failed" : "pending";
974	        const parked = releaseOwned(
975	          job,
976	          "parking a locked partial",
977	          `download_status = ?, retry_count = ?, resume_count = ?, partial_file_path = ?, best_progress = ?, last_error = ?`,
978	          [status, retry.retryCount, resumeCount, partial, retry.bestProgress, msg.slice(0, 500)],
979	        );
980	        logError("download", `${job.id} ${job.title}: ${msg}`);
981	        if (!parked) return;
982	        if (retry.exhausted) {
983	          stats.failed++;
984	          notePipelineFailure("dl", config);
985	          updateWorkerLine(id, `❌ Retry budget spent — waiting for cooldown | ${job.title}`, config);
986	        } else {
987	          updateWorkerLine(id, `🔒 Partial locked — will retry | ${job.title}`, config);
988	          await Bun.sleep(computeBackoffMs(retry.retryCount, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds));
989	        }
990	        return;
991	      }
992	      partialRemoved = true;
993	    }
994	
995	    if (retry.exhausted) {
996	      const keepPartial = partial && !partialRemoved ? partial : null;
997	      const failed = releaseOwned(
998	        job,
999	        "parking an exhausted corrupt resume",
1000	        `download_status = 'failed', retry_count = ?, resume_count = ?, partial_file_path = ?, best_progress = ?, last_error = ?`,
1001	        [
1002	          retry.retryCount,
1003	          restartFromScratch ? 0 : resumeCount,
1004	          keepPartial,
1005	          retry.bestProgress,
1006	          errMsg.slice(0, 500),
1007	        ],
1008	      );
1009	      if (!failed) return;
1010	      stats.failed++;
1011	      notePipelineFailure("dl", config);
1012	      logError("download", `${job.id} ${job.title}: ${errMsg.slice(0, 500)}`);
1013	      updateWorkerLine(id, `❌ Retry budget spent — waiting for cooldown | ${job.title}`, config);
1014	      return;
1015	    }
1016	
1017	    if (restartFromScratch) {
1018	      const restarted = releaseOwned(
1019	        job,
1020	        "restarting from scratch",
1021	        `download_status = 'pending', retry_count = ?, resume_count = 0, partial_file_path = NULL,
1022	         progress = 0, best_progress = ?, speed = 0, eta = 0, last_error = ?`,
1023	        [retry.retryCount, retry.bestProgress, errMsg.slice(0, 500)],
1024	      );
1025	      if (!restarted) return;
1026	      updateWorkerLine(id, `🗑️ Restarting from scratch | ${job.title}`, config);
1027	      await Bun.sleep(computeBackoffMs(retry.retryCount, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds));

1350	 * (or taken over by a second engine process) cannot record its output over the
1351	 * new owner's row — it reports `lostClaim` and walks away.
1352	 *
1353	 * `opts.queueConversion` flips a pre-declared `conversion_status = 'not_needed'`

1357	 * in some other container. The CASE guard leaves rows that already go through
1358	 * conversion ('pending'/'failed') exactly as they were.

1360	export function recordSuccess(
1361	  job: Job,
1362	  filePath: string,
1363	  fileSize: number,

1365	): DownloadSuccessResult {
1366	  const changes = releaseClaimedJob(
1367	    "download",
1368	    job.id,
1369	    downloadClaim(job),
1370	    `download_status = CASE WHEN pause_reason = 'user' THEN 'paused' ELSE 'downloaded' END,
1371	     pause_reason = CASE WHEN pause_reason = 'user' THEN 'user' ELSE NULL END,
1372	     file_path = ?, file_size = ?, partial_file_path = NULL,
1373	     progress = 100, best_progress = 100, last_error = NULL,
1374	     conversion_status = CASE WHEN ? = 1 AND conversion_status = 'not_needed' THEN 'pending' ELSE conversion_status END,
1375	     -- A fresh download writes into the output tree, so the media is no longer
1376	     -- in secondary storage: the relocation pass must be allowed to move it
1377	     -- again once conversion finishes (src/relocate.ts).
1378	     relocated_to = NULL`,
1379	    [filePath, fileSize, opts.queueConversion ? 1 : 0],

1391	  const row = db.query("SELECT pause_reason FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(job.id) as
1392	    | { pause_reason: string | null }
1393	    | null;

54	/**

56	 *
57	 * `workerId` (when given) registers the child in `activeConvertProcs`, which is
58	 * what lets the dashboard interrupt an in-flight encode: without it a job
59	 * deleted mid-conversion left ffmpeg running in the terminal until it finished.
60	 */
61	export async function runFfmpeg(
62	  args: string[],
63	  timeoutMs: number,
64	  workerId?: number,
65	): Promise<{ code: number; stderr: string; timedOut: boolean }> {
66	  const ctl = new AbortController();
67	  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), timeoutMs);
68	  try {
69	    const proc = Bun.spawn([ffmpeg(), ...args], { stdout: "ignore", stderr: "pipe", signal: ctl.signal });
70	    if (workerId !== undefined) activeConvertProcs.set(workerId, proc);
71	    const [stderr, code] = await Promise.all([new Response(proc.stderr).text(), proc.exited]);
72	    return { code, stderr, timedOut: ctl.signal.aborted };
73	  } finally {
74	    clearTimeout(timer);
75	    if (workerId !== undefined) activeConvertProcs.delete(workerId);
76	  }
77	}

152	        .filter(isEmbeddableSubtitleFile)

154	        .map((name) => ({ path: join(mediaDir, name), language: parseSubtitleLanguage(name, mediaBase) }))

169	  coverPath: string,
170	  outputDir: string,
171	  workerId: number,

185	export async function converterWorker(id: number, config: Config): Promise<void> {
186	  const workerId = `cv-${id}`;
187	  while (!abortController.signal.aborted) {
188	    // Re-read the config every iteration so settings changed from the dashboard
189	    // (POST /api/settings) take effect on the next job without a restart. The
190	    // parameter is only the initial value.
191	    config = getConfig();
192	    if (isPaused()) {
193	      await Bun.sleep(2000);
194	      continue;
195	    }
196	    const disk = await checkDiskSpace(config.outputRoot, config.minFreeSpaceGB);
197	    if (!disk.ok) {
198	      triggerPause(`LOW_DISK_SPACE (${disk.free.toFixed(1)}GB < ${config.minFreeSpaceGB}GB)`);
199	      await Bun.sleep(10000);
200	      continue;
201	    }
202	    const job = claimConvertJob(workerId);
203	    if (!job) {
204	      await Bun.sleep(2000);
205	      continue;
206	    }
207	    // A conversion can run for hours (ffmpeg) and emits nothing the reaper can
208	    // see, so the claim's lease is renewed here. Without this heartbeat the
209	    // fixed stale window was the only signal, and a live long encode looked
210	    // exactly like a dead worker.
211	    const stopHeartbeat = startClaimHeartbeat("conversion", job.id, claimRef("conversion", job), () => {
212	      logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost — the encode will not be recorded`);
213	      const doomed = activeConvertProcs.get(id);
214	      if (doomed && doomed.exitCode === null) {
215	        try {
216	          doomed.kill("SIGINT");
217	        } catch {}
218	      }
219	    });
220	    activeConvertJobs.set(id, job.id);
221	    try {
222	      await convertJob(job, config, id);
223	    } catch (err: any) {
224	      await handleConvertFailure(job, config, err, id);
225	    } finally {
226	      activeConvertJobs.delete(id);
227	      activeConvertProcs.delete(id);
228	      stopHeartbeat();
229	    }
230	  }
231	}

233	/**
234	 * True when this worker still owns the job's conversion claim.
235	 *
236	 * Claims can be lost mid-flight: the stale-claim reaper re-queues conversions
237	 * whose lease expired, and a second engine process could reset them at startup
238	 * if this one's lease lapsed. A converter that kept working would then race a
239	 * second converter on the same files — the loser's source gets deleted under
240	 * it, which on Windows either fails silently (locked handle) or corrupts the
241	 * winner's output. Every destructive step (source delete, secondary-storage
242	 * move, final update) therefore re-checks ownership first and walks away if it
243	 * was stolen.
244	 *
245	 * Ownership is identified by the claim TOKEN, not the worker id: `cv-1` exists
246	 * in every engine process, so a stale worker's id can look exactly like the new
247	 * owner's.
248	 */
249	function stillOwnsConversion(job: Job): boolean {
250	  return ownsClaim("conversion", job.id, claimRef("conversion", job));
251	}
252	
253	/**
254	 * The converted output a previous attempt may have left behind: same base name
255	 * as the (now missing) source, with the target extension — or .mkv, which the
256	 * multi-audio path intentionally keeps. Empty string when nothing is there.
257	 *
258	 * This is the crash-window recovery: an attempt that died after the encode but
259	 * before the database update used to leave file_path pointing at a deleted
260	 * source, and the job was then failed (or worse, re-downloaded) even though
261	 * the finished media was sitting right there.
262	 */
263	export function findConvertedOutput(sourcePath: string, wantsMp3: boolean, targetFmt: string = "mp4"): string {
264	  if (!sourcePath) return "";
265	  const base = sourcePath.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
266	  const ext = wantsMp3 ? "mp3" : targetFmt;
267	  const candidates = Array.from(new Set([`${base}.${ext}`, `${base}.mp4`, `${base}.mkv`, `${base}.webm`, `${base}.mp3`, `${base}.m4a`]));
268	  for (const c of candidates) {
269	    if (c !== sourcePath && existsSync(c)) return c;
270	  }
271	  return "";
272	}

274	/** Delete the pre-conversion source — but never out from under a stolen claim. */
275	async function deleteConvertedSource(job: Job, config: Config, sourcePath: string): Promise<void> {
276	  if (!config.deleteSourceAfterConvert) return;
277	  if (!stillOwnsConversion(job)) {
278	    logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost mid-job — keeping the source file`);
279	    return;
280	  }
281	  try {
282	    await unlink(sourcePath);
283	  } catch (e: any) {
284	    // Loud, not silent: on Windows this is usually a lock held by an
285	    // antivirus scan or an orphaned ffmpeg. A lingering source is harmless
286	    // (file_path already points at the converted output), but the operator
287	    // should see WHY it lingers instead of finding mystery duplicates.
288	    logError(
289	      "conversion",
290	      `${job.id} ${job.title}: could not delete converted source ${sourcePath}: ${e?.code || e?.message || e}`,
291	    );
292	  }
293	}
294	
295	/** Secondary-storage move, integrity hash, and the final done update. */
296	async function finalizeConversion(
297	  job: Job,
298	  config: Config,
299	  id: number,
300	  finalPath: string,
301	): Promise<void> {
302	  if (!stillOwnsConversion(job)) {
303	    logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost mid-job — not finalizing`);
304	    return;
305	  }
306	  // `relocated_to` mirrors the move: the secondary-storage root the media was
307	  // moved under, or NULL while it stays in the output tree. The relocation pass
308	  // (src/relocate.ts) treats both cases consistently — a converted file that
309	  // already reached secondary storage must never be listed as "still to move",
310	  // and a file that did not must not claim otherwise.
311	  let relocatedTo: string | null = null;
312	  if (config.secondaryStoragePath) {
313	    const moved = await moveToSecondaryStorage(job, config.secondaryStoragePath, finalPath, () =>
314	      stillOwnsConversion(job),
315	    );
316	    if (moved.stopped) {
317	      // Ownership is gone: the thief owns these files now, so nothing else is
318	      // touched (not even the DB row, whose WHERE clause would refuse it).
319	      logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost mid-move — files left where they are`);
320	      return;
321	    }
322	    finalPath = moved.path;
323	    relocatedTo = config.secondaryStoragePath;
324	  }
325	  let integrity: string | null = null;
326	  if (config.verifyIntegrity) {
327	    integrity = await hashFile(finalPath);
328	  }
329	  // The claim-token CAS makes the done-update itself atomic with ownership: if
330	  // the claim was stolen while hashing, changes is 0 and the thief owns the job
331	  // now — touch nothing further.
332	  const claimed = releaseClaimedJob(
333	    "conversion",
334	    job.id,
335	    claimRef("conversion", job),
336	    `conversion_status = 'done', file_path = ?, integrity = ?, relocated_to = ?`,
337	    [finalPath, integrity, relocatedTo],
338	    `conversion_status = 'in_progress'`,
339	  );
340	  if (claimed === 0) {
341	    logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost before finalize — files left untouched`);
342	    return;
343	  }
344	  stats.converted++;
345	  notePipelineSuccess("post");
346	  updateConvertWorkerLine(id, `✅ Done | ${job.title}`, config);
347	}

349	/**
350	 * Move a finished conversion — media plus matching sidecars — into secondary
351	 * storage, preserving the folder layout. Returns the media's new path.
352	 *
353	 * Every destructive step re-checks ownership through `canContinue`: the claim
354	 * can be stolen at any await in this sequence, and after that the files belong
355	 * to the new claim (AGENTS.md invariant 20). A stopped move reports back so the
356	 * caller can bail out; a sidecar that cannot move is a warning, while the media
357	 * itself is `required` — if it cannot land in secondary storage the job must
358	 * fail and retry rather than be marked done against the wrong path. The source
359	 * is only ever deleted after a copy that reported success (see `moveFile`).
360	 *
361	 * Exported for the tests: the failure modes here are exactly the ones that must
362	 * never lose data, and they are impossible to trigger through the full engine
363	 * without contriving a broken secondary disk.
364	 */
365	export async function moveToSecondaryStorage(
366	  job: Pick<Job, "id" | "title" | "folder">,
367	  secondaryStoragePath: string,
368	  finalPath: string,
369	  canContinue: () => boolean = () => true,
370	): Promise<{ path: string; stopped: boolean }> {
371	  const destDir = join(secondaryStoragePath, job.folder);
372	  await mkdir(destDir, { recursive: true });
373	  const srcDir = dirname(finalPath);
374	  const srcBase = basename(finalPath).replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
375	  // Move matching sidecar files (subs/thumbs/description/info.json) with
376	  // the media so everything stays together in the final location.
377	  //
378	  // The order is pinned, because `readdir` is not: NTFS hands back names in
379	  // sorted order, ext4/APFS in hash order, so the same folder walks these
380	  // destructive steps differently on different machines — and a move that is
381	  // stopped mid-sequence (ownership lost) must stop at the same place
382	  // everywhere. The video's OWN sidecars (`<base><suffix>`, e.g.
383	  // `.info.json`) go first in a fixed suffix order — with an identical base,
384	  // name order IS suffix order — followed by the language-tagged derivatives
385	  // (`<base>.<lang>.vtt`) in name order.
386	  const entries = await readdir(srcDir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
387	  const isOwnSidecar = (f: string) => SIDECAR_SUFFIXES.some((sfx) => f === srcBase + sfx);
388	  const sidecars = entries
389	    .filter((f) => f.startsWith(srcBase + ".") && SIDECAR_SUFFIXES.some((sfx) => f.endsWith(sfx)))
390	    .sort((a, b) => {
391	      const [ownA, ownB] = [isOwnSidecar(a), isOwnSidecar(b)];
392	      if (ownA !== ownB) return ownA ? -1 : 1;
393	      return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
394	    });
395	  for (const f of sidecars) {
396	    if (!canContinue()) return { path: finalPath, stopped: true };
397	    await moveFile(join(srcDir, f), join(destDir, f), job);
398	  }
399	  if (!canContinue()) return { path: finalPath, stopped: true };
400	  const destPath = join(destDir, basename(finalPath));
401	  await moveFile(finalPath, destPath, job, { required: true });
402	  return { path: destPath, stopped: false };
403	}
404	
405	/**
406	 * Move one file to secondary storage without ever destroying the only copy.
407	 *
408	 * `rename` is tried first (same volume: atomic, and the source is gone the
409	 * moment it succeeds). Across volumes it fails with EXDEV and the copy is the
410	 * only option — and THAT is where the old code was dangerous: it swallowed a
411	 * copy failure and then unlinked the source anyway, so a full secondary disk
412	 * silently deleted a sidecar that had nowhere else to live. Now the source is
413	 * removed only after a copy that reported success; a failed copy keeps BOTH
414	 * files and is logged loudly (a duplicate is recoverable, a lost file is not).
415	 *
416	 * Returns false when the move did not happen. `required` turns that into a
417	 * thrown error — the media itself must land in secondary storage or the job
418	 * must stay retryable, while a sidecar is worth only a warning.
419	 *
420	 * A source that already IS the destination (an in-place conversion of media
421	 * relocated earlier: the convert writes the new container next to the old one,
422	 * both under the secondary root) needs no move at all — on Windows the
423	 * self-rename fails and the self-copy errors, which would fail the job.
424	 */
425	async function moveFile(
426	  src: string,
427	  dest: string,
428	  job: Pick<Job, "id" | "title">,
429	  opts: { required?: boolean } = {},
430	): Promise<boolean> {
431	  if (src === dest) return true;
432	  try {
433	    await rename(src, dest);
434	    return true;
435	  } catch {
436	    // EXDEV when secondary storage is another volume (the expected case);
437	    // anything else (a locked destination) has no better answer than the
438	    // checked copy below, which keeps the source on failure.
439	    return moveFileCopy(src, dest, job, opts);
440	  }
441	}
442	
443	async function moveFileCopy(
444	  src: string,
445	  dest: string,
446	  job: Pick<Job, "id" | "title">,
447	  opts: { required?: boolean },
448	): Promise<boolean> {
449	  try {
450	    // `force` overwrites a half-written destination from an earlier crash.
451	    await cp(src, dest, { force: true });
452	  } catch (e: any) {
453	    logError(
454	      "conversion",
455	      `${job.id} ${job.title}: could not move ${src} to secondary storage (${e?.code || e?.message || e}) — keeping BOTH copies`,
456	    );
457	    if (opts.required) {
458	      throw new Error(`secondary-storage move failed for ${src}: ${e?.code || e?.message || e}`);
459	    }
460	    return false;
461	  }
462	  // Only now is the source redundant.
463	  try {
464	    await unlink(src);
465	  } catch (e: any) {
466	    logError(
467	      "conversion",
468	      `${job.id} ${job.title}: moved ${src} to secondary storage but could not remove the source (${e?.code || e?.message || e}) — duplicate left in place`,
469	    );
470	  }
471	  return true;
472	}
473	
474	async function convertJob(job: Job, config: Config, id: number): Promise<void> {
475	  updateConvertWorkerLine(id, `🔄 Converting | ${job.title}`, config);
476	  const sourcePath = job.file_path!;
477	  const targetFmt = effectiveTargetFormat(job, config);
478	  const wantsMp3 = targetFmt === "mp3";
479	  if (!sourcePath || !existsSync(sourcePath)) {
480	    // Crash-window recovery: a previous attempt may have finished the encode
481	    // and died before recording it. Adopt the finished output instead of
482	    // failing (or letting anything re-download the video).
483	    const adopted = findConvertedOutput(sourcePath, wantsMp3, targetFmt);
484	    if (adopted) {
485	      logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: source missing but already converted — adopting ${adopted}`);
486	      await finalizeConversion(job, config, id, adopted);
487	      return;
488	    }
489	    throw new Error(`Source file missing: ${sourcePath || "(null)"}`);
490	  }
491	  const mediaDir = dirname(sourcePath);
492	  const probe = await probeMediaStreams(sourcePath, id);
493	  // Multi-audio archives land as MKV holding every selected track. If an
494	  // explicit output-format setting requests conversion, map every stream;
495	  // MP4 re-encodes each audio track to AAC instead of dropping the dubs.
496	  if (probe.audioStreams >= 2) {
497	    updateConvertWorkerLine(id, `🎧 Preserving ${probe.audioStreams} audio tracks | ${job.title}`, config);
498	  }
499	  // AGENTS.md (multi-audio): an MKV that carries several audio tracks is kept
500	  // as MKV even when the target is mp4. The scanner cannot know the track count
501	  // at ingest, so the exemption is applied here — otherwise the converter would
502	  // now (since embedding routes every job through it) happily remux the dubs
503	  // away. Embedding still runs, remuxing mkv → mkv.
504	  //
505	  // The decision uses the job's cached track selection, not the ffmpeg probe:
506	  // a plain MKV reports one audio stream, and the mock/tests deliberately
507	  // report two for a multi-audio archive. `selectAudioTracks` is the same
508	  // function the download worker used to choose what to mux in.
509	  const sourceContainer = extname(sourcePath).replace(/^\./, "").toLowerCase();
510	  const selectedTracks = Math.max(
511	    1,
512	    selectAudioTracks(
513	      parseTracksJson(job.audio_tracks) ?? [],
514	      config.multiAudioMode,
515	      config.audioTrackLanguages,
516	      parseSelectionJson(job.audio_selection),
517	    ).length,
518	  );
519	  const container =
520	    !wantsMp3 && targetFmt === "mp4" && selectedTracks >= 2 && sourceContainer
521	      ? sourceContainer
522	      : targetFmt;
523	  const embed = await collectEmbedInputs(job, config, sourcePath);
524	  const preparedCover = embed.coverPath ? await prepareCoverImage(embed.coverPath, mediaDir, id) : null;
525	
526	  let finalPath = sourcePath;
527	  try {
528	    if (wantsMp3 && !sourcePath.endsWith(".mp3")) {
529	      // Audio archive: encode to the target .mp3 instead of leaving the
530	      // source container (webm/m4a) untouched. The cover is carried over (or
531	      // added from the sidecar) rather than thrown away by `-vn`.
532	      const mp3Path = sourcePath.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, ".mp3");
533	      const res = await runFfmpeg(
534	        buildMp3Args({ sourcePath, outputPath: mp3Path, probe, coverPath: preparedCover }),
535	        60 * 60 * 1000,
536	        id,
537	      );
538	      if (res.code !== 0) {
539	        throw new Error(
540	          `FFmpeg mp3 encode ${res.timedOut ? "timed out" : "failed"}: ${res.stderr.split("\n").filter((l) => l.trim()).slice(-2).join(" ")}`,
541	        );
542	      }
543	      finalPath = mp3Path;
544	      // Claim-checked: a stale worker must not point the row at a file the new
545	      // owner is not converting.
546	      updateClaimedJob("conversion", job.id, claimRef("conversion", job), `file_path = ?`, [finalPath]);
547	      await deleteConvertedSource(job, config, sourcePath);
548	    } else if (!wantsMp3) {
549	      const alreadyTarget = sourceContainer === container;
550	      const cover = preparedCover && supportsCoverArt(container) ? preparedCover : null;
551	      // A fresh sidecar cover replaces the source's own art; never add a second.
552	      const addCover = Boolean(cover) && !probe.hasAttachedPicture && !probe.hasCoverAttachment;
553	      // A sidecar subtitle set replaces whatever the source carries, so a
554	      // retried embed cannot duplicate tracks.
555	      const addSubtitles = embed.subtitles.length > 0;
556	      // The remux is not only a container change any more: an mp4 that is
557	      // already mp4 still needs a pass when subtitles or the cover are missing.
558	      const needsRemux = !alreadyTarget || addSubtitles || addCover;
559	      if (needsRemux) {
560	        const targetPath = sourcePath.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, `.${container}`);
561	        const samePath = resolve(targetPath) === resolve(sourcePath);
562	        // Writing over the file ffmpeg is reading is not allowed, and the old
563	        // file must survive a failed pass: same-container work goes to a temp
564	        // sibling that is renamed into place only after ffmpeg succeeds.
565	        const outputPath = samePath ? `${sourcePath}.yta-tmp.${container}` : targetPath;
566	        const ffmpegArgs = buildRemuxArgs({
567	          sourcePath,
568	          outputPath,
569	          container,
570	          probe,
571	          subtitles: embed.subtitles,
572	          coverPath: addCover ? cover : null,
573	        });
574	        const res = await runFfmpeg(ffmpegArgs, 30 * 60 * 1000, id);
575	        if (res.code !== 0) {
576	          // A failed/timed-out pass must not leave a half-written temp that a
577	          // later adoption probe could mistake for a finished conversion.
578	          if (samePath) await unlink(outputPath).catch(() => {});
579	          throw new Error(
580	            `FFmpeg remux to .${container} ${res.timedOut ? "timed out" : "failed"}: ${res.stderr.split("\n").filter((l) => l.trim()).slice(-2).join(" ")}`,
581	          );
582	        }
583	        if (!stillOwnsConversion(job)) {
584	          if (samePath) await unlink(outputPath).catch(() => {});
585	          logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost mid-remux — leaving the source untouched`);
586	          return;
587	        }
588	        if (samePath) {
589	          // Replace the source atomically-ish: the finished file only appears
590	          // at the recorded path once it is complete.
591	          await rename(outputPath, targetPath);
592	        } else {
593	          finalPath = targetPath;
594	          // Claim-checked: a stale worker must not point the row at a file the
595	          // new owner is not converting.
596	          updateClaimedJob("conversion", job.id, claimRef("conversion", job), `file_path = ?`, [finalPath]);
597	          await deleteConvertedSource(job, config, sourcePath);
598	        }
599	      }
600	    }
601	  } finally {
602	    if (preparedCover && preparedCover !== embed.coverPath) {
603	      await unlink(preparedCover).catch(() => {});
604	    }
605	  }
606	  await finalizeConversion(job, config, id, finalPath);
607	}
608	
609	/**
610	 * Conversion failures are usually transient (a wedged ffmpeg, a full disk), so
611	 * they get their own retry budget with exponential backoff before the job is
612	 * parked as failed for the periodic sweep.
613	 */
614	async function handleConvertFailure(job: Job, config: Config, err: any, id: number): Promise<void> {
615	  const errMsg = String(err?.message || err).slice(0, 500);
616	  const attempts = (job.conversion_retry_count || 0) + 1;
617	  const cap = perVideoCap(config);
618	  const newStatus = attempts >= cap ? "failed" : "pending";
619	  // CAS on the claim token: losing the claim means the outcome belongs to the
620	  // new owner, so this worker changes nothing and reports nothing.
621	  const landed = releaseClaimedJob(
622	    "conversion",
623	    job.id,
624	    claimRef("conversion", job),
625	    `conversion_status = ?, conversion_retry_count = ?, last_error = ?`,
626	    [newStatus, attempts, errMsg],
627	  );
628	  if (landed !== 1) {
629	    // A row that is gone was deleted on purpose (dashboard delete / purge /
630	    // source removal) — nothing to record, nothing to warn about.
631	    if (db.query("SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(job.id)) {
632	      logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: conversion claim lost before recording the failure`);
633	    }
634	    return;
635	  }
636	  if (newStatus === "failed") {
637	    stats.failed++;
638	    logError("conversion", `${job.id} ${job.title}: ${errMsg}`);
639	    notePipelineFailure("post", config);
640	    updateConvertWorkerLine(id, `❌ Failed | ${job.title}`, config);
641	  } else {
642	    // The job was released back to the queue above, so any free converter may
643	    // pick it up; this worker only pauses briefly to avoid hammering a broken
644	    // ffmpeg. The full exponential backoff is applied by the failed-job sweep
645	    // once the per-video budget is spent (see requeueFailedJobs) — sleeping the
646	    // whole backoff here just parked a worker slot for minutes on end and made
647	    // the dashboard look frozen.
648	    const backoff = Math.min(computeBackoffMs(attempts, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds), 5_000);
649	    updateConvertWorkerLine(id, `🔁 Retrying in ${Math.max(1, Math.round(backoff / 1000))}s | ${job.title}`, config);
650	    await Bun.sleep(backoff);
651	  }
652	}
653	
654	function updateConvertWorkerLine(id: number, text: string, config: Config): void {
655	  workerStatuses.set(`CV${id}`, text);
656	  updateAbsoluteLine(2 + config.maxDownloadWorkers + id, `[CV${id}] ${text}`);
657	}

56	 * Subtitles are the only sidecar that can take minutes: with the legacy "all"

121	export async function metadataWorker(id: number, config: Config): Promise<void> {
122	  const workerId = `md-${id}`;
123	  while (!abortController.signal.aborted) {
124	    // Re-read the config every iteration so settings changed from the dashboard

126	    // parameter is only the initial value.
127	    config = getConfig();
128	    if (isPaused()) {
129	      await Bun.sleep(2000);
130	      continue;
131	    }
132	    // Offline mode: every sidecar (subtitles, thumbnail, description,
133	    // info.json) is a network fetch, so the pass is skipped entirely. Jobs keep
134	    // whatever metadata_status they have — 'pending' ones are fetched, unchanged,
135	    // the next time the engine runs online.
136	    //
137	    // Note the deliberate asymmetry with conversion: a job whose metadata is
138	    // still pending stays out of the converter's reach (its claim requires
139	    // metadata to be terminal), which is the ordering the operator asked for —
140	    // offline mode finishes files that only need local work, and leaves the
141	    // rest of the pipeline exactly as it found it.
142	    if (config.offlineMode) {
143	      updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, "📴 Offline mode — sidecars need network", config);
144	      await Bun.sleep(3000);
145	      continue;
146	    }
147	    const disk = await checkDiskSpace(config.outputRoot, config.minFreeSpaceGB);
148	    if (!disk.ok) {
149	      triggerPause(`LOW_DISK_SPACE (${disk.free.toFixed(1)}GB < ${config.minFreeSpaceGB}GB)`);
150	      await Bun.sleep(10000);
151	      continue;
152	    }
153	    const job = claimMetadataJob(workerId);
154	    if (!job) {
155	      await Bun.sleep(2000);
156	      continue;
157	    }
158	    // The metadata pass spawns yt-dlp for up to ten minutes and used to give
159	    // the reaper nothing but `updated_at` to look at. The claim lease (owner,
160	    // token, heartbeat) is renewed here so a live fetch is never re-queued and
161	    // a stale worker can never write over the new owner.
162	    const stopHeartbeat = startClaimHeartbeat("metadata", job.id, claimRef("metadata", job), () => {
163	      logError("metadata", `${job.id} ${job.title}: metadata claim lost — the sidecar pass will not be recorded`);
164	      // Same rule as downloads: a claim we no longer own must not keep a
165	      // network fetch running against the video's folder.
166	      const doomed = activeMetadataProcs.get(id);
167	      if (doomed && doomed.exitCode === null) {
168	        try {
169	          doomed.kill("SIGINT");
170	        } catch {}
171	      }
172	    });
173	    activeMetadataJobs.set(id, job.id);

176	    } catch (err: any) {

178	    } finally {
179	      activeMetadataJobs.delete(id);
180	      activeMetadataProcs.delete(id);

186	async function stopMetadataProcess(proc: Bun.Subprocess): Promise<void> {
187	  if (proc.exitCode === null) {
188	    try {
189	      proc.kill("SIGINT");
190	    } catch {
191	      // It may have exited between the check and the signal.
192	    }
193	    let graceTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
194	    let exited: boolean;
195	    try {
196	      exited = await Promise.race([
197	        proc.exited.then(() => true, () => true),
198	        new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
199	          graceTimer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 2_000);
200	        }),
201	      ]);
202	    } finally {
203	      if (graceTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(graceTimer);
204	    }
205	    if (!exited && proc.exitCode === null) {
206	      try {
207	        proc.kill("SIGKILL");
208	      } catch {
209	        // The child may have exited just before the force-kill.
210	      }
211	    }
212	  }
213	  await proc.exited.catch(() => {});
214	}

216	async function runMetadataJob(job: Job, config: Config, id: number): Promise<void> {
217	  updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, `📎 Metadata | ${job.title}`, config);
218	
219	  if (!job.file_path || !existsSync(job.file_path)) {
220	    throw new Error("Downloaded file missing — cannot fetch metadata");
221	  }
222	
223	  // Write sidecars next to the downloaded file using the same basename.
224	  const mediaDir = dirname(job.file_path);
225	  const mediaBase = basename(job.file_path).replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "");
226	  const outTemplate = join(mediaDir, `${mediaBase}.%(ext)s`);
227	  const mediaFilename = basename(job.file_path);
228	  const entriesBefore = await readdir(mediaDir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
229	  const existingSidecars = findSidecarFiles(entriesBefore, mediaBase, mediaFilename);
230	  const missing = missingMetadataKinds(
231	    existingSidecars,
232	    {
233	      subtitles: Boolean(job.want_subtitles),
234	      thumbnail: Boolean(job.want_thumbnail),
235	      description: Boolean(job.want_description),
236	      infoJson: config.writeInfoJson,
237	    },
238	    parseUnavailableMetadataKinds(job.metadata_unavailable),
239	  );
240	  if (missing.length === 0) {
241	    if (isPaused()) {
242	      releaseClaimedJob("metadata", job.id, metadataClaim(job), `metadata_status = 'pending'`);
243	      return;
244	    }
245	    recordMetadataSuccess(job, config, id, existingSidecars, true);
246	    return;
247	  }
248	
249	  const args = [
250	    ytDlp(),
251	    job.url,
252	    ...cookiesArgs(config),
253	    ...jsRuntimeArgs(),
254	    "--skip-download",
255	    "--no-simulate",
256	    "-o",
257	    outTemplate,
258	    "--socket-timeout",
259	    "15",
260	    "--retries",
261	    "5",
262	    "--extractor-retries",
263	    "3",
264	    "--newline",
265	    "--no-colors",
266	  ];
267	  args.push(...missingSidecarArgs(config, missing));
268	
269	  const timeoutMs = metadataTimeoutMs(missing);
270	  const ctl = new AbortController();
271	  let proc: Bun.Subprocess | null = null;
272	  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
273	    ctl.abort();
274	    // Abort normally terminates the child. Force-kill as a bounded fallback so
275	    // a tool that ignores SIGTERM cannot pin this worker forever.
276	    if (proc && proc.exitCode === null) {
277	      try {
278	        proc.kill("SIGKILL");
279	      } catch {}
280	    }
281	  }, timeoutMs);
282	  let stdoutText = "";
283	  let stderrText = "";
284	  let code = -1;
285	  try {
286	    const child = Bun.spawn(args, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe", signal: ctl.signal });
287	    proc = child;
288	    activeMetadataProcs.set(id, child);
289	    // Drain both pipes concurrently to avoid deadlock.
290	    const stdoutPromise = new Response(child.stdout).text();
291	    const stderrPromise = new Response(child.stderr).text();
292	    [stdoutText, stderrText, code] = await Promise.all([stdoutPromise, stderrPromise, child.exited]);
293	  } finally {
294	    clearTimeout(timer);
295	    activeMetadataProcs.delete(id);
296	    // If pipe setup/reading fails before proc.exited settles, do not leave an
297	    // untracked yt-dlp child running against a job whose claim will be released.
298	    if (proc) await stopMetadataProcess(proc);
299	  }
300	
301	  if (isPaused()) {
302	    releaseClaimedJob("metadata", job.id, metadataClaim(job), `metadata_status = 'pending'`);
303	    return;
304	  }
305	  if (ctl.signal.aborted) {
306	    throw new Error(`Metadata fetch timed out (${Math.round(timeoutMs / 60_000)}m)`);
307	  }
308	  if (code !== 0) {
309	    // yt-dlp exits non-zero when ONE requested sidecar fails while the others
310	    // were written — a single caption language answering 403 is the common
311	    // case. Throwing here discarded that success and retried the whole pass,
312	    // burning the per-video budget against files that were already on disk.
313	    // If everything this pass asked for landed, record it (and say so).
314	    const afterFailure = await readdir(mediaDir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
315	    const landedSidecars = findSidecarFiles(afterFailure, mediaBase, mediaFilename);
316	    const stillMissing = missingMetadataKinds(
317	      landedSidecars,
318	      Object.fromEntries(missing.map((kind) => [kind, true])),
319	    );
320	    if (stillMissing.length === 0) {
321	      updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, `⚠️ Metadata wrote all files despite a yt-dlp error | ${job.title}`, config);
322	      recordMetadataSuccess(job, config, id, landedSidecars, false, missing);
323	      return;
324	    }
325	    const tail = [stderrText, stdoutText]
326	      .filter(Boolean)
327	      .join("\n")
328	      .split("\n")
329	      .filter((l) => l.trim())
330	      .slice(-3)
331	      .join(" ");
332	    throw new Error(tail || `yt-dlp exited with code ${code}`);
333	  }
334	
335	  // Record which sidecar files now exist next to the media file.
336	  const entries = await readdir(mediaDir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
337	  const sidecars = findSidecarFiles(entries, mediaBase, mediaFilename);
338	  recordMetadataSuccess(job, config, id, sidecars, false, missing);
339	}

341	/** Metadata failures retry with exponential backoff up to the per-video cap. */
342	async function handleMetadataFailure(job: Job, config: Config, err: any, id: number): Promise<void> {
343	  const errMsg = String(err?.message || err).slice(0, 500);
344	  if (isPaused()) {
345	    releaseClaimedJob("metadata", job.id, metadataClaim(job), `metadata_status = 'pending'`);
346	    return;
347	  }
348	  const attempts = (job.metadata_retry_count || 0) + 1;
349	  const permanentSourceError = isPermanentDownloadError(errMsg);
350	  const cap = perVideoCap(config);
351	  const newStatus = permanentSourceError || attempts >= cap ? "failed" : "pending";
352	  // CAS on the claim token: a worker that lost its claim leaves the outcome to
353	  // the new owner instead of overwriting it.
354	  const landed = releaseClaimedJob(
355	    "metadata",
356	    job.id,
357	    metadataClaim(job),
358	    `metadata_status = ?, metadata_retry_count = ?, last_error = ?`,
359	    [newStatus, attempts, errMsg],
360	  );
361	  if (landed !== 1) {
362	    if (db.query("SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(job.id)) {
363	      logError("metadata", `${job.id} ${job.title}: metadata claim lost before recording the failure`);
364	    }
365	    return;
366	  }
367	  if (newStatus === "failed") {
368	    stats.failed++;
369	    if (permanentSourceError) {
370	      // A private, removed, or otherwise permanently unavailable source is not
371	      // a metadata-service outage. Park it without burning the retry budget or
372	      // tripping the post-processing circuit breaker.
373	      notePipelineSuccess("post");
374	      updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, `⚠️ Metadata unavailable at source | ${job.title}`, config);
375	    } else {
376	      logError("metadata", `${job.id} ${job.title}: ${errMsg}`);
377	      notePipelineFailure("post", config);
378	      updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, `❌ Metadata failed | ${job.title}`, config);
379	    }
380	  } else {
381	    // Bounded like the converter: the job is already re-queued for any free
382	    // worker, so this delay only avoids hammering a failing endpoint. The
383	    // failed-job sweep applies the real cooldown once the budget is spent.
384	    const backoff = Math.min(computeBackoffMs(attempts, config.retryBackoffBaseSeconds, config.retryBackoffMaxSeconds), 5_000);
385	    updateMetadataWorkerLine(id, `🔁 Retrying in ${Math.max(1, Math.round(backoff / 1000))}s | ${job.title}`, config);
386	    await Bun.sleep(backoff);
387	  }
388	}

390	function updateMetadataWorkerLine(id: number, text: string, config: Config): void {
391	  workerStatuses.set(`MD${id}`, text);
392	  updateAbsoluteLine(2 + config.maxDownloadWorkers + config.maxConcurrentConverts + id, `[MD${id}] ${text}`);
393	}

1	// src/reconcile.ts — startup & periodic self-healing for the job database.
2	//
3	// Four sweeps keep the pipeline honest across crashes, hard kills, and files
4	// moved or deleted behind the engine's back:
5	//
6	//   reconcileCrashedJobs   — jobs interrupted mid-flight resume automatically
7	//   reapStaleClaims        — claims orphaned by a dead worker are re-queued
8	//   reconcileMissingFiles  — "downloaded" files that vanished are re-queued
9	//                            (and scrubbed from the yt-dlp archive)
10	//   requeueFailedJobs      — failed jobs are retried after a cooldown, with
11	//                            permanent errors (private/removed videos) skipped

35	/**

37	 * visible as paused AND automatically re-claimed (resuming where they left
38	 * off via yt-dlp --continue). User-paused jobs stay held; orphan claims left
39	 * by older per-job pause requests are cleared without resuming those jobs.
40	 */
41	export function reconcileCrashedJobs(): number {
42	  // The engine lease gates this sweep: it resets EVERY in-flight claim, so it
43	  // may only run while this process owns `archive.db`. A second engine that
44	  // skipped the lease would re-queue the live engine's work behind its back —
45	  // exactly what the port lock prevented for equal-port instances, and never
46	  // prevented for different-port ones.
47	  if (!holdsEngineLease()) {
48	    logError(
49	      "reconcile",
50	      `refusing to reconcile crashed jobs: this process does not hold the engine lease (${describeEngineLease(readEngineLease())})`,
51	    );
52	    return 0;
53	  }
54	  // Persist the on-disk resume point before flipping the status. This is also
55	  // needed at startup after a hard kill, where the normal shutdown hook never
56	  // had a chance to run its partial-path freeze.
57	  const recorded = recordPartialPaths();
58	  // The claims reset here all belong to the PREVIOUS engine generation: the
59	  // lease was free or expired when this process took it (bumping `fencing`), so
60	  // these tokens cannot belong to a live owner of this database. Clearing the
61	  // token and heartbeat is what fences a stale worker out — its late updates no
62	  // longer match the row, and the CAS helpers refuse them.
63	  const stmt = db.run(
64	    `UPDATE jobs SET
65	       download_status = CASE WHEN download_status = 'downloading' THEN 'paused' ELSE download_status END,
66	       pause_reason = CASE WHEN download_status = 'downloading' OR (download_status = 'paused' AND pause_reason IS NULL) THEN 'interrupted' ELSE pause_reason END,
67	       conversion_status = CASE WHEN conversion_status = 'in_progress' THEN 'pending' ELSE conversion_status END,
68	       metadata_status = CASE WHEN metadata_status = 'in_progress' THEN 'pending' ELSE metadata_status END,
69	       download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
70	       download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
71	       conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
72	       conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
73	       metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
74	       metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
75	       updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
76	     WHERE download_status = 'downloading'
77	        OR (download_status = 'paused' AND pause_reason IS NULL)
78	        OR (download_status = 'paused' AND pause_reason = 'user' AND download_claimed_by IS NOT NULL)
79	        OR conversion_status = 'in_progress'
80	        OR metadata_status = 'in_progress'`,
81	  );
82	  if (stmt.changes > 0) {
83	    console.log(
84	      `🔄 Reconciled ${stmt.changes} interrupted/stale-claim job(s) (${recorded} partial(s) recorded) — interrupted jobs will resume automatically.`,
85	    );
86	  }
87	  return stmt.changes;

90	/**
91	 * How long a claim's lease may stay un-renewed before `reapStaleClaims` treats
92	 * its owner as dead and re-queues the job. The download window is never shorter
93	 * than either the 20-minute baseline or the configured maximum download
94	 * timeout. Exported so the dashboard and config manager report the exact
95	 * thresholds enforced by the sweep.
96	 *
97	 * These are LEASE-EXPIRY windows: they are measured from the claim's last
98	 * heartbeat, not from the moment the work started. A download renews its lease
99	 * on every progress line, and conversion/metadata renew theirs on an interval
100	 * (`startClaimHeartbeat`), so a live long-running stage never looks stale no
101	 * matter how long it runs.
102	 */
103	export function STALE_CLAIM_THRESHOLDS(config: Pick<Config, "maxDownloadMinutes">) {
104	  return {
105	    download: `-${Math.max(20, config.maxDownloadMinutes)} minutes`,
106	    conversion: "-3 hours",
107	    metadata: "-15 minutes",
108	  };
109	}

111	/**
112	 * The one predicate that decides whether a stage's claim lease has expired.
113	 *
114	 * `modifier` is a SQLite datetime modifier built from validated numbers (the
115	 * same strings `STALE_CLAIM_THRESHOLDS` hands to the dashboard). A claim with
116	 * no heartbeat yet (legacy rows claimed before heartbeats existed, or a test
117	 * fixture) falls back to its claim timestamp.
118	 *
119	 * The sweep AND the dashboard's stale-claims count both go through this, so the
120	 * panel cannot drift from what the reaper actually does.
121	 */
122	export function staleClaimCondition(stage: ClaimStage, modifier: string, alias = ""): string {
123	  const c = claimColumns(stage);
124	  const heartbeat = `COALESCE(${alias}${c.heartbeat}, ${alias}${c.at})`;
125	  return `(${heartbeat} IS NULL OR ${heartbeat} < datetime('now', '${modifier}'))`;
126	}
