128	/**
129	 * Reclaim ONE stale claim with a compare-and-swap on the claim token, the way
130	 * the owner last looked.
131	 *
132	 * This is what keeps two reapers (or a reaper racing a live worker's renewal)
133	 * from double-resetting a job: the update lands only if the row still carries
134	 * exactly the claim that was seen AND that claim's lease is still expired at
135	 * update time. A worker that renewed its heartbeat, or a second reaper that
136	 * already re-queued the job, makes this return false and the caller leaves the
137	 * row alone.
138	 *
139	 * Exported for the tests: the cross-connection races are only observable when
140	 * the CAS can be driven independently of the sweep loop.
141	 */
142	export function reapStaleClaim(
143	  stage: ClaimStage,
144	  jobId: string,
145	  claim: ClaimRef,
146	  modifier: string,
147	): boolean {
148	  const c = claimColumns(stage);
149	  const setClause =
150	    stage === "download"
151	      ? `download_status = 'paused', pause_reason = 'interrupted'`
152	      : `${c.status} = 'pending'`;
153	  const extra = `${c.status} = '${c.claimedStatus}' AND ${staleClaimCondition(stage, modifier)}`;
154	  return releaseClaimedJob(stage, jobId, claim, setClause, [], extra) === 1;
155	}
156	
157	/**
158	 * Periodic safety net: if a worker process/thread dies mid-job the claim can
159	 * be left behind. A download claim past the config-aware stale threshold is
160	 * reclaimed only when no worker still owns that job; progress events heartbeat
161	 * the claim timestamp. Conversion and metadata claims past their thresholds
162	 * are re-queued.
163	 */
164	export interface ReapSummary {
165	  downloads: number;
166	  conversions: number;
167	  metadata: number;
168	  /** Stranded control files left by dead download workers, swept this tick. */
169	  stranded: number;
170	  /** Stranded control files that could not be swept (locked) — retried later. */
171	  locked: number;
172	}
173	
174	export async function reapStaleClaims(config: Config): Promise<ReapSummary> {
175	  const thresholds = STALE_CLAIM_THRESHOLDS(config);
176	  const reaped: ReapSummary = { downloads: 0, conversions: 0, metadata: 0, stranded: 0, locked: 0 };
177	  // Lease-aware: only the engine that owns `archive.db` may reclaim claims. A
178	  // process without the lease would be guessing about rows it does not own.
179	  if (!holdsEngineLease()) {
180	    logError(
181	      "reaper",
182	      `skipped: this process does not hold the engine lease (${describeEngineLease(readEngineLease())})`,
183	    );
184	    return reaped;
185	  }
186	  try {
187	    // Freeze each in-flight download's `.part` path while the job is still
188	    // 'downloading' (that is this function's own filter) — otherwise the
189	    // reclaimed job resumes without a partial and restarts from scratch.
190	    const recorded = recordPartialPaths();
191	    const activeJobIds = Array.from(activeDownloadJobs.values());
192	    const activeJobFilter = activeJobIds.length
193	      ? `AND id NOT IN (${activeJobIds.map(() => "?").join(", ")})`
194	      : "";
195	    // Snapshot the claims about to be reclaimed, TOKEN INCLUDED, so each
196	    // reclaim below is a CAS against exactly this claim. If the owner renews
197	    // its lease (or another reaper/worker gets there first) between this SELECT
198	    // and the UPDATE, the CAS matches nothing and the row is left alone.
199	    const dlCols = claimColumns("download");
200	    const staleDownloads = db
201	      .query(
202	        `SELECT id, "index", title, output_directory,
203	                ${dlCols.by} AS claim_by, ${dlCols.token} AS claim_token
204	           FROM jobs
205	          WHERE ${dlCols.status} = '${dlCols.claimedStatus}'
206	            AND ${staleClaimCondition("download", thresholds.download)} ${activeJobFilter}`,
207	      )
208	      .all(...activeJobIds) as {
209	      id: string;
210	      index: number;
211	      title: string;
212	      output_directory: string;
213	      claim_by: string | null;
214	      claim_token: string | null;
215	    }[];
216	    for (const row of staleDownloads) {
217	      const claim: ClaimRef = { by: row.claim_by, token: row.claim_token };
218	      if (!reapStaleClaim("download", row.id, claim, thresholds.download)) continue;
219	      reaped.downloads++;
220	      // A reclaimed download whose worker died can leave half a resume pair:
221	      // the `.aria2` control file with no data file beside it. The next attempt
222	      // hands that control file to aria2c, which can neither resume (the data
223	      // is gone) nor start over — the job wedges. Only jobs this tick actually
224	      // reclaimed are swept, so the stranded files of a live claim stay put. A
225	      // locked control file is reported and left alone, exactly like the
226	      // corrupt-partial path: retry on the next tick rather than risk
227	      // stranding.
228	      const found = await sweepStrandedControlFiles(row);
229	      reaped.stranded += found.removed;
230	      reaped.locked += found.locked;
231	    }
232	
233	    const cvCols = claimColumns("conversion");
234	    const staleConversions = db
235	      .query(
236	        `SELECT id, ${cvCols.by} AS claim_by, ${cvCols.token} AS claim_token
237	           FROM jobs
238	          WHERE ${cvCols.status} = '${cvCols.claimedStatus}'
239	            AND ${staleClaimCondition("conversion", thresholds.conversion)}`,
240	      )
241	      .all() as { id: string; claim_by: string | null; claim_token: string | null }[];
242	    for (const row of staleConversions) {
243	      if (reapStaleClaim("conversion", row.id, { by: row.claim_by, token: row.claim_token }, thresholds.conversion)) {
244	        reaped.conversions++;
245	      }
246	    }
247	
248	    const mdCols = claimColumns("metadata");
249	    const staleMetadata = db
250	      .query(
251	        `SELECT id, ${mdCols.by} AS claim_by, ${mdCols.token} AS claim_token
252	           FROM jobs
253	          WHERE ${mdCols.status} = '${mdCols.claimedStatus}'
254	            AND ${staleClaimCondition("metadata", thresholds.metadata)}`,
255	      )
256	      .all() as { id: string; claim_by: string | null; claim_token: string | null }[];
257	    for (const row of staleMetadata) {
258	      if (reapStaleClaim("metadata", row.id, { by: row.claim_by, token: row.claim_token }, thresholds.metadata)) {
259	        reaped.metadata++;
260	      }
261	    }
262	
263	    const total = reaped.downloads + reaped.conversions + reaped.metadata;
264	    if (total > 0 || reaped.stranded > 0) {
265	      const details = [
266	        reaped.downloads > 0 ? `${recorded} partial path(s) recorded` : null,
267	        reaped.stranded > 0 ? `${reaped.stranded} stranded control file(s) swept` : null,
268	      ].filter(Boolean).join(", ");
269	      const suffix = details ? ` (${details})` : "";
270	      console.log(
271	        `🧟 Reclaimed ${reaped.downloads} stale download(s)${suffix}, ${reaped.conversions} conversion(s), ${reaped.metadata} metadata job(s).`,
272	      );
273	      logError(
274	        "reaper",
275	        `reclaimed stale claims: downloads=${reaped.downloads} conversions=${reaped.conversions} metadata=${reaped.metadata}`,
276	      );
277	    }
278	    if (reaped.locked > 0) {
279	      logError(
280	        "reaper",
281	        `${reaped.locked} stranded aria2c control file(s) are locked — kept both files; the next sweep retries`,
282	      );
283	    }
284	  } catch (e: any) {
285	    logError("reaper", String(e?.message || e));
286	  }
287	  return reaped;
288	}
289	
290	/**
291	 * Sweep the stranded half of a reclaimed job's resume pair: an `.aria2` control
292	 * file whose data file is gone. Returns what happened, so the caller can report
293	 * a lock and retry later instead of pretending it cleaned something.
294	 *
295	 * Never touches a job whose pair is intact — that is live resume state.
296	 */
297	export async function sweepStrandedControlFiles(
298	  job: Pick<Job, "id" | "index" | "title" | "output_directory">,
299	): Promise<{ removed: number; locked: number }> {
300	  const result = { removed: 0, locked: 0 };
301	  const dir = job.output_directory || ".";
302	  const base = jobFittedBaseFilename(job);
303	  let entries: string[];
304	  try {
305	    entries = await readdir(dir);
306	  } catch {
307	    return result;
308	  }
309	  for (const f of entries) {
310	    if (!f.endsWith(ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX)) continue;
311	    if (!f.startsWith(base + ".")) continue;
312	    const controlPath = join(dir, f);
313	    const dataPath = controlPath.slice(0, -ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX.length);
314	    if (existsSync(dataPath)) continue; // the pair is intact: resumable state
315	    // Control file first, data file (already gone) after — the pairing rule.
316	    const removal = await removePartialFiles(dataPath);
317	    if (removal.fatal) {
318	      result.locked++;
319	      logError(
320	        "reaper",
321	        `stranded control file ${controlPath} is locked (${removal.error || "not removable"}) — kept for now, will retry`,
322	      );
323	      continue;
324	    }
325	    if (removal.controlRemoved) result.removed++;
326	  }
327	  return result;
328	}
329	
330	/**
331	 * Startup reconciliation: the database says a video is downloaded, but the
332	 * file is not on disk any more (moved, renamed, or deleted by hand). Scrub the
333	 * id from the yt-dlp archive and re-queue the job so the next run fetches it
334	 * again — otherwise the archive entry would make yt-dlp skip it forever.
335	 *
336	 * Jobs whose conversion is in progress are skipped: with
337	 * `deleteSourceAfterConvert` the converter legitimately has the media in
338	 * mid-transition (the old source path is already gone while the new one is
339	 * not recorded yet), and re-queueing the download onto a live converter is
340	 * exactly the "file deleted before conversion finished" race.
341	 *
342	 * Returns the number of jobs re-queued.
343	 */
344	export function reconcileMissingFiles(config: Config): number {
345	  if (!config.verifyExistingFiles) return 0;
346	  let fixed = 0;
347	  try {
348	    const rows = db
349	      .query(
350	        `SELECT id, file_path, download_status, conversion_status, metadata_status,
351	                want_subtitles, want_thumbnail, want_description
352	         FROM jobs
353	         WHERE file_path IS NOT NULL
354	           AND conversion_status != 'in_progress'
355	           AND (download_status = 'downloaded' OR conversion_status = 'done')`,
356	      )
357	      .all() as any[];
358	    for (const row of rows) {
359	      if (row.file_path && existsSync(row.file_path)) continue;
360	      removeFromArchive(config.archiveFile, row.id);
361	      db.run(
362	        `UPDATE jobs SET
363	           download_status = 'pending', pause_reason = NULL,
364	           retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0, best_progress = 0, progress = 0,
365	           file_path = NULL, file_size = 0, integrity = NULL, partial_file_path = NULL,
366	           conversion_status = CASE WHEN conversion_status = 'not_needed' THEN 'not_needed' ELSE 'pending' END,
367	           metadata_status = CASE
368	             WHEN COALESCE(want_subtitles,0) + COALESCE(want_thumbnail,0) + COALESCE(want_description,0) > 0 THEN 'pending'
369	             ELSE metadata_status END,
370	           metadata_unavailable = '[]',
371	           download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
372	           download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
373	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
374	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
375	           metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
376	           metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
377	           last_error = 'file missing on startup — re-queued',
378	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
379	         WHERE id = ?`,
380	        [row.id],
381	      );
382	      fixed++;
383	      logError("reconcile", `${row.id}: file gone (${row.file_path}) — re-queued`);
384	    }
385	    if (fixed > 0) {
386	      console.log(`🔍 Startup check: ${fixed} downloaded file(s) missing — re-queued for download.`);
387	    }
388	  } catch (e: any) {
389	    logError("reconcile", String(e?.message || e));
390	  }
391	  return fixed;
392	}
393	
394	/**
395	 * Sweep: keep watching `cookiesFile` for the whole run.
396	 *
397	 * Cookies are not a startup-only concern. Operators export cookies.txt from the
398	 * browser *after* the engine is already running (or replace it when it expires),
399	 * and the download attempts must start using it without a restart. Returns the
400	 * transition so tests can assert on it; null means nothing changed.
401	 *
402	 * "Changed" means the CONTENT changed (see `detectCookiesChange`). An extension
403	 * that re-exports the same bytes on a timer used to log an update every poll —
404	 * 1440 `error.log` lines a day, which is also what rotated the ~1MB log every
405	 * few hours and pushed the real failures out of its retained tail.
406	 */
407	export function cookiesWatch(config: Config): CookiesChange {
408	  const { change, state } = detectCookiesChange({
409	    cookiesFile: config.cookiesFile,
410	    onUnreadable: (msg) => logError("cookies", msg),
411	  });
412	  if (!change) return null;
413	  if (change === "appeared" || change === "updated") {
414	    // Jobs parked by a credential-shaped permanent error are the ones this
415	    // unblocks. They are NOT auto-requeued — permanent failures never are —
416	    // but the operator is told exactly how many the new cookies may rescue.
417	    const blocked =
418	      (
419	        db
420	          .query(
421	            `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM jobs
422	              WHERE download_status = 'failed'
423	                AND (lower(COALESCE(last_error, '')) LIKE '%login%'
424	                  OR lower(COALESCE(last_error, '')) LIKE '%sign in%'
425	                  OR lower(COALESCE(last_error, '')) LIKE '%age%'
426	                  OR lower(COALESCE(last_error, '')) LIKE '%cookie%')`,
427	          )
428	          .get() as any
429	      )?.n || 0;
430	    console.log(
431	      `🍪 cookies.txt ${change === "appeared" ? "found" : "changed"} (${state.size} bytes) — the next download attempt will use it.`,
432	    );
433	    if (blocked > 0) {
434	      console.log(
435	        `   ${blocked} failed job(s) look credential-related — use each job's manual Retry action to spend the new cookies on it.`,
436	      );
437	    }
438	    logError(
439	      "cookies",
440	      `cookies.txt ${change} (${state.size} bytes) at ${state.file}; ${blocked} job(s) parked with a credential-style error`,
441	    );
442	  } else {
443	    console.warn(
444	      "⚠️ cookies.txt disappeared — continuing without cookies; age-gated/private/member-only videos will now fail.",
445	    );
446	    logError("cookies", `cookies.txt disappeared (${state.file}) — continuing without cookies`);
447	  }
448	  return change;
449	}
450	
451	export interface RequeueResult {
452	  downloads: number;
453	  conversions: number;
454	  metadata: number;
455	}
456	
457	/**
458	 * Re-queue failed jobs once they have cooled down for
459	 * `requeueFailedAfterMinutes`. Permanent download failures (private, removed,
460	 * age-gated, geo-blocked, dead URLs) are never retried. A cooldown starts a
461	 * fresh retry window for each stage; the worker's per-video cap still bounds
462	 * each burst of immediate retries, while a later sweep can recover from a
463	 * longer outage without operator intervention.
464	 *
465	 * Pass `ignoreCooldown: true` (used by the "Requeue all failed" web button) to
466	 * retry every eligible job immediately.
467	 */
468	export function requeueFailedJobs(config: Config, opts: { ignoreCooldown?: boolean } = {}): RequeueResult {
469	  const result: RequeueResult = { downloads: 0, conversions: 0, metadata: 0 };
470	  const ignoreCooldown = !!opts.ignoreCooldown;
471	  if (!ignoreCooldown && config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes <= 0) return result;
472	  // SQLite modifier built only from a validated integer — never user text.
473	  // With ignoreCooldown there is no age filter at all (a `-0 minutes` modifier
474	  // would still exclude rows whose updated_at falls in the current second).
475	  const modifier = ignoreCooldown ? "" : `AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-${Math.floor(config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes)} minutes')`;
476	
477	  try {
478	    // --- Downloads -----------------------------------------------------------
479	    const failedDownloads = db
480	      .query(
481	        `SELECT id, last_error, output_directory, title, "index", partial_file_path FROM jobs
482	         WHERE download_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
483	      )
484	      .all() as any[];
485	    for (const row of failedDownloads) {
486	      if (isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
487	      // Scheduling a retry is not itself a failed attempt. Reset the current
488	      // no-progress budget here; the next worker outcome is what spends it.
489	      // Reset resume_count = 0 so the job gets a fresh resume budget for this window.
490	      let validPartial = row.partial_file_path && existsSync(row.partial_file_path) ? row.partial_file_path : null;
491	      if (!validPartial && row.output_directory && row.title) {
492	        const found = findPartialFileSync(row.output_directory, jobFittedBaseFilename(row));
493	        if (found) validPartial = found;
494	      }
495	      db.run(
496	        `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'pending', retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0,
497	           partial_file_path = ?, pause_reason = NULL,
498	           download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
499	           download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
500	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
501	        [validPartial, row.id],
502	      );
503	      result.downloads++;
504	    }
505	
506	    // --- Conversions -----------------------------------------------------------
507	    const failedConversions = db
508	      .query(
509	        `SELECT id FROM jobs
510	         WHERE conversion_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
511	      )
512	      .all() as any[];
513	    for (const row of failedConversions) {
514	      db.run(
515	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
516	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
517	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
518	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
519	        [row.id],
520	      );
521	      result.conversions++;
522	    }
523	
524	    // --- Metadata -------------------------------------------------------------
525	    const failedMetadata = db
526	      .query(
527	        `SELECT id, file_path, last_error FROM jobs
528	         WHERE metadata_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
529	      )
530	      .all() as any[];
531	    for (const row of failedMetadata) {
532	      // Without the media file or after a permanent source error the metadata
533	      // fetch cannot succeed. Leave those rows terminal; the per-job sidecar
534	      // control is the explicit retry path if the operator wants to try again.
535	      if (!row.file_path || !existsSync(row.file_path) || isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
536	      db.run(
537	        `UPDATE jobs SET metadata_status = 'pending', metadata_retry_count = 0,
538	           metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
539	           metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
540	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
541	        [row.id],
542	      );
543	      result.metadata++;
544	    }
545	
546	    const total = result.downloads + result.conversions + result.metadata;
547	    if (total > 0) {
548	      console.log(
549	        `♻️ Re-queued ${result.downloads} download(s), ${result.conversions} conversion(s), ${result.metadata} metadata job(s) after cooldown.`,
550	      );
551	    }
552	  } catch (e: any) {
553	    logError("requeue", String(e?.message || e));
554	  }
555	  return result;
556	}
557	
558	/**
559	 * Suffix aria2c appends to a partial file to store its resume state.
560	 *
561	 * aria2 keeps a *control file* next to every in-progress download — "its
562	 * filename is the filename of downloading file with .aria2 appended" — holding
563	 * which pieces arrived and how far the transfer got. yt-dlp's native
564	 * downloader has no equivalent, so this only exists when `useAria2c` picked
565	 * aria2c as the downloader.
566	 */
567	export const ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX = ".aria2";
568	
569	/** A partial download plus every sidecar that must travel with it. */
570	export function partialSidecars(partialPath: string): string[] {
571	  return [partialPath, `${partialPath}${ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX}`];
572	}
573	
574	/** What `removePartialFiles` actually managed to do. */
575	export interface PartialRemovalResult {
576	  /** The `.aria2` control file no longer exists. */
577	  controlRemoved: boolean;
578	  /** The `.part` data file no longer exists. */
579	  dataRemoved: boolean;
580	  /**
581	   * True when removal had to abort because the control file is locked (still
582	   * held open by another process). Neither file may have been touched:
583	   * deleting the data file in this state would strand the control file and
584	   * wedge aria2c permanently (see above).
585	   */
586	  fatal: boolean;
587	  /** The path and reason of the failure, when fatal. */
588	  error?: string;
589	}
590	
591	/**
592	 * Delete a partial download and everything that belongs to it.
593	 *
594	 * The pairing is load-bearing, not tidiness. aria2c defaults to
595	 * `--allow-overwrite=false`, whose documented behaviour is: *"if a file
596	 * already exists but the corresponding control file doesn't exist, then aria2
597	 * will not re-download the file."* So deleting the `.part` while stranding the
598	 * `.aria2` leaves aria2c holding a control file for data that is gone — it can
599	 * neither resume nor restart, and the job wedges and retries forever. (Exit
600	 * status 10, *"piece length was different from one in .aria2 control file"*,
601	 * is the other way this bites.)
602	 *
603	 * The control file is therefore removed FIRST, and a locked control file
604	 * aborts the whole removal: on Windows an orphaned aria2c or an antivirus scan
605	 * can hold the handle for a while, and blindly unlinking in either order can
606	 * produce exactly the stranded-control-file state above. The order also bounds
607	 * the damage of a half-finished cleanup: data-without-control merely restarts
608	 * the transfer, control-without-data wedges it. Callers that must restart a
609	 * transfer from scratch should check `.fatal` and retry later instead.
610	 */
611	export async function removePartialFiles(partialPath: string): Promise<PartialRemovalResult> {
612	  const controlPath = `${partialPath}${ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX}`;
613	  const control = await removeOne(controlPath, { strict: true });
614	  if (!control.ok) {
615	    // Locked or otherwise undeletable — do NOT touch the data file.
616	    return { controlRemoved: false, dataRemoved: false, fatal: true, error: control.error };
617	  }
618	  const data = await removeOne(partialPath);
619	  // Data file locked (or a fragment directory that would not budge) but the
620	  // control file gone: the next attempt restarts from scratch — annoying, not
621	  // fatal. The `removed` flag is what tells the caller whether the file is
622	  // really gone, so a partial that survived is never reported as cleaned.
623	  return { controlRemoved: control.removed, dataRemoved: data.removed, fatal: false };
624	}
625	
626	/**
627	 * Delete one path, reporting whether anything was actually removed.
628	 *
629	 * The control file is removed strictly: it is always a plain file, so any
630	 * failure to unlink it (EISDIR included) is treated as "locked" and aborts the
631	 * whole removal, leaving the pair intact for a later retry.
632	 *
633	 * The data path is handled more tolerantly, because `.ytdl` resume points are
634	 * *fragment directories*: `unlink()` refuses them on every platform
635	 * (EISDIR/EPERM), so a caller that only ever unlinked would silently keep them
636	 * — and would report the partial as cleaned while the stale fragments were
637	 * still there for the next attempt to pick up.
638	 */
639	async function removeOne(path: string, opts: { strict?: boolean } = {}): Promise<{ removed: boolean; ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
640	  try {
641	    await unlink(path);
642	    return { removed: true, ok: true };
643	  } catch (e: any) {
644	    if (e?.code === "ENOENT") return { removed: false, ok: true }; // already gone
645	    if (!opts.strict) {
646	      try {
647	        const s = await stat(path);
648	        if (s.isDirectory()) {
649	          await rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
650	          return { removed: true, ok: true };
651	        }
652	      } catch {
653	        return { removed: false, ok: true }; // vanished between unlink and stat
654	      }
655	    }
656	    return { removed: false, ok: false, error: `${path}: ${e?.code || e?.message || e}` };
657	  }
658	}
659	
660	/**
661	 * Locate the in-progress download for a base filename: the `.part` file
662	 * (progressive and DASH both land here) or the `.ytdl` fragment directory.
663	 * Returns the newest match, or "" when there is nothing to resume.
664	 *
665	 * Note this deliberately matches only the data file: an aria2c control file on
666	 * its own is not resumable state, it is litter (see `removePartialFiles`).
667	 */
668	export async function findPartialFile(dir: string, baseFilename: string): Promise<string> {
669	  try {
670	    const resolvedDir = resolve(dir);
671	    const files = await readdir(resolvedDir);
672	    const matches: { path: string; mtime: number }[] = [];
673	    for (const f of files) {
674	      if (!f.startsWith(baseFilename + ".")) continue;
675	      if (!f.endsWith(".part") && !f.endsWith(".ytdl")) continue;
676	      const s = await stat(join(resolvedDir, f)).catch(() => null);
677	      if (s) matches.push({ path: join(resolvedDir, f), mtime: s.mtimeMs });
678	    }
679	    matches.sort((a, b) => b.mtime - a.mtime);
680	    // Absolute: the engine, the dashboard, and any post-mortem reader all need
681	    // to resolve this regardless of their own working directory.
682	    return matches[0] ? resolve(matches[0].path) : "";
683	  } catch {
684	    return "";
685	  }
686	}
687	
688	/**
689	 * Synchronous sibling of `findPartialFile`, for paths that cannot await
690	 * (the shutdown handler and the worker's pause path run outside any async
691	 * context).
692	 */
693	export function findPartialFileSync(dir: string, baseFilename: string): string {
694	  const resolvedDir = resolve(dir);
695	  let entries: string[];
696	  try {
697	    entries = readdirSync(resolvedDir);
698	  } catch {
699	    return "";
700	  }
701	  let best = "";
702	  let bestMtime = -1;
703	  for (const f of entries) {
704	    if (!f.startsWith(baseFilename + ".")) continue;
705	    if (!f.endsWith(".part") && !f.endsWith(".ytdl")) continue;
706	    const full = join(resolvedDir, f);
707	    let mtime: number;
708	    try {
709	      mtime = statSync(full).mtimeMs;
710	    } catch {
711	      continue;
712	    }
713	    if (mtime > bestMtime) {
714	      bestMtime = mtime;
715	      best = full;
716	    }
717	  }
718	  return best ? resolve(best) : "";
719	}
720	
721	/**
722	 * Remember where each in-flight download's `.part` lives before the job stops
723	 * being "downloading", including legacy user-paused rows that still hold a
724	 * download claim.
725	 *
726	 * Without this, a graceful shutdown or a reaped stale claim leaves the job
727	 * paused+interrupted with `partial_file_path = NULL` even though the partial is
728	 * sitting right there on disk. The next attempt then restarts the video from
729	 * scratch, and the dashboard reports no resumable partial — the resume the
730	 * sweep promises never actually happens. Synchronous so it can run from the
731	 * shutdown path and from `reapStaleClaims` before the status is flipped.
732	 */
733	export function recordPartialPaths(): number {
734	  const rows = db
735	    .query(
736	      `SELECT id, "index", title, output_directory, partial_file_path FROM jobs
737	       WHERE (download_status = 'downloading'
738	          OR (download_status = 'paused' AND pause_reason = 'user' AND download_claimed_by IS NOT NULL))
739	         AND partial_file_path IS NULL`,
740	    )
741	    .all() as any[];
742	  let recorded = 0;
743	  for (const r of rows) {
744	    if (recordJobPartial(r)) recorded++;
745	  }
746	  return recorded;
747	}
748	
749	/**
750	 * Record a single job's on-disk partial, if it has one. Returns the path, or
751	 * "" when there is nothing to resume.
752	 *
753	 * Used by the bulk sweep above and by the download worker's pause path, which
754	 * parks an in-flight job as 'paused' — without this the partial on disk is
755	 * orphaned from the job and the next attempt restarts the video from zero.
756	 */
757	export function recordJobPartial(
758	  job: Pick<Job, "id" | "index" | "title" | "output_directory">,
759	): string {
760	  // The fitted name, not the raw title: that is the file yt-dlp actually wrote
761	  // (see jobFittedBaseFilename). Searching with the unfitted name finds
762	  // nothing for a long title, so no partial path is recorded and the on-disk
763	  // resume state later looks like an orphan to the sweep.
764	  const partial = findPartialFileSync(job.output_directory || ".", jobFittedBaseFilename(job));
765	  if (partial) {
766	    db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET partial_file_path = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [
767	      partial,
768	      job.id,
769	    ]);
770	  }
771	  return partial;
772	}
773	
774	/**
775	 * Key for comparing a recorded path against a path built from a directory
776	 * walk.
777	 *
778	 * The two sides come from different places and are not textually equal even
779	 * when they name the same file: `findPartialFile(Sync)` stores an absolute,
780	 * `resolve()`d path, while `cleanOrphanedFiles` builds its paths by joining the
781	 * configured `outputRoot` (`./downloads` by default — relative) with the
782	 * entries of a recursive `readdir`. Resolving both sides to an absolute path
783	 * kills that mismatch, and case-folding on Windows (a case-insensitive
784	 * filesystem) keeps a recorded `C:\Downloads` matching a walked
785	 * `c:\downloads`.
786	 */
787	export function pathKey(p: string): string {
788	  const abs = resolve(p);
789	  return process.platform === "win32" ? abs.toLowerCase() : abs;
790	}
791	
792	/** Age after which an unowned orphan partial is swept, and the same for `.superseded` backups. */
793	export const ORPHAN_PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
794	
795	/**
796	 * Age after which a partial nothing will ever resume is considered litter.
797	 * Only ever applied to non-resumable owners: a partial belonging to a job that
798	 * is going to be claimed again is never aged out (see the sweep below).
799	 */
800	export const PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
801	
802	/**
803	 * Statuses whose partial the pipeline will still resume, so the sweep must
804	 * keep it no matter how old it is:
805	 *   • `pending` / `downloading` — the next claim continues from it
806	 *   • `paused`                  — the operator holds the job; resuming later
807	 *     must continue where it stopped, even after weeks
808	 *   • `waiting_live`            — parked until the stream becomes a VOD
809	 */
810	const RESUMABLE_PARTIAL_STATUSES = new Set(["pending", "downloading", "paused", "waiting_live"]);
811	
812	/**
813	 * Housekeeping for leftover partial downloads at startup:
814	 *   • a .part belonging to a FAILED job whose immediate retry window is spent
815	 *     is deleted when cooldown requeue is disabled; a partial no job will
816	 *     resume (terminal failure, forgotten row) is deleted once it is a week old
817	 *   • orphan .part files with no matching job (DB reset, manual cleanup) are
818	 *     deleted once they are a day old
819	 *   • orphan `.superseded` backups with no matching job are deleted once they
820	 *     are a day old — a backup the DB does not reference can never be restored,
821	 *     so it is a stale duplicate next to a job that re-downloaded over it
822	 *   • everything else — including in-flight downloads from a previous run and
823	 *     resume-able partials of failed jobs waiting for cooldown — is kept so
824	 *     `--continue` can pick up exactly where the download stopped
825	 *
826	 * Deleting a partial also deletes its aria2c control file, and control files
827	 * whose data file is gone are swept on their own — a stranded `.aria2` makes
828	 * aria2c refuse to restart the transfer (see `removePartialFiles`).
829	 */
830	export async function cleanOrphanedFiles(
831	  rootDir: string,
832	  config?: Config,
833	): Promise<{ removed: number; locked: number }> {
834	  const summary = { removed: 0, locked: 0 };
835	  try {
836	    const cap = config ? perVideoCap(config) : 0;
837	    const rows = db
838	      .query("SELECT partial_file_path, download_status, retry_count, last_error FROM jobs WHERE partial_file_path IS NOT NULL")
839	      .all() as any[];
840	    const owners = new Map<string, { status: string; retries: number; lastError: string | null }>();
841	    for (const r of rows) {
842	      if (r.partial_file_path) {
843	        // Absolute + case-folded: the walk below yields paths relative to a
844	        // possibly-relative outputRoot, and a raw string compare would miss.
845	        owners.set(pathKey(r.partial_file_path), {
846	          status: r.download_status,
847	          retries: r.retry_count || 0,
848	          lastError: r.last_error || null,
849	        });
850	      }
851	    }
852	    // Backups some job still owns (including in-flight re-downloads). The
853	    // sibling form covers legacy rows only: an older build renamed the file
854	    // aside before recording the backup, so the sole association left is
855	    // `<file_path>.superseded` — and only while that `file_path` is itself
856	    // missing. A sibling next to a live output file is a leftover from a
857	    // completed re-download and may be swept.
858	    const supersededOwners = new Set<string>();
859	    const supersededRows = db
860	      .query("SELECT superseded_file, file_path FROM jobs WHERE superseded_file IS NOT NULL OR file_path IS NOT NULL")
861	      .all() as any[];
862	    for (const r of supersededRows) {
863	      if (r.superseded_file) supersededOwners.add(pathKey(r.superseded_file));
864	      if (r.file_path && !existsSync(r.file_path)) {
865	        supersededOwners.add(pathKey(`${r.file_path}${SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX}`));
866	      }
867	    }
868	
869	    // Protect all partial files belonging to pending, downloading, or paused jobs
870	    // even if partial_file_path has not been explicitly populated on their row yet.
871	    const activeJobs = db
872	      .query(`SELECT id, "index", title, output_directory FROM jobs WHERE download_status IN ('pending', 'downloading', 'paused')`)
873	      .all() as any[];
874	    const activeBasePrefixes = new Set<string>();
875	    for (const j of activeJobs) {
876	      if (j.output_directory && j.title) {
877	        activeBasePrefixes.add(pathKey(join(resolve(j.output_directory), jobFittedBaseFilename(j))));
878	      }
879	    }
880	
881	    const files = await readdir(rootDir, { recursive: true });
882	    let removed = 0;
883	    for (const file of files) {
884	      const isPartial = file.endsWith(".part") || file.endsWith(".ytdl");
885	      const isSuperseded = file.endsWith(SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX);
886	      if (!isPartial && !isSuperseded) continue;
887	      // `resolve`, not `join`: recursive readdir entries are relative to
888	      // rootDir, so joining a relative root yields a relative path that never
889	      // matches the absolute path recorded in the database.
890	      const fullPath = resolve(rootDir, file);
891	      const s = await stat(fullPath).catch(() => null);
892	      if (!s) continue;
893	      const ageMs = Date.now() - s.mtimeMs;
894	      if (isSuperseded) {
895	        if (!supersededOwners.has(pathKey(fullPath)) && ageMs > ORPHAN_PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS) {
896	          await unlink(fullPath).catch(() => {});
897	          removed++;
898	        }
899	        continue;
900	      }
901	      const owner = owners.get(pathKey(fullPath));
902	      if (owner) {
903	        const waitingForCooldownRetry =
904	          owner.status === "failed" &&
905	          !!config &&
906	          config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes > 0 &&
907	          !isPermanentDownloadError(owner.lastError);
908	        const exhausted = owner.status === "failed" && cap > 0 && owner.retries >= cap && !waitingForCooldownRetry;
909	        // Only partials no attempt will ever resume are aged out. A paused or
910	        // pending job's resume state must survive indefinitely — deleting it
911	        // because a week passed silently throws away the download progress the
912	        // job exists to continue from.
913	        const abandoned = !RESUMABLE_PARTIAL_STATUSES.has(owner.status) && !waitingForCooldownRetry;
914	        const ancient = abandoned && ageMs > PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS;
915	        if (exhausted || ancient) {
916	          // Take the aria2c control file with it, or the next attempt wedges.
917	          if (await removePartialAndReport(fullPath, summary)) removed++;
918	        }
919	      } else if (ageMs > ORPHAN_PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS) {
920	        // Orphan: no job claims it — verify it does not match an active job's prefix before removing.
921	        const normalized = pathKey(fullPath);
922	        const isBelongingToActiveJob = Array.from(activeBasePrefixes).some((prefix) => normalized.startsWith(prefix));
923	        if (!isBelongingToActiveJob && (await removePartialAndReport(fullPath, summary))) {
924	          removed++;
925	        }
926	      }
927	    }
928	
929	    // Control files whose data file is gone (hand-deleted .part, an interrupted
930	    // cleanup, a partial removed by an older build). Note a stranded control
931	    // file is still named "<name>.part.aria2" — the suffix alone says nothing,
932	    // so the data-file check below is what decides. Pure litter now, and
933	    // actively harmful: aria2c sees a control file, cannot resume, and with
934	    // --allow-overwrite=false will not start over.
935	    for (const file of files) {
936	      if (!file.endsWith(ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX)) continue;
937	      const fullPath = resolve(rootDir, file);
938	      const s2 = await stat(fullPath).catch(() => null);
939	      if (!s2) continue;
940	      // Young enough that a download may just have started writing it.
941	      if (Date.now() - s2.mtimeMs < ORPHAN_PARTIAL_MAX_AGE_MS) continue;
942	      // Its data file is still there — this is live resume state, keep it.
943	      if (existsSync(fullPath.slice(0, -ARIA2_CONTROL_SUFFIX.length))) continue;
944	      try {
945	        await unlink(fullPath);
946	        removed++;
947	      } catch (e: any) {
948	        if (e?.code !== "ENOENT") {
949	          // Locked (an orphaned aria2c, an antivirus scan). Litter that will
950	          // not move is not a failure of the engine, but it must not be
951	          // reported as removed either — the next startup sweep retries it.
952	          summary.locked++;
953	          logError(
954	            "reconcile",
955	            `stranded control file ${fullPath} is locked (${e?.code || e?.message || e}) — left in place, will retry on the next sweep`,
956	          );
957	        }
958	      }
959	    }
960	
961	    summary.removed = removed;
962	    if (removed > 0 || summary.locked > 0) {
963	      console.log(
964	        `🧹 Cleaned ${removed} stale partial/backup file(s).` +
965	          (summary.locked > 0 ? ` ${summary.locked} locked file(s) left for a later sweep.` : ""),
966	      );
967	    }
968	  } catch (e: any) {
969	    logError("reconcile", String(e?.message || e));
970	  }
971	  return summary;
972	}
973	
974	/**
975	 * Remove a stale partial and say whether the DATA file is really gone.
976	 *
977	 * `removePartialFiles` refuses to touch the data file while the control file
978	 * cannot be removed (that pairing is what keeps aria2c restartable), and it
979	 * reports that refusal as `.fatal`. Counting it as a removal anyway is how the
980	 * sweep's "🧹 Cleaned N stale partial file(s)" line lied about locked files
981	 * that were still on disk — and how a wedged aria2c could go unnoticed. A
982	 * locked pair keeps BOTH files and is retried by the next sweep (the startup
983	 * sweep for a manual lock, the reaper for a stranded control file).
984	 */
985	async function removePartialAndReport(
986	  partialPath: string,
987	  summary: { removed: number; locked: number },
988	): Promise<boolean> {
989	  const result = await removePartialFiles(partialPath);
990	  if (result.fatal) {
991	    summary.locked++;
992	    logError(
993	      "reconcile",
994	      `partial ${partialPath} is locked (${result.error || "control file not removable"}) — kept both files, will retry later`,
995	    );
996	    return false;
997	  }
998	  if (!result.dataRemoved) {
999	    // Control gone, data still there (locked file, or a directory that would
1000	    // not budge). aria2c can restart now — that was the point of the deletion —
1001	    // but the file itself is still on disk, so it is not "cleaned".
1002	    summary.locked++;
1003	    logError("reconcile", `partial ${partialPath} could not be deleted — the next attempt restarts instead of resuming`);
1004	    return false;
1005	  }
1006	  return true;
1007	}
1008	
1009	// --- Superseded media files (deliberate re-downloads) ------------------------
1010	// Retrying an already-downloaded job from the dashboard — the usual case being
1011	// a new multi-audio track selection that needs a fresh download — must not
1012	// delete the existing file up front: the re-download can still fail, and the
1013	// engine's core rule is to never throw away work that has already been done.
1014	// Instead the old media file is renamed aside (`.superseded`), which also
1015	// frees the output path: yt-dlp refuses to re-download while the target file
1016	// exists (`--no-overwrites`) and `--download-archive` must be scrubbed by the
1017	// caller. The new download deletes the backup on success
1018	// (`dropSupersededFile`); a permanent re-download failure restores it
1019	// (`restoreSupersededFile`).
1020	//
1021	// The hand-off is ordered so a crash at ANY point is recoverable: the DB row
1022	// is rewritten first (backup recorded, `file_path` cleared) and only then is
1023	// the file renamed. The in-between state — a recorded backup whose file was
1024	// never moved — is rolled back by `reconcileSupersededFiles()` at the next
1025	// startup, so the media can never end up sitting at `<path>.superseded` with
1026	// no row that knows about it.
1027	
1028	export const SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX = ".superseded";
1029	
1030	/**
1031	 * Move a downloaded job's media file aside so a re-download gets a free
1032	 * output path. Clears `file_path` (it no longer exists) and records the
1033	 * backup in `superseded_file` BEFORE the rename, so the database and the
1034	 * filesystem can never disagree about where the file went. Returns the backup
1035	 * path, or null when the job had no file on disk to protect. Throws when an
1036	 * existing file cannot be renamed — the caller should refuse the retry rather
1037	 * than start a download that yt-dlp will skip against the still-present file,
1038	 * and the row is put back so the job still looks downloaded.
1039	 */
1040	export function stashDownloadedFile(jobId: string, filePath: string | null): string | null {
1041	  if (!filePath) return null;
1042	  const backup = `${filePath}${SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX}`;
1043	  if (!existsSync(filePath)) {
1044	    // The original is already gone. If a backup for the same path survives
1045	    // (a previous stash whose caller never got to record it — see
1046	    // reconcileSupersededFiles), adopt it: the file is still worth protecting.
1047	    if (existsSync(backup)) {
1048	      db.run(
1049	        `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = NULL, file_size = 0, superseded_file = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1050	        [backup, jobId],
1051	      );
1052	      return backup;
1053	    }
1054	    // DB says downloaded but the file is already gone — nothing to protect.
1055	    db.run(
1056	      `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = NULL, file_size = 0, superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1057	      [jobId],
1058	    );
1059	    return null;
1060	  }
1061	  let size = 0;
1062	  try {
1063	    size = statSync(filePath).size;
1064	  } catch {}
1065	  // Record the intent BEFORE the filesystem rename. If the process dies
1066	  // between the two steps the database still knows where the file went, and
1067	  // `reconcileSupersededFiles` completes or rolls back the hand-off at the
1068	  // next startup. The reverse order (rename first, record after) is the bug
1069	  // this replaces: a crash in that window left the media at
1070	  // `<path>.superseded` with no row pointing at it, so the re-queue looked
1071	  // exactly like a deleted download and the backup was never managed again.
1072	  db.run(
1073	    `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = NULL, file_size = 0, superseded_file = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1074	    [backup, jobId],
1075	  );
1076	  try {
1077	    renameSync(filePath, backup);
1078	  } catch (err: any) {
1079	    // Put the row back exactly as it was: the caller aborts the retry (500),
1080	    // so the job must still look downloaded with its file in place.
1081	    db.run(
1082	      `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = ?, file_size = ?, superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1083	      [filePath, size, jobId],
1084	    );
1085	    throw new Error(`could not move the previous file aside (${filePath}): ${err?.message || err}`);
1086	  }
1087	  return backup;
1088	}
1089	
1090	/**
1091	 * The re-download succeeded — the backup of the previous file is no longer
1092	 * needed. Safe to call for jobs without a backup (no-op).
1093	 */
1094	export function dropSupersededFile(jobId: string): void {
1095	  const row = db.query("SELECT superseded_file FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(jobId) as
1096	    | { superseded_file: string | null }
1097	    | null;
1098	  const backup = row?.superseded_file || null;
1099	  db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [jobId]);
1100	  if (!backup) return;
1101	  try {
1102	    unlinkSync(backup);
1103	  } catch {
1104	    // Leftover backup is litter, not an error — the new file is in place.
1105	  }
1106	}
1107	
1108	/**
1109	 * The re-download failed permanently — put the previous file back and mark
1110	 * the job downloaded again, so the operator keeps exactly what was archived
1111	 * before the retry. Returns false when there was nothing to restore.
1112	 *
1113	 * `claim` is the download claim the caller still believes it holds (the worker
1114	 * passes its claim; the startup sweeps pass none). When given, ownership is
1115	 * verified BEFORE the file is moved and the row update is a CAS on the claim
1116	 * token, so a worker whose claim was reclaimed cannot restore an old file over
1117	 * the new owner's work.
1118	 */
1119	export function restoreSupersededFile(jobId: string, reason: string, claim?: ClaimRef): boolean {
1120	  if (claim && !ownsClaim("download", jobId, claim)) {
1121	    logError("reconcile", `${jobId}: refusing to restore the superseded backup — the download claim was lost`);
1122	    return false;
1123	  }
1124	  const row = db
1125	    .query(
1126	      `SELECT superseded_file, COALESCE(want_subtitles,0) + COALESCE(want_thumbnail,0) + COALESCE(want_description,0) AS wants
1127	       FROM jobs WHERE id = ?`,
1128	    )
1129	    .get(jobId) as { superseded_file: string | null; wants: number } | null;
1130	  const backup = row?.superseded_file || null;
1131	  if (!row || !backup || !backup.endsWith(SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX)) return false;
1132	  if (!existsSync(backup)) {
1133	    db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [jobId]);
1134	    return false;
1135	  }
1136	  const original = backup.slice(0, -SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX.length);
1137	  try {
1138	    renameSync(backup, original);
1139	  } catch (err: any) {
1140	    logError("reconcile", `${jobId} could not restore superseded file ${backup}: ${err?.message || err}`);
1141	    return false;
1142	  }
1143	  let size = 0;
1144	  try {
1145	    size = statSync(original).size;
1146	  } catch {}
1147	  // The restored file is the previous pipeline OUTPUT (already converted and
1148	  // in its final location), so conversion is not needed again; sidecars are
1149	  // re-fetched lazily if any are wanted.
1150	  const setClause = `file_path = ?, file_size = ?, superseded_file = NULL,
1151	       download_status = 'downloaded', progress = 100, best_progress = 100,
1152	       partial_file_path = NULL, retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0,
1153	       conversion_status = 'not_needed',
1154	       metadata_status = CASE WHEN ? > 0 THEN 'pending' ELSE 'not_needed' END,
1155	       last_error = ?`;
1156	  const params = [original, size, row.wants, reason] as unknown[];
1157	  if (claim) {
1158	    if (releaseClaimedJob("download", jobId, claim, setClause, params) !== 1) {
1159	      logError("reconcile", `${jobId}: superseded backup restored but the download claim was lost before recording it`);
1160	      return false;
1161	    }
1162	    return true;
1163	  }
1164	  db.run(
1165	    `UPDATE jobs SET ${setClause},
1166	       download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
1167	       download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
1168	       updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1169	    [...params, jobId] as any,
1170	  );
1171	  return true;
1172	}
1173	
1174	/** What `reconcileSupersededFiles` did at startup. */
1175	export interface SupersededReconcileResult {
1176	  /** Interrupted stashes rolled back: the media is back at its output path. */
1177	  restored: number;
1178	  /** Backups deleted because the re-download they guarded already finished. */
1179	  dropped: number;
1180	  /** Stale `superseded_file` pointers forgotten (nothing left to protect). */
1181	  cleared: number;
1182	}
1183	
1184	/**
1185	 * Startup recovery for the `.superseded` hand-off.
1186	 *
1187	 * `stashDownloadedFile` records the backup in the DB before it renames the
1188	 * file, so a crash can leave exactly one recoverable in-between state:
1189	 *
1190	 *   • `superseded_file` set, backup NOT on disk, original still in place —
1191	 *     the rename never ran (or a `renameSync` rollback raced a crash). The row
1192	 *     is put back to "downloaded with its file", so the job is never re-queued
1193	 *     against a file that vanished from the DB's point of view and the old
1194	 *     media is not left unmanaged.
1195	 *
1196	 * Two further states are healed so no backup is ever stranded:
1197	 *
1198	 *   • `superseded_file` set, backup on disk, but the backup belongs to a job
1199	 *     that is still "downloaded" and has no current file — the retry never
1200	 *     became claimable (the crash landed between the stash and the status
1201	 *     update). Rolling the file back restores the exact pre-click state; the
1202	 *     operator can retry again, and nothing re-downloads behind their back.
1203	 *   • `superseded_file` set, backup on disk, and `file_path` already points at
1204	 *     an existing file — the re-download succeeded but the crash hit between
1205	 *     `recordSuccess()` and `dropSupersededFile()`. The new file is the
1206	 *     archive's copy; the backup is deleted.
1207	 *
1208	 * The older, rename-first ordering could also leave the opposite signature —
1209	 * no `superseded_file` recorded, `file_path` pointing at a file that is not
1210	 * there, sitting next to its `.superseded` sibling. Those rows are adopted:
1211	 * the backup is put back where `file_path` says it belongs, so a previous
1212	 * build's crash window cannot turn into a pointless re-download (or a file
1213	 * that is never managed again).
1214	 *
1215	 * Runs before `reconcileMissingFiles`, which would otherwise read the missing
1216	 * `file_path` as "deleted by hand" and re-queue the video.
1217	 */
1218	export function reconcileSupersededFiles(): SupersededReconcileResult {
1219	  const result: SupersededReconcileResult = { restored: 0, dropped: 0, cleared: 0 };
1220	  try {
1221	    const rows = db
1222	      .query(
1223	        `SELECT id, file_path, superseded_file, download_status FROM jobs
1224	          WHERE superseded_file IS NOT NULL OR file_path IS NOT NULL`,
1225	      )
1226	      .all() as any[];
1227	    for (const row of rows) {
1228	      const backup: string | null = row.superseded_file || null;
1229	      const currentFile: string | null = row.file_path && existsSync(row.file_path) ? row.file_path : null;
1230	
1231	      if (backup && backup.endsWith(SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX)) {
1232	        const original = backup.slice(0, -SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX.length);
1233	        if (existsSync(backup)) {
1234	          if (currentFile) {
1235	            // The re-download finished; only the backup's deletion was lost.
1236	            db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [row.id]);
1237	            try {
1238	              unlinkSync(backup);
1239	            } catch {}
1240	            result.dropped++;
1241	          } else if (row.download_status === "downloaded") {
1242	            // The retry was never queued: the job still claims to be finished
1243	            // but its file is the backup. Put it back — the pre-click state.
1244	            if (restoreStashedMedia(row.id, backup, original)) result.restored++;
1245	          }
1246	          // Otherwise the queued/in-flight re-download owns the backup: keep.
1247	          continue;
1248	        }
1249	        if (!currentFile && existsSync(original)) {
1250	          // The intent was recorded but the rename never ran (or a
1251	          // renameSync rollback raced the crash): the file is exactly where
1252	          // the pre-stash row expects it. Put the row back — no filesystem
1253	          // work, nothing to rename.
1254	          rollBackStash(row.id, original);
1255	          result.restored++;
1256	          continue;
1257	        }
1258	        // Nothing on disk to protect any more (backup deleted by hand, or the
1259	        // whole file is gone) — forget the pointer; `reconcileMissingFiles`
1260	        // and the sweep own the rest.
1261	        db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [row.id]);
1262	        result.cleared++;
1263	        continue;
1264	      }
1265	
1266	      // Legacy rename-first crash window: no pointer was recorded, the DB's
1267	      // file_path names a file that is not there, and the `.superseded` sibling
1268	      // is what the interrupted retry left behind.
1269	      if (!backup && row.file_path && !currentFile) {
1270	        const legacyBackup = `${row.file_path}${SUPERSEDED_SUFFIX}`;
1271	        if (existsSync(legacyBackup) && row.download_status === "downloaded") {
1272	          if (restoreStashedMedia(row.id, legacyBackup, row.file_path)) result.restored++;
1273	        }
1274	      }
1275	    }
1276	    if (result.restored + result.dropped + result.cleared > 0) {
1277	      console.log(
1278	        `🧷 Superseded-file recovery: ${result.restored} restored, ${result.dropped} backup(s) dropped, ${result.cleared} stale pointer(s) cleared.`,
1279	      );
1280	    }
1281	  } catch (e: any) {
1282	    logError("reconcile", `superseded recovery: ${e?.message || e}`);
1283	  }
1284	  return result;
1285	}
1286	
1287	/**
1288	 * Forget the interrupted stash in the database only: the media never left its
1289	 * output path, so re-point `file_path` at it and drop the backup pointer.
1290	 */
1291	function rollBackStash(jobId: string, original: string): void {
1292	  let size = 0;
1293	  try {
1294	    size = statSync(original).size;
1295	  } catch {}
1296	  db.run(
1297	    `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = ?, file_size = ?, superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
1298	    [original, size, jobId],
1299	  );
1300	}
1301	
1302	/**
1303	 * Move a `.superseded` backup back to `original` and make the job row describe
1304	 * it again (downloaded, file present, no backup). Used when a re-download
1305	 * never got off the ground, so the archive keeps exactly what it had. Returns
1306	 * false (and logs) when the rename fails — the backup is then left for the
1307	 * next startup and the orphan sweep will not touch it, because the row still
1308	 * references it.
1309	 */
1310	function restoreStashedMedia(jobId: string, backup: string, original: string): boolean {
1311	  // Never clobber a file that appeared at the output path in the meantime.
1312	  if (existsSync(original)) {
1313	    db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET superseded_file = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [jobId]);
1314	    logError(
1315	      "reconcile",
1316	      `${jobId}: both ${original} and its backup ${backup} exist — keeping the output file and forgetting the backup`,
1317	    );
1318	    return false;
1319	  }
1320	  try {
1321	    renameSync(backup, original);
1322	  } catch (err: any) {
1323	    logError("reconcile", `${jobId} could not restore ${backup}: ${err?.message || err}`);
1324	    return false;
1325	  }
1326	  rollBackStash(jobId, original);
1327	  return true;
1328	}

362	             AND metadata_status IN ('done', 'not_needed', 'failed')
363	           ORDER BY created_at, rowid LIMIT 1
364	         )
365	         RETURNING *`,
366	      )
367	      .get(workerId, newClaimToken()) as Job | null;
368	    return row;
369	  });
370	
371	  // Metadata claim — sidecars (subs/thumbnail/description/info.json) for
372	  // finished downloads whose flags say metadata is wanted. The claim records
373	  // its owner, timestamp, token and heartbeat like the other two stages: the
374	  // reaper needs a lease to compare against, and the worker needs a token to
375	  // present on every later update.
376	  claimMetadataJob = db.transaction((workerId: string) => {
377	    const row = db
378	      .query(
379	        `UPDATE jobs SET metadata_status = 'in_progress',
380	           metadata_claimed_by = ?, metadata_claimed_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
381	           metadata_claim_token = ?, metadata_heartbeat_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
382	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
383	         WHERE id = (
384	           SELECT id FROM jobs
385	           WHERE download_status = 'downloaded' AND metadata_status = 'pending'
386	             -- Sidecars are fetched against the media file's path; doing that
387	             -- while the converter is renaming/moving it lands them in the
388	             -- wrong place. A job whose conversion already finished ('done')
389	             -- is still eligible — a failed-then-requeued metadata stage runs
390	             -- after conversion on purpose.
391	             AND COALESCE(conversion_status, '') != 'in_progress'
392	           ORDER BY created_at, rowid LIMIT 1
393	         )
394	         RETURNING *`,
395	      )
396	      .get(workerId, newClaimToken()) as Job | null;
397	    return row;
398	  });
399	}
