401	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
402	// Claim leases: tokens, compare-and-swap updates, heartbeats
403	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
404	
405	/** The three independently claimable pipeline stages. */
406	export type ClaimStage = "download" | "conversion" | "metadata";
407	
408	interface ClaimColumns {
409	  /** Stage status column (`downloading` for downloads, `in_progress` otherwise). */
410	  status: string;
411	  /** Status value that means "this stage is claimed right now". */
412	  claimedStatus: string;
413	  /** Human-readable owner (worker id) column. */
414	  by: string;
415	  /** Claim timestamp column. */
416	  at: string;
417	  /** Random per-claim token column. */
418	  token: string;
419	  /** Lease heartbeat column, renewed while the stage runs. */
420	  heartbeat: string;
421	}
422	
423	const CLAIM_COLUMNS: Record<ClaimStage, ClaimColumns> = {
424	  download: {
425	    status: "download_status",
426	    claimedStatus: "downloading",
427	    by: "download_claimed_by",
428	    at: "download_claimed_at",
429	    token: "download_claim_token",
430	    heartbeat: "download_heartbeat_at",
431	  },
432	  conversion: {
433	    status: "conversion_status",
434	    claimedStatus: "in_progress",
435	    by: "conversion_claimed_by",
436	    at: "conversion_claimed_at",
437	    token: "conversion_claim_token",
438	    heartbeat: "conversion_heartbeat_at",
439	  },
440	  metadata: {
441	    status: "metadata_status",
442	    claimedStatus: "in_progress",
443	    by: "metadata_claimed_by",
444	    at: "metadata_claimed_at",
445	    token: "metadata_claim_token",
446	    heartbeat: "metadata_heartbeat_at",
447	  },
448	};
449	
450	/** Column names for one stage's claim — the single source of truth. */
451	export function claimColumns(stage: ClaimStage): ClaimColumns {
452	  return CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
453	}
454	
455	/** A claim's identity: what a CAS update matches against. */
456	export interface ClaimRef {
457	  by: string | null;
458	  token: string | null;
459	}
460	
461	/**
462	 * The claim coordinates of a row, for passing to `updateClaimedJob`.
463	 *
464	 * `null`/`null` (no token, no owner) is the legacy claim written by an engine
465	 * version that predated tokens; it is still updatable, and the reaper may take
466	 * it over once its `*_claimed_at` ages out — exactly like before.
467	 */
468	export function claimRef(stage: ClaimStage, row: Record<string, unknown> | Job): ClaimRef {
469	  const c = CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
470	  const r = row as Record<string, unknown>;
471	  return {
472	    by: (r[c.by] as string | null | undefined) ?? null,
473	    token: (r[c.token] as string | null | undefined) ?? null,
474	  };
475	}
476	
477	/**
478	 * A fresh, unique claim token.
479	 *
480	 * Worker ids (`dl-1`, `cv-2`) are positional and repeat across processes: a
481	 * worker restarted in a second engine process looks like the first one. The
482	 * token is what actually identifies a claim, so a stale worker's late update
483	 * cannot be mistaken for the live owner's.
484	 */
485	export function newClaimToken(): string {
486	  return crypto.randomUUID();
487	}
488	
489	/** How often a claimed stage renews its lease (test override: YTA_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_MS). */
490	export function claimHeartbeatMs(): number {
491	  const override = Number(process.env.YTA_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_MS);
492	  return Number.isFinite(override) && override > 0 ? override : 30_000;
493	}
494	
495	/**
496	 * Compare-and-swap an update on a claimed job.
497	 *
498	 * The row is touched only when `claim` still identifies its live claim, so a
499	 * worker (or reaper) whose claim was reaped, released, or taken over by another
500	 * process cannot change job state: it gets 0 changed rows and must walk away.
501	 * The caller checks the result — `1` means the update landed.
502	 *
503	 * `extraCondition` is appended to the WHERE clause for callers that need an
504	 * additional precondition (e.g. reaping only a lease that has actually
505	 * expired, or a user pause that is still recorded).
506	 */
507	export function updateClaimedJob(
508	  stage: ClaimStage,
509	  jobId: string,
510	  claim: ClaimRef,
511	  setClause: string,
512	  params: unknown[] = [],
513	  extraCondition?: string,
514	): number {
515	  const c = CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
516	  const extra = extraCondition ? ` AND (${extraCondition})` : "";
517	  return db.run(
518	    `UPDATE jobs SET ${setClause} WHERE id = ? AND ${c.token} IS ? AND ${c.by} IS ?${extra}`,
519	    [...params, jobId, claim.token, claim.by] as any,
520	  ).changes;
521	}
522	
523	/**
524	 * The release flavour of `updateClaimedJob`: the matched claim is cleared in
525	 * the same statement that writes the new state, so a job is never left with a
526	 * status that says "finished" while a claim still points at a worker that is
527	 * gone (or worse, while a *new* owner's claim is overwritten).
528	 */
529	export function releaseClaimedJob(
530	  stage: ClaimStage,
531	  jobId: string,
532	  claim: ClaimRef,
533	  setClause: string,
534	  params: unknown[] = [],
535	  extraCondition?: string,
536	): number {
537	  const c = CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
538	  const release = [
539	    `${c.by} = NULL`,
540	    `${c.at} = NULL`,
541	    `${c.token} = NULL`,
542	    `${c.heartbeat} = NULL`,
543	    "updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP",
544	  ].join(", ");
545	  const set = [setClause, release].filter((s) => s && s.trim().length > 0).join(", ");
546	  return updateClaimedJob(stage, jobId, claim, set, params, extraCondition);
547	}
548	
549	/**
550	 * Renew a claim's lease. Returns false when the claim is no longer ours, which
551	 * the worker's heartbeat callback reports — the ownership checks and CAS
552	 * updates then keep it from touching anything the new owner controls.
553	 */
554	export function heartbeatClaim(stage: ClaimStage, jobId: string, claim: ClaimRef): boolean {
555	  const c = CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
556	  return (
557	    db.run(
558	      `UPDATE jobs SET ${c.heartbeat} = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
559	        WHERE id = ? AND ${c.token} IS ? AND ${c.by} IS ? AND ${c.status} = ?`,
560	      [jobId, claim.token, claim.by, c.claimedStatus] as any,
561	    ).changes === 1
562	  );
563	}
564	
565	/** Is this claim still the live owner of the stage on this row? */
566	export function ownsClaim(stage: ClaimStage, jobId: string, claim: ClaimRef): boolean {
567	  const c = CLAIM_COLUMNS[stage];
568	  return !!db
569	    .query(
570	      `SELECT 1 FROM jobs
571	        WHERE id = ? AND ${c.token} IS ? AND ${c.by} IS ? AND ${c.status} = ? LIMIT 1`,
572	    )
573	    .get(jobId, claim.token, claim.by, c.claimedStatus);
574	}
575	
576	/**
577	 * Keep a claim's lease alive while its stage runs, so the reaper can tell a
578	 * long conversion or metadata fetch apart from a dead worker.
579	 *
580	 * Returns the stop function — every caller must stop it when the stage ends,
581	 * including on failure, or the heartbeat would keep renewing a claim whose
582	 * outcome was already written.
583	 *
584	 * `onLost` fires AT MOST ONCE. A worker releases its own claim in the same
585	 * statement that records the outcome (retry re-queue, park-as-failed, success),
586	 * and then usually sleeps for the backoff *inside* the try-block — so the timer
587	 * outlives the claim by design and every later tick would find a dead lease.
588	 * Reporting that per tick printed one alarming
589	 * "download claim lost — the next update will not land" line every heartbeat
590	 * interval per retrying video, which buried the real error in error.log while
591	 * saying nothing the release had not already recorded.
592	 */
593	export function startClaimHeartbeat(
594	  stage: ClaimStage,
595	  jobId: string,
596	  claim: ClaimRef,
597	  onLost?: () => void,
598	  intervalMs: number = claimHeartbeatMs(),
599	): () => void {
600	  let lostReported = false;
601	  const timer = setInterval(() => {
602	    try {
603	      if (heartbeatClaim(stage, jobId, claim)) return;
604	    } catch {
605	      // The database can be mid-shutdown; the CAS updates are the real guard.
606	      return;
607	    }
608	    if (lostReported || !onLost) return;
609	    lostReported = true;
610	    // A lost lease is never renewed again: firing the callback on every later
611	    // tick would only repeat a fact the release already recorded.
612	    onLost();
613	  }, Math.max(250, intervalMs));
614	  // A heartbeat must never keep a shutting-down process alive.
615	  (timer as unknown as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
616	  return () => clearInterval(timer);
617	}
618	
619	/** Per-video failure cap: the smaller of the two knobs, so both stay honest. */
620	export function perVideoCap(config: Config): number {
621	  return Math.min(config.maxRetryAttempts, config.maxFailuresPerVideo);
622	}
623	
624	export function isVideoInDb(videoId: string): boolean {
625	  return !!db.query("SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(videoId);
626	}
627	
628	export function isVideoIgnored(videoId: string): boolean {
629	  return !!db.query("SELECT 1 FROM ignored_videos WHERE video_id = ? LIMIT 1").get(videoId);
630	}
631	
632	export interface IgnoredVideo {
633	  video_id: string;
634	  url: string;
635	  title: string;
636	  source_urls: string[];
637	  ignored_at: string;
638	}
639	
640	/**
641	 * Atomically remember explicitly deleted videos and remove their queue rows.
642	 * Source ownership is copied before the FK cascade removes job_sources. The
643	 * ignored tombstones then outlive both the job rows and engine restarts.
644	 */
645	export function deleteJobsAndIgnore(ids: Iterable<string>): { deleted: number; ignored: number } {
646	  const uniqueIds = [...new Set([...ids].filter((id): id is string => typeof id === "string" && id.length > 0))];
647	  if (uniqueIds.length === 0) return { deleted: 0, ignored: 0 };
648	  const placeholders = uniqueIds.map(() => "?").join(",");
649	  const deleteAndIgnore = db.transaction((batch: string[]) => {
650	    const jobs = db
651	      .query(`SELECT id, url, title FROM jobs WHERE id IN (${placeholders})`)
652	      .all(...batch) as { id: string; url: string | null; title: string | null }[];
653	    if (jobs.length === 0) return { deleted: 0, ignored: 0 };
654	
655	    const sourceQuery = db.prepare("SELECT source_url FROM job_sources WHERE job_id = ? ORDER BY source_url");
656	    const ignore = db.prepare(
657	      `INSERT INTO ignored_videos (video_id, url, title, source_urls, ignored_at)
658	       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
659	       ON CONFLICT(video_id) DO UPDATE SET
660	         url = excluded.url,
661	         title = excluded.title,
662	         source_urls = excluded.source_urls,
663	         ignored_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`,
664	    );
665	    for (const job of jobs) {
666	      const sources = sourceQuery.all(job.id) as { source_url: string }[];
667	      ignore.run(
668	        job.id,
669	        job.url || `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=${job.id}`,
670	        job.title || job.id,
671	        JSON.stringify(sources.map((source) => source.source_url)),
672	      );
673	    }
674	    db.run(`DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id IN (${placeholders})`, batch);
675	    // SQLite may include cascaded job_sources rows in `changes`; count the
676	    // selected job rows instead so the API reports videos, not FK side effects.
677	    return { deleted: jobs.length, ignored: jobs.length };
678	  });
679	  return deleteAndIgnore(uniqueIds);
680	}
681	
682	export function listIgnoredVideos(limit = 500): IgnoredVideo[] {
683	  const cappedLimit = Math.max(1, Math.min(1000, Math.floor(limit)));
684	  const rows = db
685	    .query(
686	      `SELECT video_id, url, title, source_urls, ignored_at
687	         FROM ignored_videos ORDER BY ignored_at DESC, video_id LIMIT ?`,
688	    )
689	    .all(cappedLimit) as {
690	      video_id: string;
691	      url: string;
692	      title: string;
693	      source_urls: string;
694	      ignored_at: string;
695	    }[];
696	  return rows.map((row) => {
697	    let sourceUrls: string[] = [];
698	    try {
699	      const parsed = JSON.parse(row.source_urls);
700	      if (Array.isArray(parsed)) sourceUrls = parsed.filter((url): url is string => typeof url === "string");
701	    } catch {
702	      // A malformed legacy value must not break the ignored-jobs panel.
703	    }
704	    return { ...row, source_urls: sourceUrls };
705	  });
706	}
707	
708	/** Remove a tombstone so future playlist scans may enqueue the video again. */
709	export function allowIgnoredVideo(videoId: string): number {
710	  return db.run("DELETE FROM ignored_videos WHERE video_id = ?", [videoId]).changes;
711	}
712	
713	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
714	// Secondary-storage relocation
715	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
716	//
717	// A job's finished media can be in the output tree even though no conversion
718	// will ever claim it again: it was converted by an earlier version, its
719	// conversion finished before secondary storage was configured, or the engine
720	// crashed between the copy and the database update. These helpers are the
721	// single source of truth for "does this file still need to move?".
722	//
723	// `relocated_to` stores the secondary-storage ROOT (not a boolean), so a job
724	// relocated to the old root becomes eligible again when the operator points
725	// `secondaryStoragePath` somewhere new — while a file that already sits under
726	// the configured root is never moved onto itself.
727	
728	/** One relocation candidate, as the pass needs it. */
729	export interface RelocationRow {
730	  id: string;
731	  title: string;
732	  folder: string;
733	  file_path: string;
734	  relocated_to: string | null;
735	}
736	
737	/**
738	 * The SQL predicate behind every relocation check: a finished, converted
739	 * download whose media is not (yet) recorded under the given root.
740	 *
741	 * `metadata_status = 'in_progress'` is excluded on purpose — the sidecar pass
742	 * writes files next to the media, and moving it out from under that writer
743	 * would leave the sidecars behind in the output tree.
744	 */
745	const RELOCATION_WHERE = `
746	  download_status = 'downloaded'
747	  AND file_path IS NOT NULL AND file_path != ''
748	  AND conversion_status IN ('done', 'not_needed')
749	  AND COALESCE(metadata_status, 'not_needed') != 'in_progress'
750	  AND (relocated_to IS NULL OR relocated_to != ?)`;
751	
752	/** Every job whose media still has to reach secondary storage, oldest first. */
753	export function listJobsAwaitingRelocation(secondaryStoragePath: string): RelocationRow[] {
754	  return db
755	    .query(
756	      `SELECT id, title, folder, file_path, relocated_to FROM jobs
757	        WHERE ${RELOCATION_WHERE}
758	        ORDER BY created_at, rowid`,
759	    )
760	    .all(secondaryStoragePath) as RelocationRow[];
761	}
762	
763	/** How many files are still waiting to move (dashboard / startup status). */
764	export function countJobsAwaitingRelocation(secondaryStoragePath: string): number {
765	  const row = db
766	    .query(`SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM jobs WHERE ${RELOCATION_WHERE}`)
767	    .get(secondaryStoragePath) as { n: number } | null;
768	  return row?.n ?? 0;
769	}
770	
771	/** Does this one job still need its file relocated? (re-checked mid-move) */
772	export function jobAwaitingRelocation(jobId: string, secondaryStoragePath: string): boolean {
773	  return !!db
774	    .query(`SELECT 1 FROM jobs WHERE id = ? AND ${RELOCATION_WHERE} LIMIT 1`)
775	    .get(jobId, secondaryStoragePath);
776	}
777	
778	/**
779	 * Record where a job's media now lives. Compare-and-swaps on the OLD path so a
780	 * job whose `file_path` changed meanwhile (re-downloaded, manually retried,
781	 * deleted) is never pointed at a file this pass did not put there.
782	 *
783	 * Used both for the move and for crash-window adoption: a file that already
784	 * sits in secondary storage because the previous run died between the copy and
785	 * this update is adopted with the same call.
786	 *
787	 * Returns the number of rows changed (0 = somebody else owns this row now).
788	 */
789	export function recordRelocatedFile(
790	  jobId: string,
791	  previousPath: string,
792	  newPath: string,
793	  relocatedTo: string,
794	): number {
795	  return db.run(
796	    `UPDATE jobs SET file_path = ?, relocated_to = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
797	      WHERE id = ? AND file_path = ?`,
798	    [newPath, relocatedTo, jobId, previousPath],
799	  ).changes;
800	}
801	
802	/** Backfill legacy jobs from a source listing before that source is removed. */
803	export function associateExistingJobsWithSource(sourceUrl: string, videoIds: Iterable<string>): number {
804	  const ids = [...new Set([...videoIds].filter(Boolean))];
805	  if (ids.length === 0) return 0;
806	  const associate = db.transaction((batch: string[]) => {
807	    const stmt = db.prepare(
808	      `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO job_sources (source_url, job_id)
809	       SELECT ?, id FROM jobs WHERE id = ?`,
810	    );
811	    let associated = 0;
812	    for (const id of batch) associated += stmt.run(sourceUrl, id).changes;
813	    return associated;
814	  });
815	  return associate(ids);
816	}
817	
818	export interface SourceJobCleanup {
819	  /** Jobs that had a recorded association with the removed/stale source. */
820	  affectedJobs: number;
821	  /** Jobs deleted because no remaining configured source needs them. */
822	  deletedJobs: number;
823	  /** Shared jobs retained for another configured source. */
824	  retainedJobs: number;
825	}
826	
827	/**
828	 * Remove a source's ownership links and delete its now-unowned jobs. A video
829	 * still referenced by another configured source remains in the queue.
830	 */
831	export function removeSourceJobsFromDatabase(
832	  sourceUrl: string,
833	  activeSourceUrls: Iterable<string>,
834	): SourceJobCleanup {
835	  const activeSources = new Set(activeSourceUrls);
836	  const cleanup = db.transaction(() => {
837	    const rows = db
838	      .query("SELECT job_id FROM job_sources WHERE source_url = ?")
839	      .all(sourceUrl) as { job_id: string }[];
840	    db.run("DELETE FROM job_sources WHERE source_url = ?", [sourceUrl]);
841	    return cleanupUnownedSourceJobs(new Set(rows.map((row) => row.job_id)), activeSources);
842	  });
843	  return cleanup();
844	}
845	
846	/**
847	 * Startup safety net for sources removed by editing config.json directly.
848	 * Only jobs that were previously source-tracked are candidates; legacy/manual
849	 * jobs without ownership metadata are left alone rather than guessed at.
850	 */
851	export function pruneJobsForUnconfiguredSources(activeSourceUrls: Iterable<string>): SourceJobCleanup {
852	  const activeSources = new Set(activeSourceUrls);
853	  const cleanup = db.transaction(() => {
854	    const links = db.query("SELECT source_url, job_id FROM job_sources").all() as {
855	      source_url: string;
856	      job_id: string;
857	    }[];
858	    const staleLinks = links.filter((link) => !activeSources.has(link.source_url));
859	    const affected = new Set(staleLinks.map((link) => link.job_id));
860	    for (const link of staleLinks) {
861	      db.run("DELETE FROM job_sources WHERE source_url = ? AND job_id = ?", [link.source_url, link.job_id]);
862	    }
863	    return cleanupUnownedSourceJobs(affected, activeSources);
864	  });
865	  return cleanup();
866	}
867	
868	/** Must be called from inside a transaction. */
869	function cleanupUnownedSourceJobs(jobIds: Set<string>, activeSources: Set<string>): SourceJobCleanup {
870	  let deletedJobs = 0;
871	  let retainedJobs = 0;
872	  for (const jobId of jobIds) {
873	    const links = db.query("SELECT source_url FROM job_sources WHERE job_id = ?").all(jobId) as {
874	      source_url: string;
875	    }[];
876	    // Drop stale links too, so a missing/manual config entry cannot keep a
877	    // deleted source's job alive indefinitely.
878	    for (const link of links) {
879	      if (!activeSources.has(link.source_url)) {
880	        db.run("DELETE FROM job_sources WHERE source_url = ? AND job_id = ?", [link.source_url, jobId]);
881	      }
882	    }
883	    const stillNeeded = db.query("SELECT 1 FROM job_sources WHERE job_id = ? LIMIT 1").get(jobId);
884	    if (stillNeeded) retainedJobs++;
885	    else deletedJobs += db.run("DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id = ?", [jobId]).changes;
886	  }
887	  return { affectedJobs: jobIds.size, deletedJobs, retainedJobs };
888	}
889	
890	/**
891	 * The playlist index a video will get, reserved for metadata fetched before its
892	 * download job exists. Returns the same number on every call for the same
893	 * video, so repeated metadata runs keep the same names.
894	 */
895	export function reserveFileIndex(folder: string, id: string): number {
896	  const row = db
897	    .query("SELECT idx FROM metadata_name_reservations WHERE folder = ? AND id = ?")
898	    .get(folder, id) as { idx: number } | null;
899	  if (row) return row.idx;
900	  const idx = getNextIndex(folder);
901	  db.run("INSERT INTO metadata_name_reservations (folder, id, idx) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [folder, id, idx]);
902	  return idx;
903	}
904	
905	/** Take back (and forget) the index reserved for a video that is being queued as a job. */
906	export function takeReservedFileIndex(folder: string, id: string): number | null {
907	  const row = db
908	    .query("SELECT idx FROM metadata_name_reservations WHERE folder = ? AND id = ?")
909	    .get(folder, id) as { idx: number } | null;
910	  if (!row) return null;
911	  db.run("DELETE FROM metadata_name_reservations WHERE folder = ? AND id = ?", [folder, id]);
912	  return row.idx;
913	}
914	
915	export function getNextIndex(folder: string): number {
916	  const row = db.query("SELECT next_index FROM playlist_state WHERE folder = ?").get(folder) as
917	    | { next_index: number }
918	    | null;
919	  const next = (row?.next_index || 0) + 1;
920	  db.run(
921	    `INSERT INTO playlist_state (folder, next_index) VALUES (?, ?)
922	     ON CONFLICT(folder) DO UPDATE SET next_index = excluded.next_index`,
923	    [folder, next],
924	  );
925	  return next;
926	}

4	// covers "downloaded, then converted, then moved in one go" — but not the files
5	// that need no conversion at all:
6	//
7	//   • a file already in the target format (the converter claims it, finds
8	//     nothing to encode, and finalizes — fine while a download/conversion is
9	//     still pending, but nothing ever revisits it once it is 'done');
10	//   • the whole existing archive on the day `secondaryStoragePath` is set;
11	//   • a conversion that finished before secondary storage was configured;
12	//   • a run that died between the copy and the database update.
13	//
14	// Offline mode is where that gap hurts most: downloads are off, metadata needs
15	// the network, so conversion and relocation are the only useful work left. This
16	// pass is that second half — for every finished job whose media is not (yet)
17	// recorded under the configured secondary storage root: adopt it if it is
18	// already there, otherwise move it and record where it went.
19	//
20	// Why there is no claim token here, unlike every other pipeline stage:
21	//   • the engine lease guarantees exactly ONE engine owns `archive.db`
22	//     (src/lease.ts), and this module keeps exactly one pass in flight per
23	//     process (see `relocationTick`), so no two movers can ever race each other;
24	//   • every step is idempotent and converges — `isPathInside` recognises a file
25	//     that already sits under the root, `jobAwaitingRelocation` re-checks the
26	//     row before each destructive step (sidecars first, media last, the same
27	//     order the converter uses), and a crash between the copy and the update is
28	//     healed by the adoption branch below;
29	//   • the final update compare-and-swaps on the OLD path, so a job that was
30	//     re-downloaded, retried, or deleted meanwhile is never pointed at a file
31	//     this pass did not put there.
32	
33	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
34	import { basename, join } from "node:path";
35	import {
36	  countJobsAwaitingRelocation,
37	  jobAwaitingRelocation,
38	  listJobsAwaitingRelocation,
39	  recordRelocatedFile,
40	  type RelocationRow,
41	} from "./db";
42	import { logError } from "./logger";
43	import { isPathInside } from "./util";
44	import { moveToSecondaryStorage } from "./workers/convert";
45	import { holdsEngineLease } from "./lease";
46	import { getConfig, isPaused } from "./state";

49	/**
50	 * How long a job waits after a failed move before it is tried again. Moving to
51	 * a NAS that is unplugged/full must not retry every 60 seconds forever, and a
52	 * per-job backoff keeps one bad destination from starving the rest of the
53	 * queue. In-memory on purpose: a restart is the operator's signal that the
54	 * destination is worth another try.
55	 */
56	const RETRY_BASE_MS = 60_000;
57	const RETRY_MAX_MS = 60 * 60_000;
58	
59	const failureBackoff = new Map<string, { attempts: number; until: number }>();
60	
61	/** What one pass did (returned for tests and for the startup/tick summary). */
62	export interface RelocationReport {
63	  /** Files moved into secondary storage by this pass. */
64	  moved: number;
65	  /** Files that were already there — the database path was corrected. */
66	  adopted: number;
67	  /** Files already sitting under the configured root (nothing to do). */
68	  alreadyThere: number;
69	  /** Candidates skipped this pass (backoff, or the row changed underneath). */
70	  skipped: number;
71	  /** Moves that failed — the source file is untouched and the job retries. */
72	  failed: number;
73	}
74	
75	/** How many files are still waiting to move (0 when no secondary storage is set). */
76	export function relocationPendingCount(config: Pick<Config, "secondaryStoragePath">): number {
77	  if (!config.secondaryStoragePath) return 0;
78	  try {
79	    return countJobsAwaitingRelocation(config.secondaryStoragePath);
80	  } catch {
81	    // The database can be mid-shutdown; a status query must never throw.
82	    return 0;
83	  }
84	}
85	
86	/** Forget the per-job failure backoff (used by tests after a forced failure). */
87	export function resetRelocationBackoff(): void {
88	  failureBackoff.clear();
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * One relocation pass: every finished job whose media has to reach secondary
93	 * storage, oldest first, moved one at a time.
94	 *
95	 * Sequential on purpose — the pass is I/O bound, and a single mover per
96	 * database is what removes the need for claim tokens here.
97	 */
98	export async function relocateFinishedJobs(config: Config): Promise<RelocationReport> {
99	  const report: RelocationReport = { moved: 0, adopted: 0, alreadyThere: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0 };
100	  const root = (config.secondaryStoragePath || "").trim();
101	  // No destination configured: nothing "needs" moving, so the pass is a no-op.
102	  if (!root) return report;
103	
104	  let candidates: RelocationRow[];
105	  try {
106	    candidates = listJobsAwaitingRelocation(root);
107	  } catch (e: any) {
108	    logError("relocation", `could not list files awaiting secondary storage: ${e?.message || e}`);
109	    return report;
110	  }
111	
112	  for (const job of candidates) {
113	    const now = Date.now();
114	    if ((failureBackoff.get(job.id)?.until ?? 0) > now) {
115	      report.skipped++;
116	      continue;
117	    }
118	    // Re-check against the live row: the listed snapshot may be stale (the job
119	    // could have been deleted, re-downloaded, or already relocated).
120	    if (!jobAwaitingRelocation(job.id, root)) {
121	      report.skipped++;
122	      continue;
123	    }
124	
125	    let outcome: "moved" | "adopted" | "already" | "skipped" | "failed";
126	    try {
127	      outcome = await relocateOne(job, root);
128	    } catch (e: any) {
129	      outcome = "failed";
130	      logError(
131	        "relocation",
132	        `${job.id} ${job.title}: could not move to secondary storage (${e?.message || e}) — the file stays where it is`,
133	      );
134	    }
135	
136	    if (outcome === "failed") {
137	      report.failed++;
138	      recordFailure(job.id);
139	    } else {
140	      failureBackoff.delete(job.id);
141	      if (outcome === "moved") report.moved++;
142	      else if (outcome === "adopted") report.adopted++;
143	      else if (outcome === "already") report.alreadyThere++;
144	      else report.skipped++;
145	    }
146	  }
147	  return report;
148	}
149	
150	/** Move (or adopt) one job's media and its sidecars. */
151	async function relocateOne(
152	  job: RelocationRow,
153	  root: string,
154	): Promise<"moved" | "adopted" | "already" | "skipped"> {
155	  const currentPath = job.file_path;
156	
157	  if (!existsSync(currentPath)) {
158	    // Crash-window recovery / hand-moved file: the media is not where the
159	    // database says it is, but the destination of this very move is exactly
160	    // where it should be. Adopt that file instead of failing on a path that no
161	    // longer exists — the alternative is a job that can never finish.
162	    const expected = join(root, job.folder, basename(currentPath));
163	    if (!existsSync(expected)) {
164	      // Nothing was moved by us: a genuinely missing file belongs to
165	      // reconcileMissingFiles / the download stage, not to relocation.
166	      return "skipped";
167	    }
168	    if (recordRelocatedFile(job.id, currentPath, expected, root) === 0) return "skipped";
169	    logError("relocation", `${job.id} ${job.title}: file already in secondary storage — adopted ${expected}`);
170	    return "adopted";
171	  }
172	
173	  if (isPathInside(currentPath, root)) {
174	    // Already under the configured root (moved by hand, or by an engine version
175	    // that predates `relocated_to`): record it and never move it onto itself.
176	    recordRelocatedFile(job.id, currentPath, currentPath, root);
177	    return "already";
178	  }
179	
180	  // The converter's own move, reused wholesale: sidecars first in a pinned
181	  // order, media last, `required` — a media file that cannot land in secondary
182	  // storage throws instead of reporting success against the wrong path. Every
183	  // destructive step re-checks that this job still wants moving: a job deleted
184	  // or re-queued mid-move stops the sequence before the next file is touched.
185	  const moved = await moveToSecondaryStorage(job, root, currentPath, () =>
186	    jobAwaitingRelocation(job.id, root),
187	  );
188	  if (moved.stopped) return "skipped";
189	  if (moved.path === currentPath) {
190	    // The move refused to do anything (destination equals source). Record what
191	    // we know rather than reporting a move that did not happen.
192	    recordRelocatedFile(job.id, currentPath, currentPath, root);
193	    return "already";
194	  }
195	  if (recordRelocatedFile(job.id, currentPath, moved.path, root) === 0) {
196	    // The row changed while the bytes moved — a re-download or a dashboard
197	    // delete took ownership. The files are in secondary storage; the new state
198	    // is not ours to overwrite.
199	    return "skipped";
200	  }
201	  return "moved";
202	}
203	
204	function recordFailure(jobId: string): void {
205	  const previous = failureBackoff.get(jobId);
206	  const attempts = (previous?.attempts ?? 0) + 1;
207	  const delay = Math.min(RETRY_BASE_MS * 2 ** (attempts - 1), RETRY_MAX_MS);
208	  failureBackoff.set(jobId, { attempts, until: Date.now() + delay });
209	}
210	
211	// One pass at a time: the interval below must never overlap itself, and a
212	// second mover inside one process is exactly what the claim-free design
213	// assumes cannot happen.
214	let passInFlight = false;
215	
216	/**
217	 * Interval driver: run a pass unless one is already running, and report the
218	 * outcome only when it did something worth a log line.
219	 */
220	export async function relocationTick(config: Config = getConfig()): Promise<void> {
221	  if (passInFlight) return;
222	  // Paused means paused for every stage, this one included — and that includes
223	  // the pause an engine-lease loss triggers: another engine may own `archive.db`
224	  // by then, and two movers are exactly what this pass's claim-free design
225	  // assumes cannot happen.
226	  if (isPaused() || !holdsEngineLease()) return;
227	  passInFlight = true;
228	  try {
229	    const report = await relocateFinishedJobs(config);
230	    const changed = report.moved + report.adopted + report.failed;
231	    if (changed > 0) {
232	      const remaining = relocationPendingCount(config);
233	      console.log(
234	        `📦 Secondary storage: moved ${report.moved}, adopted ${report.adopted}, failed ${report.failed}${remaining > 0 ? `, ${remaining} still pending` : ""}.`,
235	      );
236	    }
237	  } catch (e: any) {
238	    logError("relocation", `pass failed: ${e?.stack || e?.message || e}`);
239	  } finally {
240	    passInFlight = false;
241	  }
242	}
243	
244	/** How long between two passes. Each pass drains the whole queue it can move. */
245	const RELOCATION_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000;
246	
247	/**
248	 * Start the relocation pass: one shortly after startup (there is no reason to
249	 * wait a minute for files the operator already queued up), then on an interval.
250	 *
251	 * The live config is re-read on every tick, so turning secondary storage on
252	 * from the dashboard is picked up without a restart.
253	 */
254	export function startRelocation(): void {
255	  const config = getConfig();
256	  if (config.secondaryStoragePath) {
257	    const pending = relocationPendingCount(config);
258	    console.log(
259	      `📦 Secondary storage: ${config.secondaryStoragePath}${pending > 0 ? ` — ${pending} file(s) waiting to move` : " — nothing pending"}`,
260	    );
261	  }
262	  setTimeout(() => void relocationTick(getConfig()), 5_000);
263	  const timer = setInterval(() => void relocationTick(getConfig()), RELOCATION_INTERVAL_MS);
264	  // A timer must never keep a shutting-down process alive.
265	  (timer as unknown as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
266	}

78	function presentedWebTokens(req: Request, url: URL): string[] {

89	    } catch {

91	    }

94	  if (query) tokens.push(query.trim());
95	  return tokens.filter(Boolean);
96	}

221	 *
222	 * Bun's default is 10 s, and any handler that has not answered by then gets its

226	 *   to configure.
227	 *
228	 * That message is printed at most once per process and (in some Bun 1.4 builds)
229	 * only when stderr is flushed at exit, which is why operators report it while
230	 * pressing Ctrl+C rather than when the request actually died. Ten seconds is
231	 * far too short here: a playlist scan or a cookie export takes minutes, and the
232	 * dashboard then reported a network error for work that was still running
233	 * server-side.
234	 *
235	 * Passing `idleTimeout` explicitly also stops Bun from installing the warning
236	 * handler at all (its `should_add_timeout_handler_for_warning` is false once
237	 * the option is present), so the message cannot come back. Handlers that
238	 * legitimately outlive this value declare `deadlineSeconds` in the route table.

248	  timeout(request: Request, seconds: number): void;

251	export function startWebServer(port: number, config: Config, hostname: string = config.webBind || "127.0.0.1") {

253	    // LAN-safe default: listen on loopback unless webBind is explicitly set
254	    // (e.g. 0.0.0.0 to reach the UI from other devices on the LAN).
255	    port,
256	    hostname,
257	    idleTimeout: WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
258	    async fetch(req, server) {
259	      // Every request is wrapped: a handler crash returns JSON 500 instead of
260	      // hanging the socket, and the error lands in error.log.
261	      try {
262	        // Read the live config, not the one captured at startup: settings
263	        // changed from the dashboard (POST /api/settings) must be reflected by
264	        // every endpoint immediately, and setConfig() replaces the object.
265	        return await handleRequest(req, getConfig(), server);
266	      } catch (e: any) {
267	        logError("http", `${req.method} ${new URL(req.url).pathname}: ${e?.stack || e}`);
268	        return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Internal server error" }, { status: 500 });
269	      }
270	    },
271	  });
272	}

274	export async function handleRequest(
275	  req: Request,
276	  config: Config,
277	  server?: RequestDeadlineServer | null,
278	): Promise<Response> {
279	  const url = new URL(req.url);
280	
281	  if (!isSameOriginMutation(req, url)) {
282	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Cross-origin mutations are not allowed" }, { status: 403 });
283	  }
284	
285	  if (url.pathname === "/") {
286	    const queryToken = url.searchParams.get("token");
287	    const expected = effectiveWebToken(config);
288	    const validQueryToken = !!queryToken && !!expected && timingSafeEq(queryToken.trim(), expected);
289	    if (expected && !isAuthorized(req, url, config)) {
290	      // Missing/wrong token → the sign-in page (401 so browsers don't treat it
291	      // as the real app). Sign-in itself exchanges credentials via POST and
292	      // never puts the token in the address bar.
293	      return new Response(LOGIN_PAGE, {
294	        status: 401,
295	        headers: {
296	          "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
297	          "Cache-Control": "no-store",
298	          "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
299	        },
300	      });
301	    }
302	    if (existsSync("./web_ui.html")) {
303	      const headers: Record<string, string> = {
304	        "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
305	        "Cache-Control": "no-store",
306	        "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
307	      };
308	      // Keep the documented query-token compatibility path, but only a query
309	      // token that actually matches the configured secret may replace a cookie.
310	      if (validQueryToken) headers["Set-Cookie"] = tokenCookie(queryToken!.trim(), url);
311	      return new Response(Bun.file("./web_ui.html"), { headers });
312	    }
313	    return new Response("web_ui.html not found. Please create it.", { status: 500 });
314	  }
315	
316	  // Sign-in exchange is the only unauthenticated mutation endpoint. All other
317	  // API routes (pause/resume, purge, delete, ...) remain behind the auth gate.
318	  if (url.pathname === "/api/auth") {
319	    if (req.method !== "POST") {
320	      return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Method not allowed" }, { status: 405, headers: { Allow: "POST" } });
321	    }
322	    return exchangeToken(req, config, url);
323	  }
324	
325	  // Every API route (status, scan, pause/resume, purge, delete, ...) is gated
326	  // behind the token too — purge/delete are destructive.
327	  if (!isAuthorized(req, url, config)) {
328	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Unauthorized — token required" }, { status: 401 });
329	  }
330	
331	  // Collapse trailing slashes so /api/jobs/ and /api/jobs are the same route
332	  // (the root "/" is handled above).
333	  const pathname = url.pathname.length > 1 ? url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, "") : url.pathname;
334	  return handleApi(req, config, url, pathname, server);
335	}

337	// --- API routing --------------------------------------------------------------
338	// A route table instead of an if-chain: patterns support `:param` segments,
339	// every response shares the `{ok, ...}` envelope, unknown API paths get a JSON
340	// 404, and a known path with the wrong method gets a JSON 405 (+ Allow).
341	//
342	// Legacy action paths stay alive as aliases of the canonical per-job routes so
343	// existing bookmarks, scripts, and older dashboards keep working:
344	//   POST /api/retry/:id             → POST /api/jobs/:id/retry
345	//   POST /api/failcount/reset/:id   → POST /api/jobs/:id/reset-failures
346	//   POST /api/jobs/delete {ids}     → DELETE /api/jobs {ids}
347	
348	type RouteParams = Record<string, string>;
349	type RouteHandler = (ctx: {
350	  req: Request;
351	  config: Config;
352	  url: URL;
353	  params: RouteParams;
354	}) => Response | Promise<Response>;
355	
356	interface Route {
357	  methods: string[];
358	  pattern: string;
359	  handler: RouteHandler;
360	  /**
361	   * Seconds this handler may take before Bun closes its socket.
362	   *
363	   * Only for handlers that do real work inside the request (a playlist scan, a
364	   * cookie export, a live audio probe). Without it they are cut at
365	   * WEB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS while the work carries on server-side, so the
366	   * dashboard reports a failure for a scan that actually succeeded.
367	   */
368	  deadlineSeconds?: number;
369	}
370	
371	/** Minutes-scale work: a playlist/channel scan over a large source. */
372	const SCAN_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 15 * 60;
373	/** A browser cookie read plus the live YouTube check it performs. */
374	const COOKIE_EXPORT_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 5 * 60;
375	/** A `yt-dlp -J` audio-track probe; the probe itself gives up at 90s. */
376	const AUDIO_PROBE_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 120;
377	
378	/** Match a `/api/…/:param` pattern against path segments; null = no match. */
379	function matchRoute(pattern: string, segments: string[]): RouteParams | null {
380	  const parts = pattern.split("/").filter(Boolean);
381	  if (parts.length !== segments.length) return null;
382	  const params: RouteParams = {};
383	  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
384	    const p = parts[i];
385	    if (p.startsWith(":")) {
386	      if (!segments[i]) return null; // never bind an empty param
387	      try {
388	        params[p.slice(1)] = decodeURIComponent(segments[i]);
389	      } catch {
390	        // A malformed percent escape is an invalid path, not a handler crash.
391	        return null;
392	      }
393	    } else if (p !== segments[i]) {
394	      return null;
395	    }
396	  }
397	  return params;
398	}

402	// it carries the timestamps the drawer's Created/Updated rows and the History

404	const JOB_COLUMNS = `id, url, title, folder, output_directory, file_path, target_format, video_quality,
405	                download_status, conversion_status, metadata_status, pause_reason, metadata_files, metadata_unavailable,

408	                partial_file_path, audio_tracks, audio_selection, superseded_file, relocated_to,
409	                want_subtitles, want_thumbnail, want_description, created_at, updated_at`;

432	// A job is "in progress" (never safe to mutate from the dashboard) when any
433	// stage is running or any claim lease is still attached. Claims are identified
434	// by their token as well as the worker id, so a row whose status was flipped
435	// without releasing its claim cannot slip past the guard.
436	const ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE = `
437	  COALESCE(download_status, '') = 'downloading'
438	  OR download_claimed_by IS NOT NULL
439	  OR download_claim_token IS NOT NULL
440	  OR COALESCE(conversion_status, '') = 'in_progress'
441	  OR conversion_claimed_by IS NOT NULL
442	  OR conversion_claim_token IS NOT NULL
443	  OR COALESCE(metadata_status, '') = 'in_progress'
444	  OR metadata_claim_token IS NOT NULL
445	`;
446	
447	const PURGE_QUEUE_PREDICATE = "download_status IN ('pending', 'paused', 'waiting_live', 'failed', 'downloading')";
448	
449	type IdleJobResult<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false };
450	
451	/**
452	 * Stop every in-flight child (download / conversion / sidecar fetch) belonging
453	 * to these jobs.
454	 *
455	 * Deletion and purge used to be database-only operations: the row disappeared
456	 * while yt-dlp kept downloading in the terminal and wrote a file nobody
457	 * tracked — and the download worker then reported a lost claim. Interrupting
458	 * the children first is what makes the buttons mean what they say. The kill is
459	 * claim-safe: a worker that no longer owns its row writes nothing (see the
460	 * claim-token CAS in db.ts), and a deleted row is treated as a normal outcome.
461	 */
462	function stopActiveStages(ids: Iterable<string>) {
463	  return cancelActiveStages(ids);
464	}
465	
466	/**
467	 * First half of a deletion: announce the cancellation (so a worker that is
468	 * still waiting on the multi-audio probe refuses to spawn a downloader for a
469	 * job that is about to disappear) and interrupt whatever child is running.
470	 */
471	function beginCancellation(ids: string[]): CancelledStages {
472	  const unique = [...new Set(ids)];
473	  if (unique.length === 0) return { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
474	  for (const id of unique) markJobCancelled(id);
475	  return stopActiveStages(unique);
476	}
477	
478	/**
479	 * Second half, run right after the rows are gone: a child that registered in
480	 * the instant between the ownership re-check and the row deletion is caught
481	 * here. Workers that never spawn are caught by the cancellation mark (checked
482	 * immediately after `Bun.spawn`), so between the two no child survives a
483	 * deleted job.
484	 */
485	function finishCancellation(ids: string[]): CancelledStages {
486	  if (ids.length === 0) return { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
487	  return stopActiveStages(ids);
488	}
489	
490	/** How many distinct jobs actually had a live child interrupted, across stages. */
491	function stoppedCount(...stages: CancelledStages[]): number {
492	  const ids = new Set<string>();
493	  for (const stage of stages) {
494	    for (const id of stage.downloads) ids.add(id);
495	    for (const id of stage.conversions) ids.add(id);
496	    for (const id of stage.metadata) ids.add(id);
497	  }
498	  return ids.size;
499	}
500	
501	/**
502	 * Park a job that is mid-download as a user pause, keeping its .part for a
503	 * later resume. The claim is deliberately left in place: the worker still owns
504	 * this row, so it observes `pause_reason = 'user'` when its (now interrupted)
505	 * download returns and releases the claim through its own token.
506	 */
507	function parkDownloadingJobs(ids: string[]): void {
508	  if (ids.length === 0) return;
509	  const placeholders = ids.map(() => "?").join(",");
510	  db.run(
511	    `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'paused', pause_reason = 'user', speed = 0, eta = 0,
512	       updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
513	     WHERE id IN (${placeholders}) AND download_status = 'downloading'`,
514	    ids,
515	  );
516	}
517	
518	/** Run a synchronous job mutation only while none of its rows has a live stage claim. */
519	function withIdleJobs<T>(ids: string[], operation: () => T): IdleJobResult<T> {
520	  const placeholders = ids.map(() => "?").join(",");
521	  const transaction = db.transaction(() => {
522	    const active = db
523	      .query(`SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE id IN (${placeholders}) AND (${ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE}) LIMIT 1`)
524	      .get(...ids);
525	    if (active) return { ok: false as const };
526	    return { ok: true as const, value: operation() };
527	  });
528	  return transaction.immediate();
529	}

535	interface JobOverride {
536	  targetFormat?: string | null;
537	  videoQuality?: string | null;
538	  /** Language codes from the track picker; null restores the global audio mode. */
539	  audioTracks?: string[] | null;
540	}
541	
542	const JOB_TARGET_FORMATS = new Set(["mp4", "mkv", "webm", "mp3", "m4a"]);
543	
544	function parseJobOverride(body: unknown): { ok: true; value: JobOverride } | { ok: false; error: string } {
545	  if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body)) {
546	    return { ok: false, error: "A JSON object with at least one override is required" };
547	  }
548	  const raw = body as Record<string, unknown>;
549	  const allowed = new Set(["targetFormat", "videoQuality", "audioTracks", "retry"]);
550	  const unexpected = Object.keys(raw).find((key) => !allowed.has(key));
551	  if (unexpected) return { ok: false, error: `Unknown override field: ${unexpected}` };
552	  const value: JobOverride = {};
553	  let provided = false;
554	
555	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "targetFormat")) {
556	    provided = true;
557	    if (raw.targetFormat !== null && (typeof raw.targetFormat !== "string" || !JOB_TARGET_FORMATS.has(raw.targetFormat))) {
558	      return { ok: false, error: "targetFormat must be mp4, mkv, webm, mp3, m4a, or null" };
559	    }
560	    value.targetFormat = raw.targetFormat as string | null;
561	  }
562	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "videoQuality")) {
563	    provided = true;
564	    if (raw.videoQuality !== null && (typeof raw.videoQuality !== "string" || !Object.hasOwn(QUALITY_FORMATS, raw.videoQuality))) {
565	      return { ok: false, error: `videoQuality must be one of ${Object.keys(QUALITY_FORMATS).join(", ")} or null` };
566	    }
567	    value.videoQuality = raw.videoQuality as string | null;
568	  }
569	  if (Object.hasOwn(raw, "audioTracks")) {
570	    provided = true;
571	    if (raw.audioTracks !== null && !Array.isArray(raw.audioTracks)) {
572	      return { ok: false, error: "audioTracks must be an array of language codes or null" };
573	    }
574	    if (Array.isArray(raw.audioTracks)) {
575	      if (raw.audioTracks.length > 40 || raw.audioTracks.some((track) =>
576	        typeof track !== "string" || !track.trim() || track.trim().length > 32
577	      )) {
578	        return { ok: false, error: "audioTracks must contain up to 40 non-empty language codes (32 characters max)" };
579	      }
580	      const languages = [...new Set(raw.audioTracks.map((track) => (track as string).trim()))];
581	      value.audioTracks = languages.length ? languages : null;
582	    } else {
583	      value.audioTracks = null;
584	    }
585	  }
586	
587	  if (raw.retry !== undefined && typeof raw.retry !== "boolean") {
588	    return { ok: false, error: "retry must be a boolean" };
589	  }
590	  if (!provided && raw.retry !== true) {
591	    return { ok: false, error: "Provide at least one of: targetFormat, videoQuality, audioTracks" };
592	  }
593	  return { ok: true, value };
594	}

596	/** Apply a validated override inside the surrounding SQLite transaction. */
597	function persistJobOverride(id: string, override: JobOverride): void {
598	  const sets: string[] = [];
599	  const values: (string | null)[] = [];
600	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "targetFormat")) {
601	    sets.push("target_format = ?");
602	    values.push(override.targetFormat ?? null);
603	  }
604	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "videoQuality")) {
605	    sets.push("video_quality = ?");
606	    values.push(override.videoQuality ?? null);
607	  }
608	  if (Object.hasOwn(override, "audioTracks")) {
609	    sets.push("audio_selection = ?");
610	    values.push(override.audioTracks?.length ? JSON.stringify(override.audioTracks) : null);
611	  }
612	  if (sets.length === 0) return;
613	  db.run(`UPDATE jobs SET ${sets.join(", ")}, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`, [...values, id]);
614	}

616	interface RetryJobResult {

620	  /**
621	   * True when the retry became an in-place CONVERSION instead of a re-download:

624	   * remux what is already there.

773	           WHEN COALESCE(want_subtitles,0) + COALESCE(want_thumbnail,0) + COALESCE(want_description,0) > 0 THEN 'pending'
774	           ELSE metadata_status END,
775	         metadata_retry_count = 0,
776	         metadata_unavailable = '[]',
777	         last_error = NULL,
778	         download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
779	         download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
780	         conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
781	         conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
782	         metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
783	         metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
784	         updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
785	       WHERE id = ? AND NOT (${ACTIVE_JOB_PREDICATE})`,
786	      [conversionStatus, id],
787	    ).changes;
788	  });
789	
790	  if (!result.ok) {
791	    return { changed: "in-progress", partialWarning: null, convertedOnly: false };
792	  }
793	  // The convert-in-place branch returns its full result from the transaction —
794	  // no partial wipe follows (no download was queued, so there is no partial).
795	  if (typeof result.value === "object") return result.value;
796	  if (result.value !== 1) {
797	    return { changed: result.value, partialWarning: null, convertedOnly: false };
798	  }
799	
800	  // The job is re-queued and no longer references its partial. Wipe the partial
801	  // pair now — control file first, via removePartialFiles, so a stranded
802	  // `.aria2` can never wedge aria2c. When no path was recorded, fall back to a
803	  // directory scan: the worker resumes through the same finder, so the wipe
804	  // must cover exactly what a resume would have found.
805	  let partial: string | null = partialPath;
806	  if (!partial && fallbackDir && fallbackBase) {
807	    partial = await findPartialFile(fallbackDir, fallbackBase);
808	  }
809	  if (partial) {
810	    const removal = await removePartialFiles(partial);
811	    if (removal.fatal) {
812	      // Locked by another process (an orphaned aria2c, an antivirus scan). The
813	      // row no longer references the partial, but if the file survived on disk
814	      // the next attempt's directory scan may resume from it — say so instead
815	      // of pretending the restart is clean.
816	      logError("web", `${id}: retry could not wipe locked partial ${partial}: ${removal.error}`);
817	      return {
818	        changed: 1,
819	        partialWarning:
820	          `Partial file is locked (${removal.error}). Close the program holding it — ` +
821	          `the next attempt may resume from the leftover partial instead of starting at 0%.`,
822	        convertedOnly: false,
823	      };
824	    }
825	  }
826	  return { changed: 1, partialWarning: null, convertedOnly: false };
827	}

829	/** Save per-job settings without queuing a download. */
830	function saveJobOverrideById(id: string, config: Config, override: JobOverride): number | "in-progress" {
831	  const result = withIdleJobs([id], () => {
832	    const row = db.query("SELECT id, download_status, target_format, video_quality FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(id) as
833	      | { id: string; download_status: string; target_format: string | null; video_quality: string | null }
834	      | null;
835	    if (!row) return 0;
836	    persistJobOverride(id, override);
837	    const fresh = db.query("SELECT target_format, video_quality FROM jobs WHERE id = ?").get(id) as {
838	      target_format: string | null;
839	      video_quality: string | null;
840	    };
841	    const formatOrQualityChanged =
842	      (Object.hasOwn(override, "targetFormat") && override.targetFormat !== row.target_format) ||
843	      (Object.hasOwn(override, "videoQuality") && override.videoQuality !== row.video_quality);
844	    const needsConversion =
845	      formatOrQualityChanged || effectiveTargetFormat(fresh, config) !== "mp4" || effectiveVideoQuality(fresh, config) === "audio";
846	    // A queued job will use the new container on its next fetch. Leave an
847	    // already-downloaded job alone unless retry=true (which stashes/re-fetches
848	    // it atomically), but make sure queued work gets its post-download remux.
849	    if (row.download_status !== "downloaded" && needsConversion) {
850	      db.run(
851	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
852	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
853	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
854	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
855	        [id],
856	      );
857	    }
858	    return 1;
859	  });
860	  return result.ok ? result.value : "in-progress";
861	}

863	/** Clear every per-stage failure counter for one job. */
864	function resetFailCounters(id: string): number {
865	  if (!id) return 0;
866	  return db.run(
867	    `UPDATE jobs SET retry_count = 0, metadata_retry_count = 0, conversion_retry_count = 0, last_error = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
868	    [id],
869	  ).changes;
870	}

872	/**
873	 * Delete a set of jobs by id (bulk action from the dashboard).
874	 *
875	 * Deletion is a cancellation too: any in-flight download, encode, or sidecar
876	 * fetch is interrupted first. The database transaction also stores a durable
877	 * per-video ignore tombstone before removing each row, so the next playlist
878	 * scan cannot quietly put a deleted job back in the queue.
879	 */
880	async function deleteJobsBulk(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
881	  const body: any = await req.json().catch(() => null);
882	  const ids: string[] = Array.isArray(body?.ids)
883	    ? [...new Set<string>(body.ids.filter((x: unknown): x is string => typeof x === "string" && x.length > 0).slice(0, 500))]
884	    : [];
885	  if (ids.length === 0) {
886	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: "Expected a JSON body with a non-empty ids array" }, { status: 400 });
887	  }
888	
889	  // Cancellation is part of the deletion: mark, interrupt, atomically save a
890	  // durable ignore tombstone and delete the rows, then sweep once more.
891	  let cancellationStarted = false;
892	  let stoppedBefore: CancelledStages = { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
893	  try {
894	    cancellationStarted = true;
895	    stoppedBefore = beginCancellation(ids);
896	    const result = deleteJobsAndIgnore(ids);
897	    const late = finishCancellation(ids);
898	    return Response.json({
899	      ok: true,
900	      ...result,
901	      stopped: stoppedCount(stoppedBefore, late),
902	    });
903	  } catch (error: any) {
904	    if (cancellationStarted) {
905	      try {
906	        finishCancellation(ids);
907	      } catch {}
908	      for (const id of ids) clearJobCancelled(id);
909	    }
910	    const message = String(error?.message || error);
911	    logError("job-delete", `Bulk delete failed for ${ids.length} selected job(s): ${message}`);
912	    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: `Could not delete selected jobs: ${message}` }, { status: 500 });
913	  }
914	}

2107	/** Dispatch an API request through the route table. */
2108	async function handleApi(
2109	  req: Request,
2110	  config: Config,
2111	  url: URL,
2112	  pathname: string,
2113	  server?: RequestDeadlineServer | null,
2114	): Promise<Response> {
2115	  const segments = pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
2116	  // A static path (/api/jobs/pause) that exists with a different method is a
2117	  // 405 — it must never fall through to a :param route and be read as an id.
2118	  // Several routes may share one pattern (/api/settings GET + POST), so the
2119	  // verdict is per pattern: 405 only when NO route with that exact pattern
2120	  // accepts this method.
2121	  const exactAllow = new Set<string>();
2122	  let exactPath = false;
2123	  let exactAccepted = false;
2124	  for (const route of ROUTES) {
2125	    if (route.pattern.includes(":")) continue;
2126	    if (!matchRoute(route.pattern, segments)) continue;
2127	    exactPath = true;
2128	    for (const m of route.methods) exactAllow.add(m);
2129	    if (route.methods.includes(req.method)) exactAccepted = true;
2130	  }
2131	  if (exactPath && !exactAccepted) {
2132	    return methodNotAllowed(req.method, pathname, [...exactAllow]);
2133	  }
2134	
2135	  const allow = new Set<string>();
2136	  for (const route of ROUTES) {
2137	    const params = matchRoute(route.pattern, segments);
2138	    if (!params) continue;
2139	    if (!route.methods.includes(req.method)) {
2140	      for (const m of route.methods) allow.add(m);
2141	      continue;
2142	    }
2143	    // Give this one request its own deadline before the handler blocks for
2144	    // minutes. No server means no live socket (unit tests call handleRequest
2145	    // directly), and a handler that fails here must still run: the deadline is
2146	    // a convenience, never a reason to answer 500.
2147	    if (route.deadlineSeconds && server) {
2148	      try {
2149	        server.timeout(req, route.deadlineSeconds);
2150	      } catch {
2151	        // The request is not attached to a live connection any more.
2152	      }
2153	    }
2154	    return await route.handler({ req, config, url, params });
2155	  }
2156	  if (allow.size > 0) {
2157	    return methodNotAllowed(req.method, pathname, [...allow]);
2158	  }
2159	  return Response.json({ ok: false, error: `Unknown API path: ${pathname}` }, { status: 404 });
2160	}
2161	
2162	function methodNotAllowed(method: string, pathname: string, allow: string[]): Response {
2163	  return Response.json(
2164	    { ok: false, error: `Method ${method} not allowed for ${pathname}` },
2165	    { status: 405, headers: { Allow: allow.sort().join(", ") } },
2166	  );
2167	}

2171	function reliabilityHandler(config: Config): Response {
2172	  const partials = db
2173	    .query(
2174	      `SELECT COUNT(*) as count, COALESCE(SUM(file_size), 0) as bytes FROM jobs WHERE partial_file_path IS NOT NULL`,
2175	    )
2176	    .get() as any;
2177	  // Same eligibility rules as the sweep itself: all failed downloads except
2178	  // permanent video-level errors get another retry window after cooldown.
2179	  // Uses the shared classifier so the dashboard and sweep cannot disagree.
2180	  const failedDownloads = db
2181	    .query(
2182	      `SELECT last_error FROM jobs WHERE download_status = 'failed'`,
2183	    )
2184	    .all() as any[];
2185	  const resumableFailed = failedDownloads.filter(
2186	    (r) => !isPermanentDownloadError(r.last_error),
2187	  ).length;
2188	  const waitingLive = db
2189	    .query(`SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM jobs WHERE download_status = 'waiting_live'`)
2190	    .get() as any;
2191	
2192	  // --- Resume + self-healing state ---------------------------------------
2193	  // What will actually pick up where it left off. A partial only matters
2194	  // while its job is still in play: a failed job's partial may be discarded
2195	  // once the resume budget is spent, so it is not counted here.
2196	  const resumablePartials = db
2197	    .query(
2198	      `SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM jobs
2199	        WHERE partial_file_path IS NOT NULL
2200	          AND download_status IN ('pending', 'paused', 'downloading')`,
2201	    )
2202	    .get() as any;
2203	  // Crashed jobs: parked as paused/interrupted so they are re-claimed and
2204	  // resume from their partial rather than restarting.
2205	  const interrupted = db
2206	    .query(
2207	      `SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM jobs
2208	        WHERE download_status = 'paused' AND pause_reason = 'interrupted'`,
2209	    )
2210	    .get() as any;
2211	  // What the stale-claim reaper would reclaim right now — same thresholds,
2212	  // same lease-expiry predicate (heartbeat-based) and same active-download
2213	  // protection as the sweep itself, so the panel cannot drift.
2214	  const t = STALE_CLAIM_THRESHOLDS(config);
2215	  const activeJobIds = Array.from(activeDownloadJobs.values());
2216	  const activeJobFilter = activeJobIds.length
2217	    ? `AND id NOT IN (${activeJobIds.map(() => "?").join(", ")})`
2218	    : "";
2219	  const staleClaimsQuery = db.query(
2220	    `SELECT
2221	       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE download_status = 'downloading'
2222	          AND ${staleClaimCondition("download", t.download)} ${activeJobFilter})
2223	     + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE conversion_status = 'in_progress'
2224	          AND ${staleClaimCondition("conversion", t.conversion)})
2225	     + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE metadata_status = 'in_progress'
2226	          AND ${staleClaimCondition("metadata", t.metadata)})
2227	     AS count`,
2228	  );
2229	  const staleClaims = (activeJobIds.length ? staleClaimsQuery.get(...activeJobIds) : staleClaimsQuery.get()) as any;
2230	  // Which engine owns archive.db right now. Two engines with different web
2231	  // ports used to look fine here; the lease is what actually decides ownership.
2232	  const lease = readEngineLease();
2233	
2234	  // The four self-healing sweeps, with what each currently has in scope.
2235	  // `pending: null` means "not counted here" — the missing-files sweep has to
2236	  // stat every recorded file, which is far too expensive to run per poll.
2237	  const sweeps = [
2238	    {
2239	      id: "crashed",
2240	      label: "Crashed jobs resume",
2241	      cadence: "startup",
2242	      detail: "Jobs interrupted mid-flight are re-queued and resume from their partial.",
2243	      pending: interrupted?.count || 0,
2244	    },
2245	    {
2246	      id: "staleClaims",
2247	      label: "Stale claims reclaimed",
2248	      cadence: "every 60s",
2249	      detail: "Inactive download claims are re-queued after a timeout; live worker-owned jobs are protected.",
2250	      pending: staleClaims?.count || 0,
2251	    },
2252	    {
2253	      id: "missingFiles",
2254	      label: "Deleted files re-fetched",
2255	      cadence: "startup",
2256	      detail: "Files recorded as downloaded but no longer on disk are queued again.",
2257	      pending: null,
2258	    },
2259	    {
2260	      id: "requeueFailed",
2261	      label: "Failed jobs retried",
2262	      cadence: "every 60s",
2263	      detail: "Failed jobs retry after a cooldown; permanent failures never do.",
2264	      pending: resumableFailed,
2265	    },
2266	    {
2267	      id: "relocate",
2268	      label: "Moved to secondary storage",
2269	      cadence: "every 60s",
2270	      detail:
2271	        "Finished files that need no conversion are moved into secondary storage (sidecars included). A file already there is adopted, never copied twice.",
2272	      pending: relocationPendingCount(config),
2273	    },
2274	  ];
2275	
2276	  return Response.json({
2277	    ok: true,
2278	    paused: isPaused(),
2279	    pauseReason: getPauseReason(),
2280	    partialFiles: { count: partials?.count || 0, bytes: partials?.bytes || 0 },
2281	    resumableFailed,
2282	    waitingLive: waitingLive?.count || 0,
2283	    resume: {
2284	      resumablePartials: resumablePartials?.count || 0,

9	/**

12	 * archive cannot be read or rewritten, allowing explicit re-queue routes to
13	 * leave their ignore tombstone in place.

15	export function removeFromArchive(archiveFile: string, videoId: string): boolean {
16	  try {
17	    if (!archiveFile || !existsSync(archiveFile)) return true;
18	    const lines = readFileSync(archiveFile, "utf-8").split("\n");

25	  } catch {

27	    return false;

186	async function stopMetadataProcess(proc: Bun.Subprocess): Promise<void> {
187	  if (proc.exitCode === null) {
188	    try {
189	      proc.kill("SIGINT");
190	    } catch {
191	      // It may have exited between the check and the signal.
192	    }
193	    let graceTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
194	    let exited: boolean;
195	    try {
196	      exited = await Promise.race([
197	        proc.exited.then(() => true, () => true),
198	        new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
199	          graceTimer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 2_000);
200	        }),
201	      ]);
202	    } finally {
203	      if (graceTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(graceTimer);
204	    }
205	    if (!exited && proc.exitCode === null) {
206	      try {
207	        proc.kill("SIGKILL");
208	      } catch {
209	        // The child may have exited just before the force-kill.
210	      }
211	    }
212	  }
213	  await proc.exited.catch(() => {});
214	}

457	/**
458	 * Re-queue failed jobs once they have cooled down for
459	 * `requeueFailedAfterMinutes`. Permanent download failures (private, removed,
460	 * age-gated, geo-blocked, dead URLs) are never retried. A cooldown starts a
461	 * fresh retry window for each stage; the worker's per-video cap still bounds
462	 * each burst of immediate retries, while a later sweep can recover from a
463	 * longer outage without operator intervention.
464	 *
465	 * Pass `ignoreCooldown: true` (used by the "Requeue all failed" web button) to
466	 * retry every eligible job immediately.
467	 */
468	export function requeueFailedJobs(config: Config, opts: { ignoreCooldown?: boolean } = {}): RequeueResult {
469	  const result: RequeueResult = { downloads: 0, conversions: 0, metadata: 0 };
470	  const ignoreCooldown = !!opts.ignoreCooldown;
471	  if (!ignoreCooldown && config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes <= 0) return result;
472	  // SQLite modifier built only from a validated integer — never user text.
473	  // With ignoreCooldown there is no age filter at all (a `-0 minutes` modifier
474	  // would still exclude rows whose updated_at falls in the current second).
475	  const modifier = ignoreCooldown ? "" : `AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-${Math.floor(config.requeueFailedAfterMinutes)} minutes')`;
476	
477	  try {
478	    // --- Downloads -----------------------------------------------------------
479	    const failedDownloads = db
480	      .query(
481	        `SELECT id, last_error, output_directory, title, "index", partial_file_path FROM jobs
482	         WHERE download_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
483	      )
484	      .all() as any[];
485	    for (const row of failedDownloads) {
486	      if (isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
487	      // Scheduling a retry is not itself a failed attempt. Reset the current
488	      // no-progress budget here; the next worker outcome is what spends it.
489	      // Reset resume_count = 0 so the job gets a fresh resume budget for this window.
490	      let validPartial = row.partial_file_path && existsSync(row.partial_file_path) ? row.partial_file_path : null;
491	      if (!validPartial && row.output_directory && row.title) {
492	        const found = findPartialFileSync(row.output_directory, jobFittedBaseFilename(row));
493	        if (found) validPartial = found;
494	      }
495	      db.run(
496	        `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'pending', retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0,
497	           partial_file_path = ?, pause_reason = NULL,
498	           download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
499	           download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
500	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
501	        [validPartial, row.id],
502	      );
503	      result.downloads++;
504	    }
505	
506	    // --- Conversions -----------------------------------------------------------
507	    const failedConversions = db
508	      .query(
509	        `SELECT id FROM jobs
510	         WHERE conversion_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
511	      )
512	      .all() as any[];
513	    for (const row of failedConversions) {
514	      db.run(
515	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
516	           conversion_claimed_by = NULL, conversion_claimed_at = NULL,
517	           conversion_claim_token = NULL, conversion_heartbeat_at = NULL,
518	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
519	        [row.id],
520	      );
521	      result.conversions++;
522	    }
523	
524	    // --- Metadata -------------------------------------------------------------
525	    const failedMetadata = db
526	      .query(
527	        `SELECT id, file_path, last_error FROM jobs
528	         WHERE metadata_status = 'failed' ${modifier}`,
529	      )
530	      .all() as any[];
531	    for (const row of failedMetadata) {
532	      // Without the media file or after a permanent source error the metadata
533	      // fetch cannot succeed. Leave those rows terminal; the per-job sidecar
534	      // control is the explicit retry path if the operator wants to try again.
535	      if (!row.file_path || !existsSync(row.file_path) || isPermanentDownloadError(row.last_error)) continue;
536	      db.run(
537	        `UPDATE jobs SET metadata_status = 'pending', metadata_retry_count = 0,
538	           metadata_claimed_by = NULL, metadata_claimed_at = NULL,
539	           metadata_claim_token = NULL, metadata_heartbeat_at = NULL,
540	           updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?`,
541	        [row.id],
542	      );
543	      result.metadata++;
544	    }
545	
546	    const total = result.downloads + result.conversions + result.metadata;
547	    if (total > 0) {
548	      console.log(
549	        `♻️ Re-queued ${result.downloads} download(s), ${result.conversions} conversion(s), ${result.metadata} metadata job(s) after cooldown.`,
550	      );
551	    }
552	  } catch (e: any) {
553	    logError("requeue", String(e?.message || e));
554	  }
555	  return result;
556	}

4	 * Exponential backoff with jitter, in milliseconds.
5	 *
6	 * attempt 0 → base, 1 → 2×base, 2 → 4×base … capped at maxSeconds, plus up to
7	 * 30% random jitter so many workers that failed together don't retry in
8	 * lockstep. The RNG is injectable to keep tests deterministic.
9	 */
10	export function computeBackoffMs(
11	  attempt: number,
12	  baseSeconds: number,
13	  maxSeconds: number,
14	  rnd: () => number = Math.random,
15	): number {
16	  const a = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number.isFinite(attempt) ? attempt : 0));
17	  const base = Math.max(1, baseSeconds);
18	  const cap = Math.max(base, maxSeconds);
19	  const exponential = Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** a);
20	  const jittered = exponential * (1 + 0.3 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, rnd())));
21	  return Math.round(jittered * 1000);
22	}

10	// an imported row needs no download stage at all, just a file_path. The same

12	// job whose file is not in the chosen container (e.g. an mkv download when mp4
