17	import { readdir, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
18	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
19	import { basename, dirname, extname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
20	import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
21	import { db } from "./db";
22	import type { Config } from "./config";
23	import { hardenName, sanitizeFolderName } from "./util";
24	import { parseSelectionJson, parseTracksJson, selectAudioTracks } from "./audio-tracks";
25	
26	/** Containers treated as convertible video sources. Anything else (sidecars,
27	 * partials, control files, metadata dumps) is not a candidate. */
28	const VIDEO_EXTENSIONS = new Set([
29	  ".mp4", ".mkv", ".webm", ".avi", ".mov", ".m4v", ".ts", ".m2ts", ".mts",
30	  ".flv", ".wmv", ".mpg", ".mpeg", ".mpe", ".3gp", ".3g2", ".ogv", ".vob",
31	  ".divx", ".m1v", ".m2v", ".rmvb", ".asf", ".dv", ".f4v",
32	]);
33	
34	/** Safety rails for the directory walk. */
35	const MAX_DEPTH = 6;
36	const MAX_FILES = 5000;
37	/** Files smaller than this are fragments or placeholders, not media. */
38	const MIN_FILE_SIZE = 1024;
39	
40	export interface UnconvertedScanResult {
41	  /** Absolute root that was scanned. */
42	  root: string;
43	  /** Container every imported job is queued to convert to. */
44	  targetFormat: string;
45	  /** Every regular file encountered during the walk. */
46	  filesSeen: number;
47	  /** Files with a recognised video extension (candidates + tracked). */
48	  videoFiles: number;
49	  /** Rows actually inserted (re-runs import nothing new). */
50	  imported: number;
51	  /** Tracked, already-finished jobs re-queued because their file is NOT in the target container. */
52	  requeued: number;
53	  /** Tracked jobs left alone because they are multi-audio archives (their MKV is retained by design). */
54	  keptMultiTrack: number;
55	  /** Video files skipped because the jobs table already tracks their path. */
56	  alreadyTracked: number;
57	  /** Video files skipped for being (near-)empty. */
58	  tooSmall: number;
59	  /** True when the walk stopped at MAX_FILES. */
60	  truncated: boolean;
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Stable job id for a local file: `local-` + SHA-1 of the absolute path. The
65	 * same file always maps to the same id, so re-running the scan is idempotent
66	 * (INSERT OR IGNORE plus this deterministic key).
67	 */
68	export function localFileJobId(absolutePath: string): string {
69	  return `local-${createHash("sha1").update(resolve(absolutePath)).digest("hex")}`;
70	}
71	
72	/** Path comparison key: case-insensitive on Windows (NTFS), exact elsewhere. */
73	function pathKey(p: string): string {
74	  const r = resolve(p);
75	  return process.platform === "win32" ? r.toLowerCase() : r;
76	}
77	
78	/** Every media/partial/superseded path the jobs table already points at. */
79	function trackedPaths(): Set<string> {
80	  const rows = db
81	    .query("SELECT file_path, partial_file_path, superseded_file FROM jobs")
82	    .all() as { file_path: string | null; partial_file_path: string | null; superseded_file: string | null }[];
83	  const tracked = new Set<string>();
84	  for (const row of rows) {
85	    for (const p of [row.file_path, row.partial_file_path, row.superseded_file]) {
86	      if (p) tracked.add(pathKey(p));
87	    }
88	  }
89	  return tracked;
90	}
91	
92	/** Containers the tracked-job pass may re-queue: videos plus audio containers. */
93	const REQUEUEABLE_EXTENSIONS = new Set([
94	  ...VIDEO_EXTENSIONS,
95	  ".mp3", ".m4a", ".opus", ".ogg", ".flac", ".wav",
96	]);
97	
98	/**
99	 * How many audio tracks a job's download carries, as far as the cached probe
100	 * and per-job selection can tell. 1 when nothing is cached — the safe default,
101	 * since single-track files are the common case.
102	 */
103	function effectiveAudioTrackCount(
104	  row: { audio_tracks: string | null; audio_selection: string | null },
105	  config: Config,
106	): number {
107	  const discovered = parseTracksJson(row.audio_tracks);
108	  if (!discovered || discovered.length === 0) return 1;
109	  const selected = selectAudioTracks(
110	    discovered,
111	    config.multiAudioMode,
112	    config.audioTrackLanguages,
113	    parseSelectionJson(row.audio_selection),
114	  );
115	  return Math.max(1, selected.length);
116	}
117	
118	/**
119	 * Re-queue finished jobs whose recorded media is NOT in the requested target
120	 * container.
121	 *
122	 * This is the repair path for an archive that predates the download worker's
123	 * container check: yt-dlp does not promise the requested container (VP9/Opus
124	 * presets merge into webm/mkv), and jobs whose target was mp4 were historically
125	 * marked `not_needed`, so those files never went through the conversion stage.
126	 * The sweep flips such a
127	 * job's conversion_status back to 'pending' — the converter then remuxes the
128	 * file exactly as it would for a fresh download (video copied, audio to AAC
129	 * for mp4) — and is idempotent: once converted, the file's container matches
130	 * and the next sweep skips it.
131	 *
132	 * Multi-audio archives are left alone: keeping their MKV when the target is
133	 * mp4 is the documented behavior (AGENTS.md, multi-audio), matching the
134	 * download worker's exemption. Scope is the scanned root only — a file the
135	 * relocation pass already moved into secondary storage is outside it, and
136	 * re-converting would drag it back into the output tree.
137	 */
138	function requeueWrongContainerJobs(
139	  config: Config,
140	  targetFormat: string,
141	  root: string,
142	  result: UnconvertedScanResult,
143	): void {
144	  const rows = db
145	    .query(
146	      `SELECT id, file_path, audio_tracks, audio_selection FROM jobs
147	       WHERE download_status = 'downloaded' AND conversion_status IN ('done', 'not_needed')`,
148	    )
149	    .all() as { id: string; file_path: string | null; audio_tracks: string | null; audio_selection: string | null }[];
150	  for (const row of rows) {
151	    if (!row.file_path) continue;
152	    const key = pathKey(row.file_path);
153	    if (key !== root && !key.startsWith(root + sep)) continue;
154	    const ext = extname(key).toLowerCase();
155	    if (!REQUEUEABLE_EXTENSIONS.has(ext)) continue;
156	    if (ext.replace(/^\./, "") === targetFormat) continue;
157	    if (!existsSync(row.file_path)) continue; // missing-file sweep owns that repair
158	    if (effectiveAudioTrackCount(row, config) >= 2) {
159	      result.keptMultiTrack++;
160	      continue;
161	    }
162	    // The IN-guard keeps a job that flipped to a claimable/failed state since
163	    // the SELECT from being clobbered mid-sweep.
164	    const changes = db
165	      .run(
166	        `UPDATE jobs SET conversion_status = 'pending', conversion_retry_count = 0,
167	           last_error = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
168	         WHERE id = ? AND conversion_status IN ('done', 'not_needed')`,
169	        [row.id],
170	      )
171	      .changes;
172	    if (changes === 1) result.requeued++;
173	  }
174	}
175	
176	async function walk(root: string, depth: number, out: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
177	  if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return false;
178	  let entries;
179	  try {
180	    entries = await readdir(root, { withFileTypes: true });
181	  } catch {
182	    return false; // unreadable directory — skip it, keep scanning the rest
183	  }
184	  let truncated = false;
185	  for (const entry of entries) {
186	    if (out.length >= MAX_FILES) return true;
187	    const full = join(root, entry.name);
188	    if (entry.name.startsWith(".")) continue; // hidden files/dirs
189	    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
190	      // `.ytdl` directories are yt-dlp fragment state, never a source file.
191	      if (entry.name.endsWith(".ytdl")) continue;
192	      if (await walk(full, depth + 1, out)) truncated = true;
193	    } else if (entry.isFile()) {
194	      out.push(full);
195	    }
196	  }
197	  return truncated;
198	}
199	
200	/**
201	 * Scan `rootDir` (default: the configured output root) for video files that
202	 * are not tracked in the jobs table and insert one conversion-queued job per
203	 * file, with `targetFormat` pre-selected. Tracked jobs whose finished media is
204	 * NOT in `targetFormat` are re-queued for conversion as well (their conversion
205	 * stage re-opens; nothing is re-downloaded).
206	 *
207	 * The work is purely local (disk walk + INSERTs) — no network — so it is safe
208	 * to run while offline mode is on; the conversions themselves are ffmpeg remuxes
209	 * that also need no network.
210	 */
211	export async function scanUnconvertedVideos(
212	  config: Config,
213	  targetFormat: string,
214	  rootDir?: string,
215	): Promise<UnconvertedScanResult> {
216	  const root = resolve(rootDir ?? config.outputRoot);
217	  const tracked = trackedPaths();
218	  const files: string[] = [];
219	  const truncated = await walk(root, 0, files);
220	
221	  const result: UnconvertedScanResult = {
222	    root,
223	    targetFormat,
224	    filesSeen: files.length,
225	    videoFiles: 0,
226	    imported: 0,
227	    requeued: 0,
228	    keptMultiTrack: 0,
229	    alreadyTracked: 0,
230	    tooSmall: 0,
231	    truncated,
232	  };
233	
234	  // Pass 1: tracked jobs already finished in the wrong container get their
235	  // conversion stage re-opened (see requeueWrongContainerJobs — this is how an
236	  // archive of mkv/webm downloads requested as mp4 gets repaired in place).
237	  requeueWrongContainerJobs(config, targetFormat, root, result);
238	
239	  interface Candidate {
240	    id: string;
241	    url: string;
242	    title: string;
243	    outputDirectory: string;
244	    folder: string;
245	    filePath: string;
246	    fileSize: number;
247	  }
248	  const candidates: Candidate[] = [];
249	
250	  for (const file of files) {
251	    if (!VIDEO_EXTENSIONS.has(extname(file).toLowerCase())) continue;
252	    result.videoFiles++;
253	    if (tracked.has(pathKey(file))) {
254	      result.alreadyTracked++;
255	      continue;
256	    }
257	    let size = 0;
258	    try {
259	      size = (await stat(file)).size;
260	    } catch {
261	      continue; // vanished between the walk and the stat
262	    }
263	    if (size < MIN_FILE_SIZE) {
264	      result.tooSmall++;
265	      continue;
266	    }
267	    const outputDirectory = dirname(file);
268	    // Group label: the first folder below the scanned root ("Unconverted" when
269	    // the file sits directly in the root).
270	    const rel = relative(root, outputDirectory);
271	    const firstSegment = rel && rel !== "." ? rel.split(sep)[0] : "";
272	    candidates.push({
273	      id: localFileJobId(file),
274	      url: pathToFileURL(file).href,
275	      title: hardenName(basename(file, extname(file))) || "Untitled video",
276	      outputDirectory,
277	      folder: sanitizeFolderName(firstSegment || "Unconverted"),
278	      filePath: file,
279	      fileSize: size,
280	    });
281	  }
282	
283	  if (candidates.length === 0) return result;
284	
285	  const insert = db.transaction((batch: Candidate[]) => {
286	    const stmt = db.prepare(
287	      `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO jobs
288	         (id, url, title, output_directory, target_format, want_subtitles, want_thumbnail,
289	          want_description, folder, file_path, file_size, progress, speed, eta,
290	          download_status, conversion_status, metadata_status)
291	       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, 0, ?, ?, ?, 100, 0, 0, 'downloaded', 'pending', 'not_needed')`,
292	    );
293	    for (const c of batch) {
294	      // INSERT OR IGNORE: a concurrent scan or a re-run after a partial batch
295	      // must never duplicate a file.
296	      result.imported += stmt.run(
297	        c.id,
298	        c.url,
299	        c.title,
300	        c.outputDirectory,
301	        targetFormat,
302	        c.folder,
303	        c.filePath,
304	        c.fileSize,
305	      ).changes;
306	    }
307	  });
308	  insert(candidates);
309	
310	  return result;
311	}

1	// src/archive.ts — yt-dlp --download-archive helpers.
2	//
3	// The archive file is yt-dlp's own idempotence layer: one video id per line
4	// (optionally prefixed by the extractor). When our copy of a file disappears
5	// we must scrub the id, otherwise yt-dlp will skip the video forever.
6	
7	import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
8	
9	/**
10	 * Remove a video id from the archive file (the id is the last field of each
11	 * line) so a lost or moved file can be downloaded again. Returns false if the
12	 * archive cannot be read or rewritten, allowing explicit re-queue routes to
13	 * leave their ignore tombstone in place.
14	 */
15	export function removeFromArchive(archiveFile: string, videoId: string): boolean {
16	  try {
17	    if (!archiveFile || !existsSync(archiveFile)) return true;
18	    const lines = readFileSync(archiveFile, "utf-8").split("\n");
19	    const kept = lines.filter((l) => {
20	      const parts = l.trim().split(/\s+/);
21	      return parts.length === 0 || parts[parts.length - 1] !== videoId;
22	    });
23	    if (kept.length !== lines.length) writeFileSync(archiveFile, kept.join("\n"));
24	    return true;
25	  } catch {
26	    // Callers that promise an explicit re-queue can leave the ignore in place.
27	    return false;
28	  }
29	}
30	
31	/** All video ids currently present in the archive file. */
32	export function readArchiveIds(archiveFile: string): Set<string> {
33	  const ids = new Set<string>();
34	  try {
35	    if (!existsSync(archiveFile)) return ids;
36	    for (const line of readFileSync(archiveFile, "utf-8").split("\n")) {
37	      const parts = line.trim().split(/\s+/);
38	      const id = parts[parts.length - 1];
39	      if (id) ids.add(id);
40	    }
41	  } catch {
42	    // ignore
43	  }
44	  return ids;
45	}

306	export function isTerminalErrorMessage(message: string | null | undefined): boolean {
307	  if (typeof message !== "string") return false;

311	/**
312	 * Build the durable `jobs.last_error` value for a terminal failure.
313	 *
314	 * The raw tail is kept (trimmed and length-capped) so an operator who wonders
315	 * *why* a video was skipped still sees yt-dlp's own words; the marker and the
316	 * label in front are what the sweep, the API and the dashboard read.
317	 */
318	export function formatTerminalErrorMessage(info: TerminalErrorInfo, raw: string | null | undefined): string {
319	  const detail = String(raw ?? "")
320	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
321	    .trim()
322	    .slice(0, 300);
323	  return `${TERMINAL_ERROR_MARKER} ${info.label} — skipped, it will not be retried automatically.${detail ? ` yt-dlp: ${detail}` : ""}`;
324	}

326	/** Split a stored terminal message back into label + detail (for reports/UI). */
327	export function parseStoredTerminalError(
328	  message: string | null | undefined,
329	): { label: string; detail: string } | null {
330	  if (!isTerminalErrorMessage(message)) return null;
331	  const rest = String(message).trimStart().slice(TERMINAL_ERROR_MARKER.length).trim();
332	  const [label, ...detail] = rest.split(" — ");
333	  return { label: label.trim(), detail: detail.join(" — ").trim() };
334	}

336	// --- Format fallback ladder --------------------------------------------------
337	//
338	// "Requested format is not available" is a SELECTOR problem, not a dead video:
339	// the preset the plan asked for has no matching stream. Instead of letting the
340	// failure burn the retry budget and park the video (the old behaviour) the
341	// download worker steps the quality override DOWN one rung and immediately
342	// retries with the new selector.
343	//
344	// The ladder is monotonic — every step persists a strictly lower per-job
345	// `video_quality` override, and nothing ever moves back up — so a job can
346	// descend it at most once and the recovery needs no retry budget to be bounded.
347	// The last rung is `highest` (`bv+ba/b`): it accepts any stream the extractor
348	// found, so a failure there means the video really has no usable formats.
349	export const FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER: readonly string[] = ["4k", "1440p", "1080p", "720p", "480p", "highest"];
350	
351	/**
352	 * The next lower quality preset for `current`, or null when there is none.
353	 *
354	 * `audio` never falls back to a video preset (that would silently download a
355	 * video stream for an audio-only request) and an unknown key has no defined
356	 * position on the ladder — both end the recovery, which the worker records as a
357	 * terminal format failure.
358	 */
359	export function nextFormatFallback(current: string | null | undefined): string | null {
360	  const key = String(current ?? "")
361	    .trim()
362	    .toLowerCase();
363	  if (!key || key === "audio") return null;
364	  const index = FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER.indexOf(key);
365	  return index >= 0 && index + 1 < FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER.length ? FORMAT_FALLBACK_LADDER[index + 1] : null;
366	}
367	
368	/**
369	 * The message stored on a job whose selector was stepped down.
370	 *
371	 * Deliberately NOT a permanent-error shape: the job keeps running, and if it
372	 * later fails for a real reason every failure path overwrites `last_error`. The
373	 * wording also avoids the classifier phrases on purpose — a switch note left on
374	 * a row must never be mistaken for a dead video by the cooldown sweep.
375	 */
376	export function formatSwitchMessage(from: string, to: string): string {
377	  return `Requested quality ${from} is not available for this video — switched to ${to} automatically.`;
378	}

1021-// Instead the old media file is renamed aside (`.superseded`), which also
1022-// frees the output path: yt-dlp refuses to re-download while the target file
1023-// exists (`--no-overwrites`) and `--download-archive` must be scrubbed by the
1024-// caller. The new download deletes the backup on success

### **You**

improve the cookies handling feature and automatically backoff and automatically resume feature

### **Assistant**

Using the brainstorming skill to explore intent before modifying behavior.

This touches three existing flows (cookies watching/validation/export, retry backoff, and auto-resume/requeue). Let me explore the current state of each before asking what "improve" should mean here.

I've explored the three flows. Current state, briefly:

- **Cookies**: `cookies.txt` is watched (hash-based change detection), yt-dlp uses a working copy, browser export is staged/verified, and a recheck probe runs every 30 min. But credential-blocked jobs (age-gate, bot-check, members-only, login errors) are **never auto-requeued** when fresh cookies arrive — the operator must click Retry on each one. Also, when the file changes, its validity is not re-probed (only logged), so a swapped-in broken file isn't detected until downloads start failing.
- **Backoff**: per-video exponential backoff with jitter exists, plus a cooldown sweep (`requeueFailedAfterMinutes`). The circuit breaker (`TOO_MANY_FAILURES`) pauses the engine and **stays paused until a human resumes** — it never retries on its own.
- **Auto-resume**: only the network monitor's own pause (`NETWORK_DISCONNECTED`) auto-resumes. `LOW_DISK_SPACE` requires manual resume *even after disk space is freed* (the workers check disk before claiming, but the pause flag is never cleared), and `TOO_MANY_FAILURES`/`BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS` never self-heal.

First clarifying question — the biggest policy decision:

That's everything I need. This is a bounded change set (all flows already exist in the repo), so here's the short design — please confirm before I implement.

## Design: self-healing cookies, circuit-breaker backoff, and auto-resume

**1. Cookies: validate on change + auto-requeue rescued jobs**
- When `cookiesWatch` reports `appeared`/`updated`, the engine (in its existing 60s tick in `engine.ts`) runs a background validity probe of the new file (reusing `probeCookieFile`/`validateCookies`, already bounded at 120s) and logs the verdict — a swapped-in broken file is caught before downloads fail, instead of after.
- If the probe says the new cookies are usable, a new `requeueCredentialBlockedJobs(config)` in `reconcile.ts` re-queues `failed` rows whose reason is credential-shaped (**age-gated, bot-check, members-only, login/cookies-required** — via a new pure predicate in `retry.ts`), with fresh retry budgets, capped at nothing per your choice (all of them, one cycle). Genuinely dead videos (private, geo-blocked, removed) stay parked — cookies can't rescue those, and the `[terminal]` marker is only cleared for the rescuable labels.

**2. Circuit breaker: auto-resume with escalating backoff** (`resilience.ts`)
- On trip, record the trip count and pause time (in memory, next to `failureCircuit`). A pure `circuitResumeDecision(trips, pausedAtMs, nowMs)` returns the current cooldown: **10 min × 2^trips, capped at 6h** (10m → 20m → 40m → … → 6h). The 60s engine tick calls it; a successful download after resume resets the trip count, so a stable engine doesn't inherit the history. One line of config-free policy, matching how `networkMonitorTick` is already structured and unit-tested.

**3. Auto-resume for the remaining pause reasons**
- **`LOW_DISK_SPACE`**: the worker loops already re-check disk space every iteration — when the check passes again and the pause reason starts with `LOW_DISK_SPACE`, they call `triggerResume()` instead of sleeping forever. It re-pauses immediately if space vanishes again, so this is strictly safe.
- **`BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`**: when `POST /api/settings` applies a patch touching any downloader key (`useAria2c`, `connectionsPerDownload`, `minSplitSize`, `httpChunkSize`, `bufferSize`, `userAgent`, `aria2cPath`) and the pause reason matches, the pause is cleared and the parked job force-requeued (the cause was just fixed).
- **User pauses and `ENGINE_LEASE_LOST` stay manual** — the first is operator intent, the second means another engine owns the database.

**Files touched**: `src/retry.ts` (predicate), `src/reconcile.ts` (credential requeue), `src/tools.ts` (cache reset on change), `src/resilience.ts` (circuit backoff + disk resume), `src/engine.ts` (wire the tick), `src/web.ts` (downloader-args resume on settings change), plus unit tests in the existing files and a README/AGENTS.md update.

**Testing**: unit tests for the predicate, the requeue sweep (rescues age/bot/members/login rows; leaves private/geo/removed parked; fresh budgets), the pure circuit-cooldown math, and disk/settings-triggered resume. Integration scenario for the circuit auto-resume if the mock harness supports it without excessive scaffolding.

Two notes on deliberate policy reversals this makes: the README/AGENTS.md currently document "credential-blocked jobs are never auto-requeued" — that sentence changes. And `triggerResume()` clears the failure circuit, so the auto-resume path resets counters by design (a resumed engine gets a clean slate rather than instantly re-tripping).

204	 * credential change from a touch of the same bytes.
205	 */
206	export function cookiesWatchState(
207	  config: { cookiesFile: string },
208	  onUnreadable?: (msg: string) => void,
209	): CookiesWatchState {
210	  const base = cookiesState(config);
211	  let hash: string | null = null;
212	  if (base.present) {
213	    try {
214	      hash = createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(base.file)).digest("hex");
215	    } catch (e: any) {
216	      // Locked (a browser mid-export) or vanished between the stat and the read.
217	      // A missing hash is never treated as a content change; the caller may log
218	      // that the check was skipped.
219	      onUnreadable?.(`cookies.txt could not be read for the change check (${e?.code || e?.message || e})`);
220	    }
221	  }
222	  return { file: base.file, present: base.present, size: base.size, mtimeMs: base.mtimeMs, hash };

231	 * cookies.txt dropped in *after* startup is already used by the next attempt —
232	 * silently. This is the part that makes it observable: the engine polls it
233	 * (see `reconcile.ts cookiesWatch`) so the operator sees the file being picked
234	 * up, replaced, or vanishing instead of wondering why age-gated videos
235	 * suddenly work or suddenly fail.
236	 *
237	 * `updated` means the BYTES changed. A re-export of identical content is not a
238	 * credential change and must not be reported as one.
239	 */
240	export function detectCookiesChange(config: {
241	  cookiesFile: string;
242	  onUnreadable?: (msg: string) => void;
243	}): { change: CookiesChange; state: CookiesWatchState } {
244	  const state = cookiesWatchState(config, config.onUnreadable);
245	  const prev = cookiesBaseline;
246	  cookiesBaseline = state;
247	  if (!prev) return { change: null, state }; // first observation = baseline
248	  if (!prev.present && state.present) return { change: "appeared", state };
249	  if (prev.present && !state.present) return { change: "disappeared", state };
250	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.hash !== null && state.hash !== null) {
251	    return { change: prev.hash !== state.hash ? "updated" : null, state };
252	  }
253	  // Hashing was impossible for one of the two observations: fall back to the
254	  // size signal (mtime alone is exactly what false-positives) so an unreadable
255	  // file never turns the watcher off completely.
256	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.size !== state.size) {
257	    return { change: "updated", state };
258	  }
259	  return { change: null, state };
260	}

119	export function interruptChild(proc: Bun.Subprocess | undefined): boolean {
120	  if (!proc || proc.exitCode !== null) return false;
121	  const children = killProcessTree(proc, "SIGINT");
122	  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
123	    try {
124	      killProcessTree(proc, "SIGKILL");

127	          process.kill(cpid, "SIGKILL");

131	  }, KILL_GRACE_MS);
132	  (timer as unknown as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
133	  return true;
134	}

362	  const signal = opts.signal ?? abortController.signal;
363	  let consecutiveFails = 0;
364	  console.log("🌐 Network monitor started.");

366	    // Don't even issue a probe in offline mode. Re-check after the awaited

368	    const offlineBeforeProbe = getConfig().offlineMode;

379	    );
380	    consecutiveFails = decision.consecutiveFails;

## Design: self-healing cookies, circuit-breaker backoff, and auto-resume

**1. Cookies: validate on change + auto-requeue rescued jobs**
- When `cookiesWatch` reports `appeared`/`updated`, the engine (in its existing 60s tick in `engine.ts`) runs a background validity probe of the new file (reusing `probeCookieFile`/`validateCookies`, already bounded at 120s) and logs the verdict — a swapped-in broken file is caught before downloads fail, instead of after.
- If the probe says the new cookies are usable, a new `requeueCredentialBlockedJobs(config)` in `reconcile.ts` re-queues `failed` rows whose reason is credential-shaped (**age-gated, bot-check, members-only, login/cookies-required** — via a new pure predicate in `retry.ts`), with fresh retry budgets, capped at nothing per your choice (all of them, one cycle). Genuinely dead videos (private, geo-blocked, removed) stay parked — cookies can't rescue those, and the `[terminal]` marker is only cleared for the rescuable labels.

**2. Circuit breaker: auto-resume with escalating backoff** (`resilience.ts`)
- On trip, record the trip count and pause time (in memory, next to `failureCircuit`). A pure `circuitResumeDecision(trips, pausedAtMs, nowMs)` returns the current cooldown: **10 min × 2^trips, capped at 6h** (10m → 20m → 40m → … → 6h). The 60s engine tick calls it; a successful download after resume resets the trip count, so a stable engine doesn't inherit the history. One line of config-free policy, matching how `networkMonitorTick` is already structured and unit-tested.

**3. Auto-resume for the remaining pause reasons**
- **`LOW_DISK_SPACE`**: the worker loops already re-check disk space every iteration — when the check passes again and the pause reason starts with `LOW_DISK_SPACE`, they call `triggerResume()` instead of sleeping forever. It re-pauses immediately if space vanishes again, so this is strictly safe.
- **`BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`**: when `POST /api/settings` applies a patch touching any downloader key (`useAria2c`, `connectionsPerDownload`, `minSplitSize`, `httpChunkSize`, `bufferSize`, `userAgent`, `aria2cPath`) and the pause reason matches, the pause is cleared and the parked job force-requeued (the cause was just fixed).
- **User pauses and `ENGINE_LEASE_LOST` stay manual** — the first is operator intent, the second means another engine owns the database.

**Files touched**: `src/retry.ts` (predicate), `src/reconcile.ts` (credential requeue), `src/tools.ts` (cache reset on change), `src/resilience.ts` (circuit backoff + disk resume), `src/engine.ts` (wire the tick), `src/web.ts` (downloader-args resume on settings change), plus unit tests in the existing files and a README/AGENTS.md update.

**Testing**: unit tests for the predicate, the requeue sweep (rescues age/bot/members/login rows; leaves private/geo/removed parked; fresh budgets), the pure circuit-cooldown math, and disk/settings-triggered resume. Integration scenario for the circuit auto-resume if the mock harness supports it without excessive scaffolding.

Two notes on deliberate policy reversals this makes: the README/AGENTS.md currently document "credential-blocked jobs are never auto-requeued" — that sentence changes. And `triggerResume()` clears the failure circuit, so the auto-resume path resets counters by design (a resumed engine gets a clean slate rather than instantly re-tripping).

244	  const state = cookiesWatchState(config, config.onUnreadable);

248	  if (!prev.present && state.present) return { change: "appeared", state };
249	  if (prev.present && !state.present) return { change: "disappeared", state };
250	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.hash !== null && state.hash !== null) {
251	    return { change: prev.hash !== state.hash ? "updated" : null, state };

254	  // size signal (mtime alone is exactly what false-positives) so an unreadable
255	  // file never turns the watcher off completely.
256	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.size !== state.size) {
257	    return { change: "updated", state };
258	  }
259	  return { change: null, state };
260	}

312	export function networkMonitorTick(
313	  consecutiveFails: number,
314	  isUp: boolean,

316	  currentPauseReason: string | null,

359	export async function networkMonitor(opts: NetworkMonitorOptions = {}): Promise<void> {

363	  let consecutiveFails = 0;

368	    const offlineBeforeProbe = getConfig().offlineMode;

383	      console.log("🌐 Network down detected. Pausing engine gracefully.");
384	    }
385	    if (decision.shouldResume) {
386	      console.log(offlineNow ? "🌐 Offline mode: clearing the network-caused pause for local work." : "🌐 Network restored!");

这是整合了 cookie 提取功能后的完整方案。范围是有限的——所有流程都已经存在；这旨在扩展它们。

## 方案：自我修复 cookies、回退 (backoff)、自动恢复 + 改进的提取

### A. 之前商定的事项（简述，无变化）
- 检测到 cookies.txt 发生变更时：对其进行重新验证，并使用新的预算自动重新排队受凭据阻塞的任务（在 `retry.ts` 中添加新的纯谓词，在 `reconcile.ts` 中进行清理）。
- 断路器自动恢复，采用递增冷却时间（10分钟 × 2^第n次触发，上限 6 小时；下载成功时重置）。使用纯 `circuitResumeDecision()` 实现，风格与 `networkMonitorTick` 一致。
- 当磁盘空间再次可用时自动恢复 `LOW_DISK_SPACE`；在应用涉及下载器的设置补丁时自动恢复 `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`。用户暂停和 `ENGINE_LEASE_LOST` 保持手动控制。

### B. Cookie 提取改进
1. **过期自动导出** — 在现有的 30 分钟 cookie 重检（`engine.ts`）中，当 `resolveCookieSource` 发现 cookies.txt 缺失或本地诊断无效，但配置的浏览器探测为已登录时，引擎会通过现有的 `exportBrowserCookies()` 从该浏览器自动导出到 cookies.txt 并记录日志。受以下条件限制：仅限在线模式，同时只能运行一个导出任务（重用现有的标志），每次重检最多尝试一次，且失败的自动导出绝不会重新触发自身。额外的状态将被写入 `resolveCookieSource` 已经收集的探测结果中。
2. **在导出时修剪过期 cookies** — `exportBrowserCookies` 在验证后会丢弃 expiry 在过去的行（`cookie-file.ts` 中新增一个纯 `pruneExpiredCookies(text, nowMs)` 函数），报告 `exported/pruned` 计数，并保留未设置/会话过期（值为 0）的行。
3. **失败时尝试其他浏览器** — 当请求的浏览器导出失败时，路由会尝试剩余配置的浏览器（按 `cookieBrowsers` 顺序）并报告成功的是哪一个。封装函数 `exportBrowserCookiesWithFallback(...)` 返回尝试的每个浏览器的结果，因此 UI 可以显示“edge 失败（原因），vivaldi 成功”。
4. **导出时间** — `/api/status` 增加了一个 `cookies` 块（包含 `present`、`file`、`ageSeconds`（来自 cookies.txt 的 mtime，由于引擎从不重写该文件，因此 mtime 即导出时间）、`source`（file 或 browser））。Cookie 导出模态框和设置会显示“exported 2h ago · 130 cookies · from firefox”。同时会显示自动导出。

**涉及文件**：`src/cookie-file.ts`（修剪）、`src/cookies-export.ts`（修剪 + 后备包装器）、`src/tools.ts`（解析结果重用）、`src/retry.ts`（凭据谓词）、`src/reconcile.ts`（重新排队清理）、`src/resilience.ts`（断路器冷却时间 + 磁盘恢复）、`src/engine.ts`（挂载 tick + 自动导出）、`src/web.ts`（设置触发的恢复、状态 cookies 块、导出路由中的后备）、`web_ui.html`（显示年龄 + 后备结果）。

**测试**：针对修剪、谓词、冷却计算和磁盘恢复决策进行单元测试；`exportBrowserCookiesWithFallback` 和自动导出路径针对伪造的 yt-dlp 进行测试（类似于现有的 `tests/cookie-export.test.ts`）；`/api/status` 的 cookies 块通过 web-ui 契约测试进行固定。按照 `AGENTS.md` §12 更新文档。

**政策说明**：README 中关于“自动导出”的声明将会改变（现在保持 engine 自身的凭据处于活跃状态）；在 cookies.txt 变更时进行的重新排队取代了“手动逐个任务重试”的说明。

51	  }

31	  const trimmed = text.trim();
32	  if (!trimmed) {
33	    return { entries: 0, siteEntries: 0, signedIn: false, problem: "cookies.txt is empty." };
34	  }
35	  if (trimmed.startsWith("[") || trimmed.startsWith("{")) {
36	    return {
37	      entries: 0,
38	      siteEntries: 0,
39	      signedIn: false,
40	      problem:
41	        "This is JSON, not a Netscape cookies.txt. Export with a \"Netscape\" / \"cookies.txt\" exporter, or use Save Browser Cookies.",
42	    };
43	  }
44	
45	  let entries = 0;
46	  let siteEntries = 0;
47	  let signedIn = false;
48	  let expiredSession = false;
49	  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
50	    // #HttpOnly_ marks HttpOnly cookies and is still a cookie line.
51	    const line = raw.startsWith("#HttpOnly_") ? raw.slice("#HttpOnly_".length) : raw;
52	    if (!line.trim() || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
53	    const fields = line.split("\t");
54	    if (fields.length !== NETSCAPE_FIELDS) continue;
55	    entries++;
56	    const domain = fields[0].trim().toLowerCase();
57	    const onSite = domain.endsWith("youtube.com") || domain.endsWith("google.com");
58	    if (!onSite) continue;
59	    siteEntries++;
60	    if (!(SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES as readonly string[]).includes(fields[5])) continue;
61	    const expires = Number(fields[4]);
62	    if (!Number.isFinite(expires) || expires === 0 || expires * 1000 > nowMs) signedIn = true;
63	    else expiredSession = true;
64	  }
65	
66	  let problem: string | null = null;
67	  if (entries === 0) {
68	    problem =
69	      "No cookie lines found. Each cookie must be one line with 7 fields separated by TAB characters (not spaces).";
70	  } else if (siteEntries === 0) {
71	    problem = "The file has cookies, but none for youtube.com or google.com.";
72	  } else if (!signedIn && expiredSession) {
73	    problem = "The YouTube/Google session cookies have expired. Sign in to YouTube again and export again.";
74	  } else if (!signedIn) {
75	    problem = "The file has YouTube/Google cookies, but no session cookie (SID / __Secure-3PSID). Sign in to YouTube and export again.";
76	  }
77	  return { entries, siteEntries, signedIn, problem };
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * The most useful line from yt-dlp's stderr when it fails. yt-dlp's last line is
82	 * often a generic "failed to load cookies"; the real cause (a locked Chrome
83	 * database, a missing profile, DPAPI) is the line before it.
84	 */
85	export function ytDlpFailureReason(stderr: string): string {
86	  const lines = stderr
87	    .split(/\r?\n/)
88	    .map((line) => line.trim())
89	    .filter((line) => /^(?:ERROR|WARNING):/.test(line))
90	    .map((line) => line.replace(/^(?:ERROR|WARNING):\s*/, ""))
91	    .filter((line) => line && !/^failed to load cookies$/i.test(line));
92	  if (lines.length === 0) {
93	    const fallback = stderr.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean).pop() || "no output from yt-dlp";
94	    return fallback.slice(0, 300);
95	  }
96	  const cookieish = lines.filter((line) =>
97	    /cookie|database|profile|decrypt|dpapi|keyring|copy|locked|permission|could not|not found|unable/i.test(line),
98	  );
99	  return (cookieish.at(-1) ?? lines.at(-1)!).slice(0, 300);
100	}

#### Thinking

Now I understand the extraction flow. Current weaknesses in cookie extraction:

1. **Profile/container support missing**: `--cookies-from-browser firefox` only reads the default profile. yt-dlp supports `firefox:PROFILE`, `chrome:PROFILE`, keyring/container specifiers (`firefox:default:containers`, `chrome:PROFILE:KEYRING`). Users with multiple profiles (very common!) can't export — the config `cookieBrowsers` is a strict enum of bare names. This is a real gap.

2. **Expiry-based pruning**: the exported jar keeps expired cookies; diagnosis flags expired sessions but nothing prunes them.

3. **After export, working copy**: `resolveCookieSource` force re-check happens, but does `cookieWorkingCopy` cache get reset when the file changes? Looking at `cookieWorkingCopy` — it compares mtime+size of source; after a change it re-copies. OK that's handled.

4. **Export failure when browser is running**: Chrome locks its DB on Windows; yt-dlp error explains. Could improve by suggesting close. Already partially done via ytDlpFailureReason.

5. **No automatic periodic re-export**: browser cookies expire; the engine could auto-refresh cookies.txt from the resolved browser source periodically (e.g., before it expires). The engine already uses `--cookies-from-browser` directly as fallback though.

6. **Export doesn't remove the `.bak` / doesn't notify cookie watcher baseline** — the watcher will pick it up.

7. **Browser detection**: export requires user to pick a browser. Could auto-detect which browsers are installed/signed-in.

What are the highest-value improvements? Let me ask the user, since "improve the cookie extraction feature" is vague. Options:

A. **Profile support** (firefox/chrome profiles, containers) — config schema change: `cookieBrowsers` entries can carry `browser[:profile[:keyring]]`. Validation. UI.

B. **Auto-export**: scheduled/triggered re-export from the resolved browser source when cookies.txt is missing/expired (e.g., at the 30-min recheck, if no valid cookies.txt, re-export from browser). Ties into earlier design: when credential-blocked jobs exist and cookies.txt is absent but a browser source is available.

C. **Prune expired cookies on export** and better diagnosis.

D. **Multi-browser fallback export**: try all configured browsers, use the first signed-in one (currently export is one explicit browser; the resolve loop probes but doesn't save a file).

Let me ask which of these they want. Also keep the earlier approved design in mind — combined implementation afterward.

这是整合了 cookie 提取功能后的完整方案。范围是有限的——所有流程都已经存在；这旨在扩展它们。

## 方案：自我修复 cookies、回退 (backoff)、自动恢复 + 改进的提取

### A. 之前商定的事项（简述，无变化）
- 检测到 cookies.txt 发生变更时：对其进行重新验证，并使用新的预算自动重新排队受凭据阻塞的任务（在 `retry.ts` 中添加新的纯谓词，在 `reconcile.ts` 中进行清理）。
- 断路器自动恢复，采用递增冷却时间（10分钟 × 2^第n次触发，上限 6 小时；下载成功时重置）。使用纯 `circuitResumeDecision()` 实现，风格与 `networkMonitorTick` 一致。
- 当磁盘空间再次可用时自动恢复 `LOW_DISK_SPACE`；在应用涉及下载器的设置补丁时自动恢复 `BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS`。用户暂停和 `ENGINE_LEASE_LOST` 保持手动控制。

### B. Cookie 提取改进
1. **过期自动导出** — 在现有的 30 分钟 cookie 重检（`engine.ts`）中，当 `resolveCookieSource` 发现 cookies.txt 缺失或本地诊断无效，但配置的浏览器探测为已登录时，引擎会通过现有的 `exportBrowserCookies()` 从该浏览器自动导出到 cookies.txt 并记录日志。受以下条件限制：仅限在线模式，同时只能运行一个导出任务（重用现有的标志），每次重检最多尝试一次，且失败的自动导出绝不会重新触发自身。额外的状态将被写入 `resolveCookieSource` 已经收集的探测结果中。
2. **在导出时修剪过期 cookies** — `exportBrowserCookies` 在验证后会丢弃 expiry 在过去的行（`cookie-file.ts` 中新增一个纯 `pruneExpiredCookies(text, nowMs)` 函数），报告 `exported/pruned` 计数，并保留未设置/会话过期（值为 0）的行。
3. **失败时尝试其他浏览器** — 当请求的浏览器导出失败时，路由会尝试剩余配置的浏览器（按 `cookieBrowsers` 顺序）并报告成功的是哪一个。封装函数 `exportBrowserCookiesWithFallback(...)` 返回尝试的每个浏览器的结果，因此 UI 可以显示“edge 失败（原因），vivaldi 成功”。
4. **导出时间** — `/api/status` 增加了一个 `cookies` 块（包含 `present`、`file`、`ageSeconds`（来自 cookies.txt 的 mtime，由于引擎从不重写该文件，因此 mtime 即导出时间）、`source`（file 或 browser））。Cookie 导出模态框和设置会显示“exported 2h ago · 130 cookies · from firefox”。同时会显示自动导出。

**涉及文件**：`src/cookie-file.ts`（修剪）、`src/cookies-export.ts`（修剪 + 后备包装器）、`src/tools.ts`（解析结果重用）、`src/retry.ts`（凭据谓词）、`src/reconcile.ts`（重新排队清理）、`src/resilience.ts`（断路器冷却时间 + 磁盘恢复）、`src/engine.ts`（挂载 tick + 自动导出）、`src/web.ts`（设置触发的恢复、状态 cookies 块、导出路由中的后备）、`web_ui.html`（显示年龄 + 后备结果）。

**测试**：针对修剪、谓词、冷却计算和磁盘恢复决策进行单元测试；`exportBrowserCookiesWithFallback` 和自动导出路径针对伪造的 yt-dlp 进行测试（类似于现有的 `tests/cookie-export.test.ts`）；`/api/status` 的 cookies 块通过 web-ui 契约测试进行固定。按照 `AGENTS.md` §12 更新文档。

**政策说明**：README 中关于“自动导出”的声明将会改变（现在保持 engine 自身的凭据处于活跃状态）；在 cookies.txt 变更时进行的重新排队取代了“手动逐个任务重试”的说明。

52	  if (read.jar === null) {
53	    // yt-dlp writes the jar on exit; no file means the browser store was never read.
54	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Could not read ${browser} cookies: ${ytDlpFailureReason(read.stderr)}` };
55	  }

58	  const diagnosis = diagnoseCookiesText(text);
59	  if (diagnosis.siteEntries === 0) {

63	      error: `${browser} has no YouTube or Google cookies. Sign in to YouTube in ${browser} and try again.`,
64	    };
65	  }
66	  if (!diagnosis.signedIn) {
67	    return {
68	      ok: false,
69	      browser,
70	      error: `${browser}: ${diagnosis.problem ?? "not signed in to YouTube"}`,
71	    };
72	  }
73

75	  const incoming = `${cookiesFile}.incoming`;
76	  let backup: string | undefined;
77	  try {
78	    await writeFile(incoming, text, "utf8");
79	    if (existsSync(cookiesFile)) {

81	      await copyFile(cookiesFile, backup);
82	    }
83	    await rename(incoming, cookiesFile);
84	  } catch (error: any) {
85	    await rm(incoming, { force: true }).catch(() => {});
86	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Could not write ${cookiesFile}: ${error?.message || error}` };
87	  }
88	  return { ok: true, browser, file: cookiesFile, cookies: diagnosis.siteEntries, backup };

1	// src/cookie-file.ts — read and explain Netscape cookies.txt files, and pull the
2	// useful reason out of yt-dlp's output when a cookie source fails.
3	//
4	// Pure functions only (no spawning, no config), so both the probe in tools.ts
5	// and the browser export in cookies-export.ts can use them without an import cycle.
6	
7	/** Cookies that mean "signed in to YouTube/Google". */
8	export const SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES = ["SID", "__Secure-1PSID", "__Secure-3PSID", "LOGIN_INFO"] as const;
9	
10	export interface CookieFileDiagnosis {
11	  /** Lines that are real cookie entries (7 TAB-separated fields). */
12	  entries: number;
13	  /** Entries for youtube.com or google.com. */
14	  siteEntries: number;
15	  /** A session cookie for those sites is present. */
16	  signedIn: boolean;
17	  /** Plain-language reason the file cannot be used, or null when it looks valid. */
18	  problem: string | null;
19	}
20	
21	/** Netscape cookie lines have exactly 7 TAB-separated fields. */
22	const NETSCAPE_FIELDS = 7;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Parse the text of a cookies.txt file. Never throws.
26	 *
27	 * Checked locally, with no network: a signed-in session is a session cookie
28	 * whose expiry (field 5, seconds; 0 = browser-session cookie) is still ahead.
29	 */
30	export function diagnoseCookiesText(text: string, nowMs: number = Date.now()): CookieFileDiagnosis {
31	  const trimmed = text.trim();
32	  if (!trimmed) {
33	    return { entries: 0, siteEntries: 0, signedIn: false, problem: "cookies.txt is empty." };
34	  }
35	  if (trimmed.startsWith("[") || trimmed.startsWith("{")) {
36	    return {
37	      entries: 0,
38	      siteEntries: 0,
39	      signedIn: false,
40	      problem:
41	        "This is JSON, not a Netscape cookies.txt. Export with a \"Netscape\" / \"cookies.txt\" exporter, or use Save Browser Cookies.",
42	    };
43	  }
44	
45	  let entries = 0;
46	  let siteEntries = 0;
47	  let signedIn = false;
48	  let expiredSession = false;
49	  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
50	    // #HttpOnly_ marks HttpOnly cookies and is still a cookie line.
51	    const line = raw.startsWith("#HttpOnly_") ? raw.slice("#HttpOnly_".length) : raw;
52	    if (!line.trim() || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
53	    const fields = line.split("\t");
54	    if (fields.length !== NETSCAPE_FIELDS) continue;
55	    entries++;
56	    const domain = fields[0].trim().toLowerCase();
57	    const onSite = domain.endsWith("youtube.com") || domain.endsWith("google.com");
58	    if (!onSite) continue;
59	    siteEntries++;
60	    if (!(SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES as readonly string[]).includes(fields[5])) continue;
61	    const expires = Number(fields[4]);
62	    if (!Number.isFinite(expires) || expires === 0 || expires * 1000 > nowMs) signedIn = true;
63	    else expiredSession = true;
64	  }
65	
66	  let problem: string | null = null;
67	  if (entries === 0) {
68	    problem =
69	      "No cookie lines found. Each cookie must be one line with 7 fields separated by TAB characters (not spaces).";
70	  } else if (siteEntries === 0) {
71	    problem = "The file has cookies, but none for youtube.com or google.com.";
72	  } else if (!signedIn && expiredSession) {
73	    problem = "The YouTube/Google session cookies have expired. Sign in to YouTube again and export again.";
74	  } else if (!signedIn) {
75	    problem = "The file has YouTube/Google cookies, but no session cookie (SID / __Secure-3PSID). Sign in to YouTube and export again.";
76	  }
77	  return { entries, siteEntries, signedIn, problem };
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * The most useful line from yt-dlp's stderr when it fails. yt-dlp's last line is
82	 * often a generic "failed to load cookies"; the real cause (a locked Chrome
83	 * database, a missing profile, DPAPI) is the line before it.
84	 */
85	export function ytDlpFailureReason(stderr: string): string {
86	  const lines = stderr
87	    .split(/\r?\n/)
88	    .map((line) => line.trim())
89	    .filter((line) => /^(?:ERROR|WARNING):/.test(line))
90	    .map((line) => line.replace(/^(?:ERROR|WARNING):\s*/, ""))
91	    .filter((line) => line && !/^failed to load cookies$/i.test(line));
92	  if (lines.length === 0) {
93	    const fallback = stderr.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean).pop() || "no output from yt-dlp";
94	    return fallback.slice(0, 300);
95	  }
96	  const cookieish = lines.filter((line) =>
97	    /cookie|database|profile|decrypt|dpapi|keyring|copy|locked|permission|could not|not found|unable/i.test(line),
98	  );
99	  return (cookieish.at(-1) ?? lines.at(-1)!).slice(0, 300);
100	}

When the watcher sees usable cookies arrive, this sweep gives each of\n * them a fresh retry window (budgets reset, terminal marker cleared) so the\n * operator does not have to click Retry per job. Genuinely dead videos\n * (private, geo-blocked, removed) never match `isCredentialBlockedError`, so\n * they stay parked exactly as before.\n *\n * Lease-gated for the same reason every mutating sweep is: rows in a database\n * another engine owns are not ours to re-arm.\n */\nexport function requeueCredentialBlockedJobs(config: Config): number {\n  if (!holdsEngineLease()) return 0;\n  let rescued = 0;\n  try {\n    const rows = db\n      .query(`SELECT id, last_error FROM jobs WHERE download_status = 'failed'`)\n      .all() as { id: string; last_error: string | null }[];\n    for (const row of rows) {\n      if (!isCredentialBlockedError(row.last_error)) continue;\n      // The IN-guard keeps a job that flipped to an active/claimable state\n      // since the SELECT from being clobbered mid-sweep.\n      const changes = db\n        .run(\n          `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'pending', pause_reason = NULL,\n             retry_count = 0, resume_count = 0, best_progress = 0, progress = 0,\n             last_error = NULL,\n             download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,\n             download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,\n             updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n           WHERE id = ? 1	# Writing Good Tests
2	
3	**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or
4	adding cleanup/helper methods for tests.
5	
6	## Overview
7	
8	A test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything
9	here:
10	
11	```
12	1. Every test names the break it catches
13	2. Every test exercises the real thing
14	```
15	
16	Strict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched
17	failing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns
18	a mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.
19	
20	## Principle 1: Name the Break
21	
22	Before writing the test body, answer: **what production change should
23	make this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test
24	earns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong
25	argument, boundary case, or broken contract.
26	
27	**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked
28	fixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred
29	shape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —
30	passes no matter what that code does:
31	
32	```typescript
33	// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true
34	const expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });
35	expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);
36	
37	// ✅ Hand-derived literal
38	expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:"urgent"');
39	```
40	
41	**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —
42	a constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires
43	on redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on
44	the decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but "a failing call is
45	retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens."
46	
47	**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config
48	contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run
49	scripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or
50	exit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming
51	agent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no
52	test at all.
53	
54	**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at
55	its boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload
56	you produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write
57	(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that
58	is the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely
59	surprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the
60	assumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,
61	getters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they
62	validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —
63	otherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.
64	
65	### Gate Function
66	
67	```
68	BEFORE writing the test body:
69	  Name the production change that would make this test fail.
70	
71	  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior
72	  "The source text changed"  → run the artifact and assert its effects
73	  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior
74	                               that depends on the decision
75	
76	  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.
77	  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:
78	    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture
79	```
80	
81	## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing
82	
83	**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock
84	is present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the
85	component. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you
86	are checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.
87	
88	```typescript
89	// ✅ Real behavior
90	expect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();
91	
92	// ❌ Mock existence
93	expect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();
94	```
95	
96	**your human partner's correction:** "Are we testing the behavior of a
97	mock?"
98	
99	**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method
100	before replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what
101	the test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real
102	implementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.
103	
104	```typescript
105	// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads
106	vi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({
107	  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)
108	}));
109	
110	// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real
111	vi.mock('MCPServerManager');
112	```
113	
114	**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are
115	part of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies
116	nothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or
117	spy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.
118	
119	**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists
120	in reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.
121	Partial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:
122	the test passes while integration breaks.
123	
124	**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only
125	tests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the
126	production class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this
127	class own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.
128	
129	**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows
130	the test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests
131	break when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real
132	components. **your human partner's question:** "Do we need to be using a
133	mock here?"
134	
135	### Gate Function
136	
137	```
138	BEFORE adding a mock or test helper:
139	  List the real method's side effects; keep the ones the test
140	  depends on real — mock the slow/external level below them.
141	
142	  Mock responses mirror the complete real structure.
143	
144	  A method only tests call lives in test utilities, not production.
145	
146	  About to assert on the mock itself?
147	    Unmock it or delete the assertion.
148	```
149	
150	## Tests Ship With the Implementation
151	
152	The TDD cycle — failing test, minimal implementation, refactor — is what
153	"complete" means. Ship the tests the behavior needs and only those:
154	trivial code and human prose earn none, and a test written to satisfy
155	process costs maintenance forever.
156	
157	## The Mutation Check
158	
159	Before finishing, mentally mutate the production code; at least one test
160	should fail for each realistic mutation:
161	
162	- Wrong constant or argument
163	- Wrong branch handler
164	- Missing state change or side effect
165	- Empty or default return
166	- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input
167	
168	A mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the
169	test as tautological.
170	
171	## Quick Reference
172	
173	| When you... | Do |
174	|-------------|-----|
175	| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |
176	| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; never with the code under test |
177	| Test a script or document | Run it / pressure-test its consumer; never grep its text |
178	| Reach for a dependency test | Test your boundary contract, not their documented mechanics |
179	| Want to assert on a mocked element | Test the real component, or unmock it |
180	| Are about to mock a method | Learn its side effects; mock the slow/external level |
181	| Build a mock response | Mirror the real structure completely |
182	| Need cleanup only tests use | Put it in test utilities |
183	| Watch mock setup balloon | Switch to an integration test with real components |
184	| Finish a test file | Run the mutation check |
185	
186	## Warning Signs
187	
188	- Setup and assertion share the same object, guaranteeing equality
189	- The test can fail only through a panic, crash, or missing selector
190	- The test fails on every intentional change, never on accidental breakage
191	- Expected values are hidden behind loops, builders, or helpers
192	- The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed
193	- The test would still matter if only the framework remained
194	- The test exists for coverage, checking no side effect or outcome
195	- An assertion checks a `*-mock` test ID, or fails if you remove the mock
196	- A method is called only from test files
197	- Mock setup is more than half the test, or you can't explain why the mock is needed
198	- Mocking "just to be safe"
199
