1	// src/resilience.ts — pause/resume, circuit breaker, network monitor, disk guard.
2	//
3	// The engine pauses (rather than dies) whenever something systemic goes
4	// wrong: the network drops, the disk fills, cookies expire overnight. Every
5	// in-flight yt-dlp is interrupted, its job is parked as
6	// paused+interrupted, and the job resumes from its .part file on the next
7	// attempt — nothing already downloaded is thrown away.
8	
9	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
10	import { statfs } from "node:fs/promises";
11	import { resolve } from "node:path";
12	import { db } from "./db";
13	import { logError } from "./logger";
14	import {
15	  activeConvertJobs,
16	  activeConvertProcs,
17	  activeDownloadJobs,
18	  activeMetadataJobs,
19	  activeMetadataProcs,
20	  activeProcs,
21	  abortController,
22	  isPaused,
23	  getPauseReason,
24	  getConfig,
25	  setPaused,
26	} from "./state";
27	import type { Config } from "./config";
28	
29	/**
30	 * How long an interrupted child gets to exit on SIGINT before SIGKILL. yt-dlp
31	 * needs the grace period to stop its own aria2c child cleanly; ffmpeg usually
32	 * dies immediately, and a wedged one must never pin a worker.
33	 */
34	const KILL_GRACE_MS = 2_000;
35	
36	/** Recursively discover all descendant process IDs before a parent process is killed. */
37	export function findDescendantPids(pid: number): number[] {
38	  if (process.platform === "win32" || !pid || pid <= 1) return [];
39	  const descendants: number[] = [];
40	  const queue = [pid];
41	  const visited = new Set<number>([pid]);
42	
43	  while (queue.length > 0) {
44	    const current = queue.shift()!;
45	    try {
46	      const res = Bun.spawnSync(["pgrep", "-P", String(current)]);
47	      const out = res.stdout.toString().trim();
48	      if (out) {
49	        for (const line of out.split(/\s+/)) {
50	          const cpid = parseInt(line, 10);
51	          if (cpid && Number.isFinite(cpid) && cpid > 1 && !visited.has(cpid)) {
52	            visited.add(cpid);
53	            descendants.push(cpid);
54	            queue.push(cpid);
55	          }
56	        }
57	      }
58	    } catch {}
59	  }
60	  return descendants;
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Signal a process and all its descendant children (e.g. aria2c spawned under yt-dlp).
65	 * Returns the list of descendant PIDs that were discovered and signaled.
66	 */
67	export function killProcessTree(
68	  proc: Bun.Subprocess | { pid: number } | undefined,
69	  signal: "SIGINT" | "SIGTERM" | "SIGKILL" = "SIGINT",
70	): number[] {
71	  if (!proc) return [];
72	  const pid = proc.pid;
73	  if (!pid || pid <= 1) return [];
74	
75	  try {
76	    if (process.platform === "win32") {
77	      try {
78	        Bun.spawnSync(["taskkill", "/pid", String(pid), "/t", "/f"]);
79	      } catch {}
80	      return [];
81	    }
82	
83	    // Crucial: discover all descendants BEFORE signaling the parent, because once the
84	    // parent terminates, children get adopted by PID 1 (init) and `pgrep -P <pid>` is empty!
85	    const children = findDescendantPids(pid);
86	
87	    // Try killing process group first if pgid == pid
88	    try {
89	      process.kill(-pid, signal);
90	    } catch {}
91	
92	    // Kill all descendants with SIGTERM (and signal) so background tools (like aria2c) exit gracefully
93	    for (const cpid of children) {
94	      try {
95	        process.kill(cpid, signal === "SIGKILL" ? "SIGKILL" : "SIGTERM");
96	      } catch {}
97	      if (signal !== "SIGTERM") {
98	        try {
99	          process.kill(cpid, signal);
100	        } catch {}
101	      }
102	    }
103	
104	    // Signal the root process itself
105	    try {
106	      (proc as Bun.Subprocess).kill?.(signal);
107	    } catch {}
108	    try {
109	      process.kill(pid, signal);
110	    } catch {}
111	
112	    return children;
113	  } catch {
114	    return [];
115	  }
116	}
117	
118	/** SIGINT a child and all its descendants (aria2c/ffmpeg), escalating to SIGKILL after the grace period. */
119	export function interruptChild(proc: Bun.Subprocess | undefined): boolean {
120	  if (!proc || proc.exitCode !== null) return false;
121	  const children = killProcessTree(proc, "SIGINT");
122	  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
123	    try {
124	      killProcessTree(proc, "SIGKILL");
125	      for (const cpid of children) {
126	        try {
127	          process.kill(cpid, "SIGKILL");
128	        } catch {}
129	      }
130	    } catch {}
131	  }, KILL_GRACE_MS);
132	  (timer as unknown as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
133	  return true;
134	}
135	
136	export function triggerPause(reason: string): void {
137	  if (isPaused() && getPauseReason() === reason) return;
138	  setPaused(true, reason);
139	  console.log(`⏸️ Triggering pause: ${reason}`);
140	  for (const [, proc] of activeProcs.entries()) {
141	    try {
142	      interruptChild(proc);
143	    } catch {}
144	  }
145	}
146	
147	export interface CancelledStages {
148	  /** Jobs whose in-flight download process was interrupted. */
149	  downloads: string[];
150	  /** Jobs whose in-flight ffmpeg conversion was interrupted. */
151	  conversions: string[];
152	  /** Jobs whose in-flight sidecar fetch was interrupted. */
153	  metadata: string[];
154	}
155	
156	function stagesFor(predicate: (jobId: string) => boolean): CancelledStages {
157	  const result: CancelledStages = { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
158	  for (const [workerId, jobId] of activeDownloadJobs) {
159	    if (!predicate(jobId)) continue;
160	    result.downloads.push(jobId);
161	    interruptChild(activeProcs.get(workerId));
162	  }
163	  for (const [workerId, jobId] of activeConvertJobs) {
164	    if (!predicate(jobId)) continue;
165	    result.conversions.push(jobId);
166	    interruptChild(activeConvertProcs.get(workerId));
167	  }
168	  for (const [workerId, jobId] of activeMetadataJobs) {
169	    if (!predicate(jobId)) continue;
170	    result.metadata.push(jobId);
171	    interruptChild(activeMetadataProcs.get(workerId));
172	  }
173	  return result;
174	}
175	
176	/**
177	 * Interrupt every in-flight child (yt-dlp download, ffmpeg conversion, sidecar
178	 * fetch) that belongs to one of `jobIds`.
179	 *
180	 * This is what makes a dashboard Delete / Purge / Remove-source actually stop
181	 * the work: without it the job row disappears but the child process keeps
182	 * downloading in the terminal and writes a media file nobody tracks. The kill
183	 * is deliberately fire-and-forget — the workers reap their own children and
184	 * their claim-guarded updates decide what, if anything, is recorded.
185	 */
186	export function cancelActiveStages(jobIds: Iterable<string>): CancelledStages {
187	  const wanted = new Set(jobIds);
188	  if (wanted.size === 0) return { downloads: [], conversions: [], metadata: [] };
189	  return stagesFor((jobId) => wanted.has(jobId));
190	}
191	
192	/**
193	 * Interrupt only the in-flight DOWNLOADS of `jobIds`. A pause parks the
194	 * transfer and nothing else: a sidecar fetch or conversion for the same job
195	 * keeps running. Killing those on pause used to record a failed metadata
196	 * attempt (with yt-dlp's stderr tail as the error) for a pause the user never
197	 * meant as a failure.
198	 */
199	export function interruptActiveDownloads(jobIds: Iterable<string>): string[] {
200	  const wanted = new Set(jobIds);
201	  const interrupted: string[] = [];
202	  for (const [workerId, jobId] of activeDownloadJobs) {
203	    if (!wanted.has(jobId)) continue;
204	    interrupted.push(jobId);
205	    interruptChild(activeProcs.get(workerId));
206	  }
207	  return interrupted;
208	}
209	
210	/** Interrupt every in-flight child regardless of job (shutdown / pause-all). */
211	export function cancelAllActiveStages(): CancelledStages {
212	  return stagesFor(() => true);
213	}
214	
215	export function triggerResume(): void {
216	  setPaused(false, null);
217	  try {
218	    // Re-queue ALL paused jobs (global + user-paused) on an explicit Resume All.
219	    // In-flight jobs still holding a claim finish naturally in their worker —
220	    // the claim's owner and token are left exactly as they are, so the worker's
221	    // own release still matches.
222	    const stmt = db.run(
223	      `UPDATE jobs SET download_status = 'pending', pause_reason = NULL,
224	         download_claimed_by = NULL, download_claimed_at = NULL,
225	         download_claim_token = NULL, download_heartbeat_at = NULL,
226	         updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
227	       WHERE download_status = 'paused' AND download_claimed_by IS NULL`,
228	    );
229	    if (stmt.changes > 0) console.log(`▶️ Re-queued ${stmt.changes} paused job(s).`);
230	  } catch {}
231	  // A human resumed the engine — give the failure circuit a clean slate.
232	  failureCircuit.dl = 0;
233	  failureCircuit.post = 0;
234	}
235	
236	// --- Circuit breaker ---------------------------------------------------------
237	// maxFailures is a consecutive-failure tripwire per pipeline stage: a run of
238	// hard failures with no successes in between (expired cookies overnight, a
239	// YouTube outage, a broken ffmpeg) pauses the whole engine instead of letting
240	// it burn through the queue one video at a time.
241	const failureCircuit = { dl: 0, post: 0 };
242	
243	export function notePipelineSuccess(stage: "dl" | "post"): void {
244	  if (stage === "dl") failureCircuit.dl = 0;
245	  else failureCircuit.post = 0;
246	}
247	
248	export function notePipelineFailure(stage: "dl" | "post", config: Config): void {
249	  if (stage === "dl") failureCircuit.dl++;
250	  else failureCircuit.post++;
251	  const worst = Math.max(failureCircuit.dl, failureCircuit.post);
252	  if (worst >= config.maxFailures) {
253	    const detail = `TOO_MANY_FAILURES (${failureCircuit.dl} consecutive download / ${failureCircuit.post} consecutive post-processing failures, limit ${config.maxFailures})`;
254	    failureCircuit.dl = 0;
255	    failureCircuit.post = 0;
256	    logError("circuit", `pausing engine: ${detail}`);
257	    triggerPause(detail);
258	  }
259	}
260	
261	// --- Network monitor ---------------------------------------------------------
262	// Tried in order: the first reachable host means "online". Multiple endpoints
263	// keep the monitor honest on networks that block one host but not another.
264	const NETWORK_PROBES = [
265	  "https://www.youtube.com/favicon.ico",
266	  "https://youtu.be/favicon.ico",
267	  "https://manifest.googlevideo.com/favicon.ico",
268	  "https://1.1.1.1",
269	  "https://www.google.com/favicon.ico",
270	  "https://cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace",
271	];
272	
273	export type NetworkProbe = () => Promise<boolean>;
274	
275	export async function defaultNetworkProbe(): Promise<boolean> {
276	  for (const url of NETWORK_PROBES) {
277	    try {
278	      const controller = new AbortController();
279	      const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000);
280	      try {
281	        await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, method: "HEAD", redirect: "follow" });
282	      } finally {
283	        clearTimeout(timeout);
284	      }
285	      return true;
286	    } catch {
287	      // try the next probe
288	    }
289	  }
290	  return false;
291	}
292	
293	export async function checkInternet(probe?: NetworkProbe): Promise<boolean> {
294	  return (probe ?? defaultNetworkProbe)();
295	}
296	
297	export interface NetworkMonitorDecision {
298	  /** Consecutive failure count after this tick. */
299	  consecutiveFails: number;
300	  /** Whether the engine should be paused (network down). */
301	  shouldPause: boolean;
302	  /** Whether a network-caused pause should be resumed. */
303	  shouldResume: boolean;
304	}
305	
306	/**
307	 * Pure decision logic for one network-monitor tick.
308	 *
309	 * Separated from the async loop so it is unit-testable without timers or the
310	 * shared `abortController`.
311	 */
312	export function networkMonitorTick(
313	  consecutiveFails: number,
314	  isUp: boolean,
315	  currentlyPaused: boolean,
316	  currentPauseReason: string | null,
317	  offlineMode = false,
318	): NetworkMonitorDecision {
319	  // Offline work must not be gated by connectivity. Clear only a pause that
320	  // this monitor itself caused; a user, disk, or circuit-breaker pause remains.
321	  if (offlineMode) {
322	    return {
323	      consecutiveFails: 0,
324	      shouldPause: false,
325	      shouldResume: currentlyPaused && currentPauseReason === "NETWORK_DISCONNECTED",
326	    };
327	  }
328	  if (!isUp) {
329	    const next = consecutiveFails + 1;
330	    return {
331	      consecutiveFails: next,
332	      shouldPause: next >= 2 && !currentlyPaused,
333	      shouldResume: false,
334	    };
335	  }
336	  return {
337	    consecutiveFails: 0,
338	    shouldPause: false,
339	    shouldResume: consecutiveFails > 0 && currentPauseReason === "NETWORK_DISCONNECTED",
340	  };
341	}
342	
343	export interface NetworkMonitorOptions {
344	  /** Injectable probe (default: real fetch against YouTube endpoints). */
345	  probe?: NetworkProbe;
346	  /** Milliseconds between probes (default: 15 000). */
347	  intervalMs?: number;
348	  /** Optional lifetime signal; production defaults to the engine shutdown signal. */
349	  signal?: AbortSignal;
350	}
351	
352	/**
353	 * Continuously monitor network reachability.
354	 *
355	 * Two consecutive failures pause the engine; a successful probe after a
356	 * network-caused pause resumes it. User pauses are never cleared by the
357	 * monitor (only "NETWORK_DISCONNECTED" is eligible for auto-resume).
358	 */
359	export async function networkMonitor(opts: NetworkMonitorOptions = {}): Promise<void> {
360	  const probe = opts.probe ?? defaultNetworkProbe;
361	  const intervalMs = opts.intervalMs ?? 15_000;
362	  const signal = opts.signal ?? abortController.signal;
363	  let consecutiveFails = 0;
364	  console.log("🌐 Network monitor started.");
365	  while (!signal.aborted) {
366	    // Don't even issue a probe in offline mode. Re-check after the awaited
367	    // probe as well: the setting may have changed while a request was in flight.
368	    const offlineBeforeProbe = getConfig().offlineMode;
369	    const isUp = offlineBeforeProbe ? false : await checkInternet(probe);
370	    // Preserve the offline observation even if the mode was turned off before
371	    // the next line; no probe actually ran during that tick.
372	    const offlineNow = offlineBeforeProbe || getConfig().offlineMode;
373	    const decision = networkMonitorTick(
374	      consecutiveFails,
375	      isUp,
376	      isPaused(),
377	      getPauseReason(),
378	      offlineNow,
379	    );
380	    consecutiveFails = decision.consecutiveFails;
381	    if (decision.shouldPause) {
382	      triggerPause("NETWORK_DISCONNECTED");
383	      console.log("🌐 Network down detected. Pausing engine gracefully.");
384	    }
385	    if (decision.shouldResume) {
386	      console.log(offlineNow ? "🌐 Offline mode: clearing the network-caused pause for local work." : "🌐 Network restored!");
387	      triggerResume();
388	    }
389	    await Bun.sleep(intervalMs);
390	  }
391	}
392	
393	// --- Disk space guard --------------------------------------------------------
394	let diskCheckWarned = false;
395	
396	/** Volume sizes in bytes, or -1 when no probe could determine them. */
397	export interface DiskUsage {
398	  freeBytes: number;
399	  totalBytes: number;
400	  /** Why every probe failed, when they all did (for the error log). */
401	  error?: string;
402	}
403	
404	/**
405	 * Injection points for the disk-probe fallback chain. Production callers pass
406	 * nothing; the tests use them to force each step of the chain (a build with no
407	 * `statfs`, a Windows host, a shell that hangs or answers nonsense) on any
408	 * machine — the unsupported-`statfs` and PowerShell branches are otherwise
409	 * unreachable off a broken Windows box.
410	 */
411	export interface DiskProbeOptions {
412	  /** statfs implementation. `null` = this Bun build has none (calling it throws). */
413	  statfs?: typeof statfs | null;
414	  /** Platform gate for the PowerShell fallback. */
415	  platform?: NodeJS.Platform;
416	  /** Existence gate for the fallback's "nothing on disk to measure" rule. */
417	  pathExists?: (path: string) => boolean;
418	  /** The bounded PowerShell round-trip; resolves to the shell's stdout, or null. */
419	  runPowerShell?: (drive: string) => Promise<string | null>;
420	  /** Ceiling for the PowerShell round-trip. */
421	  timeoutMs?: number;
422	}
423	
424	/**
425	 * Free + total bytes for the volume holding `path`.
426	 *
427	 * statfs first (one syscall, no child process). Some Bun builds on Windows do
428	 * not implement it at all — then `statfs` is `undefined` and *calling* it
429	 * throws a TypeError synchronously, which a `.catch()` chained on the call can
430	 * never see. That is why every caller goes through here rather than calling
431	 * statfs directly: this function's `try` catches the synchronous throw too,
432	 * and falls back to PowerShell's Get-PSDrive on win32.
433	 *
434	 * Returns -1/-1 rather than throwing when no probe works, so a machine without
435	 * a usable disk probe degrades (no low-disk guard, dashboard shows "unknown")
436	 * instead of failing whatever asked. A path that does not exist always lands
437	 * here, on every platform: the shell fallback deliberately refuses to answer
438	 * for a drive when there is nothing on it to measure.
439	 */
440	export async function diskUsage(path: string, opts: DiskProbeOptions = {}): Promise<DiskUsage> {
441	  const statfsFn = opts.statfs === undefined ? statfs : opts.statfs;
442	  try {
443	    // Exactly what an unimplemented Bun build does: the call itself throws a
444	    // TypeError, before any promise exists to catch.
445	    if (!statfsFn) throw new TypeError("statfs is not a function");
446	    const stats = await statfsFn(path);
447	    return { freeBytes: stats.bavail * stats.bsize, totalBytes: stats.blocks * stats.bsize };
448	  } catch (e: any) {
449	    const fallback = await windowsDiskUsage(path, opts);
450	    if (fallback) return fallback;
451	    return { freeBytes: -1, totalBytes: -1, error: String(e?.code || e?.message || e) };
452	  }
453	}
454	
455	/** Hard ceiling on the PowerShell probe — a hung shell must never stall a caller. */
456	const POWERSHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;
457	/** A cold PowerShell start costs seconds; /api/status polls on every request. */
458	const POWERSHELL_MEMO_TTL_MS = 15000;
459	const driveMemo = new Map<string, { at: number; usage: DiskUsage }>();
460	
461	/**
462	 * The drive letter a path explicitly names (`D:\…`, `c:/…`), or "" when it
463	 * names none.
464	 *
465	 * The test is deliberately syntactic: only a `X:` prefix answers. Resolving
466	 * first would make the answer depend on the HOST rather than on the path — on
467	 * win32 `resolve("/tmp/videos")` and `resolve("./downloads")` both land on the
468	 * current directory's drive, so every relative path (and every POSIX-style
469	 * absolute one) would come back as "C". That is a guessed volume, and "no
470	 * drive, nothing to measure" is exactly what the PowerShell fallback needs to
471	 * be able to say. Callers that do know their run directory resolve the path
472	 * before asking — see `windowsDiskUsage`.
473	 */
474	export function driveLetterOf(path: string): string {
475	  const drive = /^([A-Za-z]):/.exec(path.trim());
476	  return drive ? drive[1] : "";
477	}
478	
479	/** Get-PSDrive probe for win32; null when it cannot answer. */
480	async function windowsDiskUsage(path: string, opts: DiskProbeOptions = {}): Promise<DiskUsage | null> {
481	  try {
482	    if ((opts.platform ?? process.platform) !== "win32") return null;
483	    const exists = opts.pathExists ?? existsSync;
484	    // A path that is not on disk has no volume to measure, and the shell would
485	    // happily answer for the *drive* it sits under — which would silently mask
486	    // the "unknown" state the dashboard and the low-disk guard exist to surface.
487	    // Cheaper than the spawn too, which matters: no statfs means every probe
488	    // here costs a PowerShell start.
489	    if (!exists(path)) return null;
490	    // A relative output root ("downloads", or the default "./downloads") is
491	    // still on a drive, and `driveLetterOf` only answers for an explicit `X:`
492	    // prefix — so resolve such a path against the run directory instead of
493	    // declaring the volume unknown.
494	    const drive = driveLetterOf(path) || driveLetterOf(resolve(path));
495	    if (!drive) return null;
496	    const key = drive.toUpperCase();
497	    const memo = driveMemo.get(key);
498	    if (memo && Date.now() - memo.at < POWERSHELL_MEMO_TTL_MS) return memo.usage;
499	    const usage = await getPSDriveFreeSpace(drive, opts);
500	    // Only successful answers are memoized; a failure must stay retryable.
501	    if (usage) driveMemo.set(key, { at: Date.now(), usage });
502	    return usage;
503	  } catch {
504	    return null;
505	  }
506	}
507	
508	/** One bounded Get-PSDrive round-trip; null on any failure. */
509	async function getPSDriveFreeSpace(drive: string, opts: DiskProbeOptions = {}): Promise<DiskUsage | null> {
510	  const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? POWERSHELL_TIMEOUT_MS;
511	  // The outer race bounds the *injected* probe too (and any implementation
512	  // that ignores its signal), so a hung shell can never stall a caller even if
513	  // the child-process timeout below is bypassed.
514	  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
515	  const timeoutGuard = new Promise<null>((resolveTimeout) => {
516	    timer = setTimeout(() => resolveTimeout(null), timeoutMs);
517	  });
518	  try {
519	    const work = opts.runPowerShell ? opts.runPowerShell(drive) : runPSDriveProbe(drive, timeoutMs);
520	    const out = await Promise.race<string | null>([work, timeoutGuard]);
521	    if (out === null) return null;
522	    return parsePSDriveOutput(out);
523	  } catch {
524	    return null;
525	  } finally {
526	    if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer);
527	  }
528	}
529	
530	/**
531	 * Parse Get-PSDrive's `"<free> <used>"` line. Exported for tests: the shell's
532	 * output shapes (bytes, an error banner, an empty string) are the part that
533	 * decides degraded vs measured, and they are impossible to produce on demand
534	 * from a real shell.
535	 */
536	export function parsePSDriveOutput(out: string): DiskUsage | null {
537	  const [free, used] = out.trim().split(/\s+/).map((n) => parseFloat(n));
538	  if (!Number.isFinite(free)) return null;
539	  return {
540	    freeBytes: free,
541	    totalBytes: Number.isFinite(used) ? free + used : -1,
542	  };
543	}
544	
545	/** Spawn `powershell … Get-PSDrive`, hard-killed at `timeoutMs`; stdout or null. */
546	async function runPSDriveProbe(drive: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string | null> {
547	  const proc = Bun.spawn(
548	    [
549	      "powershell",
550	      "-NoProfile",
551	      "-NonInteractive",
552	      "-Command",
553	      `$d = Get-PSDrive -Name '${drive}'; "$($d.Free) $($d.Used)"`,
554	    ],
555	    { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" },
556	  );
557	  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
558	  try {
559	    const timedOut = new Promise<null>((resolveTimeout) => {
560	      timer = setTimeout(() => {
561	        try {
562	          proc.kill("SIGKILL");
563	        } catch {}
564	        resolveTimeout(null);
565	      }, timeoutMs);
566	    });
567	    const reading = Promise.all([new Response(proc.stdout).text(), proc.exited]);
568	    const result = await Promise.race<[string, number] | null>([reading, timedOut]);
569	    if (!result) return null; // shell never answered
570	    const [out, code] = result;
571	    return code === 0 ? out : null;
572	  } catch {
573	    return null;
574	  } finally {
575	    if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer);
576	  }
577	}
578	
579	export async function checkDiskSpace(
580	  path: string,
581	  minGB: number,
582	  opts: DiskProbeOptions = {},
583	): Promise<{ free: number; ok: boolean }> {
584	  const usage = await diskUsage(path, opts);
585	  if (usage.freeBytes < 0) {
586	    // Degraded mode: never permanently brick the engine over a failed probe —
587	    // log once and allow (yt-dlp will still surface a real disk-full error).
588	    if (!diskCheckWarned) {
589	      diskCheckWarned = true;
590	      console.warn("⚠️ Could not determine free disk space — continuing without the low-disk guard.");
591	      logError(
592	        "disk",
593	        `statfs/PowerShell probe failed for ${path} (${usage.error || "unknown"}); low-disk guard disabled for this run`,
594	      );
595	    }
596	    return { free: -1, ok: true };
597	  }
598	  const freeGB = usage.freeBytes / 1024 ** 3;
599	  return { free: freeGB, ok: freeGB > minGB };
600	}
601	
602	// --- Child-process bookkeeping ----------------------------------------------
603	// Kill in-flight children on shutdown; called by the lifecycle module.
604	export function killActiveChildren(): void {
605	  for (const [, proc] of activeProcs) {
606	    try {
607	      proc.kill("SIGINT");
608	    } catch {}
609	  }
610	  for (const [, proc] of activeConvertProcs) {
611	    try {
612	      proc.kill("SIGINT");
613	    } catch {}
614	  }
615	  for (const [, proc] of activeMetadataProcs) {
616	    try {
617	      proc.kill("SIGINT");
618	    } catch {}
619	  }
620	}

292	          completedSources++;
293	          logError("scan", `${url}: ${e?.message || e}`);
294	          console.error(`❌ Failed to scan ${url}:`, e?.message || e);
295	        }
296	      }
297	    };
298	    const workers = Array.from({ length: SCAN_CONCURRENCY }, () => runScanWorker());
299	    await Promise.all(workers);

318	    networkMonitor();

321	  }
322	  setInterval(() => {

324	    // already reported by the reaper. The void + catch keeps the interval from
325	    // surfacing an unhandled rejection if the DB is mid-shutdown.
326	    void reapStaleClaims(getConfig()).catch(() => {});
327	  }, 60_000);
328	  // Dynamic download-slot autoscaling (no-op when autoscaleEnabled=false). The
329	  // pool is topped up first, so a raised maxDownloadWorkers gets its processes
330	  // before the autoscaler is allowed to use the new ceiling.
331	  setInterval(() => {
332	    ensureDownloadWorkers();
333	    autoscaleTick();
334	  }, 15_000);
335	  // Failed-job sweep: re-queue transient failures after their cooldown. It also
336	  // re-queues failed CONVERSIONS, which is exactly what offline mode wants, so
337	  // the sweep keeps running; download re-queues simply wait for the mode to end.
338	  // Lease-gated like the reaper: without the lease this process must not flip
339	  // job rows another engine owns, and a paused engine (BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS,
340	  // disk full, ENGINE_LEASE_LOST) must not re-arm rows the operator parked.
341	  setInterval(() => {

343	    requeueFailedJobs(getConfig());
344	  }, 60_000);
345	  // Cookies sweep is local filesystem observation (not a network fetch), so it
346	  // stays registered through offline mode and is ready if the mode ends live.
347	  setInterval(() => {
348	    if (cookiesWatch(getConfig())) void resolveCookieSource(getConfig(), { force: true });
349	  }, 60_000);
350	  // Browser cookies can expire or the browser can be closed/unlocked later on,
351	  // so the chosen source is re-checked periodically.
352	  setInterval(() => void resolveCookieSource(getConfig()), COOKIE_SOURCE_RECHECK_MS);
353	  // Secondary-storage relocation: files that need no conversion still have to
354	  // reach secondary storage (src/relocate.ts).
355	  startRelocation();
356

358	  //    download → metadata → converter, all driven by job status in the DB.
359	  ensureDownloadWorkers();
360	  for (let i = 1; i <= config.maxMetadataWorkers; i++) {
361	    supervise(`metadata-worker-${i}`, () => metadataWorker(i, config));
362	  }
363	  for (let i = 1; i <= config.maxConcurrentConverts; i++) {
364	    supervise(`converter-worker-${i}`, () => converterWorker(i, config));
365	  }
366

368	  // checks live offlineMode before every scan and resumes on a later tick.
369	  if (config.daemonMode) startAutonomousPolling(config);

371	  setInterval(renderDashboard, 2000);
372	  console.log(

1	// src/lease.ts — the database-level engine lease: one engine per `archive.db`.
2	//
3	// The web port is the HTTP lock, but it is not an ownership primitive for the
4	// job database: two engines configured with different `webPort` values bind
5	// their own ports happily and then both run the startup reconciliation on the
6	// same rows — each resetting the other's in-flight claims, which looks exactly
7	// like workers fighting over jobs. The port also says nothing about a *stale*
8	// engine whose process died without releasing it.
9	//
10	// The lease lives in the database, so it is shared by every process that can
11	// touch the jobs table:
12	//
13	//   • acquisition happens in a short SQLite write transaction BEFORE any
14	//     startup sweep, so a second engine refuses to start instead of
15	//     re-queueing the live engine's work;
16	//   • `owner` is a random per-process token — not the port, not the pid alone —
17	//     so two processes can never mistake each other for themselves;
18	//   • `expires_at` is renewed by a heartbeat, and an expired lease can be taken
19	//     over (a crashed engine must not wedge the archive forever);
20	//   • `fencing` increases monotonically on every acquisition, so "this row was
21	//     written by the previous generation of the engine" is decidable — the
22	//     claim tokens in `db.ts` use the same idea per job.
23	//
24	// The lease is released on graceful shutdown (so a restart is never blocked by
25	// a process that exited cleanly); a hard kill simply lets it expire.

34	export const ENGINE_LEASE_RENEW_MS = 20_000;
35	
36	/** The lease row as stored (times are SQLite UTC `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`). */
37	export interface EngineLease {
38	  owner: string | null;
39	  fencing: number;
40	  /** PID of the owning process (same-host liveness checks), null for legacy rows. */
41	  pid: number | null;
42	  /** Hostname the owning process ran on, null for legacy rows. */
43	  host: string | null;
44	  acquiredAt: string | null;
45	  heartbeatAt: string | null;
46	  expiresAt: string | null;
47	}
48	
49	export interface LeaseAcquireResult {
50	  /** True when this process now owns the lease. */
51	  acquired: boolean;
52	  /** The lease row after the attempt (the live holder's when refused). */
53	  lease: EngineLease | null;
54	  /** True when an expired lease was taken over from a previous owner. */

56	}
57	
58	/** This process's lease identity; minted once, reused on re-acquire/renew. */
59	let processOwnerToken: string | null = null;
60	/** Set while this process holds the lease (owner + generation). */
61	let currentLease: { owner: string; fencing: number } | null = null;
62	
63	/** Test-only override for the TTL, read like `YTA_AUDIO_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`. */
64	export function engineLeaseTtlMs(): number {

66	  return Number.isFinite(override) && override > 0 ? override : ENGINE_LEASE_TTL_MS;

3	// Everything the download worker needs to know about HOW to fetch a video is
4	// decided here: which downloader engine (aria2c multi-connection vs yt-dlp's
5	// native downloader), how many connections/fragments to use, how the bandwidth
6	// cap is split across active slots, and the watchdog timeout for this video.
7	//
8	// yt-dlp reference behaviour this encodes (verified against yt-dlp source):
9	//   • `--downloader aria2c` makes yt-dlp hand the transfer to aria2c with
10	//     `-x16 -s16 -j16 --min-split-size 1M` by default; extra args arrive as a
11	//     single `--downloader-args aria2c:…` argv element (yt-dlp shlex-splits
12	//     the text after `aria2c:` — see the quoting note at the call site).
13	//   • yt-dlp maps `--limit-rate` to aria2c's `--max-overall-download-limit`,
14	//     so the global bandwidth cap keeps working on both engines.
15	//   • aria2c only speaks http/https/ftp — for HLS/live streams yt-dlp silently
16	//     falls back to its native downloader, so no special-casing is needed.
17	//   • External downloads still land in yt-dlp's `<name>.part` temp file, so
18	//     partial-file tracking and `--continue` resume behave identically.

52	/**
53	 * The value for yt-dlp's `--downloader-args aria2c:…` — one argv element,
54	 * without inner quotes (see the call site in `buildDownloadPlan` for why).
55	 *
56	 * yt-dlp already defaults aria2c to `-x16 -s16 -j16 --min-split-size 1M`, so we
57	 * only emit what differs from that baseline — fewer moving parts, and an
58	 * explicit `-k` only when the operator changed the split threshold.
59	 *
60	 * aria2c hard-caps `--max-connection-per-server` (`-x`) at **16** — its own
61	 * help says "Possible Values: 1-16" — and answers anything else with exit 28
62	 * ("bad/unrecognized option") *before transferring a byte*, printing that
63	 * help block. Passing an unclamped config value therefore fails every single
64	 * download in the batch identically, so `-x` is clamped here while `-s`/`-j`
65	 * (no such cap) keep the configured value: a higher setting still splits the
66	 * file finer, it just cannot open a 17th connection to one server.
67	 */
68	export const ARIA2C_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_SERVER = 16;
69	export const ARIA2C_MIN_SPLIT_SIZE_BYTES = 1048576; // 1M (aria2c rejects anything lower with exit 28)
70	
71	export function parseAria2cSplitSizeBytes(sizeStr: string): number | null {
72	  const match = sizeStr.trim().match(/^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([KkMmGg]?)[Bb]?$/);
73	  if (!match) return null;
74	  const num = parseFloat(match[1]);
75	  if (!Number.isFinite(num) || num <= 0) return null;
76	  const unit = match[2].toUpperCase();
77	  if (unit === "K") return Math.floor(num * 1024);
78	  if (unit === "M") return Math.floor(num * 1024 * 1024);
79	  if (unit === "G") return Math.floor(num * 1024 * 1024 * 1024);
80	  return Math.floor(num);
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * Engine-wide budget of parallel connections (aria2c) and fragment requests
85	 * (native), shared by every active download slot. Each download's own setting
86	 * is the ceiling for that download; the budget lowers it as slots are added so
87	 * that N slots never open N × 32 connections at once. At up to 4 slots the
88	 * Aggressive profile (32 connections, 64 fragments) runs unchanged; past that
89	 * each download gets its share. These are judgement values, not a YouTube
90	 * limit: raise them if throughput per slot is too low, lower them if the
91	 * transfers start failing as the slot count grows.
92	 */
93	export const CONNECTION_BUDGET = 128;
94	export const FRAGMENT_BUDGET = 256;
95	/** Floor for a per-download share, so a large pool never degenerates to 1. */
96	export const MIN_TRANSFERS_PER_DOWNLOAD = 4;
97	
98	/**
99	 * The transfer count one download may use while `activeSlots` slots run: the
100	 * configured value, reduced to its share of `budget` but never below the floor
101	 * and never above the configured value.
102	 */
103	export function perDownloadTransfers(configured: number, activeSlots: number, budget: number): number {
104	  const wanted = Math.max(1, Math.floor(configured));
105	  const slots = Math.max(1, Math.floor(activeSlots));
106	  const share = Math.floor(budget / slots);
107	  return Math.max(1, Math.min(wanted, Math.max(MIN_TRANSFERS_PER_DOWNLOAD, share)));
108	}
109	
110	export function buildAria2cArgs(config: Config, activeSlots = 1): string {
111	  const n = perDownloadTransfers(config.connectionsPerDownload, activeSlots, CONNECTION_BUDGET);
112	  const x = Math.min(n, ARIA2C_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_SERVER);
113	  const parts = [`-x ${x}`, `-s ${n}`, `-j ${n}`];
114	  const split = (config.minSplitSize || "").trim();
115	  const bytes = split ? parseAria2cSplitSizeBytes(split) : null;
116	  if (split && bytes === null) {
117	    // Not a size at all ("banana", "5X", "1 MB"): hand the value to aria2c
118	    // verbatim instead of dropping it. aria2c validates every option before it
119	    // transfers a byte and answers an unusable `--min-split-size` with exit 28
120	    // plus the option's help block, which the worker turns into the actionable
121	    // BAD_DOWNLOADER_ARGS pause — the whole batch stops once, with the reason,
122	    // instead of looking like a healthy run that quietly ignores the setting.
123	    // Dropping it here would be a silent coercion: the operator asked for a
124	    // different split threshold and would never learn their typo was ignored
125	    // (the same rule the offline switch follows — an unparsable value is
126	    // surfaced, never guessed at).
127	    parts.push(`--min-split-size ${split}`);
128	  } else if (bytes !== null && bytes > ARIA2C_MIN_SPLIT_SIZE_BYTES) {
129	    // A well-formed size above aria2c's 1M floor: yt-dlp's own default is 1M,
130	    // so this is the only case that changes anything.
131	    parts.push(`--min-split-size ${split}`);
132	  }
133	  // A well-formed size at or below the floor is deliberately omitted: yt-dlp's
134	  // default (1M) is the closest satisfiable value and there is no typo to
135	  // surface, so pausing the run over "512K" would be hostile.
136	  return parts.join(" ");
137	}

139	/**
140	 * The per-process bandwidth cap in bytes per second.
141	 *
142	 * yt-dlp's `--limit-rate` is per process, so the configured cap in KB/s is
143	 * divided across the currently active download slots and converted to an
144	 * integer byte rate. Do not impose a per-worker minimum: that silently exceeds
145	 * small configured caps (e.g. 10 KB/s split across 20 workers must not become
146	 * 64 KB/s per worker). Returns null when no cap is configured.
147	 */
148	export function computePerWorkerLimitBytesPerSec(config: Config, activeSlots: number): number | null {
149	  if (config.maxBandwidthKBps <= 0) return null;
150	  const slots = Math.max(1, Math.floor(activeSlots));
151	  return Math.max(1, Math.floor((config.maxBandwidthKBps * 1024) / slots));
152	}

1	// src/cookie-file.ts — read and explain Netscape cookies.txt files, and pull the
2	// useful reason out of yt-dlp's output when a cookie source fails.
3	//
4	// Pure functions only (no spawning, no config), so both the probe in tools.ts
5	// and the browser export in cookies-export.ts can use them without an import cycle.
6	
7	/** Cookies that mean "signed in to YouTube/Google". */
8	export const SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES = ["SID", "__Secure-1PSID", "__Secure-3PSID", "LOGIN_INFO"] as const;
9	
10	export interface CookieFileDiagnosis {
11	  /** Lines that are real cookie entries (7 TAB-separated fields). */
12	  entries: number;
13	  /** Entries for youtube.com or google.com. */
14	  siteEntries: number;
15	  /** A session cookie for those sites is present. */
16	  signedIn: boolean;
17	  /** Plain-language reason the file cannot be used, or null when it looks valid. */
18	  problem: string | null;
19	}
20	
21	/** Netscape cookie lines have exactly 7 TAB-separated fields. */
22	const NETSCAPE_FIELDS = 7;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Parse the text of a cookies.txt file. Never throws.
26	 *
27	 * Checked locally, with no network: a signed-in session is a session cookie
28	 * whose expiry (field 5, seconds; 0 = browser-session cookie) is still ahead.
29	 */
30	export function diagnoseCookiesText(text: string, nowMs: number = Date.now()): CookieFileDiagnosis {
31	  const trimmed = text.trim();
32	  if (!trimmed) {
33	    return { entries: 0, siteEntries: 0, signedIn: false, problem: "cookies.txt is empty." };
34	  }
35	  if (trimmed.startsWith("[") || trimmed.startsWith("{")) {
36	    return {
37	      entries: 0,
38	      siteEntries: 0,
39	      signedIn: false,
40	      problem:
41	        "This is JSON, not a Netscape cookies.txt. Export with a \"Netscape\" / \"cookies.txt\" exporter, or use Save Browser Cookies.",
42	    };
43	  }
44	
45	  let entries = 0;
46	  let siteEntries = 0;
47	  let signedIn = false;
48	  let expiredSession = false;
49	  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
50	    // #HttpOnly_ marks HttpOnly cookies and is still a cookie line.
51	    const line = raw.startsWith("#HttpOnly_") ? raw.slice("#HttpOnly_".length) : raw;
52	    if (!line.trim() || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
53	    const fields = line.split("\t");
54	    if (fields.length !== NETSCAPE_FIELDS) continue;
55	    entries++;
56	    const domain = fields[0].trim().toLowerCase();
57	    const onSite = domain.endsWith("youtube.com") || domain.endsWith("google.com");
58	    if (!onSite) continue;
59	    siteEntries++;
60	    if (!(SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES as readonly string[]).includes(fields[5])) continue;
61	    const expires = Number(fields[4]);
62	    if (!Number.isFinite(expires) || expires === 0 || expires * 1000 > nowMs) signedIn = true;
63	    else expiredSession = true;
64	  }
65	
66	  let problem: string | null = null;
67	  if (entries === 0) {
68	    problem =
69	      "No cookie lines found. Each cookie must be one line with 7 fields separated by TAB characters (not spaces).";
70	  } else if (siteEntries === 0) {
71	    problem = "The file has cookies, but none for youtube.com or google.com.";
72	  } else if (!signedIn && expiredSession) {
73	    problem = "The YouTube/Google session cookies have expired. Sign in to YouTube again and export again.";
74	  } else if (!signedIn) {
75	    problem = "The file has YouTube/Google cookies, but no session cookie (SID / __Secure-3PSID). Sign in to YouTube and export again.";
76	  }
77	  return { entries, siteEntries, signedIn, problem };
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * The most useful line from yt-dlp's stderr when it fails. yt-dlp's last line is
82	 * often a generic "failed to load cookies"; the real cause (a locked Chrome
83	 * database, a missing profile, DPAPI) is the line before it.
84	 */
85	export function ytDlpFailureReason(stderr: string): string {
86	  const lines = stderr
87	    .split(/\r?\n/)
88	    .map((line) => line.trim())
89	    .filter((line) => /^(?:ERROR|WARNING):/.test(line))
90	    .map((line) => line.replace(/^(?:ERROR|WARNING):\s*/, ""))
91	    .filter((line) => line && !/^failed to load cookies$/i.test(line));
92	  if (lines.length === 0) {
93	    const fallback = stderr.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean).pop() || "no output from yt-dlp";
94	    return fallback.slice(0, 300);
95	  }
96	  const cookieish = lines.filter((line) =>
97	    /cookie|database|profile|decrypt|dpapi|keyring|copy|locked|permission|could not|not found|unable/i.test(line),
98	  );
99	  return (cookieish.at(-1) ?? lines.at(-1)!).slice(0, 300);
100	}

1	// src/cookies-export.ts — save a browser's YouTube cookies as cookies.txt.
2	//
3	// yt-dlp reads a browser's cookie store (`--cookies-from-browser`) and writes its
4	// cookie jar to a file (`--cookies`) when it exits, so one yt-dlp run with a
5	// known video (see readBrowserCookieJar in tools.ts) is an export. The export
6	// only replaces cookies.txt when the jar verifiably contains a signed-in YouTube
7	// session, so a failed export never overwrites a working file. The previous file
8	// is kept as `<cookiesFile>.bak`.
9	
10	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
11	import { copyFile, rm, writeFile, rename } from "node:fs/promises";
12	import { COOKIE_BROWSER_NAMES } from "./config";
13	import { diagnoseCookiesText, ytDlpFailureReason } from "./cookie-file";
14	import { readBrowserCookieJar } from "./tools";
15	
16	export interface CookieExportResult {
17	  ok: boolean;
18	  browser: string;
19	  /** The cookies.txt that was written (only when ok). */
20	  file?: string;
21	  /** YouTube/Google cookie entries that were exported. */
22	  cookies?: number;
23	  /** Previous cookies.txt kept as a backup, when there was one. */
24	  backup?: string;
25	  /** Plain-language reason it failed (only when not ok). */
26	  error?: string;
27	}
28	
29	export interface CookieExportOptions {
30	  /** Override the yt-dlp executable (tests). */
31	  ytDlp?: string;
32	  timeoutMs?: number;
33	}
34	
35	/** Export the cookies of `browser` into `cookiesFile`. Never throws. */
36	export async function exportBrowserCookies(
37	  browser: string,
38	  cookiesFile: string,
39	  opts: CookieExportOptions = {},
40	): Promise<CookieExportResult> {
41	  if (!(COOKIE_BROWSER_NAMES as readonly string[]).includes(browser)) {
42	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Unknown browser "${browser}".` };
43	  }
44	  if (!cookiesFile.trim()) {
45	    return { ok: false, browser, error: "No cookies.txt path is configured (cookiesFile)." };
46	  }
47	
48	  const read = await readBrowserCookieJar(browser, { ytDlp: opts.ytDlp, timeoutMs: opts.timeoutMs });
49	  if (read.timedOut) {
50	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Reading ${browser} cookies took too long. Close ${browser} and try again.` };
51	  }
52	  if (read.jar === null) {
53	    // yt-dlp writes the jar on exit; no file means the browser store was never read.
54	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Could not read ${browser} cookies: ${ytDlpFailureReason(read.stderr)}` };
55	  }
56	
57	  const text = read.jar;
58	  const diagnosis = diagnoseCookiesText(text);
59	  if (diagnosis.siteEntries === 0) {
60	    return {
61	      ok: false,
62	      browser,
63	      error: `${browser} has no YouTube or Google cookies. Sign in to YouTube in ${browser} and try again.`,
64	    };
65	  }
66	  if (!diagnosis.signedIn) {
67	    return {
68	      ok: false,
69	      browser,
70	      error: `${browser}: ${diagnosis.problem ?? "not signed in to YouTube"}`,
71	    };
72	  }
73	
74	  // Verified: replace cookies.txt atomically, keeping the old file as a backup.
75	  const incoming = `${cookiesFile}.incoming`;
76	  let backup: string | undefined;
77	  try {
78	    await writeFile(incoming, text, "utf8");
79	    if (existsSync(cookiesFile)) {
80	      backup = `${cookiesFile}.bak`;
81	      await copyFile(cookiesFile, backup);
82	    }
83	    await rename(incoming, cookiesFile);
84	  } catch (error: any) {
85	    await rm(incoming, { force: true }).catch(() => {});
86	    return { ok: false, browser, error: `Could not write ${cookiesFile}: ${error?.message || error}` };
87	  }
88	  return { ok: true, browser, file: cookiesFile, cookies: diagnosis.siteEntries, backup };
89	}

58	 * yt-dlp binaries already ship them and ignore the fetch.
59	 */
60	export function jsRuntimeArgs(runtime: JsRuntime | null = resolvedTools.jsRuntime): string[] {
61	  if (!runtime) return [];
62	  const path = (runtime.path || "").trim();
63	  if (!path) return [];
64	  return ["--js-runtimes", `${runtime.name}:${path}`, "--remote-components", "ejs:github"];
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * When this process *is* the bun interpreter (not a compiled archive.exe),
69	 * yt-dlp can use it as a last-resort JS runtime. Compiled binaries keep
70	 * `process.versions.bun` but `execPath` is not a JS runtime.
71	 */
72	export function bunInterpreterPath(execPath: string = process.execPath): string | null {
73	  const base = basename(execPath).replace(/\.exe$/i, "").toLowerCase();
74	  return base === "bun" ? execPath : null;
75	}
76	
77	export interface CookiesState {
78	  /** The configured path, used verbatim in argv (relative paths still work). */
79	  file: string;
80	  /** Exists AND non-empty — a 0-byte cookies.txt is not usable cookies. */
81	  present: boolean;
82	  size: number;
83	  mtimeMs: number;
84	}
85	
86	/** Snapshot of the cookies file right now. Never throws. */
87	export function cookiesState(config: { cookiesFile: string }): CookiesState {
88	  const file = config.cookiesFile || "";
89	  try {
90	    const s = statSync(file);
91	    return { file, present: s.size > 0, size: s.size, mtimeMs: s.mtimeMs };
92	  } catch {
93	    return { file, present: false, size: 0, mtimeMs: 0 };
94	  }
95	}
96	
97	/** How often browser cookies are re-probe (and the file re-validated) while running. */
98	export const COOKIE_SOURCE_RECHECK_MS = 30 * 60_000;
99	
100	/**
101	 * Cookie source resolved by `resolveCookieSource()`.
102	 *
103	 *   • `fileCookieValid`: result of the last cookies.txt probe (null = not probed).
104	 *   • `browserCookieSource`: the first browser in `cookieBrowsers` whose cookies
105	 *     passed the probe, or null when none did.
106	 */
107	let fileCookieValid: boolean | null = null;
108	let browserCookieSource: string | null = null;
109	let browserCheckedAt = 0;
110	let resolving: Promise<void> | null = null;
111	
112	/**
113	 * yt-dlp does not only READ `--cookies FILE`: on exit it dumps its cookie jar
114	 * back into that file (its help says "read cookies from and dump cookie jar
115	 * in"). Every engine run that pointed yt-dlp at the operator's export therefore
116	 * rewrote it, which the watcher then reported as "cookies.txt updated" every
117	 * minute, and which overwrote the browser export itself.
118	 *
119	 * So yt-dlp is given a private working copy, `<cookiesFile>.working`, that the
120	 * engine refreshes from the export whenever the export changes. The export is
121	 * only ever read.
122	 */
123	export function cookieWorkingCopyPath(cookiesFile: string): string {
124	  return `${cookiesFile}.working`;
125	}
126	
127	let workingCopySource: { mtimeMs: number; size: number } | null = null;
128	
129	/**
130	 * Path to hand yt-dlp for the cookies file. Re-copies the export when it is
131	 * new or has changed since the last copy. Falls back to the export itself if
132	 * the copy cannot be made, so the old behaviour is the worst case.
133	 */
134	export function cookieWorkingCopy(cookiesFile: string): string {
135	  const working = cookieWorkingCopyPath(cookiesFile);
136	  try {
137	    const src = statSync(cookiesFile);
138	    const same =
139	      existsSync(working) &&
140	      workingCopySource !== null &&
141	      workingCopySource.mtimeMs === src.mtimeMs &&
142	      workingCopySource.size === src.size;
143	    if (!same) {
144	      copyFileSync(cookiesFile, working);
145	      workingCopySource = { mtimeMs: src.mtimeMs, size: src.size };
146	    }
147	    return working;
148	  } catch {
149	    return cookiesFile;
150	  }
151	}
152	
153	/**
154	 * The cookie arguments for a yt-dlp call. Order of preference:
155	 *   1. cookies.txt, when it exists and has not failed validation;
156	 *   2. the browser that was resolved from `cookieBrowsers`;
157	 *   3. cookies.txt even though it failed validation (the old behaviour);
158	 *   4. nothing (anonymous).
159	 * Stays synchronous and cheap: it only reads cached state and stats the file.
160	 */
161	export function cookiesArgs(config: { cookiesFile: string }): string[] {
162	  const s = cookiesState(config);
163	  if (s.present && fileCookieValid !== false) return ["--cookies", cookieWorkingCopy(s.file)];
164	  if (browserCookieSource) return ["--cookies-from-browser", browserCookieSource];
165	  return s.present ? ["--cookies", cookieWorkingCopy(s.file)] : [];
166	}
167	
168	/** The browser currently supplying cookies, or null. For logs and the dashboard. */
169	export function activeBrowserCookieSource(): string | null {
170	  return browserCookieSource;
171	}
172	
173	export type CookiesChange = "appeared" | "disappeared" | "updated" | null;
174	
175	/**
176	 * What the cookies watcher remembers between polls: identity of the file plus a
177	 * SHA-256 of its bytes.
178	 *
179	 * `size`/`mtimeMs` alone are NOT a content signal. A browser extension that
180	 * re-exports cookies.txt on its own timer (or a cloud-sync client / an
181	 * antivirus touch) rewrites the file with byte-identical content, and a
182	 * metadata-only rewrite can even keep the size. Judged on mtime that reads as a
183	 * fresh credential set on EVERY poll — one "cookies.txt updated" line per minute
184	 * in `error.log`, forever, which buries the failures the log exists to show.
185	 */
186	export interface CookiesWatchState {
187	  /** The configured path, used verbatim in messages (relative paths work). */
188	  file: string;
189	  /** Exists AND non-empty — a 0-byte cookies.txt is not usable cookies. */
190	  present: boolean;
191	  size: number;
192	  mtimeMs: number;
193	  /** SHA-256 of the content, or null when it could not be read (locked file). */
194	  hash: string | null;
195	}
196	
197	/**
198	 * Watcher-side snapshot. Never throws.
199	 *
200	 * The read is deliberately NOT inside `cookiesState()`: that one runs on the hot
201	 * path (`cookiesArgs()` before every yt-dlp invocation) and stays a single stat.
202	 * A cookies.txt is a few KB of text and the watcher runs once a minute, so
203	 * hashing it here is affordable — and it is the only way to tell a real
204	 * credential change from a touch of the same bytes.
205	 */
206	export function cookiesWatchState(
207	  config: { cookiesFile: string },
208	  onUnreadable?: (msg: string) => void,
209	): CookiesWatchState {
210	  const base = cookiesState(config);
211	  let hash: string | null = null;
212	  if (base.present) {
213	    try {
214	      hash = createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(base.file)).digest("hex");
215	    } catch (e: any) {
216	      // Locked (a browser mid-export) or vanished between the stat and the read.
217	      // A missing hash is never treated as a content change; the caller may log
218	      // that the check was skipped.
219	      onUnreadable?.(`cookies.txt could not be read for the change check (${e?.code || e?.message || e})`);
220	    }
221	  }
222	  return { file: base.file, present: base.present, size: base.size, mtimeMs: base.mtimeMs, hash };
223	}
224	
225	let cookiesBaseline: CookiesWatchState | null = null;
226	
227	/**
228	 * Compare the cookies file with the last observation and remember this one.
229	 *
230	 * `cookiesArgs()` re-stats the file on every yt-dlp invocation, so a
231	 * cookies.txt dropped in *after* startup is already used by the next attempt —
232	 * silently. This is the part that makes it observable: the engine polls it
233	 * (see `reconcile.ts cookiesWatch`) so the operator sees the file being picked
234	 * up, replaced, or vanishing instead of wondering why age-gated videos
235	 * suddenly work or suddenly fail.
236	 *
237	 * `updated` means the BYTES changed. A re-export of identical content is not a
238	 * credential change and must not be reported as one.
239	 */
240	export function detectCookiesChange(config: {
241	  cookiesFile: string;
242	  onUnreadable?: (msg: string) => void;
243	}): { change: CookiesChange; state: CookiesWatchState } {
244	  const state = cookiesWatchState(config, config.onUnreadable);
245	  const prev = cookiesBaseline;
246	  cookiesBaseline = state;
247	  if (!prev) return { change: null, state }; // first observation = baseline
248	  if (!prev.present && state.present) return { change: "appeared", state };
249	  if (prev.present && !state.present) return { change: "disappeared", state };
250	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.hash !== null && state.hash !== null) {
251	    return { change: prev.hash !== state.hash ? "updated" : null, state };
252	  }
253	  // Hashing was impossible for one of the two observations: fall back to the
254	  // size signal (mtime alone is exactly what false-positives) so an unreadable
255	  // file never turns the watcher off completely.
256	  if (prev.present && state.present && prev.size !== state.size) {
257	    return { change: "updated", state };
258	  }
259	  return { change: null, state };
260	}
261	
262	/** Forget the observed cookies state (tests, and a config path change). */
263	export function resetCookiesBaseline(): void {
264	  cookiesBaseline = null;
265	}
266	
267	/**
268	 * Cheap validity probe for any yt-dlp cookie source (one metadata call):
269	 * `["--cookies", file]` or `["--cookies-from-browser", "firefox"]`.
270	 * A browser that cannot be read (not installed, database locked, no profile)
271	 * makes yt-dlp exit non-zero, which counts as "not usable".
272	 */
273	/**
274	 * Upper bound for one cookie probe. Startup waits for the probes, so a yt-dlp
275	 * that hangs (a stalled network, a browser database that never unlocks) must
276	 * not stall the engine: the probe is killed and counts as "not usable".
277	 */
278	export const COOKIE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
279	
280	/**
281	 * A real video used only to make yt-dlp load a browser's cookies and write the
282	 * jar on exit. `--skip-download --playlist-items 0` means nothing is downloaded.
283	 * The video is fetched (about 30 seconds), which is the proven command for this
284	 * export. If the video is ever removed, change this constant.
285	 */
286	export const COOKIE_JAR_URL = "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Are3UkcYytw";
287	
288	/** Result of reading one browser's cookie store into a Netscape jar. */
289	export interface BrowserCookieJar {
290	  /** The jar text, or null when yt-dlp wrote no file (the store was never read). */
291	  jar: string | null;
292	  stderr: string;
293	  timedOut: boolean;
294	}
295	
296	/** Read `browser`'s cookies with yt-dlp into a temp jar. Never throws. */
297	export async function readBrowserCookieJar(
298	  browser: string,
299	  opts: { ytDlp?: string; timeoutMs?: number } = {},
300	): Promise<BrowserCookieJar> {
301	  const dir = await mkdtemp(join(os.tmpdir(), "yta-cookies-"));
302	  const jarPath = join(dir, "jar.txt");
303	  try {
304	    let child: Bun.PipedSubprocess;
305	    try {
306	      child = Bun.spawn(
307	        [
308	          opts.ytDlp ?? ytDlp(),
309	          "--cookies-from-browser",
310	          browser,
311	          "--cookies",
312	          jarPath,
313	          "--skip-download",
314	          "--playlist-items",
315	          "0",
316	          COOKIE_JAR_URL,
317	        ],
318	        { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" },
319	      );
320	    } catch (error: any) {
321	      return { jar: null, stderr: `could not start yt-dlp: ${error?.message || error}`, timedOut: false };
322	    }
323	    let timedOut = false;
324	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
325	      timedOut = true;
326	      try {
327	        child.kill("SIGKILL");
328	      } catch {
329	        // already exited
330	      }
331	    }, opts.timeoutMs ?? COOKIE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS);
332	    let stderr = "";
333	    try {
334	      [stderr] = await Promise.all([new Response(child.stderr).text(), child.exited]);
335	    } finally {
336	      clearTimeout(timer);
337	    }
338	    const jar = await readFile(jarPath, "utf8").catch(() => null);
339	    return { jar, stderr, timedOut };
340	  } finally {
341	    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {});
342	  }
343	}
344	
345	/**
346	 * Is `browser` signed in to YouTube? Reads its cookie store with yt-dlp (about
347	 * 30 seconds, mostly the video fetch) and checks for a live session cookie.
348	 */
349	export async function probeBrowserCookies(browser: string): Promise<CookieProbe> {
350	  const read = await readBrowserCookieJar(browser);
351	  if (read.timedOut) {
352	    return { ok: false, reason: `reading ${browser} cookies did not finish within ${COOKIE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000}s; retried at the next cookie check` };
353	  }
354	  if (read.jar === null) {
355	    return { ok: false, reason: `could not read ${browser} cookies: ${ytDlpFailureReason(read.stderr)}` };
356	  }
357	  const diagnosis = diagnoseCookiesText(read.jar);
358	  if (diagnosis.problem !== null) return { ok: false, reason: diagnosis.problem };
359	  return { ok: true, reason: "" };
360	}
361	
362	/** Is cookies.txt a signed-in YouTube export? Local check, no network. */
363	export function probeCookieFile(file: string): CookieProbe {
364	  const problem = diagnoseCookiesText(readCookiesTextSafely(file)).problem;
365	  return problem === null ? { ok: true, reason: "" } : { ok: false, reason: problem };
366	}
367	
368	/** Outcome of one cookie probe, with the reason it failed (empty when ok). */
369	export interface CookieProbe {
370	  ok: boolean;
371	  reason: string;
372	}
373	
374	export async function probeCookieArgs(source: string[]): Promise<CookieProbe> {
375	  let child: Bun.PipedSubprocess;
376	  try {
377	    child = Bun.spawn(
378	      [
379	        ytDlp(),
380	        ...source,
381	        ...jsRuntimeArgs(),
382	        "--no-warnings",
383	        "--dump-single-json",
384	        "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ",
385	      ],
386	      { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" },
387	    );
388	  } catch (error: any) {
389	    return { ok: false, reason: `could not start yt-dlp: ${error?.message || error}` };
390	  }
391	  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
392	  const timedOut = new Promise<"timeout">((resolve) => {
393	    timer = setTimeout(() => {
394	      try {
395	        child.kill();
396	      } catch {
397	        // already exited
398	      }
399	      resolve("timeout");
400	    }, COOKIE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS);
401	  });
402	  try {
403	    const finished = Promise.all([
404	      new Response(child.stdout).text(),
405	      new Response(child.stderr).text(),
406	      child.exited,
407	    ]).then(([, stderr, code]) => ({ stderr, code }));
408	    const result = await Promise.race([finished, timedOut]);
409	    if (result === "timeout") {
410	      return {
411	        ok: false,
412	        reason: `yt-dlp did not answer within ${COOKIE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000}s (a slow first run, a busy network, or a browser store still being read). It is retried at the next cookie check.`,
413	      };
414	    }
415	    if (result.stderr.toLowerCase().includes("login required")) {
416	      return { ok: false, reason: "YouTube asked for a login, so these cookies were not accepted" };
417	    }
418	    if (result.code === 0) return { ok: true, reason: "" };
419	    return { ok: false, reason: ytDlpFailureReason(result.stderr) };
420	  } catch (error: any) {
421	    return { ok: false, reason: `yt-dlp probe failed: ${error?.message || error}` };
422	  } finally {
423	    clearTimeout(timer);
424	  }
425	}
426	
427	/** Boolean form of probeCookieArgs(), for callers that do not need the reason. */
428	export async function validateCookieArgs(source: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
429	  return (await probeCookieArgs(source)).ok;
430	}
431	
432	/** Cookies file text for diagnosis; an unreadable file gives an empty string. */
433	export function readCookiesTextSafely(file: string): string {
434	  try {
435	    return readFileSync(file, "utf8");
436	  } catch {
437	    return "";
438	  }
439	}
440	
441	/** Cheap validity probe for a cookies file (one yt-dlp metadata call). */
442	export async function validateCookies(cookiesFile: string): Promise<boolean> {
443	  if (!existsSync(cookiesFile)) return false;
444	  return validateCookieArgs(["--cookies", cookieWorkingCopy(cookiesFile)]);
445	}
446	
447	/**
448	 * Decide where cookies come from for this run, and remember the answer:
449	 *
450	 *   1. cookies.txt, if present and (when validateCookiesOnStart) it passes the probe;
451	 *   2. otherwise the first browser in `cookieBrowsers` whose cookies pass the probe;
452	 *   3. otherwise anonymous downloads.
453	 *
454	 * Browser probes are re-run at most every COOKIE_SOURCE_RECHECK_MS unless `force`
455	 * is set (the engine forces a re-run when cookies.txt appears, changes or goes).
456	 * Offline mode does no network work, so nothing is probed then.
457	 */
458	export function resolveCookieSource(
459	  config: {
460	    cookiesFile: string;
461	    validateCookiesOnStart: boolean;
462	    cookieBrowsers: string[];
463	    offlineMode: boolean;
464	  },
465	  opts: { force?: boolean; log?: (msg: string) => void } = {},
466	): Promise<void> {
467	  if (config.offlineMode) return Promise.resolve();
468	  if (resolving) return resolving;
469	  resolving = doResolve(config, opts).finally(() => {
470	    resolving = null;
471	  });
472	  return resolving;
473	}
474	
475	async function doResolve(
476	  config: { cookiesFile: string; validateCookiesOnStart: boolean; cookieBrowsers: string[] },
477	  opts: { force?: boolean; log?: (msg: string) => void },
478	): Promise<void> {
479	  const log = opts.log ?? ((msg: string) => console.log(msg));
480	  const s = cookiesState(config);
481	
482	  if (s.present && config.validateCookiesOnStart) {
483	    const probe = probeCookieFile(s.file);
484	    fileCookieValid = probe.ok;
485	    if (fileCookieValid) {
486	      browserCookieSource = null;
487	      log("✅ cookies.txt has a signed-in YouTube session (checked locally).");
488	      return;
489	    }
490	    // Say WHY, so a bad export is fixable: a format problem, a signed-out
491	    // browser, or an expired session look different in the log.
492	    log("⚠️ cookies.txt is invalid or expired — trying browser cookies.");
493	    log(`   cookies.txt: ${probe.reason}`);
494	  } else if (s.present) {
495	    // Validation switched off: trust the file as before, never probe browsers.
496	    fileCookieValid = null;
497	    browserCookieSource = null;
498	    return;
499	  } else {
500	    fileCookieValid = null;
501	  }
502	
503	  if (!opts.force && Date.now() - browserCheckedAt < COOKIE_SOURCE_RECHECK_MS) return;
504	  browserCheckedAt = Date.now();
505	
506	  const tried: string[] = [];
507	  for (const browser of config.cookieBrowsers) {
508	    const probe = await probeBrowserCookies(browser);
509	    if (probe.ok) {
510	      browserCookieSource = browser;
511	      log(`🍪 Using cookies from ${browser} (${s.present ? "cookies.txt invalid" : "no cookies.txt"}).`);
512	      return;
513	    }
514	    tried.push(`${browser} — ${probe.reason}`);
515	  }
516	  browserCookieSource = null;
517	  if (tried.length === 0) {
518	    log(
519	      `ℹ️ No ${config.cookiesFile} and no cookieBrowsers configured — downloads run anonymously. Drop the file in while the engine runs and it is picked up within a minute.`,
520	    );
521	  } else {
522	    for (const line of tried) log(`   browser ${line}`);
523	    log(
524	      `ℹ️ No usable cookies (cookies.txt missing or rejected; browsers tried: ${config.cookieBrowsers.join(", ")}) — downloads run anonymously. Drop cookies.txt in while the engine runs and it is picked up within a minute.`,
525	    );
526	  }
527	}
528	
529	/**
530	 * Injectable view of the machine, for the discovery search below.
531	 *
532	 * The search itself is the thing that decides "aria2c is not installed", and
533	 * that decision is unreachable in a test on a box that has aria2c (the bare
534	 * name resolves through the real PATH, and on Windows the package-manager shim
535	 * folders are probed whether or not PATH has it). Production passes nothing;
536	 * tests pin the search space so a genuinely missing binary can be discovered
537	 * deterministically — the fallback the engine promises.
538	 */
539	export interface ToolSearchEnv {
540	  /** Stand-in for the app folder (`process.cwd()`). */
541	  cwd?: string;
542	  /** Stand-in for the folder holding the running executable. */
543	  exeDir?: string;
544	  platform?: NodeJS.Platform;
545	  /** Explicit deno path configured by the operator. */
546	  denoPath?: string;
547	  /**
548	   * Environment for the probe's child process (PATH included).
549	   *
550	   * When set, this environment IS the search space: with no PATH in it, the
551	   * bare-name candidates are skipped instead of spawned. Bun/Windows resolves a
552	   * bare name through the *invoking* process's PATH (CreateProcess semantics),
553	   * so an injected empty environment would otherwise still "find" a binary that
554	   * is installed on the machine — and the "nothing is installed" case this
555	   * switch exists for would be untestable there.
556	   */
557	  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
558	  /** Existence gate for absolute candidates. */
559	  exists?: (path: string) => boolean;
560	  /**
561	   * Last-resort bun interpreter (production: `bunInterpreterPath()`). Tests
562	   * omit this so an empty search space really finds nothing.
563	   */
564	  bunInterpreter?: string | null;
565	}
566	
567	async function probeBinary(
568	  bin: string,
569	  args: string[],
570	  search: ToolSearchEnv = {},
571	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; version: string }> {
572	  try {
573	    const proc = Bun.spawn([bin, ...args], {
574	      stdout: "pipe",
575	      stderr: "pipe",
576	      ...(search.env ? { env: search.env } : {}),
577	    });
578	    const [out, err, code] = await Promise.all([
579	      new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
580	      new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
581	      proc.exited,
582	    ]);
583	    const firstLine = (out || err || "")
584	      .split("\n")
585	      .map((l) => l.trim())
586	      .find((l) => l) || "";
587	    return { ok: code === 0, version: firstLine.slice(0, 80) };
588	  } catch {
589	    return { ok: false, version: "" };
590	  }
591	}
592	
593	/**
594	 * Can a bare-name candidate still be resolved through PATH?
595	 *
596	 * Production passes no `env`, so the child inherits the real PATH and the
597	 * answer is always yes. An injected `env`, though, has to be able to mean
598	 * "there is no PATH here" — see `ToolSearchEnv.env` for why the OS alone cannot
599	 * be trusted to enforce that on Windows.
600	 */
601	function pathLookupAvailable(search: ToolSearchEnv): boolean {
602	  if (!search.env) return true;
603	  const pathKey = Object.keys(search.env).find((k) => k.toLowerCase() === "path");
604	  return !!pathKey && !!(search.env[pathKey] ?? "").trim();
605	}
606	
607	// Candidate search order: explicit config path → PATH → app folder → folder of
608	// the compiled exe → common Windows package-manager shims.
609	function toolCandidates(
610	  cfgPath: string,
611	  posixNames: string[],
612	  winNames: string[],
613	  search: ToolSearchEnv = {},
614	): string[] {
615	  const cands: string[] = [];
616	  if (cfgPath && cfgPath.trim()) cands.push(cfgPath.trim());
617	  const cwd = search.cwd ?? process.cwd();
618	  const exeDir = search.exeDir ?? dirname(process.execPath);
619	  const bareNameWorks = pathLookupAvailable(search);
620	  for (const n of posixNames) {
621	    if (bareNameWorks) cands.push(n); // bare name → PATH lookup
622	    cands.push(join(cwd, n)); // next to config.json / working dir
623	    cands.push(join(exeDir, n)); // next to the compiled archive.exe
624	  }
625	  if ((search.platform ?? process.platform) === "win32") {
626	    const home = os.homedir();
627	    const env = search.env ?? process.env;
628	    const progData = env.ProgramData || "C:\\ProgramData";
629	    const localAppData = env.LOCALAPPDATA || join(home, "AppData", "Local");
630	    for (const n of winNames) {
631	      cands.push(
632	        join(cwd, n),
633	        join(exeDir, n),
634	        join(progData, "chocolatey", "bin", n),
635	        join(home, "scoop", "shims", n),
636	        join(localAppData, "Microsoft", "WinGet", "Links", n),
637	      );
638	    }
639	  }
640	  const seen = new Set<string>();
641	  return cands.filter((c) => {
642	    if (seen.has(c)) return false;
643	    seen.add(c);
644	    return true;
645	  });
646	}
647	
648	/**
649	 * Walk the candidate list and return the first one that runs, or null.
650	 *
651	 * Exported (with `search`) so the "no candidate works" outcome — the one that
652	 * turns aria2c into yt-dlp's native downloader — can be tested against a real,
653	 * empty search space instead of being simulated with the `"none"` switch.
654	 */
655	export async function resolveTool(
656	  cfgPath: string,
657	  versionArgs: string[],
658	  posixNames: string[],
659	  winNames: string[],
660	  search: ToolSearchEnv = {},
661	): Promise<{ path: string; version: string } | null> {
662	  const exists = search.exists ?? existsSync;
663	  for (const cand of toolCandidates(cfgPath, posixNames, winNames, search)) {
664	    const isBare = !cand.includes("/") && !cand.includes("\\");
665	    if (!isBare && !exists(cand)) continue;
666	    const probe = await probeBinary(cand, versionArgs, search);
667	    if (probe.ok) return { path: cand, version: probe.version };
668	  }
669	  return null;
670	}
671	
672	const JS_RUNTIMES: { name: JsRuntimeName; posix: string[]; win: string[] }[] = [
673	  { name: "deno", posix: ["deno"], win: ["deno.exe"] },
674	  { name: "node", posix: ["node"], win: ["node.exe"] },
675	  { name: "bun", posix: ["bun"], win: ["bun.exe"] },
676	  { name: "quickjs", posix: ["qjs"], win: ["qjs.exe"] },
677	];
678	
679	/**
680	 * Find a JS runtime yt-dlp can use to solve YouTube's n-challenge.
681	 *
682	 * Preference matches yt-dlp's own: Deno (sandboxed, default) → Node → Bun →
683	 * QuickJS. A missing runtime is never fatal — the engine still starts — but
684	 * every YouTube download will then fail the n-challenge until one appears.
685	 * An operator can specify an explicit Deno executable via `denoPath`.
686	 */
687	export async function resolveJsRuntime(search: ToolSearchEnv = {}): Promise<JsRuntime | null> {
688	  const customDeno = (search.denoPath || "").trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
689	  const denoDisabled = customDeno.toLowerCase() === "none";
690	  if (customDeno && !denoDisabled) {
691	    const found = await resolveTool(customDeno, ["--version"], ["deno"], ["deno.exe"], search);
692	    if (found) return { name: "deno", path: found.path };
693	  }
694	
695	  for (const rt of JS_RUNTIMES) {
696	    if (rt.name === "deno" && denoDisabled) continue;
697	    const found = await resolveTool("", ["--version"], rt.posix, rt.win, search);
698	    if (found) return { name: rt.name, path: found.path };
699	  }
700	  const bun = (search.bunInterpreter ?? null) || null;
701	  if (bun && bun.trim()) return { name: "bun", path: bun.trim() };
702	  return null;
703	}
704	
705	export async function checkDependencies(
706	  config: {
707	    ytDlpPath: string;
708	    ffmpegPath: string;
709	    aria2cPath?: string;
710	    useAria2c?: boolean;
711	    /**
712	     * Offline mode never spawns yt-dlp (no scanning, no downloads, no sidecar
713	     * fetches), so a missing yt-dlp is a note there — not the fatal install
714	     * hint it is for a normal run. ffmpeg stays required: conversion is the
715	     * whole point of an offline pass.
716	     */
717	    offlineMode?: boolean;
718	    denoPath?: string;
719	  },
720	  search: ToolSearchEnv = {},
721	): Promise<void> {
722	  console.log("🔎 Checking dependencies...");
723	  const missing: string[] = [];
724	  // The special value "none" skips aria2c discovery entirely — an operator
725	  // (or the test suite) can force yt-dlp's native downloader even when a
726	  // real aria2c is installed on this machine.
727	  const aria2Disabled = (config.aria2cPath || "").trim().toLowerCase() === "none";
728	  const [ytdlp, ffm, aria2] = await Promise.all([
729	    resolveTool(config.ytDlpPath, ["--version"], ["yt-dlp"], ["yt-dlp.exe"], search),
730	    resolveTool(config.ffmpegPath, ["-version"], ["ffmpeg"], ["ffmpeg.exe"], search),
731	    // aria2c is probed regardless of the flag so the status line can report
732	    // why it is (not) being used; a missing binary is never fatal.
733	    aria2Disabled
734	      ? Promise.resolve(null)
735	      : resolveTool(config.aria2cPath || "", ["--version"], ["aria2c"], ["aria2c.exe"], search),
736	  ]);
737	  const jsRt = await resolveJsRuntime({
738	    ...search,
739	    denoPath: search.denoPath ?? config.denoPath,
740	    bunInterpreter: search.bunInterpreter ?? bunInterpreterPath(),
741	  });
742	
743	  if (ytdlp) {
744	    resolvedTools.ytDlp = ytdlp.path;
745	    console.log(
746	      `  ✅ yt-dlp: ${ytdlp.version || "ok"}${ytdlp.path.includes("/") || ytdlp.path.includes("\\") ? `  [${ytdlp.path}]` : "  [PATH]"}`,
747	    );
748	  } else if (config.offlineMode) {
749	    console.log("  ⚪ yt-dlp: not found — offline mode only converts and moves existing files");
750	  } else {
751	    console.error("  ❌ yt-dlp: not found (PATH, app folder, winget/scoop/chocolatey, ytDlpPath)");
752	    missing.push(
753	      `yt-dlp — Install: winget install yt-dlp  |  scoop install yt-dlp  |  pipx install yt-dlp  |  or set "ytDlpPath" in config.json`,
754	    );
755	  }
756	  if (ffm) {
757	    resolvedTools.ffmpeg = ffm.path;
758	    console.log(
759	      `  ✅ ffmpeg: ${ffm.version || "ok"}${ffm.path.includes("/") || ffm.path.includes("\\") ? `  [${ffm.path}]` : "  [PATH]"}`,
760	    );
761	  } else {
762	    console.error("  ❌ ffmpeg: not found (PATH, app folder, winget/scoop/chocolatey, ffmpegPath)");
763	    missing.push(
764	      `ffmpeg — Install: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg  |  scoop install ffmpeg  |  choco install ffmpeg  |  or set "ffmpegPath" in config.json`,
765	    );
766	  }
767	
768	  resolvedTools.aria2cPath = aria2 ? aria2.path : null;
769	  if (aria2Disabled) {
770	    console.log(`  ⚪ aria2c: disabled (aria2cPath = "none") — using yt-dlp's native downloader`);
771	  } else if (aria2) {
772	    if (config.useAria2c === false) {
773	      console.log(`  ⚪ aria2c: ${aria2.version || "ok"}  [disabled in config — using yt-dlp's native downloader]`);
774	    } else {
775	      console.log(
776	        `  ✅ aria2c: ${aria2.version || "ok"}${aria2.path.includes("/") || aria2.path.includes("\\") ? `  [${aria2.path}]` : "  [PATH]"}  [multi-connection downloads enabled]`,
777	      );
778	    }
779	  } else if (config.useAria2c !== false) {
780	    console.log(
781	      "  ⚪ aria2c: not found — using yt-dlp's native downloader (install it for multi-connection speed: winget install aria2.aria2 | scoop install aria2 | choco install aria2)",
782	    );
783	  }
784	
785	  resolvedTools.jsRuntime = jsRt;
786	  if (jsRt) {
787	    const where = jsRt.path.includes("/") || jsRt.path.includes("\\") ? `  [${jsRt.path}]` : "  [PATH]";
788	    console.log(`  ✅ JS runtime: ${jsRt.name}${where}  [YouTube n-challenge solver]`);
789	  } else {
790	    console.log(
791	      "  ⚪ JS runtime: not found — YouTube downloads need Deno (recommended), Node.js ≥ 22, or Bun to solve the n-challenge. See https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/EJS",
792	    );
793	  }
794	  if (config.denoPath && config.denoPath.trim() && config.denoPath.trim().toLowerCase() !== "none") {
795	    if (!jsRt || jsRt.name !== "deno") {
796	      console.warn(`  ⚠️ Deno: not found or invalid at "${config.denoPath}" — falling back to other runtimes or none`);
797	    }
798	  }
799	
800	  if (missing.length > 0) {
801	    console.error("\n❌ Missing dependencies:");
802	    for (const m of missing) console.error(`   • ${m}`);
803	    process.exit(1);
804	  }
805	  console.log("✅ All dependencies satisfied.");

7	// instead of "not found", a candidate list that never ends) would go unnoticed.

#### Thinking

**Evaluating SQL Resumption**

I’m analyzing how SQL handles interruptions and statuses. I think it’s crucial that we keep manual controls for backward compatibility, avoiding any automatic processes that could disrupt user leases. I’ll ensure that any automatic resumption verifies exact patterns without allowing arbitrary values. It seems that my approach should include testing call options and checking disk space while comparing outputs effectively after each operation. Keeping track of pipeline failures will help avoid unnecessary overwriting of user leases.

207	/** A tiny executable that stands in for yt-dlp: `body` runs with `argValue()` available. */
208	async function fakeYtDlp(name: string, body: string): Promise<string> {
209	  const path = join(dir, `fake-${name}.ts`);
210	  const script = [
211	    "#!/usr/bin/env bun",
212	    "const argValue = (flag) => { const i = process.argv.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? process.argv[i + 1] : ''; };",
213	    body,
214	    "process.exit(0);",
215	  ].join("\n");
216	  await writeFile(path, script + "\n", "utf8");
217	  await chmod(path, 0o755);

9	/**
